items.title: Hollow Knight Silksong Sea of Sorrow DLC: Release Date, New Regions, Bosses, and More
items.content:
After nearly a year of vague “2026” promises, Team Cherry has finally announced a release date for Silksong’s first expansion. The highly anticipated DLC to Steam’s 2026 Game of the Year, Sea of Sorrow, is all set to launch next month, and existing players will be able to enjoy it for free.
Here’s everything you need to know about the Hollow Knight: Silksong Sea of Sorrow DLC ahead of its full release.
Hollow Knight Silksong Sea of Sorrow Release Date and Platforms
Team Cherry has officially confirmed that the Sea of Sorrow expansion will hit Hollow Knight: Silksong on December 11, 2026. The date was revealed on November 27 during a short “Cherry Time” presentation, alongside a fresh trailer.
The expansion arrives on every platform the base game supports, including PC, PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo Switch, and Switch 2. The expansion was first teased back in December 2025, which means players have waited roughly eleven months for specifics.
Hollow Knight Silksong Sea of Sorrow: New Regions, Bosses, and More Content
The footage shown in the initial presentation points to a major change of scenery coming with the Hollow Knight Silksong Sea of Sorrow expansion. The studio describes the expansion as a high-seas adventure with fresh areas to explore, and the trailer shows Hornet traveling across and beneath the water.
“In Sea of Sorrow, players will voyage above and beneath Pharloom’s forgotten ocean, across islands, through forts and into deep caverns beneath the waves,” Team Cherry said in a statement. “We’ve spent the whole year stuffing this adventure full with all the things you’d expect from Hollow Knight: Silksong – crazed characters, high adventure, and epic bosses!”
Expect larger and stranger fights than usual. The developers promise some epic boss fights, and the trailer also shows several interesting new bosses. New characters are also on the way, which suggests fresh quests and dialogue to go with the combat.
Lastly, the final seconds of the trailer suggest a potential fishing minigame coming to Silksong with the Sea of Sorrows expansion. In the trailer, Hornet can be seen casting a thread into the sea, seemingly in an attempt to catch fish. Whether that becomes a full-fledged fishing minigame or just a one-off gag is unclear, but it fits the nautical theme.
We’ve embedded the official trailer for Hollow Knight: Silksong’s Sea of Sorrows expansion below for your convenience.

items.title: PalVerse Style Suits Puella Magi Madoka Magica Characters for Figures
items.content:
With Bushiroad’s PalVerse line, the company always depicts characters from game and anime series in chibi styles, but with still somewhat realistic proportions. It’s an approach that’s worked for series like Umamusume and Demon Slayer, but maybe not as well for things like Disney characters. The good news is that the Puella Magi Madoka Magica characters look great in the PalVerse figure style, but these being blind box, budget figures coming in around $10-17 each depending on where you buy them does mean the execution can vary.
In my case, I managed to find the blind boxes for $8 each and took a chance on two. As you can see, I was lucky enough to get Madoka Kaname and Homura Akemi. These aren’t scale figures and the sizes aren’t accurate, as in-series Madoka is shorter than Homura. Each one is also a static figure that comes with a small plastic part to wedge onto their left foot in order to help stabilize them so they can stand on their own. It is helpful, though I did find my Madoka seemed to be pretty good about being able to stand up under her own power. (Why? Oh, you’ll see why.) The nature of the character designs from the original series means that this chibi direction doesn’t look too far off from how each individual normally looks too. The paint job is generally pretty good for each as well. However, there are some design choices I found a bit questionable for a character.
Photos by Siliconera
Of the two, I think the Homura Akemi Puella Magi Madoka Magica PalVerse figure seemed better executed. She’s great! Her pose comes across as a bit pensive, which suits her personality. She seems thoughtful! Her plastic “anchor” fit perfectly into her high heel and foot. It even seemed helpful, given her leg positions. But I found she could stand even without it, since Bushiroad designed it in a way that ensures both feet are stable on the ground and the weight is distributed well. The paint job means the accent lines on her uniform look good, and the diamonds on her tights are perfect. Even though there is the copyright information on the back of her left leg, it doesn’t feel as obvious as it could be (and I could just use an acrylic marker or something to black it out).
Photos by Siliconera

Meanwhile I like the concept behind the Puella Magi Madoka Magica PalVerse Madoka figure, but there are a few quirks to it. If I only owned that one, I probably wouldn’t even notice! The paint job here is great too, with even the white flourishes on the skirt appearing alongside the red trim and ribbons and bodice color distinctions being accurate. The pose is also cute and seems more innocent, keeping with her personality and role. However, the pose also means she has this odd pitch forward that puts her at a constant lean. It’s very noticeable alongside Homura, and it means she’s a little less stable when placed on a surface. Her plastic anchor stand also doesn’t affix as well to her foot (I tried the left and right ones, even). She’s usually able to stand without it, but that angle means I do prefer it to be there. The copyright information being in white right across the hem of her skirt also stands out in a bad way, though hopefully it being on the back of the figure should hide that a bit. (Why couldn’t Bushiroad have put it on her foot? Or both character’s feet, for that matter?)
Photos by Siliconera
The PalVerse Puella Magi Madoka Magica blind box figures suit the style of the characters and series, but some turned out better than others. I like both the Homura Akemi and Madoka Kaname ones, and there’s a lot of detail in these well-handled paint jobs. But I also think the Madoka pose could have been handled better so she wasn’t leaning in such a way. Also, the stands included help, but a flat plastic stand might have been more beneficial across the board.
The PalVerse Puella Magi Madoka Magica blind box figures of characters are available worldwide. The US release date for the theatrical debut of Puella Magi Madoka Magica the Movie: Walpurgisnacht Rising is January 16, 2027. ThePuella Magi Madoka Magica: The Movie Trilogy 4KUltra HD Blu-ray set will debut on October 15, 2026, and those three films will be streaming on Crunchyroll on November 8, 2026 and Netflix on January 2, 2027. Yen Press handles books tied to the series.

How to Get Doki Doki Literature Club Fortnite Skins
items.content:
Doki Doki Literature Club Fortnite outfits are now live in the game. Players can use all four outfits in every Fortnite game mode. Each outfit costs 1,200 V-Bucks in the Fortnite Item Shop. A bundle with Sayori, Yuri, and Natsuki costs 1,800 V-Bucks. Monika comes free with Doki Doki Literature Club Plus on the Epic Games Store and Epic Games Mobile.
This article covers prices, the bundle, the Monika deal, and the sale on the game.
Doki Doki Literature Club Fortnite Outfits: Release Date and Details
Serenity Forge and Team Salvato teamed up with Epic Games for the crossover. It lets players dress as the Literature Club classmates in any Fortnite mode.
Fortnite confirmed the collaboration on November 26 through its X account. The post included a trailer and gave November 27 as the release date. The wiki also lists the outfits under the Gaming Legends Series.
Sayori, Natsuki, Yuri and Monika from Doki Doki Literature Club are now in the Shop! pic.twitter.com/tC2h95BmsU
— Fortnite (@Fortnite) November 28, 2026
All four outfits are sold in a dedicated Doki Doki Literature Club section of the Fortnite Item Shop. Players buy them with V-Bucks.
Prices for the Sayori, Natsuki, Yuri, and Monika Outfits
The Item Shop lists each outfit at 1,200 V-Bucks. The Doki Doki Literature Club bundle covers three of them and costs less than buying each one alone.
The three bundle outfits would cost 3,600 V-Bucks if bought separately. The bundle cuts that price in half. Monika is not part of the bundle.
How to Get the Fortnite Monika Skin for Free
The Fortnite Monika skin has a second route besides the Item Shop. Players who own Doki Doki Literature Club Plus on the Epic Games Store or Epic Games Mobile now have the outfit in their Fortnite Locker.
New buyers get it too. The Monika outfit stays a free gift with every purchase of the game on those two storefronts. Players who only want Monika can still buy her for 1,200 V-Bucks.
Buying the game does not unlock Sayori, Natsuki, or Yuri. Those three outfits are only available through the Item Shop.
Doki Doki Literature Club Plus Sale and Free Update
Doki Doki Literature Club Plus is 33% off on the Epic Games Store and Epic Games Mobile until December 1. The sale ties into the Fortnite release, since the game purchase includes the Monika outfit.
The Epic Games Store version also received a free update on the same day. It adds:
Controller support
Achievements
Extra gallery art from the mobile version
General optimizations
Dan Salvato released the original psychological horror game in 2017. It became one of the top-rated games of that year. Serenity Forge and Team Salvato say it has passed 30 million downloads worldwide.
The 2021 release, Doki Doki Literature Club Plus, brought the game to consoles. It added remastered visuals and new content. The game has also launched on iOS and Android over the past year.

items.title: Ramayana Is Getting a ‘GTA-Style’ Video Game, Producer Namit Malhotra Reveals
items.content:
Namit Malhotra, the producer behind the Ramayana films, says a “GTA-style” video game based on the epic is in production. He made the comment on DD News, Doordarshan’s news channel, during an interview on Decode with Sudhir Chaudhary that aired on 27 November. Malhotra gave no studio, platform or release window, but he made it clear the game is part of a much bigger plan for the franchise.
The interview was broadcast in the same month that Ramayana: Part 1 reached cinemas, and Malhotra spent much of it on what comes next for the story. His comments about the game spread across social media on 28 November, a little over a week after Grand Theft Auto VI launched. DD News shared a clip from the conversation on X, with the full show on its YouTube channel.
#Decode | From Vision to Big Screen: Namit Malhotra's Ramayana Journey
When Will the Next Chapter of Ramayana Arrive?
Watch Full Show : https://t.co/ZdK2jJl1hR@sudhirchaudhary @malhotra_namit@WAVES_OTT#Decode #DecodeWithSudhirChaudhary #SudhirChaudhary #Ramayana… pic.twitter.com/kTVZofAX0p
— DD News (@DDNewslive) November 27, 2026
What Namit Malhotra said about the Ramayana game
The interview was in Hindi, and the lines below are the English versions carried by several outlets that reported it. “Even a GTA-type game is coming, but I will reveal more at the right time,” Malhotra said. He added that he wants every child to play Ramayana the way they play GTA, and to learn from it while they play.
He also gave a first idea of what players might do in the game. According to the same reports, Malhotra said players will be able to fly with Jatayu and fight with Ravana, and that this is what the team will show in a game that is already in production. Jatayu is the giant vulture who tries to rescue Sita from Ravana in the epic, so a flying sequence would fit the story closely.
Malhotra also pointed to the size of the games business, saying that the gaming industry has overtaken the film industry. He also spoke about theme parks, museums and animation built around the Ramayana. He did not explain what “GTA-style” means beyond those examples, so it is not yet clear whether the game will be open world.
This is not the first time he has linked Ramayana to games. At the film’s Telugu pre-release event in October, Malhotra played a behind-the-scenes video that listed video games, theme park attractions and a Broadway musical among the planned spin-offs. He told the audience then that “Ramayana is a universe”, and in the DD News interview he went a step further by saying a game is already in production.
Why the GTA comparison sets a high bar
The timing of the comparison is hard to miss. Grand Theft Auto VI launched on 19 November and became one of the biggest entertainment releases of the year, with a record launch that our launch week recap followed day by day. Even Prime Minister Narendra Modi joined in, as we reported when his post said India is playing a whole new game.
Rockstar’s games are also famous for how long they take to make. The first GTA VI trailer arrived in December 2023, almost three years before the game finally reached players on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. A game that truly matches GTA in scale would need a large studio and years of work, which is why Malhotra’s comparison has drawn both excitement and doubt online.
At this stage, the only confirmed details are the ones from the interview itself. Malhotra has not named a developer or publisher, and he has not said whether the game is aimed at consoles, PC or phones. Players will have to wait for the reveal he promised “at the right time” before judging how close it comes to Rockstar’s open world.
Ramayana’s film and gaming universe so far
Ramayana: Part 1 opened worldwide on 5 November 2026, directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Prime Focus Studios with Yash’s Monster Mind Creations. Ranbir Kapoor plays Rama, Yash plays Ravana and Sai Pallavi plays Sita, and the film was shot for IMAX with visual effects from DNEG, where Malhotra is chief executive. Trade figures reported this week put its net collection in India above ₹1,000 crore within its first four weeks.
Part 2 is not due until Diwali 2028, after the makers moved it back to allow more production time. That leaves a long gap in which a game, an animated series or other spin-offs could keep the story in front of audiences. Malhotra, who also founded Prime Focus, shares updates on the franchise through his X account.
His game would not be the first major project built on the epic. Pune-based Tara Gaming is developing The Age of Bhaarat, a dark fantasy action-adventure game that uses the Ramayana as its backdrop, with Amitabh Bachchan and author Amish Tripathi among its co-founders. The studio had raised $20 million by October 2025 and was targeting an alpha version for PC and consoles by the end of 2026.

items.title: How to Get the Rainbow Rolex Daytona in GTA 6
items.content:
The Rainbow Rolex Daytona in GTA 6 is a free luxury watch that players can pick up from a mansion on Casanova Island. Its in-game name is the Crowex Octane ‘Kaleidoscope’ (Sapphires & Gold). The island sits in the northeastern part of Vice City. Players do not need to finish Chapter 1 to reach it.
This guide explains the location, the steps to collect the watch, how to save it in the wardrobe, and what it adds to the 34 Luxury Watches collection.
Rainbow Rolex Daytona in GTA 6 Location and Features
The Rainbow Rolex Daytona is the Crowex Octane ‘Kaleidoscope’. It has a gold bracelet and a rainbow gemstone bezel. It has a gold chronograph with a rainbow sapphire bezel.
The watch is inside a mansion on the north side of Casanova Island. The island is in northeastern Vice City, near Vice Beach.
The mansion stands opposite the house that holds the Pegassi Toros, the game’s Lamborghini Urus. Inside, the watch is upstairs in the left bedroom, on the bedside table. The spot is a small table by a red chair.
You do not pay for the watch. You walk into the mansion and take it.
How to Get the Rainbow Rolex Daytona in GTA 6
Follow these steps to collect the watch:
Travel to northeastern Vice City and head to the northern side of Casanova Island.
Zoom in on your map, count the 5th mansion from the left, and enter it.
Walk up the driveway and move past the parked luxury cars.
Follow the passage around the back of the mansion.
Enter through the rear glass door and go upstairs.
Take the bedroom on your left.
Press Triangle or Y to collect the Crowex Octane ‘Kaleidoscope’.
How to Save the Crowex Octane Kaleidoscope
Picking up the watch is not the last step. You need to equip it to keep it permanently.
Go to any safehouse or clothing store with a wardrobe. Open Wardrobe, then Accessories, then Watches. Equip the Crowex Octane ‘Kaleidoscope’ there.
Extra Loot in the Mansion
The bedroom across the hallway holds more items. You can find Anabolics, a collectible trading card, and a Protein Bar inside.
The driveway has 3 luxury vehicles, including a pink sports car. All 3 have alarms. You need a Key Cloner if you want to steal them without drawing attention.
GTA 6 Luxury Watches and Cheats
The Crowex Octane ‘Kaleidoscope’ counts toward the GTA 6 luxury watches collection. Rockstar has hidden 34 luxury watches across Leonida. Those 34 watches are part of the 79 collectible styles each player can find.
Collecting watches also unlocks 2 time cheats. Here are the milestones:
Both GTA 6 cheats only work after you finish the main story. An active cheat disables trophies and saving. The button codes are not confirmed yet, and Rockstar has not published an official list of the watches or the cheats.
You can track your count in the game. Go to Map, then Progress, then Discovered Styles.
Real-World Watch Behind the Kaleidoscope
Rockstar cannot use real brands, so Crowex stands in for Rolex. The Crowex Octane ‘Kaleidoscope’ is inspired by the Rolex Daytona Rainbow.
Rolex introduced the real Daytona Rainbow in 2012 as reference 116595RBOW. Its bezel is set with 36 baguette-cut rainbow sapphires.

items.title: PUBG Gets Its Own Counter-Strike: 5v5 Demolition Mode Arrives on 2 December
items.content:
PUBG: Battlegrounds is getting a 5v5 round-based mode called Demolition, and it lands on PC on 2 December before reaching consoles on 10 December. The PUBG team calls it a new permanent Arcade mode, so it will stay in the game rather than rotate out after a short event. Its trailer shows a buy menu, two marked sites and a reactor to plant, which makes it unlike anything PUBG has run before.
The mode was first teased on 22 November as a permanent Arcade mode built for intense 5v5 attack-and-defend combat. A full trailer followed on 27 November, with a post on the official PUBG account setting out the main features and both launch dates. The dates are given in UTC, and the developers say every detail will be in the Update 44.2 patch notes on 1 December.
Every round counts. Every decision matters.
Demolition brings a new competitive experience to PUBG with fast-paced 5v5 tactical combat, round-based weapon purchases, and skill-based matchmaking powered by a dedicated Demolition RP system.
Battle across Hacienda and Paradise in… pic.twitter.com/CDfmxWG7h0
— PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS (@PUBG) November 27, 2026
How PUBG’s Demolition mode works
Demolition puts two teams of five against each other, with one side attacking and the other defending. In place of a bomb, the trailer shows attackers carrying a device called the Blue Zone Reactor and installing it at one of two marked sites, A or B. Defenders win a round by neutralising the reactor, and the on-screen messages in the trailer read “Blue Zone Reactor Installed” and “Blue Zone Reactor Neutralized”.
Attackers install the Blue Zone Reactor at Site B in round five. Source: PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS Demolition trailer (KRAFTON)
The trailer’s interface also fills in the structure of a match. The round counter reads “Round 1/13”, so a match can run to 13 rounds, and the official post confirms that the first team to win seven rounds takes it. A radial menu lets players mark Site A, Site B or the middle of the map, and attackers get an “Escort Reactor” call to rally teammates around the carrier.
Matches take place on two maps, Hacienda and Paradise. The names echo Hacienda del Patrón on Miramar and Paradise Resort on Sanhok, and the trailer shows sandy compounds, tiled roofs and palm trees, but PUBG has not yet published full layouts. The end of the trailer shows a 7 to 3 win, with a results screen that tracks how many reactors each team installed or dismantled.
A 7 to 3 win on the match results screen. Source: PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS Demolition trailer (KRAFTON)
Demolition also gets its own skill-based matchmaking, powered by a dedicated Demolition RP system. That means a separate set of rank points for the mode, so a player’s battle royale rank should not decide who they face in 5v5. Battle royale ranked keeps its own Season 44 rewards, which are set out in the Update 44.1 patch notes.
What the Demolition trailer shows about the buy menu
Players buy their weapons at the start of each round instead of looting them from the floor, which is the biggest break from how PUBG normally plays. The trailer shows a 15-second buy phase in round one with 1,000 credits to spend. The menu is split into pistols, SMGs and shotguns, assault rifles and LMGs, sniper rifles and DMRs, throwables, armour and tactical gear. Buttons at the bottom let players purchase, refund or request an item from a teammate.
The round one buy menu, with 1,000 credits to spend. Source: PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS Demolition trailer (KRAFTON)
Prices in the trailer start at 200 credits for the P92 pistol, while the Deagle and P18C cost 700 each. The UMP costs 1,150, the SCAR-L 2,200, the ACE32 2,600 and the Beryl M762 3,200, with the Kar98k at 1,400. Stun grenades, frag grenades and Molotov cocktails cost 300 each, a level 2 helmet costs 400 and a level 2 police vest costs 600.
These figures come from pre-release footage, so they could still change before launch. The Update 44.2 notes on the official PUBG patch notes page should confirm the final prices, the round timer and how much money each team earns per round. Update 44.1 followed the same pattern, with its notes published a day before the PC servers updated on 4 November.
Five players a side, two sites and a weapon shop between rounds is the formula Counter-Strike has used for more than two decades. Counter-Strike fans spotted the likeness straight away, and DanskiCS quoted the trailer on X with “WE GOT CS:PUBG”. Counter-Strike 2’s competitive matches run to 13 round wins, while Demolition ends at seven, so a full match should be far shorter. The timing helps the comparison too, with the PGL Singapore Major under way this week.
PUBG already has a team mode in its Arcade line-up, but it works very differently. The Arcade page lists Team Death Match, where 16 players split into two teams and race to a target score with quick respawns. Demolition removes the respawns and makes every round a fresh start, so a single mistake can cost a team the round.
Demolition arrives in a busy December for PUBG
The mode’s PC launch on 2 December lands on the same day as PUBG’s THE SQUAD music project with IVE. December is also the biggest month of the year for PUBG esports. According to the official tournament details, the PUBG Global Championship 2026 runs from 1 to 13 December with 32 teams, and its Grand Finals take place from 11 to 13 December.
A mode with its own rank points also puts more weight on fair play. KRAFTON set out new measures against cheat distribution and ban evasion in its November anti-cheat dev letter, and it publishes weekly ban notices for PUBG. It has also acted on competitive integrity before, permanently banning Himass and TanVuu after a stream-sniping investigation in September.
The trailer and two short announcements are all the PUBG team has shared so far, with the full rule set still to come. Weapon prices, round timers and the Demolition RP tiers should all become clearer once the notes are out. The Update 44.2 patch notes are due on 1 December, Demolition goes live on PC on 2 December, and console players get the mode on 10 December.

Where to Find Red Hulk in GTA 6: Kyle McKittrick’s Missions and Both Endings
items.content:
Quick answer
Red Hulk is Kyle McKittrick, and you meet him at McKittrick Farm in Frogswater, Kelly County, north-east of the Starlet Motel.
Start in Chapter 2 with the Pilot Wanted flyer at the Starlet Motel reception, then finish all three of Kyle’s Strangers & Freaks missions.
Helping the police take him down pays $5,000, while sparing him ends with a hug and no cash.
The Red Hulk in GTA 6 is Kyle McKittrick, a strawberry farmer in Kelly County whose chemical experiments go badly wrong. Finding him takes three side missions spread across Chapters 2 and 3, and the trail starts with a job advert pinned up at a roadside motel. Miss that advert and the whole storyline can pass you by, because nothing in the main story points you towards it.
Kyle became one of the most shared characters in Leonida soon after GTA 6 launched on 19 November. A clip from an IShowSpeed stream showed a huge red figure smashing out of a building, and players quickly nicknamed him Red Hulk. The clip below, shared on X that evening, shows the encounter most players are now trying to reach for themselves.
A creature similar to The Hulk has been found in GTA 6.
(via: @ishowspeedsui) pic.twitter.com/0qE6Kw5jqM
— DiscussingFilm (@DiscussingFilm) November 19, 2026
Where to find Red Hulk in GTA 6
Kyle’s story is one of the Strangers & Freaks side strands in Grand Theft Auto VI on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and it becomes available in Chapter 2. The trigger is a Pilot Wanted flyer for McKittrick Farm, posted at the reception of the Starlet Motel in Kelly County. The motel sits east of Port Gellhorn, one of the Leonida locations Rockstar highlights on its official site.
Interacting with the flyer starts the job at McKittrick Farm, which lies north-east of the motel in the Frogswater area. Either Jason or Lucia can pick it up, so it does not matter which protagonist you are controlling when you reach the motel. The flyer is easy to walk past, because it sits on the wall by the reception desk rather than out on the road.
Guides have not confirmed whether the flyer stays up once Chapter 2 is over. The safest approach is to grab it the first time the story takes you to the Starlet Motel, before you push the main plot forward. Red Hulk himself only appears at the farm in Chapter 3, after the first two jobs are done.
How to unlock all three Kyle McKittrick missions
The first mission, Check Out McKittrick Farm, is a crop-dusting job over Kyle’s strawberry fields. Players take his small plane up and spray a chemical mix across the crops in several low passes. Guides warn that crashing the plane or letting Kyle die can break the rest of the chain, so make a manual save before take-off.
Roughly one in-game day later, Kyle gets in touch about the second job, Collect Chemicals for Kyle. He needs a chemical shipment from the Final Chapter biker gang, who are holding it at a drug lab and want $5,000 for the load. You can pay the gang or steal its van and drive the shipment back to the farm yourself.
Several guides recommend taking the van and keeping the money for the rest of the game. Stealing it means getting past the armed bikers first, so go in ready for a fight. Once the van is parked at McKittrick Farm, Kyle’s part of Chapter 2 is finished.
The final mission, Buddy? (Check on Kyle), unlocks in Chapter 3 after one last message from him. That message can take several in-game days to arrive, so carry on with the main story rather than waiting around at the farm. Players who still see nothing should check they are on the latest patch, because Rockstar’s launch updates page lists a 23 November fix for phone calls that were not triggering correctly.
That fix covered calls that progress the story or unlock mission content, the same kind of problem behind our guide to Raul not calling Lucia. Our breakdown of update 01.002.002 explains how that patch reached PS5 and Xbox Series X|S players on 23 November. If the message still does not appear after updating, spend a few more in-game days in Leonida before heading back to the farm.
Should you kill or spare Red Hulk in GTA 6?
When you return for Buddy? (Check on Kyle), police and hazmat crews from a company called Mutandis have sealed off the farm. Kyle has locked himself inside the barn, and he is no longer the farmer you met in the first two jobs. The game never shows a simple kill or spare prompt, so the ending depends on how you act once you reach the police line.
To side with the police, tell the officers you are Kyle’s friend and then say you are fine. A Mutandis agent hands you a hazmat suit and leads you into the barn, where Kyle soon breaks loose as the Red Hulk. Bringing him down before he wipes out the squad pays $5,000, the only cash reward at the end of the strand.
To spare him, keep your distance, stay out of the crossfire and let the rampage run its course. Kyle tears through the officers, then sits down beside the barn once the fighting is over. Approach him slowly and he asks for a hug that costs some health, then bounds away with no money changing hands. Either way, this is the scene from the viral clips. Kyle overpowers the officers, flips cars and brings down a helicopter by hurling a man into it. Both routes complete the storyline, although whether Kyle appears again later after the spare ending has not been confirmed.
If money matters more than sentiment, the police route is the one to take. Sparing Kyle is the kinder ending, but it leaves you with less health and an empty wallet. Both endings count as finishing his Strangers & Freaks strand, and both begin with the same Pilot Wanted flyer at the Starlet Motel in Chapter 2.

items.title: KRAFTON India Awards 2026: All 18 Categories Revealed, Fan Voting Opens 7 December
items.content:
KRAFTON India has revealed the categories for the KRAFTON India Awards 2026, and fan voting opens on 7 December. The second edition has 18 awards across esports, creators, broadcast talent and community work, and four of the biggest esports awards will be decided purely by data, with no jury and no fan vote. KRAFTON India announced the list on Instagram with the campaign tag #CrownTheYear.
The ceremony is set for Goa in January 2027, as KRAFTON India confirmed during BMIC 2026 and as we set out in our report on the KRAFTON India Awards second edition in Goa. The judging is the biggest change from the first edition, with each category now carrying its own published mix of data, jury and fan votes.
All KRAFTON India Awards 2026 categories
The awards are split into five groups: Decided by Data, Esports, Creators, Talents and Honouring. Here is every category and how its winner will be chosen.
Four esports awards will be decided by data only
Esports Player, Esports Team, In-Game Leader and Emerging Star of the Year will all be decided by “verified KRAFTON India Esports season stats”, according to the announcement. KRAFTON India says these four will have “no jury” and “no vote”, which takes popularity out of the biggest competitive awards. The season data covers events such as BGIS, BMPS, BMSD and BMIC 2026, which also feed the KRAFTON India Esports rankings after BMIC 2026.
The change answers one of the main complaints about the first edition, when fan voting played a big part in several esports categories. KRAFTON India has not yet published which stats it will use, such as finishes, damage, placements or titles, or how they will be weighted.
How the fan and jury votes work
Most of the other categories use a 70% jury and 30% fan split. That covers the KIE Contributor award, all three creator awards and Caster of the Year, so fans can influence the result but cannot decide it alone. Host of the Year is the only category left entirely to fans.
Two esports awards use their own systems. For Clutch Moment of the Year, the jury will shortlist five clips and fans will vote for the winner. The Players’ Choice Award will be voted on by rostered players, which makes it the only award decided by the pros themselves.
Creator and talent awards split by gender and language
Content Creator and Rising Creator of the Year each have separate male and female awards, and Caster of the Year has separate Hindi and English awards. KIE Contributor of the Year is split into Entertainment and Insights. Those splits take the total to 18 awards, one more than the 17 categories in the first edition.
Legacy Award and Social Impact Initiative
The Honouring group has two awards, the Legacy Award and Social Impact Initiative of the Year. KRAFTON India has not said how either will be picked, and neither carries a jury or fan split in the announcement. The first edition also recognised CSR work and the KRAFTON India Gaming Incubator, which has since picked eight indie studios at its PitchFest.
The first KRAFTON India Awards were held in Mumbai on 9 January 2026 as an invite-only event, with 17 categories across esports, influencers, media, CSR and KIGI, according to KRAFTON India’s announcement of the first edition. Jonathan was the biggest winner of the night, taking Influencer of the Year, Favourite Creator of the Year (Male) and Favourite Esports Player of the Year. He has had another huge year since, recently passing 8 million YouTube subscribers.
Fan voting for the 2026 edition opens on 7 December. KRAFTON India has not yet named the nominees or said where voting will take place, and those details are expected when voting goes live.

items.title: A game of cards that could change the world - All Will Rise appeals because it's unafraid to have a perspective
What are we all playing this weekend?
How Team Soul Went Toe-to-Toe with the World’s Best in PMGC 2026 Gauntlet
items.content:
Team SouL showcased an impressive performance in PUBG Mobile 2026 Gauntlet stage to qualify for the highly prestigious Grand Finals. After the conclusion of the first day and six matches, Team SouL was in 11th position with a total 33 points. However, on the second day, the team showed a phenomenal performance and jumped to 6th position with 91 points.
Team SouL acquired 58 points on the second day alone, which makes the average of 9.67 points per match as compared to 5.5 points per match on the first day. Notably, the team secured 45 points in the last three matches, which were a spectacle to watch.
A team the world hadn’t seen
Going in, Team SouL was the fan favorite for every Indian fan, because they were representing the country. But honestly, nobody had any idea how they would actually do against their global counterparts. The Indian region is locked in its own bubble when it comes to PUBG Mobile competition. Battlegrounds Mobile India (BGMI), the India-specific variant of PUBG Mobile, does not have global matchmaking. So the only time Indian teams play international opposition is at the BGMI International Cup (BMIC), where we get to see South Korean and Japanese teams, or at a global PUBG Mobile event, which needs a dedicated Indian slot. Indian teams have only started getting those slots recently. Team SouL earned this one by winning the Battlegrounds Mobile India Showdown (BMSD) 2026.
India’s record on global PUBG Mobile stage
Before this, Orangutan, GodLike Esports, and True Rippers had represented India at global PUBG Mobile events. They did decently well. Orangutan and GodLike both made it to the PMWC 2026 Grand Finals in Paris, the first Indian teams ever to get that far. But none of them had shown this level of performance yet. Orangutan played the PMGC 2025 Gauntlet stage too but finished at 11th position, and then ended PMGC 2025 in 35th place, while True Rippers Esports finished at 36th position.
A look at who Team SouL was up against
It’s only the start of the tournament, I know. Still, Team SouL has so far met the fans, the organization, and the supporters’ expectations. And it gets more impressive when you look at which teams they competed against.
S2G Esports won the PUBG Mobile World Cup (PMWC) 2026 in Paris. Wolves Esports won the PUBG Mobile Global Open (PMGO) 2026 Season 2 in Lahore. 4Thrives Esports won PMGO 2026 Season 1 in Jakarta. Nongshim RedForce won the PUBG Mobile Macao Invitational 2026. All Gamers won the Peacekeeper Elite League (PEL) Spring 2026.
All top-tier teams. Every one of those teams played the Gauntlet alongside Team SouL.
New to the global stage
On the other hand, if you look at Team SouL. They do not have a broad experience in competing in global events. Nakul “NakuL” Sharma, the IGL, is playing his first global event. Same goes for the team’s assaulter, Yash “LEGIT” Choudhary. The team’s support player Khush “Jokerr” Singh has a number of official BGMI trophies under his belt, but this is his first global event too. Same goes for Aaryaman “Thunder” Seth, the fifth player. Only Harsh “Goblin” Paudwal, the entry fragger, had played a global PUBG Mobile tournament before this, and that too was back in 2022, where the former roster of Team SouL finished at 11th position in the PUBG Mobile World Invitational 2022 in Riyadh.
What made Team SouL perform well?
So how did a team this new to the global stage keep up with that field? They played to their strength, and their strength is gun power. This team can take a fight with any team in the world.
This is reflected in the Gauntlet stage stats. Team SouL finished the Gauntlet with 71 finishes, the second highest of any team, while they had just 20 placement points, of which 10 came from a single WWCD. Nearly four of every five points they scored came from eliminations.
With Team SouL qualifying for the PMGC 2026 Grand Finals, the hype for the tournament has only multiplied. The Grand Finals will take place from 11th to 13th December. It will be exciting to see how Team SouL keeps up against the competition and whether it maintains its consistency.

items.title: Delaware Magistrate Orders Supermicro to Hand a Pension Fund Its Audit Minutes and a Grand Jury Subpoena
items.content:
A Delaware Court of Chancery magistrate has ruled that Super Micro Computer must hand a Chicago teachers’ pension fund more of its internal records, including Audit Committee minutes from December 2024. The ruling also covers, under strict conditions, a federal grand jury subpoena from New York linked to the export case against its co-founder. The findings are set out in a post-trial report by Magistrate Mitchell of the Court of Chancery, issued under seal on 17 November and published in redacted form on 25 November 2026. Either side can still challenge the report through exceptions before it is put into effect.
The plaintiff in case 2026-0615-LM is the Public School Teachers’ Pension and Retirement Fund of Chicago, and the defendant is Super Micro Computer. It is a books and records action, which means the fund asked to inspect company documents rather than suing anyone for damages. The report finds that the fund has a proper purpose for that inspection, but it states plainly that it does not establish wrongdoing by Supermicro or any of its directors.
The first page of the magistrate's report. Source: Delaware Court of Chancery, Public School Teachers' Pension and Retirement Fund of Chicago v. Super Micro Computer, Inc., C.A. No. 2026-0615-LM, report dated 17 November 2026
What the Delaware magistrate ordered Supermicro to hand over
The pension fund has held Supermicro shares since 2019 and sent its inspection demand on 7 February 2025, under Section 220 of the Delaware General Corporation Law. Supermicro turned down the demand but agreed to share documents under a confidentiality agreement, producing material between March 2025 and January 2026. The fund said key records were still missing, filed suit on 13 May 2026, and the court held a half-day trial on the papers on 17 September.
The fund asked for five more categories of documents, and dropped one interim report from its request at trial. The report grants four of the remaining requests in a limited form. Supermicro must produce the relevant parts of its Audit Committee minutes and agendas from meetings on 19 and 30 December 2024, which dealt with the auditor’s follow-up requests after the Special Committee’s report.
It must also produce existing material recording an oral interim presentation the Special Committee gave to auditor Ernst & Young on 2 October 2024, or informal records showing its substance if nothing formal exists. A third order covers supplemental findings the Special Committee shared with auditors in February 2025, including findings drawn from mobile devices, where the board or a committee considered them. In each case the order is limited to material the fund cannot already get from documents Supermicro has produced.
The most striking item is the grand jury subpoena. Supermicro confirmed at trial that a subpoena from the Southern District of New York exists, but argued it was discussed by the Special Committee rather than handed to it. The report found that the committee’s minutes and report refer to the subpoena without describing its scope, so it ordered production as long as no minutes or report describe that scope.
The relief section, including the condition on the grand jury subpoena. Source: Delaware Court of Chancery, Public School Teachers' Pension and Retirement Fund of Chicago v. Super Micro Computer, Inc., C.A. No. 2026-0615-LM, report dated 17 November 2026
One of the fund’s five requests failed outright. Its demand for separate whistleblower reports was denied without prejudice, because the record did not show that such reports exist apart from compilations Supermicro had already produced. Everything the company hands over remains covered by the parties’ confidentiality agreement, so none of these documents will become public through this order.
Why the pension fund cleared Delaware’s credible basis test
To win a books and records case, a shareholder investigating possible misconduct only has to show a credible basis from which wrongdoing might be inferred. The report calls this the lowest burden of proof recognised under Delaware law. Because the fund sent its demand before 17 February 2025, the older version of Section 220 applies rather than the amended statute.
The report points to three pieces of evidence. Ernst & Young resigned as Supermicro’s auditor on 30 October 2024, saying it could no longer rely on representations by management and the Audit Committee. Special Committee minutes refer to federal grand jury subpoenas, and the New York indictment alleges export control violations involving a former director and others linked to the company.
The Special Committee was set up in August 2024, with director Susie Giordano as its only member. In November 2024 it concluded that it had found no evidence Supermicro knowingly tried to circumvent export controls. According to the report, reading that conclusion together with the later, unproven allegations against Liaw strengthened the case for a targeted inspection. The report adds that it does not treat the indictment’s allegations as established facts.
The export case against Wally Liaw behind the subpoena request
Federal prosecutors in Manhattan unsealed the indictment on 19 March 2026. The charges, announced by the US Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York, name three men. They accuse Supermicro co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw, Taiwan-based manager Ruei-Tsang “Steven” Chang and broker Ting-Wei “Willy” Sun of conspiring to divert servers containing US AI technology to China. Prosecutors allege that about $2.5 billion of servers were bought in 2024 and 2025, and that at least $510 million worth were diverted.
An indictment is an accusation, and the defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty. Liaw pleaded not guilty in April, Bloomberg reported. Supermicro itself is not a defendant, and it said in a statement on 19 March that the alleged conduct went against its policies and compliance controls, and that it was cooperating fully with the government.
The company told investors in a filing with the SEC that Liaw resigned from its board on 20 March 2026, and that his resignation was not the result of a disagreement. It also named DeAnna Luna as acting chief compliance officer. The case sits alongside wider scrutiny of where AI servers end up, from Nvidia’s missing Taiwan disclosure to restricted Blackwell hardware found at a Shanghai data centre.
Washington has tightened the rules since the indictment, and Nvidia halted server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries after a new US chip rule this month. Lawmakers are also pushing tighter controls on AI chip exports. The Delaware report is subject to the Court of Chancery’s rule on exceptions, and unless either side files them in time, the parties must submit an order putting it into effect within seven days.
The post Delaware Magistrate Orders Supermicro to Hand a Pension Fund Its Audit Minutes and a Grand Jury Subpoena appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Take-Two Files Macca the Gator and Rockstar R* Music Trademarks in a Second Wave of GTA 6 Filings
items.content:
Take-Two Interactive filed 26 more US trademark applications on 29 and 30 October, starting the day after the 16 Vice City filings TalkEsport reported last month. The new batch includes the first applications for Macca the Gator, the cartoon alligator on Rockstar’s own GTA 6 merchandise, and a filing for the Rockstar R* logo on music recordings, CDs and vinyl. All 26 are listed under Take-Two Interactive Software in the US Patent and Trademark Office’s records, and none has been assigned to an examiner yet.
Most of the 28 October filings protected names such as Vice City and Vice City Leonida as plain words. Most of the new applications cover logos instead. Ten are for a stylised Vice City logo and five for a Vice City Leonida logo, while three cover a VI logo filled with palm trees and six cover the R* badge. The remaining two are word marks for Macca the Gator, filed on 29 October, three weeks before Grand Theft Auto VI launched on 19 November.
Macca the Gator gets two trademark applications from Take-Two
The first Macca the Gator application, serial number 50189569, covers toys, including action figures, collectible figures, plush toys, playing cards, puzzles and board games. The second application, serial number 50189508, covers shot glasses, drinking glasses, mugs, cocktail stirrers and decorative mirrors. Both were filed on an intent-to-use basis, which means Take-Two has not yet claimed that it sells goods under the name.
Source: USPTO trademark record, serial number 50189569, owned by Take-Two Interactive Software. Screenshot of the TSDR status page taken on 28 November 2026
The filings themselves do not say what Macca the Gator is, but Rockstar’s store does. Its listing for The Goodtime State: Vice City Collection, a $399.99 box that does not include the game, describes the set as inspired by Leonida’s hit TV show, Macca the Gator. The box contains a Macca the Gator figure and a Macca the Gator magnetic mirror, and both item names carry a trademark symbol on the store page.
Those two items line up with the two applications, one covering toy figures and the other covering decorative mirrors. Rockstar first promoted the box in a Newswire post in September, and TalkEsport’s GTA 6 merch price list covers every item in it. The applications do not mention any other Macca products, and a trademark filing on its own is not an announcement of one.
Rockstar’s R* logo filed for music on CD and vinyl
The most unusual application in the batch is the R* music filing, serial number 50191187, which Take-Two filed on 30 October. It covers audio recordings featuring music, pre-recorded CDs, vinyl records and downloadable music files. The record describes the mark as a stylised R with a five-pointed star on its bottom right leg, enclosed in a square with rounded corners.
Source: USPTO trademark record, serial number 50191187, owned by Take-Two Interactive Software. Screenshot of the TSDR status page taken on 28 November 2026
Take-Two filed this one on an intent-to-use basis as well, so it has not claimed any music sales under the logo yet. The filing does not say which music it would cover. The other five R* applications use the badge without the square and cover bags, jewellery, printed materials, clothing and lighters.
Those five are all use-based, which means Take-Two says the logo is already on sale on those goods. The bags, jewellery and lighter filings give a first-use date of 8 October 2026, the day Rockstar opened its GTA 6 collection on the Rockstar Store. The printed materials filing claims first use on 9 November 1999, and the clothing filing claims 21 August 2001.
The three VI filings follow the same pattern. The VI logo application for bags describes stylised letters with the interior filled by palm trees, and it claims first use on 8 October 2026 like the matching jewellery filing. The third VI application covers lighters and was filed on an intent-to-use basis.
The Vice City and Vice City Leonida logos in the second wave
The ten Vice City logo applications describe the name in lowercase cursive script, with a thick underline that rises from beneath the first word and curves down at the right. They cover game software, online games and entertainment services, sunglasses, jewellery, printed materials, bags, glassware, clothing, toys and lighters. The game software and entertainment filings claim first use on 29 October 2002, the day Grand Theft Auto: Vice City came out in North America.
The Vice City lighter filing claims first use on 8 October 2026, and the other seven Vice City logo applications were filed on an intent-to-use basis. All five Vice City Leonida logo applications are intent-to-use as well. They describe “vice” stacked above “city” in block letters, with “Leonida” overlapping the bottom, and they cover sunglasses, jewellery, printed materials, bags and glassware.
Companies often file across many classes to protect a brand from copycats, so the spread of goods is not a product list. Even so, the goods follow the contents of the $399.99 box closely, from the sunglasses and the crossbody bag to the stickers, the poster and the swizzle spoon. All 26 applications were still awaiting assignment to an examining attorney when TalkEsport checked the USPTO records on 28 November.
The post Take-Two Files Macca the Gator and Rockstar R* Music Trademarks in a Second Wave of GTA 6 Filings appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: GameStop Pays $3.5 Million to End Lawsuit Over Ryan Cohen’s Withdrawn Billion Dollar Pay Award
items.content:
GameStop has agreed to pay $3.5 million to the lawyers behind a shareholder lawsuit that tried to block a vote on Ryan Cohen’s multibillion dollar stock option award. The company disclosed the payment in a Form 8-K filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on 25 November 2026. The Delaware Court of Chancery dismissed the case a day earlier, on 24 November.
The money is described in the filing as a mootness fee, paid to the plaintiff’s counsel for attorneys’ fees, expenses and costs. GameStop says it agreed to the payment “without admitting any fault or wrongdoing” and in its business judgment. The filing also states that the court did not review the amount, and did not pass judgment on whether the fee was reasonable.
The passage on the $3.5 million mootness fee, highlighting added by TalkEsport. Source: GameStop Form 8-K filed with the SEC on 25 November 2026
What GameStop’s 8-K says about the $3.5 million fee
The disclosure sits under Item 8.01 of the report, the section headed “Other Events”. It is signed by Mark Robinson, GameStop’s general counsel and corporate secretary, and SEC records show it was accepted on the afternoon of 25 November. The report gives 24 November 2026 as the date of the earliest event it covers, which is the day the court signed off on the dismissal.
According to the filing, the court approved a stipulation and order dismissing all claims with prejudice as to the plaintiff. Claims by any other members of the proposed class were dismissed without prejudice, so the order does not shut them out. GameStop adds that the case will be closed once an affidavit confirming this disclosure has been filed with the court.
The cover page of the 8-K, which reports events from 24 November 2026. Source: GameStop Form 8-K filed with the SEC on 25 November 2026
A mootness fee is paid when a company takes steps that make a lawsuit’s main demand unnecessary, and the plaintiff’s lawyers then seek payment for that result. In this case the steps came in June, when GameStop pulled Cohen’s award from the ballot and published extra information about a second proposal. The plaintiff withdrew its request for a temporary restraining order the next day, citing that supplement and “certain other agreements” made with the defendants.
The Pontiac pension fund lawsuit over Cohen’s award and 1.5 billion new shares
The case was filed on 15 June 2026 as a proposed class action by The City of Pontiac Reestablished General Employees’ Retirement System, a public pension fund in Michigan. It named GameStop and all five of its directors, Ryan Cohen, Alan Attal, Larry Cheng, Jim Grube and Nathaniel Turner, under case number 2026-0785-JTL. The defendants deny any and all wrongdoing, according to the 8-K.
The 8-K describes the lawsuit and the two shareholder votes it tried to stop. Source: GameStop Form 8-K filed with the SEC on 25 November 2026
The lawsuit sought to stop two votes at GameStop’s annual meeting on 7 July. Proposal 4 asked shareholders to approve the CEO Performance Award for Cohen, while Proposal 5 asked them to raise GameStop’s authorised Class A shares to 2.5 billion. GameStop’s proxy supplement of 23 June said the complaint alleged a breach of fiduciary duty over that share increase, which would add 1.5 billion authorised shares.
The complaint’s main argument was about how the share vote would be counted. It alleged that GameStop’s charter required a majority of all voting power, so abstentions should count as votes against, while a supplement issued on 8 June said only a majority of votes cast was needed. GameStop said it believed the claim was without merit under Delaware law and that it intended to defend it vigorously.
Shareholders approved the share increase on 7 July with 231,693,497 votes for and 104,566,841 against, according to GameStop’s voting results. A total of 448,691,227 shares were entitled to vote on the record date. By TalkEsport’s arithmetic, the votes in favour equal about 51.6% of those shares, so the amendment also cleared the stricter standard the lawsuit argued for.
Ryan Cohen’s withdrawn option award and the eBay bid behind it
The award at the centre of the case was large by any measure. GameStop’s 2026 proxy statement describes 171,537,327 performance-based stock options with an exercise price of $20.66, split into nine tranches over a ten-year term. The tranches were tied to market value targets from $20 billion to $100 billion and cumulative performance EBITDA targets from $2 billion to $10 billion.
The board approved the award on 6 January 2026, with Cohen recusing himself, subject to a shareholder vote. The proxy said early estimates put its grant date fair value at about $2.5 billion, and that it was designed to give Cohen 20% of the market value created up to the highest target. Cohen is GameStop’s chairman and chief executive, roles he took on in the years after the 2021 stock surge and the exit of former chief executive George Sherman.
The 23 June supplement explained why Cohen asked for the award to be withdrawn. It said GameStop had not yet decided to pursue an acquisition of eBay when the board approved the award in January. Cohen wanted the company’s leadership fully focused on GameStop’s operating performance and the proposed eBay deal, according to the supplement. In May, eBay had already told GameStop that its $56 billion takeover bid was neither credible nor attractive.
The case was heard in the Delaware Court of Chancery, the main venue for disputes over the governance of companies incorporated in Delaware, as GameStop is. Shareholders can follow the company’s filings through its investor relations site, which links directly to its SEC records. The 8-K was filed with the SEC on 25 November 2026, the day after the court approved the dismissal.
The post GameStop Pays $3.5 Million to End Lawsuit Over Ryan Cohen’s Withdrawn Billion Dollar Pay Award appeared first on TalkEsport.

NVIDIA Taiwan Revenue Hits $30B, as Key Disclosure Vanishes
items.content:
Nvidia has stopped publishing its estimate of where the data centre hardware bought by its Taiwan-headquartered customers finally ends up, even as Taiwan has grown into more than a quarter of its revenue. The estimate put 86% of that revenue with end customers in the United States and Europe in the quarter to October 2025. It is missing from Nvidia’s quarterly reports for the three months to April and July 2026. Customers headquartered in Taiwan bought a record $30.30 billion in the quarter to 25 October 2026, according to the supplemental financial information Nvidia filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on 17 November.
TalkEsport went through every quarterly and annual report Nvidia has filed since May 2024 to see how its Asian sales moved while Washington tightened chip exports. Besides the missing Taiwan estimate, two other shifts stand out in the company’s own figures. Revenue from China-headquartered customers collapsed and then recovered to $11.05 billion a quarter, and Singapore disappeared from the tables.
The Taiwan estimate missing from Nvidia’s 2026 filings
When Nvidia switched to counting revenue by customer headquarters in November 2025, it added a footnote estimating where the data centre products bought by Taiwan-headquartered customers finally ended up. For the quarter to October 2025, it estimated that 86% of that revenue was attributed to end customers in the United States and Europe. Its annual report for the year to January 2026 gave a figure of 76% for the full year.
That footnote was the only figure in Nvidia’s filings that followed the Taiwan money to its destination. The headquarters count shows who pays Nvidia, not where the hardware is installed, and Nvidia’s own filings warn that end customers and shipping locations can differ from a customer’s headquarters. Without the estimate, readers of the filings cannot tell how much of Nvidia’s Taiwan revenue ends up with customers outside the United States and Europe. That includes Asia and the Middle East, the regions at the centre of the US export debate.
That estimate does not appear in Nvidia’s quarterly reports for the three months to April and July 2026. It is also absent from the supplemental data for the quarter to October, and none of those documents explains why it was dropped. Over the same three quarters, Taiwan’s revenue rose from $12.01 billion to $30.30 billion, and its share of the total climbed from 15% to 26%. The question of where Nvidia hardware finally lands has already produced headlines this month, including Bloomberg’s report on restricted Blackwell hardware at a Shanghai data centre. Nvidia’s board has also set up a national security committee as Washington presses for answers on China chips.
The growth behind those numbers has been steady across both years. Taiwan-headquartered customers bought $6.19 billion in the quarter to October 2024 and $30.30 billion two years later, more than twice the $13.75 billion of a year earlier. In the first nine months of the current fiscal year they bought $69.29 billion, already well above the $42.35 billion recorded for the whole of the previous year.
Nvidia’s China revenue, quarter by quarter since 2024
Nvidia now groups revenue by the country where each direct customer has its headquarters, and it warns that the end customer and shipping location may be different. On that basis, customers headquartered in China accounted for $8.14 billion, or 23% of revenue, in the quarter to October 2024. Their share fell to 8.5% in the quarter to July 2025 and to 4.5% in the quarter to January 2026.
The slide followed the US decision in April 2025 to require a licence for exports of the H20, the chip Nvidia had designed for the Chinese market. Nvidia booked a $4.5 billion charge on unsold H20 stock in that quarter, according to its latest quarterly report. Licences granted from August 2025 did not help, because Beijing restricted the purchases and the H20 inventory went unsold.
The recovery began in 2026, when revenue from China-headquartered customers rose to $4.55 billion in the quarter to April and $7.88 billion in the quarter to July. It reached $11.05 billion in the quarter to October, 3.7 times the $2.97 billion of a year earlier. Nvidia’s CFO commentary says shipments of its Hopper data centre products to China were $2.4 billion in the latest quarter.
Those Hopper sales run through a licence scheme the US opened in February 2026 for small volumes of H200 chips to named China-based customers. In the quarter to July, Nvidia said such shipments were less than 1% of Data Center revenue, and that each chip passes a US inspection that triggers a 25% tariff. Even so, Nvidia is not assuming any China data centre compute revenue in its forecast for the current quarter.
Nvidia’s “customer headquarters” rule took Singapore off its revenue tables
Until late 2025, Nvidia grouped revenue by the customer’s billing location, and Singapore was one of its largest markets on paper. Revenue billed to Singapore peaked at $10.16 billion in the quarter to July 2025, or 22% of the total. Nvidia said customers used Singapore to centralise invoicing, and that shipments to Singapore were less than 2% of revenue in the year to January 2025.
In its quarterly report filed on 19 November 2025, Nvidia switched to the headquarters count and recast earlier periods. It said the new method provides a better representation of the geographic profile of its revenue. The recast lifted revenue from China-headquartered customers for the year to January 2025 to $25.05 billion, from $17.11 billion on the billing count, which raised China’s share of that year’s sales from 13% to 19%.
Southeast Asia has since moved to the centre of the export debate. US lawmakers are pushing tighter controls after reports that Megaspeed arranged $12 billion in chips for Chinese companies, which Megaspeed denies. A Commerce Department rule that took effect on 19 November now requires licences for advanced chip exports to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil. A week later, Nvidia halted server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries, according to a Financial Times report.
Nvidia’s next filing will show whether the Taiwan estimate returns. Its full quarterly report for the three months to 25 October has not yet been filed. Under SEC rules for large companies, it is due within 40 days of the quarter’s end, on 4 December 2026.
The post NVIDIA Taiwan Revenue Hits $30B, as Key Disclosure Vanishes appeared first on TalkEsport.

1 Million Subscribers, Zero Income: Onca Says YouTube Demonetised Every Channel It Runs
items.content:
Onca, an animation studio whose main YouTube channel has just passed one million subscribers, says YouTube has removed monetisation from every channel it runs. In a post on X on 28 November, the studio offered to trade its Gold Play Button for a five-minute conversation with a real person at YouTube. Onca says it pays 15 animators and has spent three weeks dealing with what it describes as a chatbot instead of a human.
The post follows a longer statement Onca published on 25 November, the day it says its main channel reached one million subscribers. In it, the studio says YouTube approved appeals on two of its older channels, then demonetised the same channels again months later for the same reason. It says YouTube then removed monetisation from its other channels under its related channel rules, which left the studio with no monetised channels at all.
Hey @YouTube, can I trade my Gold Play Button for 5-minute conversation with an actual human being?
We just hit 1 MILLION subscribers, but instead of celebrating, we're fighting to save our entire business. YouTube approved our appeals, demonetized those same channels again… pic.twitter.com/giu87SoOWw
— onca (@onca_yt) November 28, 2026
Lost monetisation on every channel it runs
According to Onca’s statement, the trouble began months ago, when two older channels called Extremify and HardClipped were demonetised for reused content. The studio says it submitted video appeals showing its creative process, and YouTube approved both of them. Onca says it then stopped uploading to those channels and moved its time and money into new, original projects.
Both channels sat inactive for months, the studio says, before YouTube demonetised them again for the same reason. This time the action did not stop there, according to Onca. It says YouTube went on to remove monetisation from the channels it had built since, including its biggest channel, ONCA, as well as GAGA Global and James Films.
YOUTUBE WILL TAKE AWAY YOUR ENTIRE LIVELIHOOD OVERNIGHT. EVEN IF YOU FOLLOW THEIR OWN POLICIES.
PLEASE read this until the end. What happened to us could happen to you, regardless of how successful you are.
Months ago, two of our older YouTube channels were demonetized for… pic.twitter.com/nDZDcEOZY4
— onca (@onca_yt) November 25, 2026
The channels involved are large by any measure. The ONCA YouTube channel showed 1.01 million subscribers and more than 1.58 billion total views on 28 November, across 236 videos. Most of its recent uploads are animated Shorts that retell viral real life stories, many with several million views each.
James Films, which also makes animated stories based on real events, has around 321,000 subscribers, while GAGA Global, a music channel, has around 406,000. Onca says the ONCA channel alone pulls in more than 400 million monthly views. The studio also says it employs scriptwriters, researchers, editors and sound designers alongside its 3D animators.
What YouTube’s policies say about reused content and related channels
YouTube’s channel monetisation policies describe reused content as channels that repurpose material already on YouTube without adding meaningful original commentary or substantive changes. The same page lists critical reviews, reaction videos with commentary and edited footage with an added storyline as acceptable examples. Clips stitched together with little or no narrative are given as examples of what is not allowed.
The page also explains how far a penalty can reach. If a channel breaks these rules, YouTube says the action may apply to all of a creator’s existing channels, any new ones they create and channels they appear on regularly. It adds that reviewers regularly check whether monetised channels still follow the policies, which means approval is not a permanent guarantee.
YouTube renamed its former repetitious content policy to inauthentic content in July 2025, and the policy page says that kind of content has always been ineligible for monetisation. Onca’s statement points out that YouTube said at the time there was no change to its reused content policy. The studio argues that nothing in its content or in the policy changed between the approval and the second demonetisation.
The appeal route itself is also tightly defined by YouTube. YouTube’s appeal guide asks for an unlisted video under five minutes that shows how the channel is made, submitted within 21 days of a suspension. YouTube says it replies within 14 days, and a rejected channel has to wait 90 days before it can apply again.
TeamYouTube’s response and a week of reused content replies
TeamYouTube did respond publicly to Onca’s first statement. On 25 November, the support account replied to Onca to say it was sending the studio a direct message and understood how important the case was. Three days later, Onca’s new post says it still cannot reach anyone at YouTube who can actually help.
Onca is not the only channel TeamYouTube has answered about reused content this week. In one reply on 24 November, the account told another creator that a manual review had found a significant part of their channel did not match the reused content rules. Similar replies to other creators recommended adding original commentary, educational value or high quality editing before reapplying.
Onca has also turned YouTube’s own words back on the company. In his 2026 letter to creators, YouTube chief executive Neal Mohan wrote that creators call YouTube home because “we offer the most stable path to earn”. The same letter says YouTube has paid more than $100 billion to creators, artists and media companies over four years.
The case lands in a busy year for YouTube and its creators, from changes to how it counts views on TV screens to record viewing around launches such as GTA 6’s first week on the platform. Monetisation rows are not new either, and YouTube also removed monetisation features from Dr Disrespect’s channel in 2024. Onca has asked creators to tag TeamYouTube and Neal Mohan, and its 25 November statement had been viewed more than 126,000 times on X by 28 November.
The post 1 Million Subscribers, Zero Income: Onca Says YouTube Demonetised Every Channel It Runs appeared first on TalkEsport.

Where Are the Virtus.pro Golden Five Now? pashaBiceps Runs an Energy Drink Brand as TaZ and NEO Coach at the Major
items.content:
Jarosław “pashaBiceps” Jarząbkowski is a Major champion, and these days he is also the chief executive of a snack and energy drink company. On 27 November, the Polish Counter-Strike legend told his followers on X that he has been selling his own products for almost two years, and that Papito Energy now ships across Europe. The post jokingly signed off from a “part-time businessman”, and it is a good moment to check in on the rest of the Virtus.pro line-up that fans still call the Golden Five.
Hello guys!
Maybe you didn’t know, but I have my own products. It’s almost 2 years already.
You can find some really tasty wafers, energy drinks with natural caffeine, they getting really great reviews.
We now ship all over Europe, so you can order them and try it
Who knows…… pic.twitter.com/Q9VHIWgKjy
— paszaBiceps (@paszaBiceps) November 27, 2026
The five Poles, pashaBiceps, Wiktor “TaZ” Wojtas, Filip “NEO” Kubski, Janusz “Snax” Pogorzelski and Paweł “byali” Bieliński, played together from late 2013 until early 2018. Their biggest night came in March 2014, when Virtus.pro won EMS One Katowice, the first Counter-Strike: Global Offensive Major held in Poland, by beating Ninjas in Pyjamas 2-0 in the grand final. The same core went on to win ELEAGUE Season 1 in 2016, and it stayed one of the most loved rosters in the game long after it split.
pashaBiceps swaps the AWP for wafers and energy drinks with Papito
Papito Energy is based in Warsaw and sells its range through its own online shop at papitoenergy.com. The line-up includes energy drinks made with natural caffeine, energy gels, a wafer range called Fajny Wafel and clothing such as hoodies and oversized T-shirts. One of the drinks is named Lemon Mint Flashbang, and one shirt carries the line “What is your max ELO”, so the Counter-Strike roots are hard to miss.
The brand opened its X account in March 2025, and pasha now lists himself as its chief executive in his profile. He also runs Esport Ninja, which mixes esports with physical activity, and the Pasha Gaming Camp, which held esports and sports camps in Masuria in September and in the Tatra mountains in October. His joke about delivering orders on his bike is not a random one, either. In 2023 he cycled from Poland to Paris to follow 9INE at the BLAST Paris Major, as we covered in our report on his 1,000 mile ride.
Business has not replaced the community work that made him a fan favourite. In April 2026, pasha sold his Factory New Karambit Fade for more than $21,000 during a Polish charity stream and gave every cent to a children’s cancer charity, according to our story on the knife sale. He left Virtus.pro in February 2019 and has worked as a streamer and content creator ever since.
TaZ and NEO both brought teams to the PGL Singapore Major
Two of the Golden Five are now coaches, and both of them were in Singapore this month. TaZ joined BC.Game as head coach in January 2026, taking charge of a team built around s1mple and electroNic, as we reported when he returned to coaching. BC.Game went out of the Major without a win, finishing 0-3 in Stage 1, according to our Stage 1 recap.
TaZ took responsibility for the result in a long post on X on 26 November. He told fans that his team needed to do better, and that it had put in a lot of work in the weeks before the event. “Unfortunately life is not a TikTok and we can’t fix things instantly,” he wrote, adding that every loss is a lesson.
NEO has the more successful coaching record of the two. He took over as FaZe Clan’s coach in 2023 and led the team to three Major finals, at Copenhagen and Shanghai in 2024 and at Budapest in 2025. FaZe and NEO parted ways in March 2026. Astralis named him head coach in July, and the Danish team opened its Stage 2 campaign in Singapore against Imperial on 28 November.
Snax steps back from GamerLegion while byali streams on Kick
Snax spent most of this season as a starting player for GamerLegion. He rejoined GamerLegion as its in-game leader in December 2025, as our report on the move explains, and the team reached the grand final of IEM Atlanta during his second spell. On 21 October, GamerLegion announced that Snax would move out of the active roster, with shalfey taking over as the team’s caller.
Snax later said that he had asked the team to look for a replacement about six weeks earlier, because the season had taken a heavy toll on him. He also said that his contract had only two months left to run. GamerLegion thanked him for its playoff run at BLAST Rivals and for the IEM Atlanta final, and it signed off its post with a Polish thank you.
byali now spends most of his time streaming, and he keeps a close eye on the Polish scene. In July 2025, he asked his followers to join him on Kick after problems with his Twitch channel, and he still posts regularly to around 66,000 followers on X. When GamerLegion announced the Snax news, byali joked that there was no longer anyone on the team worth watching.
Eight years after the line-up split, the five have gone in very different directions. TaZ and NEO are coaching, byali is streaming and Snax has stepped away from GamerLegion’s active roster. The most visible of them all is now running a food and drink brand from Warsaw. His Papito post went out on 27 November to more than 438,000 followers on X.

8 Classic PlayStation Games That Are Barely Playable Today
items.content: If you’ve ever watched someone play an old PlayStation game and wondered why their character keeps spinning around in circles, congratulations, you’ve already met tank controls. If you’re unfamiliar, here’s your quick introduction: With tank controls, pressing up moves your character forward in whatever direction they’re facing, and pressing left or right only rotates them, so with the stick alone, you can’t sidestep or turn on a dime. That’s manageable in a hallway. It’s much less so when you’re sneaking past a guard, lining up a shot, or timing a leap across a pit, which is why the same scheme caused trouble in just about every genre during the PS1 era. These eight classic games are the hardest to go back to, whether the culprit is tank controls or something else entirely.

items.title: PARIVISION eliminates Aurora Gaming to stay alive at Dota 2 BLAST Slam 9
items.content:
PARIVISION players have kept their BLAST Slam 9 campaign alive after defeating Aurora Gaming in the lower-bracket quarterfinals. The CIS squad bounced back from its earlier surprising defeat to Team Liquid, winning 2-1 to eliminate Aurora Gaming and secure another shot at the tournament title.
With their victory against Aurora Gaming, PARIVISION players are set to face 1w Team, another squad that fell to Team Liquid earlier in the upper-bracket quarterfinals.
PARIVISION vs. Aurora Gaming at BLAST Slam 9
After suffering a one-sided defeat in Game 3 against Team Liquid, PARIVISION found themselves in a difficult position at BLAST Slam 9. This was an unexpected setback for one of the tournament’s strongest contenders, especially after the team finished at the top of Group C and secured a direct spot in the upper-bracket semifinals through the seeding matches.
Now forced to fight their way back into contention, PARIVISION must keep their championship hopes alive in a do-or-die series against Aurora Gaming in the playoffs, where another loss would bring its tournament run to an end.
PARIVISION started the series strongly, taking the opening game against Aurora Gaming, courtesy of Alan “Satanic” Gallyamov’s Sven, using his BKBs and God’s Strength wisely during teamfights.
Game 1 of Aurora vs. PARIVISION (Image credit: BLAST)
However, Aurora refused to go down without a fight, delivering a comeback performance in Game 2 to force a deciding third map. Aurora Gaming’s hero lineup consisting of a Tiny-Queen of Pain combo paired with HP-sustaining offlane and support allowed them to quickly burst PARIVISION’s cores.
Game 3 finally fell to the hands of PARIVISION, using an unorthodox Arc Warden for their position 4 player, Edgar “9Class” Naltakian. PARIVISION wasted no more time in pressuring Aurora Gaming, ending Game 3 in just under 35 minutes.
Deciding game of Aurora vs. PARIVISION (Image credit: BLAST)
The result sent Aurora Gaming out of BLAST Slam 9 in fifth to sixth place, while PARIVISION advanced to the next round of the lower bracket.
PARIVISION’s road to the BLAST Slam 9 grand final
Despite their recent setback against Team Liquid, PARIVISION remained in contention for the BLAST Slam 9 championship. The CIS team remained a dominant force in the current Dota 2 scene and is known for regularly reaching the Tier 1 tournament grand finals even if they need to do it from the lower bracket.
If they manage to win their lower bracket semifinal series against 1w Team, they’ll face either Team Yandex or Team Liquid, potentially giving them a chance to avenge their earlier upper-bracket defeat from Erik “tOfu” Engel’s squad.
