items.title: Anthropic Briefly Lost Its $1 Trillion Value, Then Closed Back Above It
items.content:
A widely shared post on X on 25 November declared that Anthropic “is no longer worth $1 trillion”, less than a week after the company behind Claude made its stock market debut. The claim was true for part of Wednesday’s trading session, when the shares fell as low as $73.85. They then recovered to close at $82.79, which values the company at about $1.11 trillion using the share count in its final prospectus.
US stock markets are closed on 26 November for Thanksgiving, so that Wednesday close is the latest price. The swing still matters, because Anthropic has now closed below its $83 offering price twice in a row. For gaming, it is also the first real market test of a company whose models are already being used to build games, run AI squadmates and port old titles.
What happened to Anthropic’s share price this week
Anthropic priced its shares at $83 in a final prospectus dated 18 November, and they began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT the next day. The offering raised $81.34 billion before costs, and a separate $26 billion private placement brought in Google, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft and TSMC as investors at the same price. The stock opened at $111.50, touched $115.10 and closed its first day at $97.17.
The slide began within days of the debut, during a wider sell-off in technology stocks. The shares closed at $81.90 on 24 November, down 6.5 per cent and below the offering price for the first time. On 25 November they dropped to $73.85 at their low, about 11 per cent under $83 and 36 per cent below the debut high. A late recovery then left them at $82.79, according to Google Finance data.
Analysts quoted by City AM blamed poor timing amid a wider sell-off in technology stocks, and said the underwriters could not hold the price after exercising their option to buy extra shares on 20 November. Investors are also weighing a lock-up release that reportedly lets up to 303 million shares be sold from 15 December. Yahoo Finance reported that chief executive Dario Amodei and president Daniela Amodei each sold about $280 million of shares in the IPO, at the offering price. Anthropic has not commented on the share price.
Why reports of Anthropic’s value do not agree
Different outlets have put very different values on the same share price, so TalkEsport worked the numbers out from Anthropic’s own filing. The prospectus lists 7.73 billion Class A shares, including the underwriters’ extra shares, and 5.64 billion Class N shares after the offering. That makes about 13.37 billion shares in total, which puts the $1 trillion line at roughly $74.81 a share.
On that basis, Anthropic dipped to roughly $987 billion at Wednesday’s low and finished the day at about $1.11 trillion, close to the value implied by its offering price. Reports that the company was worth $1.76 trillion or even $2 trillion on its first day only work with a much larger share count, such as a fully diluted figure that includes employee stock awards. City AM’s $998.2 billion figure at $77.30 on Tuesday implies a smaller count of about 12.9 billion shares.
The filing itself gives both sides of the argument. Third-quarter revenue reached $17 billion, up 1,127 per cent from a year earlier, while compute and infrastructure costs grew 382 per cent. Anthropic has also committed about $900.9 billion to compute and infrastructure, with about $451.6 billion of that due before the end of 2030, according to its registration statement.
What Anthropic’s IPO means for games made with Claude
Games are not part of the pitch to investors. A full-text search of Anthropic’s SEC filings finds Claude named in 15 of them, but the words “games”, “gaming” and “video game” in none. That is despite games being among the most visible ways people have used its models this month.
When Claude Fable 5.2 launched on 9 November, users quickly posted whole games built from a single prompt, including a first-person shooter that cost about $550 at API prices. Krafton’s research for PUBG Ally put Claude Opus 4.8 at $7.10 per replayed match, against two cents for Google’s Gemma, and Krafton later released its own small on-device model. Krafton’s paper said Opus was impractical at scale, which is why it picked Gemma to collect its training data.
The legal limits are being tested as well. Activision took down AI-built Call of Duty browser ports in October, and the AnyPS5 project now has its own rules for AI coding agents. Fable’s availability has also been interrupted before, when Anthropic suspended access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 on 12 June to comply with a US export control directive.
Anthropic restored access to both models on 1 July, after the directive was lifted, and Fable 5.2 followed in November. That release is the version behind the one-prompt game demos shared on X this month. Anthropic’s shares are next due to trade on 27 November, in a shortened session after the Thanksgiving holiday.
The post Anthropic Briefly Lost Its $1 Trillion Value, Then Closed Back Above It appeared first on TalkEsport.

GTA 6 PC Port Running on 25 FPS Hits Russian Torrent Sites
items.content:
An unofficial PC version of GTA 6 has started circulating on Russian torrent sites, a week after the game launched on PS5 and Xbox Series X and S. Several Russian outlets reported on 26 November that a build said to come from a port project called CGBJ had been posted for download. Posts on X claim it runs at 25 to 30 frames per second, but nothing about the release is official, and the claims have not been independently tested.
One X post describing the build said the port had “officially” reached the torrent sites, which gives the wrong impression. Rockstar has not announced a PC version of GTA VI, and the official GTA VI site still lists the game for PS5 and Xbox Series X and S only. Every PC build in circulation depends on files taken from the Xbox version of the game.
What has appeared on Russian torrent sites
Russian sports outlet Championat reported that a user posted the first build of the port to torrent trackers on 26 November. That was three days after hacking group Cyberleek leaked the executable needed to launch the game, according to the same report. Mail.ru’s Hi-Tech section reported the same release and said the CGBJ project’s GitHub repository disappeared less than an hour after it went public. TalkEsport has not downloaded the files and will not link to them.
The port builds on a leaked Xbox Series build that has been spreading since Cyberleek claimed the leak on 20 November. Within days, modders were saying the game was already booting on PC, and dozens of separate projects started racing to make it playable. A fan-run tracker now lists 39 such projects, according to a technical write-up on the Russian tech community site Habr.
The requirements quoted for the CGBJ build are steep. Mail.ru listed a Ryzen 5 3600 or Core i5-10400 processor, 32GB of RAM, a graphics card with 16GB of video memory and 209GB of SSD space. The size alone shows the download is the full game rather than a small patch, which matters for the legal questions around it.
How fast the leaked GTA 6 PC builds really run
The 25 to 30 frames per second figure comes from the projects themselves and the fan tracker that follows them. That tracker reports an average of about 25 frames per second in normal play and close to 30 indoors and in cutscenes. German outlet PC Games Hardware reported lower developer measurements, with a median of 17 to 18 frames per second.
Progress on the ports has still been remarkably fast over the past few days. The Habr write-up says the first projects reached the open world at under one frame per second on the morning of 25 November, and that several reached playable frame rates a day later. It reports that around 80 per cent of the story is playable on the CGBJ build, while rival projects sit at around 16 frames per second and 8 frames per second.
The builds also come with serious limits that the headline numbers leave out. The same write-up says the builds suffer from memory leaks, and one rival project uses 40 to 46GB of system memory. It advises readers not to download or play any of them yet, because stable builds could still be days or weeks away. Other unofficial routes such as the AnyPS5 project cannot convert GTA 6 at all so far.
Why downloading a GTA 6 PC torrent is risky
For anyone tempted to try a build, the biggest practical danger is malware. Since the Leonida project vanished, fake GTA 6 PC downloads have been used to spread malicious software, and the Habr write-up says fake repositories and torrents carry password stealers and crypto miners. Even a genuine build cannot be checked by players, because the files come from anonymous uploaders.
The legal position is also clear from Take-Two’s own actions. Its 24 November copyright notice said the Xbox Series files behind these ports were stolen, and it used that notice to take down 3,007 repositories on GitHub. GitHub explains how it handles such requests in its DMCA takedown policy.
Rockstar’s policy on copyrighted material also covers videos and streams of leaked content, which is why clips of the PC builds keep disappearing. Neither Take-Two nor Rockstar has commented publicly on the torrent release. The modder known as omonkey stopped streaming his port on 25 November after saying Rockstar had emailed him.

WoW Forever reworks Alterac Valley in latest patch
items.content:
WoW Forever's latest patch introduces major Alterac Valley changes, with Blizzard aiming to push players back towards the battleground's objectives instead of racing straight for the opposing faction's General.
In developer notes accompanying the update, Blizzard acknowledged that many Alterac Valley matches were ending with players largely ignoring objectives in favour of quickly defeating the enemy faction leader. To address this, the studio has significantly reduced the Honor and reputation earned from killing the General, while increasing rewards tied to capturing towers, graveyards and mines.
Reputation gains from killing enemy NPCs and Lieutenants have been increased, while the threshold for earning the battleground's long-match reputation bonus has been reduced to 20 minutes. According to Blizzard, the goal is for players to earn roughly the same amount of Honor as before, while making longer matches feel more rewarding.
The battleground itself is also becoming more challenging. Enemy creatures throughout Alterac Valley now have increased health and damage, while Generals and their supporting Warmasters and Marshals have all been strengthened. Warmasters and Marshals now leash if pulled too far from their rooms, while Generals have received additional damage, stealth detection and defensive improvements.
While the Alterac Valley changes are the headline feature of this week's updates, the patch also includes a sizeable list of class adjustments and bug fixes. Druids received the largest set of class-specific changes, alongside various fixes for Hunters, Paladins, Rogues, Shamans, Warlocks and Warriors.
KitGuru says: Alterac Valley has gone through many different metas over the years. Do you prefer longer objective-focused matches, or the faster General-rush style that many players have gravitated towards?

Mark's enthusiasm for computers dampened at an early age by the rubber-keyed Sinclair Spectrum 48K and feelings of Commodore 64 envy. However, in the mid-80s, hope in a digital future was rekindled by the purchase of an Atari 520 STe. Since that time Mark has used a multitude of computers for fun and professional endeavors. He often owned both Macs and PCs but went cold on the former after OS9 was killed off, and warmed to the latter with the introduction of Windows XP.

Early work years were spent in artwork and reprographics but in the late noughties, Mark started to blog about computers, Taiwanese food culture, and guitar design. This activity led to a full-time position writing about breaking PC tech news for HEXUS, for the best part of a decade. When HEXUS was abruptly closed, Mark helped with the foundation of Club386, before finding a new home at Tom's Hardware.

When not wearing through the keycap legends on his PC keyboards, Mark can be found wandering the computer malls of Taiwan's neon-lit conurbations and enjoying local and international cuisine.

items.title: PGL Major Singapore 2026: Can Team Liquid and 100 Thieves Challenge the CS2 Favorites After FaZe’s Exit?
items.content:
The Counter-Strike 2 calendar has reached its biggest event of the second half of 2026, with the PGL Major Singapore bringing 32 teams together from 24 November to 13 December. The tournament has a prize pool of $1.25 million, and after three days of Stage 1 it has already produced its first big casualty.
Teams such as Team Vitality, MOUZ and Team Spirit are considered to be the main contenders, but there are also several organizations looking to disrupt their plans. FaZe Clan, Team Liquid and 100 Thieves all began their campaigns in Stage 1, in accordance with the Swiss format, hoping to earn a place in the later rounds. Three days in, those three campaigns have gone in very different directions: Liquid are through to Stage 2, 100 Thieves are still alive at 2-2, and FaZe are on their way home.
Who Are the Favorites at PGL Major Singapore 2026?
According to experts and recent results, the clear favorite is Team Vitality. Their back-to-back Major titles in 2025 established them as the team to beat, while ZywOo and ropz provide the kind of individual quality that can decide matches against almost any opponent.
MOUZ are another serious contender. They actually lead the 2 November Valve Regional Standings with 1,960 points, narrowly ahead of Vitality’s 1,922. The team is especially dangerous in longer series, as it is able to maintain the quality of its performance and has a great team structure.
Team Spirit also deserves attention, especially with donk and sh1ro capable of taking over games through individual performances. Meanwhile, FURIA brings an aggressive approach and considerable firepower. It is also important to note that because of the format of this tournament, the favorites start their competition at Stage 3, which allows them to prepare and strategize while Stage 1 sorts out the rest of the field.
The Major’s global audience also shows how closely gaming and digital finance now overlap, with more fans buying games, skins and subscriptions with cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and Ethereum. Readers who want to understand that side of the ecosystem can find crypto news, market explainers and beginner guides at CryptoManiaks.
FaZe Clan: Experience Was Not Enough This Time
FaZe Clan arrived with one of the most recognisable lineups in the tournament, including Twistzz, frozen, Neityu, jcobbb and JBOEN. Twistzz brings experience few players can match, while frozen has established himself as one of the more dependable individual performers in the roster. Past performance did not favor FaZe, however, after back-to-back 1-2 defeats against FURIA and Team Falcons at IEM Beijing 2026 left them 13th to 16th, and Singapore followed the same pattern.
Twistzz, who calls for FaZe Clan, took the blame for the Stage 1 exit. Photo: Esports Kingdom, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons.
Their opening match against Wildcard on 24 November ended in a 13-9 loss on Nuke. FaZe recovered later that day with a 13-3 win over GOSH on Mirage, but a 13-10 defeat to PARIVISION on Anubis on 25 November pushed them into an elimination series. HEROIC then won it 2-1 on 26 November, taking Mirage 13-3 and Nuke 13-3 around FaZe’s 13-11 win on Ancient. FaZe leave with a 1-3 record, their worst at a Major since IEM Rio 2022, and our report on FaZe’s 1-3 exit covers what Twistzz said afterwards.
https://x.com/pglesports/status/2125872788087230703
Team Liquid: Consistency Finally Pays Off
Team Liquid is a mixture of experience and newer talent, with NAF, EliGE, malbsMd, JT and Jorko making up the lineup for Singapore. Their earlier results were a mixed bag, since Liquid beat Aurora 2-0 and TYLOO by the same scoreline at IEM Beijing but also lost to PARIVISION and BetBoom. The question before the Major was whether they could string wins together, and so far the answer has been yes.
Their opening opponent was GOSH, the renamed team featuring s1mple and Magisk, and Liquid won 13-1 on Nuke before beating Wildcard 13-8 on Mirage to reach 2-0. Ninjas in Pyjamas stopped them in the first qualification series on 25 November, but Liquid came straight back on 26 November and beat Imperial 2-0, winning Anubis 13-7 and then holding on to take Cache 16-13 in overtime. That 3-1 record sends them to Stage 2, where the opposition gets tougher but the pressure of the opening Swiss rounds is behind them. Our report on s1mple’s difficult start with GOSH shows how one-sided that first match was.
100 Thieves: The Dark Horse Is Still Standing
100 Thieves remain one of the most interesting teams in the tournament. The organization secured its Major invitation by winning the FiRe Last Chance tournament in Buenos Aires, which required five consecutive victories, and Singapore is its first appearance at a Counter-Strike Major. The lineup combines experienced veterans dev1ce and rain with younger players Gizmy, sirah and poiii, a balance that has already been tested.
Their opening match against Chinggis Warriors on 24 November ended in a 13-6 win, but losses to Imperial and Eternal Fire left them 1-2 and facing elimination. Against 9z on 26 November they lost Nuke 13-5, then turned the series around by winning Dust2 13-6 and Ancient 13-5. rain led the comeback with 26 kills on Dust2, and poiii posted the most damage per round across the series. At 2-2, 100 Thieves now play one more deciding series on 27 November for a place in Stage 2, with HEROIC among the other teams in the same position.
Can Liquid and 100 Thieves Reach the Playoffs?
FaZe, Team Liquid and 100 Thieves started Singapore with different strengths, and the first three days have separated them. FaZe’s inconsistency caught up with them in Stage 1, while Liquid have shown they can beat good opponents and recover from a setback, which is exactly what they will need against the stronger field in Stage 2.
The Swiss format means a team needs three victories to advance, while three losses mean elimination, and only eight places are available from each stage. For 100 Thieves that leaves no margin at all on 27 November, and for Liquid it means starting again from zero in the next stage. The full Stage 1 Day 2 recap and our PGL Major Singapore 2026 wiki track every result, while PGL on X posts the schedule for each day. The playoffs run from 10 to 13 December at the Singapore Indoor Stadium, and by then the picture for all three teams will be very different again.
The post PGL Major Singapore 2026: Can Team Liquid and 100 Thieves Challenge the CS2 Favorites After FaZe’s Exit? appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: AnyPS5 Passes 61,000 GitHub Stars as GTA 6 Fans Look for a Way Onto PC
items.content:
AnyPS5, an open-source project that converts PlayStation 5 games into native Windows and Linux programs, has become one of the most-watched repositories on GitHub in the week GTA 6 arrived on consoles. GitHub itself drew attention to it on 26 November, saying the project had passed 58,000 stars since its August launch. By the afternoon of the same day, the repository showed about 61,700 stars, roughly 6,000 forks and more than 1,100 contributors.
The surge is easy to explain, because GTA 6 is only available on PS5 and Xbox Series X and S. Rockstar has not announced a PC version, so many PC players are watching any project that promises to move console games onto their machines. The project’s own records show it is nowhere near running GTA 6, however, and even GTA 5 is still rough.
GTA 6 is finally here, sparking one of the biggest weeks in gaming and open source on GitHub.
The repo AnyPS5 has passed 58K stars since its August launch, rewriting PS5 executables to run on Windows and Linux. Does changing where games run cross a legal line? Share your take.… pic.twitter.com/WY7i9pg1G0
— GitHub (@github) November 26, 2026
How AnyPS5 runs PS5 games without an emulator
AnyPS5 describes itself as a relinker rather than an emulator. It takes a PS5 game’s executable and converts it into the target system’s native format, then links it against its own reimplementations of the PS5’s system libraries. There is no separate runtime process imitating the console, which is the approach used by traditional emulators.
The project says it does not include or distribute any copyrighted software, firmware, keys or Sony libraries. Its documentation also says the tool does not extract or decrypt game files, and that it needs an executable that has already been decrypted. PS5 games are encrypted on the console, and a claimed game dump on firmware 14.22 this month showed how much effort goes into getting files off it.
The scale of the effort is unusual for a project of this kind. The repository passed 51,000 commits on 26 November and had about 2,400 open pull requests at the same time. It has a set of rules written specifically for AI coding agents, and every pull request has to state whether AI tools were used to make it.
Where GTA 5 and GTA 6 stand on AnyPS5
The best result so far is the PS5 version of GTA 5. In the project’s public bring-up thread, a contributor reported the North Yankton prologue playing with working rendering, sound and HUD on a separate testing branch. Performance mode ran at around 27 to 28 frames per second in one scene on an RTX 5080, while the ray-traced modes managed only a few frames per second.
That result has not reached the main version of the tool yet. The same thread said that, as of 9 October, the main branch still stopped at boot without a set of open pull requests, which contributors were working through. The tester also noted that the frame rate drops depending on where the player is and where they look.
GTA 6 is much further away, according to the project’s own records. Its GTA 6 bring-up thread lists the game as not converting at all, with no version tested and no system tested, and the thread has since been closed. Anyone claiming to offer a working GTA 6 PC build through AnyPS5 is not describing anything the project itself has shown, and fake GTA 6 PC downloads have already been used to spread malware.
Why GitHub is asking whether AnyPS5 crosses a legal line
GitHub’s post asked its followers whether “changing where games run” crosses a legal line, and it had been viewed more than 150,000 times on X by the afternoon. The question is a live one in the GTA 6 scene this week. Take-Two used a single notice to take down 3,007 repositories tied to the Leonida PC port, which was built to run the Xbox version of the game on PC.
In that 24 November notice, Take-Two rejected the argument that asking users to supply their own game files protects a project. GitHub’s DMCA takedown policy sets out how such notices are handled, including counter-notices for projects that believe they were removed in error. In the United States, getting around copy protection is covered separately by the anti-circumvention rules that the US Copyright Office reviews every three years.
AnyPS5 says it is intended for interoperability, research, preservation and compatibility, and that users are responsible for making sure their files are obtained legally. Sony has not commented publicly on the project, although it has already cut PSN access for hacked consoles this year. Its own PlayStation terms of service bar users from reverse engineering its content or getting around its encryption. The official GTA VI site still lists the game for PS5 and Xbox Series X and S only.
The post AnyPS5 Passes 61,000 GitHub Stars as GTA 6 Fans Look for a Way Onto PC appeared first on TalkEsport.

9z CEO Says CS2 Pros Are Discussing a Boycott of the Next Major
items.content:
Professional Counter-Strike players are discussing a possible boycott of the next Major, according to Francisco “Frankkaster” Postiglione, the chief executive of Argentine organisation 9z. He made the claim on X on 26 November, during the PGL Major Singapore, after saying that the money teams earn from Majors no longer covers the cost of the staff they send. No player, team or players’ group has confirmed any plan publicly, so at this stage it is talk reported by one team owner rather than an organised action.
Frankkaster’s first post went up at 01:54 UTC, hours before 9z played their final match of the event. Writing in Spanish, he said the Major situation was bordering on disastrous, because teams could not even cover the travel costs of the staff who support players and create content. His comments add a team owner’s voice to a complaint that has been building across the scene for most of the season.
Lo del major ya rosa lo nefasto, no llegas ni a cubrir al personal que viaja para asistir jugadores y crear contenido
— 𓆰Francisco Postiglione𓆪 (@FrankkasterX) November 26, 2026
What Frankkaster said about the Major boycott talk
The boycott claim came in a reply rather than in his original post. At 02:27 UTC, an X user named Alfonsina asked whether it was true that players wanted to organise and stay away from the next Major, adding a one-word call for them to unionise. Frankkaster answered at 04:39 UTC, and his reply is the only direct evidence so far that such a discussion exists.
In that reply, he wrote that “it’s happening”, and said the Argentina Major would be the event to suffer, which angered him most of all. He did not say which players or teams were involved, how many of them backed the idea, or whether anything had been put to Valve or the organisers. Skin-trading accounts on X then spread the exchange in English, describing it as a report that pros were discussing a boycott.
Esta ocurriendo y la va a ligar el major de argentina, eso es lo que mas bronca da
— 𓆰Francisco Postiglione𓆪 (@FrankkasterX) November 26, 2026
Nobody else has added to the claim in public so far. We could find no statement on the subject from Valve, from PGL as the organiser in Singapore, or from FiReSPORTS, which is running the next Major. No player has spoken on the record about joining a boycott either, and 9z itself has not commented beyond its chief executive’s posts.
Why sticker money no longer covers a Major trip
The complaint is not new, and it has grown louder since Valve rebuilt the Major sticker system. In its Cologne Major announcement, Valve replaced sticker capsules with a Major Shop and tied every team’s royalty to its seeding and final placing. The organiser now takes 5 per cent of Major Shop and Major Pass revenue. The 32 team positions share 45 per cent, from 2.85 per cent for the winner down to 0.72 per cent for last place.
That share is then split equally between the organisation and its five players, as Counter-Strike’s official account set out when the change was announced. For Singapore, Valve went back to fixed sticker prices in a 17 November update, after its demand-based pricing failed earlier in the year. Our editorial on the CS2 sticker money crisis estimates that a bottom seed could take home only a few hundred dollars from this Major’s early sales.
The idea that teams might stay away has been circulating all week. On 25 November, a well-followed community account claimed that teams wanted to skip future Majors unless the sticker system changed. Presenter Sam “TechGirl” Wright has also warned that legacy organisations could quit CS2 if they keep missing Majors. Frankkaster is the first team chief executive to suggest publicly that players are talking about acting on it.
What a boycott would mean for the Buenos Aires Major
The next Major is the first ever held in Argentina, which is why the comments carry extra weight coming from an Argentine team owner. FiReSPORTS confirmed in January that it would host the first Major of 2027 in Buenos Aires, and its official website still promotes the event. The Buenos Aires and Shanghai Majors are scheduled for 31 May to 20 June and 22 November to 12 December 2027, according to the dates reported when they were revealed.
How a boycott would work in practice is far from clear. Major invitations come from Valve’s regional standings rather than from franchise slots, so a team that declined to travel would simply be replaced by the next one in the rankings. Valve has not said what would happen to a team that qualified and then withdrew, and the idea would need near-universal support among the top teams to have any effect.
For 9z, the debate arrived on a painful day. The team lost 2-1 to 100 Thieves later on 26 November and confirmed on X that it had finished 1-3 in the Swiss stage, ending its run at the PGL Major Singapore 2026. Frankkaster posted a one-word apology to fans at 12:25 UTC, about half an hour after the elimination was confirmed.
The post 9z CEO Says CS2 Pros Are Discussing a Boycott of the Next Major appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Lenny Kravitz Brings Bawma, the Pirate King of Aleph in 007 First Light, to HITMAN World of Assassination
items.content:
Summary
Grammy Award winner Lenny Kravitz makes his World of Assassination debut as Bawma, the Pirate King of Aleph from 007 First Light, in The Mutiny, a new Elusive Target available starting today through December 24.
For once, the client briefs Agent 47 personally, as Bawma guides him across Ambrose Island to deal with three rogue lieutenants, and a set of Voodoo Dolls offers one of the most creative ways to take them down.
The mission is free for new players via the Free Demo and for all HITMAN World of Assassination players, and launches alongside the new Rockstar Pack.
Agent 47 has a new client, and he isn’t usually the type to stay in the shadows. HITMAN World of Assassination’s latest Elusive Target, The Mutiny, stars Lenny Kravitz as Bawma, the magnetic and unpredictable Pirate King of Aleph, first brought to life in 007 First Light. Kravitz lends both his likeness and his voice to the character, who crosses over into the World of Assassination for the first time.
The Mutiny Elusive Target mission is available globally on Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One, ROG Xbox Ally X, ROG Xbox Ally, and PC starting Thursday, November 26, through Thursday, December 24, 2026.
From the opening briefing, it’s clear this assignment is unusual. Diana never lets a client brief 47 directly, but Bawma has paid the Agency generously and insists on directing the operation himself. Little is known about the man behind the alias: intelligence suggests he was raised as a child soldier before building Aleph, a sprawling black-market hub in the Western Hemisphere that he calls his kingdom.
Now he’s hiding out on Ambrose Island, and 47’s objective is simple: find Bawma, make contact, and await further instructions.
Once 47 tracks Bawma down through the island’s ruins and jungles, it soon becomes clear that something far more valuable is at stake. Three of Bawma’s rogue lieutenants stand in the way, and none of them will part with what they’re holding easily.
Bawma stays in 47’s ear throughout the mission, and with its bright, upbeat tone and easygoing holiday feel, The Mutiny is one of the most laid-back contracts in the World of Assassination. On Ambrose Island, though, nothing is ever straightforward, and fortune favors the bold.
Bold players will want to pay a visit to Madame Serafine. All three targets can be eliminated with a Voodoo Doll: gather the ingredients, add them to the Ritual Bowl, and pick up the doll Madame Serafine creates.
Then “kill” the doll to take out its target, whether that means stabbing it with a knife, throwing it in water, shooting it or blowing it up, hitting it with a thrown sharp object, or exposing it to fire or electricity.
As with all Elusive Targets, The Mutiny will be removed from the game when it expires on December 24. However, players who own HITMAN World of Assassination or the Ambrose Island location will keep access to The Retaliator, the Arcade version of the mission, as well as its Special Assignment, completely for free.
Players who complete The Mutiny with an IOI Account while it’s live will also unlock the Rock Royalty Duck, a regal rubber duck in flashy sunglasses that detonates when it detects nearby motion.
Launching alongside The Mutiny, IO Interactive is also releasing the Rockstar Pack, a collection of outfits, weapons, gear, and Freelancer Safehouse cosmetics inspired by the bold style and electric energy of rock ’n’ roll icons. The pack is available for $5.99/€5.99/£4.99 and includes:

Review: Tom the Postgirl Pairs Peeping With Absurdity
items.content:
Tom the Postgirl is an unusual kind of adventure game. There are some point-and-click elements, as the side quests involve getting specific items to fulfill supplemental goals. There’s a very loose story. But it’s really more about stalking, peeping through windows, and spying on weird people throughout a strange town while making unusual deliveries and maybe getting up to mischief. It’s not as robust as something like Thank Goodness You’re Here, but definitely feels like it. The finished game is a strange little comedic dalliance that is basically a way to pass an afternoon.
Tom is the newest post office employee in a small rural town. She starts as an intern delivering packages to a few houses. However, after a few successful deliveries, she’s quickly bumped up to a full-fledged employee. Which means more packages to deliver and people to spy on as she does.
Each act of Tom the Postgirl goes about the same. You get to a new area with an array of packages given to you by your boss. You visit each house and make the delivery. However, you don’t just knock on the door or ring the bell and hand over the item. While there, you can also peek in on everyone in the area. This might mean looking at things like trees, in bushes, or in hay bales or peeking through windows and loose boards in buildings to see what’s happening in all those spots. Doing so before and after a delivery can cause the scenes to change, suggesting more insights into these impromptu storylines and potentially illicit affairs.
All of these require no thought to complete. When you enter a building where a delivery will be made, you don’t need to find the right package. It will automatically appear. Peeping is optional, but it’s very boring if you don’t. It’s really more about being a voyeur and enjoying the silly, absurd moments you see as a result.

This isn’t to say there’s no gameplay in Tom the Postgirl. While the actual deliveries are straightforward (peeping aside), each area also has a side quest associated with it. For example, spoilers aside, the first act involves finding seven missing chickens. You’ll get a pair of binoculars to use use to help with that. This means searching the scenes you know of to see where the missing birds might be. (And then slapping a stamp on ‘em and kicking ‘em home again.) Another act involves a garden event side quest, which involves Tom entering at the last minute and potentially “preparing” her own plot for judging as she goes about her rounds.
Images via Oopsie Daisies and Arte France
I referenced Thank Goodness You’re Here earlier and, Tom the Postgirl does feel similar. It can also be quite silly, dark, and obscure. The personalities of other characters help provide additional antics to enjoy. It’s going to be weird. Maybe even off-putting sometimes. But it’s always going to be goofy in a stylish, cartoonish sort of way and let you engage as much as you’d like.
Tom the Postgirl is goofy fun, though some of the humorous situations are a bit niche and might not be to everyone’s taste. If you’re looking for more of an adventure, which might require thought and input to puzzle out situations and keep stalking, you won’t find it here. items.title: Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition announced as a free update
items.content:
Studio Playtonic has amassed a solid reputation for itself over the years. While the team’s first project – the 3D collectathon Yooka-Laylee – suffered from plenty of gameplay-related issues at launch, their follow-up release ‘Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair‘ proved to be much more of a critical success. In the wake of the arrival of their vastly-improved Yooka-Replaylee last year (a pseudo-remake of the first game), Playtonic have now announced a surprise ‘Definitive Edition’ coming to ‘The Impossible Lair’.
Set to be released on the 15th of December as a free upgrade for all owners of the original, Yooka-Laylee and The Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition focuses primarily on improving the game’s visuals and performance.
Unlike the first Yooka-Laylee, which suffered from plenty of issues on a gameplay front, The Impossible Lair was highly celebrated straight from the get-go, with many praising it as being one of the best Donkey Kong Country-esque 2.5D platformers to have been released in quite some time. As such, it makes sense that Playtonic would want to keep the Definitive Edition close to the original experience, albeit with current-gen improvements.
Coming to PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch 2 and Steam (though not Xbox oddly enough), Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition takes advantage of current-gen hardware in a number of ways, with the listed improvements being as follows:
4K resolution at 120fps
Enhanced lighting and ambient occlusion effects
Higher-fidelity shadows
Two orchestrated soundtracks
Trowzer's Top Tonic Pack DLC included
While exact details on the resolution side were not shared for Switch 2, Playtonic have promised that those using Nintendo’s latest will benefit from “higher resolutions in both docked and handheld modes” as well as a separate 120fps mode – though all other improvements remain in-tact.
Steam users meanwhile will benefit from “the same visual enhancements and additional content featured in the PlayStation 5 version” via a new ‘Ultra’ graphics preset.
While the lack of an Xbox version is curious to say the least, being able to experience the slick and satisfying gameplay / movement of The Impossible Lair at 120fps is highly appreciated. With both ‘Yooka-Laylee’ and ‘The Impossible Lair’ having now achieved their final forms, it will be interesting to see what Playtonic has planned for the future.

items.title: Gentle Mates Sign Boaster and Alfajer for VCT 2027, Confirm Rainbow Six Siege Entry
items.content:
Gentle Mates have signed Jake “Boaster” Howlett to lead their VALORANT roster for VCT EMEA 2027 and confirmed their entry into Rainbow Six Siege esports. The French organisation revealed both moves during its 2027 Keynote stream on 25 November 2026. Boaster joins with his Fnatic teammate Emir “Alfajer” Ali Beder, ending a Fnatic run of nearly six years.
The Keynote also confirmed that Gentle Mates will host Call of Duty League (CDL) Major 1 2027 at the Plenitude Arena in Paris from 12 to 14 February.
Gentle Mates VALORANT roster for 2027:
Gentle Mates posted the full five player lineup on X after the stream. Former Sentinels head coach Adam “kaplan” Kaplan leads the team from the bench.
Jake “Boaster” Howlett (from Fnatic)
Emir “Alfajer” Ali Beder (from Fnatic)
Uğur “Ruxic” Güç (from NAVI)
Denis-Stefan “kozzy” Aionitoaei
Martin “MAGNUM” Peňkov
Head coach: Adam “kaplan” Kaplan
Kozzy is a 16 year old Romanian duelist, which makes him the youngest player on the roster. The lineup mixes two of EMEA’s most experienced players with younger talent, and Boaster takes over as in game leader.
Gentle Mates hold a VCT partner slot for the 2027 and 2028 seasons, and 2027 is their first year in the programme. About a month ago, the club released all five players from its 2026 roster, marteen, starxo, Minny, Proxh and H1ber, along with head coach Jiri “KUNDIKUNDI” Honkala and assistant coach Erim “Mavera” Sasal.
As a partner team, Gentle Mates get an automatic place in VCT EMEA 2027 Kickoff. The rebuild is one of the biggest moves of an offseason that has also seen TenZ sign with T1 for VCT Pacific 2027 and Vitality promote Scutt to head coach. Fnatic now has to replace both its captain and Alfajer, after a 2026 season in which several big names were among the teams that missed VALORANT Champions 2026.
Gentle Mates join Rainbow Six Siege esports
Gentle Mates closed the Keynote with a teaser marked “R6”, confirming that the organisation will join Rainbow Six Siege esports in partnership with Ubisoft. The club will be part of the R6 Share programme from the 2027 season. It is the first new R6 Share partner since 100 Thieves, who were confirmed at the Six Invitational 2026.
Gentle Mates and Ubisoft have not said which region the team will play in, and no Rainbow Six roster has been announced yet. Europe and MENA already has six R6 Share teams: G2 Esports, Team Falcons, FNATIC, Team Secret, Virtus.pro and Shifters.
Beyond VALORANT and Rainbow Six, Gentle Mates used the Keynote to set out plans across Rocket League and Call of Duty. The CDL Major 1 event in February will be the club’s first major international event as host in its home city of Paris.

items.title: How To Fix The GTA VI Weather Bug and Bring Back Rain
items.content:
The GTA 6 weather bug keeps Leonida stuck on clear skies for long stretches, and players on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S still report it. Rockstar released update 01.002.002 on November 23 to fix weather that does not change for extended periods. Many players say the problem remains. A manual workaround is now spreading.
This guide covers the steps for both consoles, what the patch changed, and what to expect after you try the fix.
GTA 6 Weather Bug Fix
GTA 6 launched on November 19, 2026, for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Soon after, players said rain and storms rarely appeared. Weather did change for some of them, but far less often than intended, and some conditions lasted too long.
Rockstar responded with update 01.002.002. Its patch notes say the update fixed an issue that stopped weather from changing for extended periods. Some players still see the same problem after installing it.
Clearing the system cache is the workaround players now use. Rockstar also provides its own support steps for clearing the Xbox cache.
Cache clearing does not remove your saves or inventory. On Xbox, Rockstar says the steps reset brightness and language settings.
How to Fix the GTA 6 Weather Bug on PS5
These steps work on the PS5 and PS5 Pro. Save your game first.
Turn off the console completely.
Hold the power button until it beeps 2 times. Safe mode starts.
Plug in your DualSense controller with a USB cable and press the PS button.
Select option 6: Clear Cache and Rebuild Database.
Choose option 1: Clear System Software Cache.
Select OK when the message says the cache will be cleared.
Let the console restart, then launch GTA 6.
How to Fix the GTA 6 Weather Bug on Xbox Series X|S
The Xbox method is a full power cycle. It takes about 5 minutes.
Press the power button to shut the console down completely.
Unplug the power cable from the console.
Wait 2 minutes.
Reconnect the cable and turn the Xbox back on.
Players also advise quitting GTA 6 fully instead of using Quick Resume. Some say rain returned after a clean restart.
What to Expect After Clearing the Cache
Do not expect rain the moment you load in. GTA 6 weather is still dynamic, so you may need to explore Leonida before the next storm arrives.
Results differ by player. Some report a storm right after loading. Others say rain only appeared after several more hours of play following the patch. Some players believe the fix is not fully implemented and that weather shifts feel too sudden.
Weather in GTA 6 is also local. Rockstar has confirmed rain that can soak one part of the map while another stays sunny. If it is dry where you stand, driving to a different area can help.
It does not change how likely rain is. Rain was already in the game, and the bug locked conditions in place.

items.title: Delta Force Metal Gear Solid Collab: Release Date and Rewards
items.content:
The Delta Force Metal Gear Solid collab starts on November 27, 2026, during Season Aurora. Team Jade confirmed the date in an official Steam post on November 25. The event adds a Naked Snake appearance for Nox and a free legendary SR-3M skin. The update rolls out on November 26 and 27 with no downtime. The collab runs until December 31. Team Jade first planned it for December 2025, then postponed it.
Read on for the release date and every reward you can earn.
Delta Force Metal Gear Solid Collab Release Date
The Delta Force Metal Gear Solid collab goes live on Friday, November 27, 2026. Team Jade announced the date in a Steam post titled “The Wait Is Over.”
The update arrives over November 26 and 27. Team Jade says gameplay and matchmaking will not be affected. Players with an outdated client must update to the latest version before they can log in.
Naked Snake arrives as an appearance for Nox, an Assault operator. Players can try for it in a prize pool that runs until December 31. The free legendary SR-3M appearance comes from the Collab Legendary Gift event, which ends on December 27.
The post lists dates only. It gives no start times or time zones. If the event tab looks empty early on November 27, check again later that day.
Delta Force Metal Gear Solid Event Schedule
The announcement lists 5 Metal Gear events. Two more Operations events start on the same day. Here is the full schedule:
Faction Flagship Task and Special Drink Crafting are not Metal Gear events. They close earlier than the collab, so players should check their end dates.
How to Get the Free SR-3M Skin
The METAL GEAR SOLID Δ SR-3M is the free legendary reward of the collab. It comes from the Collab Legendary Gift event, which runs from November 27 to December 27.
Players need to play Operations, Warfare, or Detonation and finish activity missions. One example is surviving in matches. Each milestone unlocks Tactical Armament Vouchers. The final milestone gives the SR-3M appearance.
All 3 modes count toward progress. Team Jade has not published the number of milestones or how much progress each match gives.
The Phantom Blade Zero collab used the same event name, Collab Legendary Gift. Check the banner in the event tab to make sure you are tracking the right one.
Delta Force Naked Snake Prize Pool for Nox
Naked Snake is not a free mission reward. Players enter the prize pool with Delta Tickets or Delta Coins. The pool runs from November 27 to December 31.
Every attempt gives either an appearance from the pool or Naked Snake Coins. The pool holds these items:
Naked Snake appearance for Nox
METAL GEAR SOLID Δ S12K shotgun appearance
Name card, avatar, calling card, and spray paint
A voice item
Naked Snake Coins
Appearances cannot repeat, but Naked Snake Coins can drop many times. Players can spend the coins in the Fortune Store on any pool appearance they do not own yet. They can also spend them on this season’s TurBricks.
Unspent Naked Snake Coins are cleared when the event ends, so players should spend them before December 31. Team Jade has not published attempt prices, exchange prices, or drop odds. The announcement does not list any stat changes for the skin.
Earlier reports suggested that David Hayter would voice Naked Snake. The new announcement lists a voice item but gives no details about it.
Cardboard Box Rewards in Operations
The Operations event runs from November 27 to December 17. METAL GEAR SOLID Δ Cardboard Box containers appear in matches. They can hold rare loot, including limited edition figurines.
Players can claim the Cardboard Box Stealth action by logging in during the event. The Warfare and Detonation events also give the action through in-match missions. Search missions in Operations pay out Tactical Armament Vouchers.
Team Jade has not said which maps or locations have the boxes. The figurines are a chance drop, not a guaranteed reward.
Why the Delta Force Metal Gear Solid Collab Was Delayed
Konami and Team Jade confirmed the collab in September 2025. In November 2025, reports said Naked Snake would arrive on January 1, 2026. The collab events were set for December 19, 2025.
Team Jade postponed the collab on December 11, 2025. The post said the delay was due to operational changes. The studio gave no other reason. Today’s Steam post is the first new date since then.

Hideki Kamiya wants to make a “truly insane” Castlevania game
items.content:
Since his departure from Platinum Games, industry veteran Hideki Kamiya has been a bit of an open book, with the Devil May Cry / Bayonetta creator sharing his thoughts and desires regarding future potential projects as part of his new endeavour under studio Clovers. While the team remains hard at work on the sequel to the PS2 classic Okami, Kamiya has revealed that he would love to work with publisher Konami on a “truly insane” new entry in the Castlevania series if given the opportunity.
Following his departure from PlatinumGames back in 2023, studio co-founder Hideki Kamiya opened up a YouTube channel to candidly discuss all manner of topics from his past work to personal anecdotes and more. Over a year on from his last video, Kamiya returned to his channel with a new post.
While the video was technically filmed back in July of 2025, it still includes plenty of interesting revelations including the exact nature of studio Clovers’ relationship with Capcom as it pertains to the Okami sequel.
Perhaps the most interesting part of the video however came in his discussions surrounding hypothetical projects. Though Kamiya expressed desires to “keep building a good relationship with Capcom” while also wanting “to be on good terms with Nintendo” other platforms for potential collaborations included both PlayStation and Xbox.
That said, Konami is where Kamiya’s strongest ideas appear to be stemming from, with the creative making explicit reference to Castlevania, stating (as translated by Automaton-Media): “We’ll definitely make Castlevania. If you let us work on it, we can make something truly insane, so just contact us and we’ll be at your service.”
It is worth noting that many of these suggestions were just that – suggestions, with Kamiya himself following up by claiming to be “a bit busy right now”. Whether in jest or not, a Castlevania game headed by Hideki Kamiya would certainly be interesting, especially if they were to go down the 3D route.
Of course, Kamiya and Clovers are currently hard at work on Okami 2, and so we will have to wait and see how it turns out. That said, it is encouraging to see Kamiya getting his mojo back and seemingly quite excited to work in the video games industry once again.

items.title: Contexto Hints & Answer For November 26, 2026
FaZe Crash Out of the Singapore Major at 1-3
items.content:
FaZe Clan are out of the PGL Major Singapore 2026 after HEROIC beat them 2-1 in a Stage 1 elimination series on 26 November. The defeat left FaZe with a 1-3 record in the opening Swiss stage, which places them 28th to 30th at the 32-team Major. PGL confirmed the exit on X at 08:42 UTC, moments after HEROIC closed out the deciding map on Nuke.
It is FaZe’s worst record at a Major since IEM Rio 2022, where the defending champions went 0-3 in the Legends Stage and finished 15th to 16th. This time the team never left the first stage, playing all four of its matches before the Major had reached its fourth day. FaZe started in Stage 1 because they were 20th in Valve’s global standings of 2 November, too low for a later invite on the Singapore Major schedule.
FaZe's run at the PGL Major Singapore 2026 ends here @heroicgg survive the 2-1 thriller to move to 2-2 and keep their Major alive. @FaZeEsports exit the tournament with a 1-3 record.#PGLMajor pic.twitter.com/wK4XIkNo96
— PGL (@pglesports) November 26, 2026
How HEROIC knocked FaZe out on Mirage and Nuke
HEROIC against FaZe opened the third day as one of three elimination series on PGL’s Day 3 schedule, with the winner staying alive and the loser going home. FaZe picked Mirage for the first map and lost it 13-3, falling one map from elimination inside the first hour. They answered on HEROIC’s pick of Ancient, winning it 13-11, and the team’s account quickly posted that FaZe still had life.
Nuke, the map left over after both sides made their bans, ended the series in one direction. HEROIC won it 13-3, the same score as the opener, and FaZe managed only six rounds across the two maps they lost. HEROIC, who sat 18th in the same Valve standings, wasted little time on X and pointed FaZe towards the airport in a post minutes after the win.
It is not the first time HEROIC have ended a FaZe Major either, as they also beat FaZe 2-1 in the quarterfinals of the 2023 Paris Major. HEROIC’s lineup of Brollan, MartinezSa, nilo, Chr1zN and susp now moves to 2-2 and plays again on 27 November for a place in Stage 2. FaZe fielded frozen, Twistzz, jcobbb, Neityu and JBOEN, with Twistzz calling the team since the departure of karrigan.
Out of the Major pic.twitter.com/2Ya2ydpZqW
— FaZe Esports (@FaZeEsports) November 26, 2026
FaZe’s four Stage 1 matches in Singapore
FaZe’s Major began badly on 24 November, when Wildcard beat them 13-9 on Nuke in the opening round. The first three rounds of Stage 1 are best-of-one matches, so a single bad map was enough to push FaZe straight into the 0-1 pool. They recovered later that day with a 13-3 win on Mirage over GOSH, the former BC.Game roster that includes s1mple, after s1mple’s team had already lost to Team Liquid.
The second day brought another best-of-one defeat, this time 13-10 to PARIVISION on Anubis. PARIVISION are playing the Major as PVISION, one of four teams PGL renamed because the companies behind them are not licensed in Singapore. That loss dropped FaZe into the 1-2 pool with five other teams, and the Stage 1 Day 2 results then paired them with HEROIC.
Across six maps in Singapore, FaZe won 51 rounds and lost 66. Their only map wins came on Mirage against GOSH and on Ancient against HEROIC. Three of their four matches were best-of-one games, and FaZe lost two of those by four rounds or fewer.
Why the 1-3 exit stings for FaZe after a hard year
Singapore was FaZe’s only Major of 2026, because they were not at the IEM Cologne Major in June after missing out on a place through Valve’s standings. Karrigan had left FaZe in April, and he went on to lift the Cologne trophy as a Falcons stand-in. Only a year earlier, FaZe had reached the grand final of the StarLadder Budapest Major, where they lost 3-1 to Team Vitality.
The rest of FaZe’s season followed a similar pattern at other events. They lost both of their series at IEM Beijing at the start of November, going down 2-1 to FURIA and to Falcons. On 15 November they lost to fnatic and HEROIC in the closed qualifier for PGL Cluj-Napoca 2027. Earlier in the year, PGL’s own posts recorded a 1-3 exit at PGL Cluj-Napoca 2026 in February and a 0-3 exit in Bucharest in April.
Twistzz took the blame as captain when he spoke on PGL’s broadcast after the series, according to HLTV. He said FaZe were “not a team that felt extremely competitive coming into this event”. He also said the team’s chemistry had faded the longer the players stayed together, and that he needed more input from a young lineup.
The early exit also cuts into FaZe’s share of the Major Shop money. Valve’s Singapore Major update says half of the proceeds from tournament items go to players, teams and the organiser, shared according to each team’s initial seed and final placement. A finish of 28th to 30th puts FaZe close to the bottom of that split, at a time when sticker money for teams is already under scrutiny.
Stage 1 finishes on 27 November, and the Major moves to the Singapore Indoor Stadium for the playoffs from 10 to 13 December. FaZe had not announced any roster changes by the time of writing. JBOEN, the AWPer they signed on loan from BIG in June, is on a loan that runs only until the end of 2026.

All Gamers Sign Jinggg as the Paper Rex Star Heads to VCT China for 2027
items.content:
All Gamers have signed Jinggg as a starting player for the 2027 VCT China season, bringing one of the Pacific region’s most recognisable duelists into the Chinese league. The Chinese organisation confirmed the move on its official Valorant account on 26 November, after weeks of reports linking the Singaporean with the team. It is the third personnel announcement All Gamers have made in two days, following a new coach and a second new starter on 25 November.
Jinggg, whose real name is Wang Jing Jie, has been a free agent since he left Paper Rex on 31 October after five years with the team. All Gamers said the deal followed thorough talks between both sides and respected the player’s wishes, and that he joins the starting lineup with immediate effect. Sheep Esports first reported in early November that the 23-year-old was set to make the switch to China.
【AG Personnel announcement】
After thorough communication and friendly consultations between both sides, and with respect for the player's wishes, we are happy to announce that, starting today, player Jingjie Wang (ID: Jinggg) officially becomes a starting player for AG ！ pic.twitter.com/BVTSwY7I3u
— AG-VALORANT (@AG_VALORANT) November 26, 2026
How Jinggg’s five years at Paper Rex came to an end
Paper Rex brought Jinggg into its Valorant roster in September 2021, and he quickly became a core part of a side known for its fast, aggressive style. His Raze play turned into one of the team’s trademarks, although he has also played Omen and Phoenix at the top level. The Singaporean organisation became one of the most consistent finalists in international Valorant during his time there.
Paper Rex won Masters Toronto in 2025 for its first international title, and also finished second at Masters Copenhagen in 2022 and Champions Los Angeles in 2023. The team reached two more international finals in 2026, at Masters Santiago and Masters London, after winning VCT Pacific Stage 1. Their season ended at Champions Shanghai, where a 2-1 loss to T1 on 9 October completed an unusual record of finishing in every placement bracket at international events.
The break-up came three weeks later, when Paper Rex announced on 31 October that Jinggg and d4v41 were leaving the roster. In its farewell message, the organisation said Jinggg had been a core member ever since he joined and wished him well for the future. Jinggg wrote that Paper Rex had “helped me grow as an individual in and outside the game”, and thanked teammates, staff and fans for half a decade of support.
Hello everyone, today marks the end of an incredible chapter in my life. I am officially parting ways with Paper Rex, the team that has helped me grow as an individual in and outside the game. 5 years ago when i got called up to join PRX i never imagined my life would be like… https://t.co/1BO8NXJUXG
— Jinggg (@Jingggxd) October 31, 2026
What All Gamers are building for VCT China 2027
All Gamers go into the 2027 season with something to prove in Valorant. The team beat Xi Lai Gaming in the upper bracket final of the 2026 VCT China Kickoff to become the first Chinese side through to Masters Santiago. It could not carry that form through the rest of the year. China’s four places at Champions Shanghai went to TYLOO, JD Gaming, EDward Gaming and Xi Lai Gaming, leaving All Gamers among the big names that missed out.
The organisation’s place in the league is secure for the next two seasons, because All Gamers are one of the eight VCT partner teams in China for 2027 and 2028. Its wider esports group is also coming off its best year, after AG.AL won the Esports World Cup 2026 Club Championship in Paris with 5,300 points. The Club Championship carried a $7 million top prize, and the win ended Team Falcons’ two-year reign as champions.
The Valorant rebuild began in earnest on 25 November. All Gamers first named Liu “Septem7” Zhening as coach of the division, then confirmed Liu “Spring” Junting as a starting player half an hour later. Spring, a Taiwanese player, has spent the last three seasons with Wolves Esports, one of the organisations left without a VCT China partnership for 2027.
Jinggg joins a growing list of imports heading to China
The best-known import already at All Gamers is f4ngeer, the Russian player who joined the team ahead of the 2026 season and played for them at Masters Santiago. All Gamers have not yet published their full starting five for 2027, so it is not yet clear who will line up around the new arrivals. Septem7 will begin his tenure with at least two new starters to build around, and one of them has won a Masters title.
Jinggg is not the only established name taking a chance on China this winter. Former G2 star babybay was reported to be joining Weibo Gaming for 2027, another sign that Chinese teams are looking abroad for proven international talent. Paper Rex have been reshaping their own lineup too, with something reportedly cleared as a Pacific resident to free up an import slot. Jinggg’s farewell post from 31 October has been viewed more than 2.3 million times on X.

items.title: REIGNITE Interview: “An Energy Unlike Anything We Had Ever Felt,” Japan’s PUBG Mobile Team on BMIC 2026
items.content:
Japanese PUBG Mobile teams rarely get much attention in India, even though five of them flew to Mumbai for BMIC 2026. REIGNITE was one of those five, and after three days at The Dome in Worli the squad finished 11th of 16 on 88 points. That put them one point ahead of Team SouL, who are now representing India at PMGC 2026 in Istanbul, and only behind KINOTROPE gaming among the Japanese sides.
The result does not tell the whole story, however. REIGNITE went the full 18 matches without a Chicken Dinner, and the team admits it left Mumbai frustrated. In an email interview with TalkEsport, team manager Arakawa Harutaro answered on behalf of the roster and coach Razzy, explaining how an amateur squad became a REIGNITE division, what the Indian crowd felt like from the stage, and why Japan’s scene still has a gap to close on Korea and India. The full standings are in our BMIC 2026 results and points table.
From an Amateur Squad to The Dome in Mumbai
TalkEsport: Please introduce REIGNITE. When did the organisation start, and how did the PUBG Mobile division come together?
REIGNITE: The team originally competed as an amateur team. To focus solely on PUBG Mobile and achieve better results in tournaments, our coach Razzy took the lead in searching for an organisation to join. As a result, the team joined REIGNITE in September 2025.
TalkEsport: Who was on the BMIC 2026 roster, and what does each player do?
REIGNITE: YamaK is our IGL, and Nagon20, miz and Taikizzz play as attackers.
TalkEsport: How did the team qualify for BMIC 2026, and what did it mean to compete in Mumbai?
REIGNITE: In PMJL Season 6 Phase 1, we finished fourth overall, which was lower than our goal. After improving our practice routine, we placed second in PMJL Season 6 Phase 2 and earned our spot at BMIC. Competing in Mumbai meant more to us than just a chance to qualify for PMGC. It was a valuable opportunity to gain offline tournament experience and to face international teams, which we rarely get to do.
REIGNITE's players checked in from India before BMIC 2026. Video: REIGNITE Esports.
That last point comes up again and again in REIGNITE’s answers. Japanese teams play most of their year in the PUBG Mobile Japan League, so a LAN against Korea’s best and six Indian sides is a rare test, and the roster clearly treated it as a lesson as much as a qualifier. Our BMIC 2026 rosters guide sets out how all 16 teams earned their places.
What Mumbai Taught a Japanese Team About Korea and India
TalkEsport: What was your first impression of India, and of the Indian crowd at the event?
REIGNITE: The incredible passion, and an energy in the crowd unlike anything we had ever felt before. It is a truly enviable environment in every way.
TalkEsport: How did your preparation for BMIC differ from your usual tournaments in Japan?
REIGNITE: India and Korea are among the strongest regions in the world. Winning through good rotations is of course important, but we focused even more than usual on not losing gunfights, compared to our matches in Japan.
TalkEsport: Which match or moment from BMIC will the team remember most, and why?
REIGNITE: Match 3 on Erangel on Day 3. We controlled the zone well in the mid-game and kept winning the battles for position against other teams, carrying us into the endgame. In the end, we got caught between DK and KRX and missed the Chicken Dinner, but we felt the process of getting to that point was excellent.
TalkEsport: Indian and Japanese teams play quite differently. What stood out to you about the Indian and other Asian teams you faced?
REIGNITE: They seemed to place great importance on sticking to their own style no matter the situation. Compared to Japanese teams, we felt that many of them don’t change their style just to adapt.
The points table shows where the gap sits. REIGNITE took 50 of their 88 points from finishes and 38 from placement, so the fighting the team prepared for was there. Champions Nongshim RedForce, by comparison, added 85 placement points to 148 from finishes and won five Chicken Dinners, as our report on NS RedForce’s BMIC win explains. Turning strong mid-games like that Erangel round into top-two finishes is the step REIGNITE describe below.
REIGNITE's PUBG Mobile roster. Photo: REIGNITE.
Practice, Loyalty and a Sponsor Call for 2027
TalkEsport: How is the PUBG Mobile scene in Japan growing, and what does it still need to reach the next level?
REIGNITE: To reach the next level, we feel the scene needs an overwhelming amount of practice, along with players who care even more about their team.
TalkEsport: What are REIGNITE’s goals for 2027?
REIGNITE: Of course, to win first place in every tournament!
TalkEsport: Is there a message you’d like to share with your fans, and with the Indian players who supported you?

Take-Two Took Down 3,007 GTA 6 PC Port Repositories With One Notice, and Says the Xbox Build Was Stolen
items.content:
Take-Two Interactive’s legal team used a single copyright notice to take down 3,007 GitHub repositories tied to the biggest GTA 6 PC port project, according to the notice published in GitHub’s public DMCA archive. The 24 November filing targets a repository called Leonida, which described itself as a native PC recompilation of the Xbox version of the game, along with more than 2,900 copies of it. GitHub says it processed the request against the whole network because it was too large to review fork by fork.
The notice is the first public, on-the-record explanation from Rockstar’s parent company of why the port projects have been disappearing. Project Leonida vanished from GitHub and Discord late on 23 November, which set off a wave of fake GTA 6 PC downloads carrying malware. Two days later, the modder known as omonkey said Rockstar had emailed him and ended his live streams.
What Take-Two’s GTA 6 takedown notice says
The filing comes from Take-Two’s IP Enforcement Team and makes three main claims. It says stolen game files from an Xbox Series build of Grand Theft Auto VI were publicly distributed on 20 November 2026, the day after the game launched. It says the Leonida repository opened the following day with the purpose of running that Xbox Series version on PC, and that its instructions required Xbox Series game files as input.
Take-Two also argues that asking users to supply their own game files does not protect the project. The notice says the timing of the repository and its explicit focus on Grand Theft Auto make clear that the files users must supply are the leaked ones, and that the developers were aware of that. It describes the repository as a derivative work and says it breaks section 2.3 of Rockstar’s terms of service, which bars users from decompiling, reverse engineering or creating derivative works from its games.
The language at the end of the notice leaves no room for a compromise. Take-Two asked GitHub to disable the repositories and every associated fork, writing that “this content must be completely disabled”. GitHub added a note at the top of the published notice explaining that it processed the takedown against the entire network of 3,007 repositories.
Why GitHub removed thousands of forks at once
GitHub normally treats forks as separate projects, because they belong to different users and may have changed significantly from the original. Its DMCA takedown policy says that disabling a parent repository does not automatically disable its copies. Copyright owners usually have to name every fork they believe is infringing in their notice.
The policy makes an exception for very large networks. If a network has more than 100 repositories, GitHub may disable all of it at once. The rights holder must swear that it has reviewed a representative sample and believes all or most forks infringe to the same extent. Take-Two’s notice says Leonida had more than 2,900 forks, which shows how quickly the code spread in the three days it was online.
This was not Take-Two’s only filing on GitHub this month. On 18 November, the day before GTA 6 launched, it filed four notices against unofficial ports of Grand Theft Auto V, including a project called glue5 and its 349 forks. Those projects were built around a WebAssembly version of GTA V, and Take-Two rejected their disclaimers about users supplying their own files in the same terms.
Rockstar’s second Grand Theft Auto VI trailer. Rockstar has not announced a PC version of the game. Video: Rockstar Games/YouTube
What the takedown means for the remaining PC ports
For players, the practical risk has not changed at all. Every PC build depends on files stolen from an Xbox Series version of the game, which is exactly what Take-Two’s notice targets. Anyone offering a download link is either distributing leaked material or, more often since Leonida disappeared, spreading malware disguised as a port. Rockstar’s policy on copyrighted material also explains why streams of leaked content can be taken down quickly.
The company’s response fits a pattern that began before launch. Take-Two chief executive Strauss Zelnick said the company expected the game to be pirated after release, and the leak gathered pace once modders claimed it was already booting on PC. Take-Two and Rockstar have not commented publicly on the ports beyond the notices, and the official GTA VI site still lists the game for PS5 and Xbox Series X and S only.
The post Take-Two Took Down 3,007 GTA 6 PC Port Repositories With One Notice, and Says the Xbox Build Was Stolen appeared first on TalkEsport.
