items.title: CS2’s Sticker Crisis Is a Warning That Esports Cannot Survive on Scraps From Publishers
items.content:
A single post on X has put words to something many people in Counter-Strike have suspected for months. Lobanjica, a well-followed community voice, wrote on 25 November that professional CS2 teams want to skip future Majors unless Valve changes how sticker money works. The reason given was simple: sticker income no longer covers the cost of travelling to the event. The post names no team, owner or source, and no organisation has confirmed it publicly. The fact that it sounds believable is the real story, and the numbers around this week’s PGL Major Singapore 2026 explain why.
NEW LEAK – CS2 Pro teams want to skip going to future Majors if Valve dont make a change to stickers.
Why?
Currently the sticker money does not even cover traveling expenses and its worth more qualifying but skipping.
Is this a W or L?
— Lobanjica (@LobanjicaCS) November 25, 2026
This is bigger than one game and one sales system. Esports was built on the promise that publishers would share enough of the money their games generate to keep teams, players and tournaments alive. When that share shrinks, the damage spreads quietly, from the smallest organisations upwards. Counter-Strike is now showing what that looks like in real time, and other publishers should pay close attention.
How Valve turned Major stickers from a lifeline into loose change
For years, Major stickers were the closest thing Counter-Strike had to a pension plan for teams. Fans bought capsules of team logos and player autographs, and Valve shared half of the proceeds with the tournament organiser, the teams and the players. A deep run at a Major could fund an organisation for a year, and even an early exit brought in enough money to justify the trip.
Valve tore that model up for IEM Cologne in June 2026. Its Cologne Major announcement replaced capsules with a Major Shop where fans bought any sticker directly with tokens, at prices set by demand. Royalties were also tiered by performance, so the organiser now takes 5 per cent of all Major Shop and Major Pass revenue, while the 32 team positions share 45 per cent between them. First place earns 2.85 per cent, last place 0.72 per cent, and every team’s share is split equally between the organisation and its five players.
The demand-based pricing system failed almost as soon as it launched. In a Ranked Series update on 29 July, Valve admitted that its dynamic system had not produced reasonable prices and released cheaper stickers to compensate. HLTV reported that a team knocked out in Stage 1 at the Budapest Major in December 2025 made about $600,000 from stickers, against roughly $120,000 for a comparable team at Cologne. Aurora owner Valery Kharitonov said on Telegram that Cologne was by far the worst Major he had seen for sticker sales, and the fall in sticker revenue seen in July has not reversed.
For Singapore, Valve has gone back to fixed prices, saying in its 17 November update that it had heard the feedback. The early signs from the first week are still grim. The community tracker cs2stickertracker estimated total sticker revenue for Valve and the teams at about $40,403 after eight days, based on stickers applied in game. That is an estimate rather than an official figure, but it would leave a bottom seed with roughly $291, of which about $145 belongs to the organisation.
Singapore 2026 Sticker analysis:Estimated total revenue for Valve/teams: $40,403
In total, there are:
• 10,472 Papers
• 2,282 Foils
• 4,119 Holos
• 47 Golds
However, most of the numbers come from 'The One':
• 5,916 Papers — 56.5%
• 1,100 Foils — 48.2%
• 2,172 Holos —… pic.twitter.com/4raJxcfsHH
— cs2stickertracker (@cs_2_sticker) November 25, 2026
No organisation has published what it costs to fly five players, a coach and staff to Singapore, house them for weeks and run a bootcamp first. Anyone who has booked a long-haul trip for a team knows it costs far more than a few hundred dollars. That gap explains why the Kansas City Pioneers owner, who posts as BignTallMatt, is holding back from entering CS. He said in July that sticker money no longer carries a smaller organisation’s climb to a Major.
I’ve been asked over and over, when will KCP get into CS? With the recent news and reports, here’s where my head is at least. Ever since the last sticker announcement, I’ve been worried and this news isn’t helping.
For a long time, the path into CS made sense for a team like…
— KCP – BignTallMatt (@BignTallMatt) July 20, 2026
The logic in the leaked post is that a team could secure its place, and with it a seeded sticker share, without spending heavily on the trip itself. Valve has not said what would happen to a team that qualified and then declined to travel, and the idea may never get beyond private grumbling. Under the open circuit, though, invites come from the Valve Regional Standings rather than franchise slots, so every organisation is running its own sums on whether a Major still pays.
The trade-up update that wiped billions off CS2 inventories
Stickers are only half of the problem, because Valve has also shaken the economy that sits underneath them. On 22 October 2025, a routine Counter-Strike 2 update extended trade-up contracts so that five Covert skins could be exchanged for a knife or a pair of gloves. Until then, knives and gloves were the rarest items in the game, reachable mainly through cases with tiny drop rates. Overnight, cheap red skins became raw material for the most expensive items in anyone’s inventory.
The market reacted the way any market reacts to a sudden supply shock. Pricempire, one of the main price trackers, posted the next day that the total CS2 market had fallen to $4.27 billion. Its revised series now puts the market at $10.07 billion on the day of the update and $6.66 billion four days later, a drop of more than a third in under a week. Knives lost between 40 and 50 per cent of their value in the first days, according to tracker data, while some gloves lost far more.
Current CS2 Market Cap: $4.27 billion pic.twitter.com/ot5sKUKtap
— Pricempire.com (@pricempire) October 23, 2025
A year on, there has been no reversal. Pricempire put the market at about $5.19 billion on 23 November 2026, below even the crash bottom of 2025. CSMarketCap, a second tracker, recovered to a record $8.71 billion in March 2026 before sliding to about $4.76 billion this week, which is also below its post-crash low. Whatever Valve intended, the result has been a year of lost confidence in items that many players treated as savings. The viral story of a woman trying to cash out her boyfriend’s CS2 skins this week showed how normal that idea has become.
Calling the trade-up change controversial is generous, and calling it lazy would not be unfair. Valve may well have wanted to cool an item economy that had grown into a multibillion-dollar asset market. It chose to do that by flooding supply at the top of the market without warning, which punished the collectors who had trusted its scarcity for a decade. Valve still collects a 10 per cent Counter-Strike 2 fee on every Community Market sale, on top of Steam’s 5 per cent transaction fee, so it earns on the churn whichever way prices move.
The same rules push the most valuable trades away from Valve’s own storefront. Steam caps any single Community Market listing at about $1,800, so knives and gloves worth more than that change hands on third-party sites, where Valve’s own protections do not apply. A change that cut the value of those items hit the traders and collectors who held them hardest, while the cheap Covert skins used as inputs briefly spiked. Ordinary players, many of whom treat an inventory as a small savings account, were left holding items worth far less than they had paid.
The two issues meet at the Major Shop. Stickers sell when players feel confident spending money on cosmetic items, and a year of falling inventory values does not build that confidence. Tournaments cannot lean on the skin economy for sponsorship either, because Valve’s tournament licence bars organisers from taking sponsors whose revenue relies on Valve’s game economies. The economy that pays for Counter-Strike’s biggest events is one that only Valve can monetise, and Valve keeps cutting the share it passes on.
If publishers keep trimming the cut, the whole esports economy breaks
The frustrating part is that a working model already exists in the same industry. Riot Games shared $105.2 million with VCT partner teams in 2025, more than $86 million of it from digital goods, according to its season wrap-up in December. That approach has its own critics and its own pressure points, but the record VCT revenue share proved that item sales can carry teams when a publisher treats them as partners.
Even Riot is tightening the terms around that money. Its plan for VCT 2027, published in June, ends guaranteed paths for partner teams beyond Kickoff, so they must keep earning their places in later Cups. In League of Legends, Riot removed regional split prize pools in its Global Revenue Pool regions for 2026, saying the money would go elsewhere. Activision Blizzard’s Overwatch League did not survive at all, ending in 2023 after its teams voted to take a termination payment instead of continuing.
Outside the publishers, the largest pots of money now come from state-backed events. The Esports World Cup offers a $75 million prize pool in 2026, including $30 million for its Club Championship, while the Singapore Major pays out $1.25 million across 32 teams. That money is welcome, but it is concentrated, conditional and controlled by one funder, which is not the same thing as a healthy ecosystem built on a game’s own revenue.
The Esports World Cup Foundation has also become a direct paymaster for teams. Its third Club Partner Program, announced in March, splits $20 million between 40 clubs, with up to $1 million each, and the foundation says more than $100 million has gone directly to clubs over three years. Next to the sticker estimates coming out of Singapore, a cheque of up to $1 million is a different order of magnitude. It also comes with conditions set by a single funder rather than by the games teams compete in.
The cost of getting this wrong is already visible. Evil Geniuses ceased competitive and day-to-day operations on 2 November 2026, and chief executive Chris DeAppolonio blamed “limited sponsorship and the rising cost of competing at the top level”. Complexity had already left Counter-Strike after 22 years, citing financial pressure. A FlyQuest executive warned on The Four Horsemen podcast in October that most organisations can survive one bad Major, but several in a row would cause serious problems.
pic.twitter.com/cInzqC4zvx
— Evil Geniuses (@EvilGeniuses) October 20, 2026
The cycle is easy to describe and hard to stop once it starts. When organisations leave, the scene loses the brands and storylines that bring casual viewers in, and fewer viewers mean weaker sponsorship and fewer sticker buyers. Weaker sales then push more organisations towards the exit, until the publisher is left with a premium event that nobody can afford to attend. If teams really do skip Majors, Valve loses the very product that sells its stickers, its viewer passes and its souvenirs.
PGL’s official trailer for the PGL Major Singapore 2026. Video: PGL/YouTube
None of this needs a radical or expensive fix. Valve could guarantee every qualified team a minimum royalty or a travel allowance, publish total sticker revenue after each Major, and give fans a sales window long enough to matter. Riot, Valve and every other publisher with an esports scene could also accept a simple principle, which is that the teams carrying their events need a predictable share of what those events sell. Valve already asks this of others in its own licence. Organisers that share revenue with players must do so equally or by an objective measure, one of the 2025 tournament rules brought in for the open circuit.
Until something changes, every Major will be judged by the same uncomfortable question that Lobanjica’s post raised. Is it still worth qualifying if the trip costs more than the reward? The Singapore Major began its opening stage on 24 November, and its playoffs run at the Singapore Indoor Stadium from 10 to 13 December.
The post CS2’s Sticker Crisis Is a Warning That Esports Cannot Survive on Scraps From Publishers appeared first on TalkEsport.

KRAFTON India Opens BGMI Transfer Window: Check Dates Inside
items.content:
KRAFTON India has opened the BGMI player transfer window, which runs from 26 November to 26 December 2026. For these 30 days, registered esports clubs can sign, release and trade players, and every roster move has to be finished before the window closes. This is the third transfer window since KRAFTON India introduced the system in October 2025.
The window is opening later than first planned. At BMIC 2026, Karan Pathak, KRAFTON India’s Associate Director of Esports, told TalkEsport the window would open on 15 November and would probably close on 20 December. The new dates move the opening back by 11 days and the closing by six.
BGMI transfer window dates
Opens: 26 November 2026
Closes: 26 December 2026
Duration: 30 days
How the BGMI transfer window works
The transfer window is a set period when verified clubs can make official changes to their rosters. Every registered club is run by a verified owner or in-game leader, who signs off on player movement for that club. KRAFTON India reviews each transfer to keep the process fair and within the rules.
Free agents, meaning players who aren’t attached to any club, can join a team whenever they like. Players under contract with a registered club can only move while a window is open. KRAFTON India laid out these rules when it introduced the Player Transfer Window for BGMI esports. Its official transfer window announcement gives the first window’s dates as 1 October to 15 November 2025.
Why this window matters for BGMI teams
For Indian BGMI teams, this is the biggest roster reshuffle of the year. It follows a packed season that included the Battlegrounds Mobile India Showdown (BMSD) 2026 and the BGMI International Cup (BMIC) 2026. Teams that dropped in the KIE rankings after BMIC 2026 now have a month to rebuild before the next season starts.
There has been a lot of roster talk in recent weeks. Several teams and players have spoken openly about exits and poaching. One of them is Aadi, who alleged poaching while explaining why he targeted Team SouL in BMSD 2026. Any deals agreed in that time can only become official now that the window is open.
Earlier BGMI transfer windows
The first window opened on 1 October 2025 and was meant to close on 15 November 2025. KRAFTON India later extended the deadline to 30 November 2025 for teams in BMPS 2025, BMSD 2025 and BMIC 2025. The second window opened on 1 April 2026, after the BGIS 2026 Grand Finals in Chennai and before the Battlegrounds Mobile Pro Series (BMPS) 2026.

items.title: Nvidia Halts Server Shipments to Four Southeast Asian Countries After New US Chip Rule
items.content:
Nvidia has told its manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers built with its chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, the Financial Times reported on 26 November, citing three people familiar with the matter. Partners that package Nvidia’s AI chips into servers, including Dell and Supermicro, have told buyers in those four countries that Nvidia will not allow their orders to ship. The report said it was unclear whether the halt is temporary, as Nvidia and its partners work through new US export rules that took effect last week.
Nvidia, Dell and Supermicro did not immediately respond to requests for comment from Reuters, which carried the FT’s report, and none of the three had commented publicly by the time of writing. The move lands only days after Jensen Huang returned to the top job, after Nvidia reinstated Huang as CEO. It also follows a fortnight in which the company’s links to Southeast Asian data centres have come under heavy scrutiny in Washington.
FT Exclusive: The chipmaker has told its manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers to four south-east Asian countries, as the US steps up export controls to prevent Chinese access to AI computing power. https://t.co/q9hoD57lL2 pic.twitter.com/RaFm5K4cWe
— Financial Times (@FT) November 26, 2026
What the new US export rule requires
The Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security released the rule on 16 November, calling it a measure to stop restricted buyers from reaching American chips through remote computing arrangements, including data centres in third countries. It was published in the Federal Register as Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors on 19 November and took effect the same day. Exporters now need a licence to send advanced computing items, including Nvidia’s top data centre GPUs, to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil.
There is an exclusion when the buyer is headquartered in the United States, but exporters who use it must file monthly reports, with the first due on 1 December. A second control covers data centres anywhere that provide more than 12 million units of total processing performance to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other countries in US Country Group D:5. Data centres already supplying that much compute to such customers must obtain a licence within 90 days of the rule taking effect, which points to mid-February 2027.
The rule also formally removes the Biden-era AI Diffusion framework, which the government says was never enforced. The Semiconductor Industry Association said it was still assessing the change, welcomed the end of the diffusion rule and described the new approach as more targeted in its statement on the rule. Public comments are open until 19 January 2027.
Why Southeast Asia’s data centres are in the firing line
Washington’s concern is that Chinese AI developers have been renting the computing power they cannot legally import. Data centres in the region can buy Nvidia hardware and then sell remote access to it, which earlier export controls on physical shipments did not fully cover. The Commerce and Justice departments have confirmed a criminal investigation into Singapore-based Megaspeed, as our report on the US statement on Megaspeed explains. Lawmakers had already pushed for tighter curbs after a report that the company arranged $12 billion in chips for China.
The money at stake is already visible in the region’s financing deals. Bloomberg reported on 18 November that five banks led by DBS had frozen work on a $480 million loan for Aolani Cloud, a Singapore-based provider. The loan was meant to buy Nvidia chips for a Malaysian data centre that ByteDance planned to use remotely. DBS declined to comment, and Aolani said it was working with regulators and lenders to keep the project compliant. Posts on X summarising the story have described this as a $500 million Singapore deal, but the reporting puts it at $480 million for a project in Malaysia.
Singapore has said it is studying the measure closely and engaging with both the affected companies and US authorities. Josephine Teo, the Minister for Digital Development and Information, said on 17 November that the government wants legitimate businesses to keep trusted access to critical AI infrastructure. Singapore’s ministries have also said the country does not condone companies using it to get around other nations’ laws.
What Nvidia’s Singapore revenue figure really shows
One number spreading alongside the news needs correcting. Posts claim that Nvidia’s Singapore subsidiary drove $104 billion of revenue in 2025, but no Nvidia filing shows that figure. Nvidia’s annual report for the year to 26 January 2025 put revenue billed to customers in Singapore at $23.7 billion, or 18 per cent of its $130.5 billion total.
The same filing explains why that figure is misleading on its own. Nvidia said customers use Singapore to centralise invoicing while its products are almost always shipped elsewhere, and that shipments to Singapore were less than 2 per cent of revenue that year. The city state matters to Nvidia as a billing and data centre hub, but the hardware it pays for mostly sits in other countries.
Nvidia is not short of demand elsewhere, having reported record quarterly revenue of $68.1 billion for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. The open questions are how long the pause on server shipments lasts and how quickly licences are granted. The board set up a new national security committee last week, and existing data centre arrangements covered by the rule must be licensed within 90 days of 19 November.

items.content:
Most idle games ask you to tap a few times and then leave. Keeper Wanted: Idle Defense, the new pixel-art tower defense game from South Korean solo developer Boreumdal (FullMoon), starts with a job offer instead. A strange ad promises $10,000,000 to whoever keeps a remote lighthouse burning for 1,000 days, and the only condition is that the light must never go out at night. The game launched on Google Play on 24 November and on the App Store a day later, and it is free on both.
It is the second release from Boreumdal, whose previous game was the ink-styled action title Ink Parry: Seonbi Swordsman. This time, however, the developer has moved from tight duels to a slower, more relaxed genre, while keeping enough hands-on action that it never plays itself entirely.
The official Keeper Wanted: Idle Defense trailer. Video: Boreumdal (FullMoon).
A Harpoon, a Lighthouse and a Very Suspicious Job Ad
The story opens as a webtoon, with the hero finding the advert in a tiny rooftop room and taking the contract almost on a whim. From there, the core loop is simple to pick up. You tap the sea to throw a harpoon, hold to reel a monster in, and then smash it against the rocks below the lighthouse. From day three, harpoon guns mounted on the tower join the fight on their own, so gold keeps piling up even while the game is closed, which is the idle half of the design.
The clever part is how the game handles failure. When a run stalls, you deliberately put out the light, keep the pearls you have earned and sign the contract again, stronger than before. In other words, the one rule the job ad warns you never to break is also the game’s prestige system, and it turns the usual idle-game reset into part of the story rather than a menu option.
From day three, harpoon guns on the lighthouse fight on their own. Image: Boreumdal (FullMoon).
Every Sea Monster Needs Its Own Trick
Rather than throwing the same enemy at you in larger numbers, Keeper Wanted gives each monster a rule of its own. Sharks cannot be hit while only their fin shows above the water, so timing matters. Drowned hands drag back whatever you are reeling in, while puffers bounce the harpoon away whenever they inflate. As a result, even the active part of the game asks you to read the sea before you throw.
On set nights, a giant boss rises from the water for a tug of war. Bosses fly into a rage once they fall below half health, and players answer with three special abilities: Flash, Net and Harpoon Rain. Meanwhile, the setting changes with the seasons, moving from autumn moonlight to winter aurora, foggy spring and red summer storms, with the monsters and music shifting alongside them over the 1,000 nights.
That variety matters more than it might seem, because the biggest weakness of idle tower defense games is that the active part usually stops mattering once upgrades take over. By tying each enemy type to a specific counter, Keeper Wanted keeps a reason to pick the phone up and play properly, even deep into a contract when the automated harpoon guns are doing most of the work.
Every sea monster needs its own trick. Image: Boreumdal (FullMoon).
Free, Fully Offline and No Paid Loot Boxes
The business model is where Keeper Wanted stands apart from much of its genre. The game is free, ads only play when you choose to watch one for a reward, and there are no paid loot boxes, although optional in-app purchases are available. That is a notable choice in South Korea, where probability disclosure for paid random items became a legal requirement in 2024 under rules overseen by the Game Rating and Administration Committee, and it sits alongside the country’s broader push to support smaller studios, including the proposed tax credit for game development.
It is also fully playable without an internet connection, which suits a game built around checking in on a lighthouse between other things. Keeper Wanted supports English, Korean, Japanese, Traditional Chinese, German, French, Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese, a wide spread for a one-person studio. While Korea’s big productions have dominated recent headlines, with Crimson Desert sweeping the 2026 Korea Game Awards, releases like this show how much of the country’s scene still comes from individual developers.
For players who enjoy planning their defences in games like Clash of Clans, where our best CoC base layouts remain a popular read, Keeper Wanted offers a lighter, story-driven take on holding the line. Screenshots, key art and trailers in eight languages, including a Korean-language trailer, are available in the developer’s press kit, and more details are on the official Keeper Wanted website.

items.title: Fuwarium Turns Your iPhone and Apple Watch Into a Glowing Aquarium Where Pets Take 30 Real Days to Grow
items.content:
Tokyo studio Code and DESIGN has released Fuwarium, a virtual pet game in which you raise glowing pixel creatures inside a tiny aquarium and pass their looks on to the next generation. It launched on the App Store on 25 November for iPhone and Apple Watch at $4.99 as a one-time purchase, with no in-app purchases and no account to create.
Virtual pets have been around since the pocket-sized keychains of the 1990s, and the formula has rarely changed much since then. Fuwarium, however, makes a few interesting choices that set it apart, particularly in how it shows a creature’s needs and how it brings Apple Watch into the routine rather than treating it as an afterthought.
No Stats, No Gauges, Just a Creature You Learn to Read
Everything starts with a single egg floating in the aquarium. You tap it gently to keep it warm until it hatches into a small glowing creature, and then you give it a name. From there, the care is familiar: you drop in meals, play chase with a ball of light and turn off the aquarium light when it falls asleep.
What is different is the absence of numbers. Fuwarium shows no stats or gauges at all, so a hungry creature’s glow simply fades, while a sleepy one closes its eyes. Personalities come through in movement too, since a curious creature might follow your finger and a shy one prefers a quiet corner. As a result, looking after one feels more like watching a real pet than managing a set of meters, which is a refreshing change in a genre built on bars that need refilling.
Eggs inherit colours and body shapes from both parents. Image: Code and DESIGN.
Thirty Real Days and Nine Lineages Worth Breeding
Patience is built into the design. A hatchling takes 30 real days to grow into an adult, and it keeps growing while the app is closed, with its pale colours slowly deepening along the way. The aquarium can be split into up to six rooms, so you decide which creatures live together, and every so often a stray egg drifts in on its own.
The game features nine creature lineages, and breeding is where it gets its long tail. Two well-cared-for adults in the same room may leave an egg whose colours and body shape show traits from both parents. Moreover, if you bring two iPhones together, you can pair your adult with a nearby friend’s creature, and each of you takes home an egg from the same two parents. The pairing happens directly between the two devices, so there are no servers, friend codes or online accounts involved.
That local-only approach has trade-offs, since you can only breed with friends who are physically nearby. However, it also gives the game a social side that feels closer to swapping creatures in a playground than trading on a server, and it means there is nothing to shut down if the studio ever moves on. For a premium game built to last 30 days per creature and beyond, that is a sensible choice.
Bring two iPhones together to breed with a friend's creature. Image: Code and DESIGN.
A $4.99 Pet That Lives on Your Wrist
The Apple Watch version is more than a notification mirror. From the watch you can pet your creature, feed it, give it medicine, clean the aquarium and turn the lights off, and when a care notification arrives you can respond straight from it. Once you have more than one creature, turning the Digital Crown lets you choose which one to visit. Given how few games make real use of the Apple Watch, a pet that genuinely lives on the wrist is a natural fit, and arguably a better home for the genre than a phone.
The pricing is just as deliberate. Like the $2.99 indie game Punch The Walls, Fuwarium asks for a small one-time payment rather than relying on in-app purchases, which is increasingly rare on mobile. It requires iOS 17 or later and watchOS 10 or later, carries a 4+ age rating and supports English, Japanese, Korean, and Simplified and Traditional Chinese.
Code and DESIGN, based in Nakameguro, Tokyo, builds its own apps and games alongside client work, and Fuwarium is one of its own products. It also arrives in a crowded end of year, as our guide to upcoming game release dates for 2026 shows, and just as The Game Awards 2026 nominees dominate the conversation. Screenshots, key art and the App Store preview videos are in the studio’s Fuwarium press kit, and the Japanese official site has more on the game.

items.title: 10 Classic Books Worth Reading Over and Over
items.content: Most of us treat classic literature like a checklist to conquer in high school or college and then never touch those books again. You power through the plot, underline a few quotes for a term paper, and move on to whatever else is new. The catch is that great books rarely reveal their most fascinating tricks on the first pass. When you already know the ending, your brain stops racing for answers and begins to notice the machinery holding all those mysteries and themes together. Suddenly, an unreliable narrator's sleight of hand becomes obvious, or a throwaway line in chapter two hits like a freight train in light of later developments.

items.title: 6 Fantasy Books Better Than Harry Potter
items.content: There's no denying that Harry Potter continues to be a phenomenon. After seven bestsellers translated into multiple languages, years of extravagant midnight release parties, eight big-budget films, a stage play, and theme parks, there's still enormous hype for both the upcoming HBO television show and an all-star re-recording of the audiobooks. Clearly, there is something about the boy who lived and his world that draws people in and keeps them captivated. All of this begs one very important question, however: how good are the Harry Potter books, really?

items.title: How to get the legendary Couch Potato Mustang .357 revolver in GTA 6
items.content:
Legendary weapons are scattered all around the map of Leonida in Grand Theft Auto 6. From silenced assault rifles to shotguns that pack a serious punch, you can immediately upgrade Jason and Lucia’s loadout with just a single one of these weapons. However, longarm weapons, like shotguns and rifles, are a bit more difficult to work with in GTA 6, as they’re not on your character at all times.
So, if you want to make use of your weapons more, you want to go with a sidearm, like a pistol. Fortunately, one of the best pistols in GTA 6 is just waiting for you fairly early on. The pistol is called the Couch Potato Mustang .357, and here’s how to get it.
Key Takeaways
The Couch Potato Mustang .357 is a legendary revolver in GTA 6
You can find the weapon by searching a very specific location in Kelly County
The weapon can be acquired right from the start of GTA 6
Table of contents
Key Takeaways
Couch Potato Mustang .357 location in GTA 6
Couch Potato Mustang .357 location in GTA 6
Technically, the Couch Potato Mustang .357 is a weapon that you can acquire after the tutorial phase in GTA 6 has concluded. However, it’s a bit of a drive from Key Lento, so you might want to wait until Chapter 2.
Chapter 2 takes you to Kelly County, which is where the legendary revolver is located. This makes obtaining the gun a lot easier and quicker, but you can also head there whenever you feel like it.
To add the Couch Potato Mustang .357 revolver to your loadout, just follow these steps in GTA 6:
Go to the trailer park located in Port Gellhorn, which is found in the western part of Kelly County, near the coast
Specifically, if you’ve made it to Chapter 2, you need to head to Dunk’s Trailer, which is a key location for the main story
If you’re not in Chapter 2 yet, you can see the location of Dunk’s Trailer in the screenshot below:
Dunk’s Trailer’s location in GTA 6. Screenshot by esports.gg
At the trailer, turn around, and you’ll see a couch hanging from a rope on a tree across the street
Take out a gun, aim at where the rope is tied to the tree, and shoot at it
This should make the hanging couch fall to the ground, and from here, you can go up to it and choose to “Sit”
Doing so will cause Jason or Lucia to go through the couch and find the legendary Couch Potato Mustang .357 revolver
This gun is automatically added to your loadout, but you can swap it out for something else by going to your car’s trunk or a gun locker at an Ammu-Nation store
And that’s all there is to acquiring the Couch Potato Mustang .357 revolver in GTA 6. In terms of difficulty, it’s easily one of the easier legendary guns to find, but it more than holds its own during gunfights.
For more GTA 6, check out our guides on the Investigate the Photos mission as well as how to get Lucia into a bikini.

GTA 6 Hyde Island Saw mission: Complete guide with screen shots
items.content:
Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6) features a not-so-subtle Easter egg for the beloved horror franchise ‘Saw.’ After you reach Hyde Island, a hunter will capture you and put you in a deadly game where you can only survive by becoming the hunter.
This guide explains everything you need to know about this side mission, including how to kill the hunter, get his sniper, and receive $20,000.
Key takeaways
You can experience the Saw mission in GTA 6 on Hyde Island
A hunter will capture you once you reach the island and try to kill you
You can scavenge the outposts in the immediate area for guns and ammo
Your goal is to neutralize the hunter, at which point you will receive your belongings and a cash prize
Table of contents
Key takeaways
Head to Hyde Island and walk ashore
Listen to the instructions from the hunter
Navigate to outposts and build your loadout
Fire upon the hunter until he dies
What happens at the end?
What is the Saw Easter egg?
Head to Hyde Island and walk ashore
Hyde Island location (Image via esports.gg)
First, head to Hyde Island, located on the northern portion of the GTA 6 map. There’s a dock south of the island where you can steal a boat or seaplane and head over there. Note that you cannot trigger this Easter egg with both Lucia and Jason together.
We tried, but it only triggered once we parted ways with Lucia and went to the island as Jason alone. A few seconds after you walk on Hyde Island, you will take a tranquilizer dart to the neck and pass out.
Listen to the instructions from the hunter
The Saw Easter egg happens here, where you will then wake up in a shipping container with a collar around your neck and a TV screen in front of you. The hunter explains what’s happening on the island along with his societal frustrations.
Navigate to outposts and build your loadout
Your goal is not only to survive this hunt, but also to become the hunter and neutralize the hunter’s attack dog and the hunter himself. Here’s how this all works
An outpost on Hyde Island in GTA 6 (Image via esports.gg)
You must scavenge for a pistol and/or shotgun, ammo, and adrenaline shots
A pistol is available in front of the container once you exit
We found a shotgun at an outpost with a single orange container atop the stairs
You must evade the hunter and his dog until you build a loadout
Once you have gathered ammo, you can go on the offensive
Fire upon the hunter until he dies
We tried a few times and had trouble at first. It wasn’t immediately clear whether you could even kill the hunter using bullets since he’s wearing body armor. We also tried fighting him hand-to-hand, but that didn’t work.
You will want to keep your distance and remain elusive as he carries a high-powered sniper rifle that deals serious damage. The shotgun is the way to go, as once we grabbed it, we stunned him with three shots and were able to kill him with relative ease.
What happens at the end?
The boathouse (Image via esports.gg)
Once you’ve survived the Hyde Island hunt in GTA 6, you can loot the hunter’s body and even grab the Island Poacher FF-50 Sniper he uses. A voice will come over the intercom and congratulate you on winning, then direct you to a boathouse to claim your belongings and the cash prize.
You will receive all your belongings and $20,000 as your reward for eliminating the hunter on Hyde Island.
What is the Saw Easter egg?
Shotgun collar from Saw III (Image via Lionsgate)
The Saw Easter egg in GTA 6 is really the whole concept of the Hyde Island mission. It forces you into a game of cat-and-mouse where you must gather resources to survive. This entire setup is Saw-inspired, right down to the collar and the hunter appearing on a tube TV to explain the instructions.
It’s also similar to films such as The Hunger Games, The Purge, Squid Game, and The Hunt. Overall, it’s yet another unique experience that GTA 6 has in abundance.

Season 1 of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 was released over three weeks ago, and it doesn’t look like Season 2 is arriving before 2027 gets here. So, the next major update for Modern Warfare 4 is Season 1 Reloaded, which is confirmed to be releasing sometime in December 2026.
Of course, between the holidays and the ongoing popularity of Grand Theft Auto 6, there’s not much time for Activision to launch Season 1 Reloaded. While Activision hasn’t confirmed any dates just yet, we do have a solid idea of when Season 1 Reloaded is coming to MW4 and Warzone. Season 1 Reloaded is the next major update in Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone

As we mentioned before, there’s currently no concrete release date for Season 1 Reloaded in MW4. However, based on when we expect Season 2 and how much time has passed since Season 1 was originally released, we have a good idea of when the update is expected to drop.

The Kastov 762 is a hard-hitting assault rifle that can deal some serious damage in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, but it’s not the best when you start out with it. Fortunately, you can use some key attachments on the Kastov 762 to make its loadout one of the best in its class in Modern Warfare 4. While it doesn’t offer the same easy-to-use nature as some of the other ARs, such as the M4, with the right loadout, the Kastov 762 can compete with any other weapon in multiplayer.
Below, you can see the strongest loadout of attachments for the Kastov 762 in MW4.
Key Takeaways
The Kastov 762 is one of the most powerful assault rifles in Modern Warfare 4
A recoil control loadout makes the Kastov 762 much easier to control at longer ranges.

The Kastov 762 is a heavy and powerful assault rifle that can shred enemies when you land your shots. However, by default, the AR has some shaky recoil control, so you need to increase accuracy above anything else.
Here’s our recommended loadout for the Kastov 762:
Muzzle: Gauge-12 Mono
Barrel: FJX Ghostfire 16.3″
Underbarrel: FSS Fireline Grip

For this Kastov 762 loadout, we’re focusing on bringing down the AR’s recoil control while also keeping its other stats high. The combination of the muzzle, underbarrel, and stock helps improve the weapon’s overall accuracy, which makes the Kastov 762 much more competitive with the other ARs in MW4, such as the Patriot XMR.
However, we also have the FJX Ghostfire 16.3″ barrel to improve damage range and the Schlager Visiv-5 laser to boost the Kastov 762’s mobility for any close-range gunfights.
This loadout also doesn’t use an optic, but if you don’t like the Kastov’s iron sights, we recommend swapping the laser for the Slimline Elite optic.

items.title: How to collect the Dynamic Op Phone in MW4 DMZ
items.content:
DMZ Order missions are some of the best ways to spend your time in the DMZ in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, but they can be tricky to complete. One of the more confusing missions for players so far in DMZ is to “collect a Dynamic Op Phone” in Cheongun Village, which sounds easy enough but can be difficult if you don’t know what you’re doing.
Fortunately, while the mission might be puzzling to start, it only takes a few minutes to complete it in MW4 DMZ. To see how to collect a Dynamic Op Phone in Cheongun Village, keep reading the guide below.
Key Takeaways
The DMZ Order mission to collect the Dynamic Op Phone only takes a few minutes in DMZ.
You don’t need to complete any specific Dynamic Op to earn a completion for this mission.
You have to travel to Cheongun Village, which is in the northern part of the Hajin map.
Table of contents
Key Takeaways
Dynamic Op Phone location in Cheongun Village in MW4 DMZ
Dynamic Op Phone location in Cheongun Village in MW4 DMZ
Unlike many of the other DMZ Order missions in DMZ, the Dynamic Op Phone doesn’t actually require you to complete a specific mission. Instead, all you really need to do is just head to Cheongun Village and find one of the green phone icons labeled on your Tac-Map.
The green phone icons indicate a Dynamic Ops mission that can be started. Fortunately, to complete the “collect a Dynamic Op Phone in Cheongun Village,” all you have to do is just find one of these icons. Follow these steps to complete the mission:
One of the green phone icons in Cheongun Village in DMZ. Screenshot by esports.gg
Head to Cheongun Village, which you can find in the northern part of Hajin
Here, open your Tac-Map and find one of the green phone icons. Any of the mission types work, as long as it’s a green phone icon
Go to the icon’s location and start the Dynamic Ops mission by interacting with the beeping phone
This will complete the “collect a Dynamic Op Phone” mission in DMZ
You don’t need to complete the Dynamic Op if you don’t want to, as you can just exfil and move on to the next DMZ Order

items.title: Radeon RX 9060 XT sets new GPU frequency world record at 4.8GHz
items.content:
A Radeon RX 9060 XT has become the first graphics card to break the 4.8GHz barrier, setting a new GPU frequency world record in the process. The record was achieved during an extreme overclocking session held at the recently opened Micro Center store in Austin, Texas.
As reported by VideoCardz, AMD's Senior Vice President and General Manager of Computing and Graphics, Jack Huynh, revealed that the record-setting run was carried out alongside veteran overclocker Bill Alverson. Using liquid nitrogen cooling, the team pushed a Radeon RX 9060 XT to a clock speed of 4,837MHz, surpassing the previous world record of 4,789MHz.
Image credit: Skatterbencher
Like most extreme overclocking records, the result was achieved using liquid nitrogen cooling rather than conventional air or water cooling. GPU-Z screenshots shared by Skatterbencher show the RX 9060 XT reaching 4,837MHz, 54.5% above AMD's reference 3,130MHz boost clock.
The Radeon RX 9060 XT is no stranger to frequency records. Earlier this year, overclockers pushed the card to 4,789MHz, while previous demonstrations from AMD had already shown the Navi 44 GPU operating well beyond 4.7GHz under extreme cooling. This latest run is the first to break through the 4,800MHz barrier, leaving AMD just 163MHz shy of the 5GHz milestone.

Zowie brings 8000Hz wireless and a display-equipped receiver to its esports mouse lineup
items.content:
Zowie has refreshed its wireless esports mouse lineup with a new range of EW Version models. While the company is sticking with its familiar competitive-focused shapes, the headline upgrades come in the form of 8000Hz wireless polling and a new receiver that allows players to adjust settings without installing additional software.
The new range spans six mice across Zowie's established EC, FK, ZA and U2 families, including the EC1-EW, EC2-EW, EC3-EW, FK2-EW, ZA13-EW and U2-EW. Alongside the hardware upgrades, each model incorporates Zowie's Rhythm Click design, which is intended to deliver a more consistent click feel, alongside a matte Dry-Touch coating designed to reduce fingerprints and improve grip.
The biggest change is the upgraded Enhanced Receiver. The device doubles as both a charging dock and a built-in control hub, allowing users to adjust DPI, polling rates up to 8000Hz and lift-off distance directly from the receiver itself. In a peripheral market increasingly reliant on companion software, Zowie is continuing its long-standing philosophy of keeping configuration as straightforward as possible.
The new lineup also includes Zowie's Auto Game Mode feature, which can automatically detect supported games and apply matching presets through the company's Setting to Share software.
All six EW Version mice carry an MSRP of €169.99. In Europe, the U2-EW, FK2-EW and EC1-EW are scheduled to arrive in early December, with the EC2-EW, EC3-EW and ZA13-EW following at a later date.

items.title: PlayStation Plus Free Games For December 2026 Revealed
Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2, Tony Hawk and Amnesia will be free on PS+ next month
items.content:
Each month, Sony refreshes its PlayStation Plus Essential line-up with three new games for subscribers to add to their libraries. For the final month of 2026, PS Plus members will be able to claim Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3+4, Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 and Amnesia: The Bunker.
Available to claim from the 1st of December through to the 4th of January, all PlayStation Plus subscribers will be able to add the following games to their libraries:
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3+4
Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2
Amnesia: The Bunker
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3+4 continued Activision's remake efforts following the success of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 1+2. The collection brings together Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3 and 4, rebuilding classic levels with modern visuals while expanding the Create-A-Skater and Create-A-Park modes with new sharing features.
Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 meanwhile remains one of Bandai Namco's most successful anime games. Despite launching a decade ago, the game has continued to receive support thanks to its character customisation systems, story content and online multiplayer modes. While getting the base game through PlayStation Plus is a nice bonus, prospective players should be aware that Xenoverse 2 has accumulated a huge amount of paid DLC over the years. As a result, those jumping in through PS Plus will be getting just a fraction of the game's total content.
Rounding out the month is Amnesia: The Bunker, Frictional Games' World War I survival horror title. Rather than relying on scripted scares, the game drops players into a World War I bunker with a persistent threat stalking them throughout the campaign, creating a far more dynamic horror experience than previous entries in the series.
In case you missed them, PlayStation Plus subscribers have until 30th November to claim November's titles, including Dead Island 2, Tomb Raider IV-VI Remastered and Monster Train 2.

Exoprimal, Capcom's Dinosaur Hero Shooter, Will Go Offline And Become Unplayable Next Year
Capcom’s Exoprimal is shutting down, and the game will become completely unplayable
items.content:
Capcom has announced plans to shut down Exoprimal in 2027, bringing an end to support for the dinosaur-themed co-op shooter. Unfortunately for those who purchased the game, the shutdown won't simply disable online matchmaking. Once Capcom's servers go offline, Exoprimal will no longer be playable at all.
In a message posted to the game's official website, Capcom confirmed that Exoprimal's end of service date is set for 29th September 2027. Just prior to this announcement, Capcom also ended the ability to purchase the game's “premium Survival Pass”, Exoprimal's battle pass equivalent for earning new cosmetics. Exoprimal and all of its DLC will also be removed from sale in March 2027, a few months ahead of the servers going offline.
When Exoprimal launched in 2023, many players immediately drew comparisons to Capcom's dormant Dino Crisis series due to its heavy focus on dinosaurs. Rather than reviving that franchise, Capcom instead built an entirely new live-service multiplayer IP around co-op PvE combat, seasonal content and online progression systems.
The shutdown announcement brings us back to an increasingly common issue across the modern games industry. Unlike older multiplayer titles that can continue through community-run servers, peer-to-peer connections or offline modes, Exoprimal (and other ‘live service' games) requires an active online connection to function. Capcom has confirmed that once service ends in September 2027, the game will no longer be playable, even for players who already own it.
This wasn't a massive shared online world or MMO-style experience. Much of Exoprimal revolved around cooperative missions and PvE encounters that, at least in theory, could have continued long after official support ended. Instead, Exoprimal joins a growing list of games that effectively disappear once publisher support comes to an end. It's a topic that has become increasingly contentious in recent years, as more players question why games they paid for should stop functioning once developers move on to new projects.

items.title: Rockstar begins taking down unofficial GTA 6 PC port efforts on GitHub and Discord
items.content:
Grand Theft Auto VI has only been available on consoles for a week, but efforts to build an unofficial PC port are already well underway. Unsurprisingly, Take-Two is also being very proactive in taking down GitHub repositories and Discord servers trying to organise development efforts.
CyberLeek has been a thorn in Rockstar's side all year, leaking a bunch of gameplay footage over the Summer and demonstrating clear access to a full working build of the game. They returned last week to drop the .exe file from the Xbox version of the game, thus opening the floodgates for unofficial PC porting and emulation efforts.
DMCA notices began targeting GitHub repositories associated with the projects, while Discord communities organising reverse-engineering efforts also found themselves being shut down due to legal notices served by Take-Two's legal team, as reported by PCGamer. That doesn't necessarily mean the work has stopped, however. Some groups are still sharing updates on their efforts on social media, with some clips showing the game actually running, albeit at unplayable frame rates.
Much of this could be avoided if Rockstar was willing to discuss its plans for PC support, but for now, the focus is entirely on the console versions of the game. Many fans likely wouldn't bother with an unofficial port at all if they had a timeline for official PC availability. Even if an unofficial port eventually emerges, an official release would almost certainly offer a far more complete experience, with proper optimisation, full feature support and continued post-launch updates.

Can you get rid of your Ultimate Edition bonus cars in GTA 6?
items.content:
The Ultimate Edition of Grand Theft Auto 6 proved to be the most popular edition of the record-breaking game, even though it costs $100 compared to the base $80. Many players simply couldn’t pass up on all of the content being offered with the Ultimate Edition in GTA 6, which is a long list.
However, while some of the Ultimate Edition content is nice, players are finding that other parts of it can be a nuisance. Specifically, the cars that come with the edition can easily be surpassed by other vehicles in GTA 6. Unfortunately, players are discovering that Ultimate Edition cars can’t be sold or unregistered, so what do you do with them once they’ve been claimed?
Key Takeaways
The Ultimate Edition of Grand Theft Auto 6 offers a slew of content, including several cars for players to redeem
These bonus cars are nice, but can often be surpassed by other vehicles in GTA 6, such as the Pink Porsche
Players have been asking for a way to get rid of the Ultimate Edition cars, as they can’t sell or unregister them
Table of contents
Key Takeaways
How to sell or unregister Ultimate Edition cars in GTA 6
How to sell or unregister Ultimate Edition cars in GTA 6
If you’re here, then you likely went to Moses or a Pay ‘n’ Spray shop in GTA 6 to register a new car, but saw you’re out of owned vehicle slots. In an attempt to free up space, you went to sell or unregister an Ultimate Edition car you redeemed, but saw a message saying you’re unable to do so.
Specifically, if you view a “Bonus Vehicle” like Jason’s ’55 Stanier or the ’67 Vapid Dominator Buggy, you’ll see a locked icon next to the vehicle and the message: “You can’t sell bonus vehicles.”
Trying to sell a bonus Ultimate Edition vehicle in GTA 6 to no avail. Screenshot by esports.gg
So, what do you do about all those bonus vehicles clogging up space in your garage? At the moment, it seems there is no way to actually get rid of them in GTA 6. As soon as you claim a bonus vehicle from the Ultimate Edition or your pre-order, it becomes a permanently stored vehicle for the rest of your playthrough.
We even tried purposely losing or destroying some of these vehicles, but to no avail; they still wound up back in our stored vehicles tab at a Pay ‘n’ Spray. Right now, this seems to be an oversight by Rockstar Games, as there are too few precious stored vehicle slots in GTA 6 for them to be taken up by vehicles that have no use.
For now, your best course of action is to purchase more garages in GTA 6, which gives you more stored vehicle slots, or progress the story to open up more slots. Hopefully, Rockstar fixes this issue in the future and lets players store these bonus vehicles separately or just lets us get rid of them entirely.

How long does it take to beat GTA 6? Story length explained
items.content:
The floodgates have been opened in Grand Theft Auto 6, as the extended gameplay look that premiered on Netflix has showcased a world of new details. Once the gameplay showcase premiered, however, Rockstar Games revealed a slew of brand new information about the game. This includes details about the story length of GTA 6, which gives us our first real indication of how long it will take to beat the game’s main campaign.
Key Takeaways
The Netflix extended gameplay showcase for GTA 6 has revealed a bunch of fresh information about the game, but Rockstar Games went into more details once the showcase went live
According to Rockstar, the main storyline of GTA 6 takes roughly 80 hours to beat if you just complete story missions
However, if you decide to complete optional side content and explore the map in its entirety, then you’re looking at a much longer time to beat
How long does it take to beat the story in GTA 6?
Rockstar Games co-studio head Rob Nelson revealed that it takes around 80 hours to just make it through the main storyline of GTA 6. This includes just beating the necessary story missions to see the end credits roll, along with a few pieces of optional side content. If you’re curious about what side content you have access to, we have a complete list of the confirmed mini-games and activities available in GTA 6.
Obviously, 80 hours for just the main story is a staggering claim, as the main story of Rockstar’s last game, Red Dead Redemption 2, takes roughly 50 hours to complete. Before that, GTA 5’s story takes around 30 hours to finish.
There are likely numerous factors in why GTA 6’s story is so long, but we can attribute a lot of that length to the overall size of the Leonida map. According to Rockstar, Leonida is 2x bigger than the GTA 5 map and 3x bigger than the RDR2 map. With so much area to cover, you might spend around a dozen hours just getting from place to place during the course of the GTA 6 story.
If we go beyond just the main story, though, GTA 6 could take players over 100 hours to finish if they decide to partake in optional side content. This includes any side missions, mini-games/activities, and trying to escape the police with the revamped Wanted system in GTA 6.
Going even further, with the map as large as it is, if players partake in all side content and explore Leonida to the fullest, it could take 110-120 hours to fully beat the entire game. This length is for the completionist type of players who don’t stop playing a game until every location has been visited, all map markers are completed, and every achievement has been obtained.
Even if you’re not a completionist, though, 80-100 hours to beat a game is quite the commitment. From what we saw during the extended gameplay look on Netflix, however, it looks like GTA 6 will be worth the effort and more.
For more, take a look at our other guide going over whether GTA 6 will feature any sort of early access or not.

Aion 2 Players Slam NC Over “Pay-To-Win” Update
items.content:
NC has been walking the fine line between free-to-play and pay-to-win with Aion 2 ever since the game’s global launch on October 5, but with today’s update, the game might just have crossed it.
At its core, Aion 2 is a free-to-play (F2P) game since the MMORPG is literally free on Steam. However, players have repeatedly raised concerns about the F2P experience being borderline “unplayable” due to the quality-of-life bonuses you can get upon purchasing a subscription.
Up until today, getting an Aion 2 subscription mostly sped up your progress, and no major progression was locked behind a paywall. The November 24 update changes that by adding a crucial progression feature to the “Wind Breeze Merchants” shop, a vendor available exclusively to subscribers.
For the unaware, today’s Aion 2 update unlocked the 5th Stigma slot for players. Players can use the extra Stigma slot for their characters by obtaining Stigma Shards in-game. To help players level up their newly added Stigma slot, this update also adds a total of 50 Stigma Shards that are obtainable through various means.
This is where the pay-to-win criticism comes in. Of those 50 Stigma Shards, 20 are locked behind the sub-only shop, meaning F2P players have no way to obtain them. For reference, 20 shards are enough to take a Stigma skill from level 0 all the way up to level 11, with the max level of each skill being 20.

items.title: CDPR continues to ramp up development on Cyberpunk 2
items.content:
CD Projekt Red's multi-project strategy continues to ramp up. The studio has now surpassed 1,000 developers across its various projects, while the team working on Cyberpunk 2 has grown to almost 200 developers as work on the sequel continues to scale up.
As part of its latest earnings report, CD Projekt Red updated its ongoing resource allocation chart, detailing how many developers are currently assigned to each project. As of October 2026, The Witcher 4 remains CD Projekt Red's largest project, with 513 developers assigned to the game, down only slightly from July's figure of 519.
Cyberpunk 2 has continued to grow too, with it having the second largest team at CD Projekt Red. The sequel has grown from around 130 developers in late 2025 to around 200 developers in late 2026, The game remains behind The Witcher 4 in headcount, but that should be expected considering that The Witcher 4 is now in full production and on the road to release, while Cyberpunk 2 isn't quite ready for production milestones just yet.
Elsewhere, Project Sirius saw the largest reduction in headcount, dropping from 84 developers to 60 since July, which isn't too surprising as that particular game saw another shake-up earlier this year. Project Hadar remained largely unchanged at 34 developers, while shared services, which includes departments such as localisation, motion capture, UX research, QA and shared technology teams, grew from 196 developers to 212 developers over the same period.

Achievement Unlocked: An Interview with the First XBOX Player to Reach 10 Million Gamerscore
items.content:
On September 9, 2026, at 3:35pm Pacific Time, SiegfriedX unlocked a 110-point XBOX Achievement that pushed his Gamerscore to a historic 10 million. With that, he became the first XBOX player in the world to reach the milestone – just in time for XBOX’s 25th anniversary celebrations.
His journey began on XBOX 360, and it took 20 years and more than 6,400 games to get there. Along the way, he has racked up some remarkable accomplishments:
What Is Gamerscore?
Gamerscore is an individual scoring system introduced with the launch of XBOX 360 in 2005. It represents the achievement points a player has earned across XBOX games.
“Since 2020, so for the past six years, I’ve unlocked at least one achievement every day,” he told XBOX Wire Brazil in an exclusive interview.
SiegfriedX is the XBOX profile of Brazilian player Marcello Malta, a 42-year-old systems analyst whose biggest hobby is hunting achievements. “I like picking up a game and unlocking every achievement, even if the last one is worth just 10 points and takes 500 hours to get. I’m still going to try,” he says.
With a milestone like that, we wanted to hear more about his passion for achievements, how it all started, and what keeps him chasing that next unlock. Here’s what he had to say.
SiegfriedX’s XBOX Playback results.
Achievements and Gamerscore were introduced with XBOX 360. What first got you interested in achievements?
Siegfried: I was hooked on achievements right away. I didn’t even know the system existed, and I don’t think it was something people really talked about at the time. It was just a feature built into the console. You certainly didn’t buy an XBOX knowing it was there, let alone knowing it would eventually influence the entire industry and inspire similar systems elsewhere.
I remember playing and suddenly seeing that notification pop up on the screen. I thought, “What is this?” So, I looked it up, found a couple of achievement websites, started learning how the system worked, and that was it. I was hooked.
Back then, achievements really encouraged you to experience everything a game had to offer: finish the campaign, beat it on the highest difficulty, find all the collectibles, and complete specific challenges along the way. To me, they felt like the developer’s vision for how they wanted you to experience the game. Almost like they were saying, “If you’ve done all of this, you’ve seen my entire game, from beginning to end, and everything I created for you.”
What Are Achievements?
Achievements are specific goals and objectives players can complete in a game to earn Gamerscore points. Examples: finishing it on hard difficulty, collecting every collectible, or defeating a set number of opponents in multiplayer.
Each game released on XBOX includes 1,000G worth of achievements to unlock. That total can increase with additional content and expansions.
What motivates you most when it comes to chasing an achievement?
Siegfried: I first fell in love with games through Nintendo, and their games have always had that focus on collecting things and completing everything. I think that mindset stuck with me from the very beginning. achievements became an extension of that, another way of going after everything a game has to offer.
I’ve never been interested in earning points just for the sake of earning points. When I start a game, I want to unlock every achievement, even if the last one is worth just 10 points and takes 500 hours to get. I’m still going to try. I might give up or not make it in the end, but I always start with the same goal: to get everything, no matter how much time or effort it takes.
You recently reached 10 million Gamerscore. How did you plan the achievement that would take you to that milestone?
Siegfried: I wanted to hit 10 million with a game that meant something to me, something I really loved and that could make the milestone feel even more special. So I decided to do it by completing the full 1,000G in Final Fantasy VII Rebirth.
The moment SiegfriedX reached 10 million Gamerscore.
Final Fantasy is a franchise I love, so it felt like the perfect choice. The final achievement I unlocked was for beating the game on its hardest difficulty. That completed the full achievement list and brought me to exactly 10 million Gamerscore.
Was being the first player to reach 10 million Gamerscore always a goal for you?
Siegfried: I never really had a specific goal in mind. Because of the way I play, always trying to complete everything, I naturally ended up second or third in the world for Gamerscore, with someone else usually ahead of me.
Over time, though, people started dropping out, either because they got tired of chasing achievements or simply decided they didn’t want to keep going. That left me at 9 million Gamerscore with a real shot at becoming the first person to reach 10 million. That’s when I really started pushing for it.
When XBOX 360 launched, the idea of anyone ever reaching 10 million Gamerscore was almost unthinkable. But I don’t have another milestone in mind now. For me, the goal has always been to play, have fun, and do what I enjoy.
“When I start a game, I see it through to the end, at least when it comes to the original achievement list. I’ve been doing that for more than 10 years.”
Looking back on your achievement journey, which one was the hardest to unlock?
Siegfried: For me difficulty comes down on how much time something takes. Some achievements can be incredibly time-consuming, and Monster Hunter: World is a great example.
Getting every gold crown in Monster Hunter: World for the Giant Crown Master achievement was one of the toughest things I’ve ever done. It can be really frustrating to play for one, two, or even three days without making any progress because so much of it comes down to luck and getting the right monsters appear. It makes you want to cry and give up. [Laughs]
What Are Mythic Achievements?
A Mythic Achievement is awarded when a player unlocks all of a game’s original achievements. Achievements added later through DLC or updates are not required, and once Mythic status has been earned, it remains permanently.
What did you have to do in the game to unlock that achievement?
Siegfried: You have to hunt both the smallest and largest monster of every species. The smallest earns you a miniature gold crown, while the largest earns you a giant gold crown.
How long did it take to complete every achievement and reach Mythic?
Siegfried: The base game, Monster Hunter: World, has 1,000G, and its expansion, Monster Hunter World: Iceborne, adds another 1,000G and is almost like a full game in itself. All told, it took me around 600 hours to unlock every achievement. It’s easily the game I’ve spent the most time completing.
Now I’m working on the new Gears, and that one is definitely a challenge…
Yes! It has some very difficult achievements, including more than 25,000 eliminations in Versus and 50,000 in Horde.
Siegfried: Those are the only two I still need to unlock to earn Mythic. They’re both a real challenge, and I know they’re going to take a long time. But I’m definitely not giving up.
On the other end of the spectrum, which achievement did you enjoy earning the most?
Siegfried: Completing Diablo II: Resurrected. I played the original throughout my teenage years. I was obsessed with Diablo and spent years playing it.
SiegfriedX’s Quick Facts
First 1000G/Mythic: N3 – Ninety-Nine Nights or Burnout Revenge on XBOX 360
Hardest Achievement: Giant Crown Master in Monster Hunter: World
Most time-consuming 1000G/Mythic: 600 hours in Monster Hunter: World
Most memorable 1000G/Mythic: Diablo II: Resurrected
Most wanted upcoming 1000G/Mythic: Gears of War: E-Day and Grand Theft Auto VI
Only 42 games in his collection remain without 1000G/Mythic completion, most of them from the XBOX 360 era.
So getting a remake of one of my favorite games, having it turn out so well, and seeing achievements that really reflected the experience of longtime players made completing it especially meaningful.
One of those, for example, was reaching level 99 with a Hardcore character. That’s probably the achievement I enjoyed earning the most. I started playing at launch in 2021, and I didn’t unlock that final achievement until March 2023. It took me two years!
Do you only stop playing a game after earning its full 1,000G/Mythic?
Siegfried: It’s been a very long time since I played something without completing the full 1,000G. I don’t think I’ve done that since the launch of XBOX One in 2013. There are a few extremely long and difficult DLC packs that I never went back to finish, but normally, when I start a game, I see it through to the end, at least for the original achievement list. I’ve been doing that for more than 10 years.
Mythic Achievements are one of the new features XBOX has introduced to celebrate its 25th anniversary. What did you think of them?
Siegfried: I think Mythic Achievements were implemented really well. Even little details like the badge design and the sound that plays when you unlock one… Microsoft always does a great job with that kind of thing. Rare Achievements were already great, and Mythic Achievements made the experience even better.
What advice would you give someone who wants to earn more achievements?
Siegfried: More than anything, games are supposed to be fun. If you focus too much on climbing the rankings and push yourself too hard, you can end up taking the fun out of it and burning yourself out.
It’s all about finding the right balance. Spend some time playing something you really enjoy, then switch things up and play something just for the achievements or take on a tougher challenge. Going back and forth between the two is key. That’s what I’ve always done.
The post Achievement Unlocked: An Interview with the First XBOX Player to Reach 10 Million Gamerscore appeared first on XBOX Wire.

Stage 1 Standings after Day 2
Teams qualified for Stage 2
Of the four teams in the 2-0 bracket after Day 1, 2 have made it to the next round of play, with Liquid’s loss to NiP coming as the first surprise of the day. Oceanic powerhouse FlyQuest came out swinging with the second upset as they clean-swept Imperial to reach Stage 2.
Teams in 2-1 bracket
Imperial and Liquid, failing to win their respective 2-0 stage matches, were knocked down to the 2-1 bracket. M80 survived a close tie against HEROIC and secured their second win of the event. Joining them will be Eternal Fire, despite being one of the strongest suitors to go 3-0. Lynn Vision and PARIVISION joined them, securing their respective clashes against Wildcards and FaZe Clan to find themselves a single win away from Stage 2.

Teams disqualified

Joining them in the 0-3 bracket are the highly inexperienced players of DENDELE. Unfortunately for these teams, their run at the Major comes to an end with nothing but memories to take back.
Day 3 Matches
Day 3 will have some teams suffering from heartbreak, along with those who will enjoy the elation. With more teams set to qualify and get eliminated, the matches will have stakes as high as possible. The schedule for it is as follows:
Day 2 has successfully thrown a spanner in the works for everybody’s PickEm, with big names failing to deliver the performances that fans expected of them. CS2 Returns to the Esports World Cup in 2027 and 2028, With $700,000 for the Riyadh Champions
items.content:
Counter-Strike 2 is staying at the Esports World Cup for at least two more years. The Esports Foundation confirmed on 25 November that CS2 will return for EWC 2027 and EWC 2028, which makes Valve’s shooter a fixture at the event for five straight years. More importantly for the teams, the 2027 edition comes with a firm date, a $2 million prize pool and a qualification system that rewards consistency across the whole first half of the season.
The Esports World Cup confirmed Counter-Strike 2 for 2027 and 2028. Image: Esports World Cup.
The tournament heads back to Esports Boulevard in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, after the 2026 finals were staged at the Accor Arena in Paris. It runs from 20 July to 1 August 2027 with 32 teams, while the 2028 edition is pencilled in for 14 to 30 July 2028. The organisers have not yet given a venue, format or prize pool for that second year, so for now 2027 is where the detail lies.
A $700,000 Top Prize and a Bo5 Grand Final in Riyadh
Every stage of the 2027 event is played in person, qualifier included. Stage 1 splits the 32 teams into four groups of eight, each run as a double-elimination bracket, and the top four from every group move on. The 16 survivors then meet in a Stage 2 playoff played as best-of-threes, with only the grand final stretched to a best-of-five. In practice, that means a team can afford one bad series in the groups but not two, which tends to favour deep, experienced rosters over hot streaks.
The money is weighted heavily towards the top. The champions take home $700,000, or roughly a third of the pool, while second place is worth $300,000, third $150,000 and fourth $90,000. Even so, nobody leaves empty-handed, since every team in the main event collects at least $10,000. The full payout table and schedule are on the official EWC 2027 Counter-Strike 2 page.
Counter-Strike 2 at EWC 2026: the official tournament recap. Video: Esports World Cup.
The May VRS Ranking Will Decide Most of the 32-Team Field
Most of the field is built from the Valve Regional Standings. Twenty places go to the best-ranked teams in the global standings, and North America, South America and Asia each get two more invites of their own, which guarantees those regions a presence however the global table looks. Two wildcard invites complete the direct list. Crucially, invitations follow the first monthly VRS publication of May 2027, and seeding uses the first ranking published in July. As a result, the first five months of next year effectively become the qualifier for most of the teams that will travel to Riyadh.
The last four places come from the Riyadh Open Qualifier on 16 to 18 July 2027, and this is where the format changes most. At EWC 2026, the final four spots went through a 64-team Last Chance Qualifier. Next year’s open qualifier allows up to 128 teams on a first-come, first-served basis, with a $100 entry fee and $100,000 shared among the teams that finish fifth to 16th. The entry fee is trivial, although the in-person, non-BYOC format means flights and hotels in Riyadh will be the real cost for any team chasing one of those four slots. Registration details have not been announced yet.
Team Spirit Defend a Title Won in Paris
Team Spirit arrive as the holders. They beat FUT Esports 3-1 in the EWC 2026 final at the Accor Arena, and Danil “donk” Kryshkovets was named MVP of the event. Spirit have barely slowed down since, adding the BLAST Open Fall 2026 title and, according to the Esports Foundation, dropping just one map on the way. At only 19, donk remains the centrepiece of a roster that will go to Riyadh as the team everyone has to beat.
Danil "donk" Kryshkovets with his MVP award at EWC 2026. Photo: Esports World Cup.
Paris also produced two of the year’s better stories. FUT beat MOUZ, G2 Esports and FURIA on their way to the final, while Legacy knocked Team Falcons out in the quarterfinals and then won the all-Brazilian third-place match against FURIA. Both are now in Singapore for the PGL Major, looking to prove that Paris was not a one-off against a full Major field.
FURIA, meanwhile, finished fourth in Paris but came into the Major as the top-ranked team in the world after winning three titles across October and November. Singapore is also set to be Gabriel “FalleN” Toledo’s last Major, so the Brazilians have more than ranking points to play for. Spirit and FURIA both start in Stage 3, and our PGL Major Singapore 2026 hub tracks every result as the bracket unfolds.
The EWC 2026 Counter-Strike 2 champions reel. Video: Esports World Cup.
The next announcement to watch is registration for the Riyadh Open Qualifier, since it is the only route into the event that does not run through the rankings. EWC will publish it through its X account and Instagram, while the organiser’s corporate updates come from the Esports Foundation on LinkedIn.

Thermal Grizzly expands enthusiast toolkit with new Delid-Heat-Mate and TG PadMate
items.content:
Thermal Grizzly has announced a pair of new products aimed at PC enthusiasts and hardware tinkerers. Alongside a new Delid-Heat-Mate fixture for CPU delidding, the company has also introduced the TG PadMate thermal pad measuring tool and an accompanying minus pad 8 Multipack kit.
The Delid-Heat-Mate is designed to simplify the heating stage of CPU delidding, supporting AMD AM5 processors as well as Intel's LGA1700, LGA1851 and LGA1954 platforms. The tool works alongside Thermal Grizzly's existing Delid-Die-Mate products, holding a CPU upside down during heating so that the integrated heat spreader can separate once the solder underneath melts.
Thermal Grizzly has also introduced the TG PadMate, a simple tool designed to help users accurately measure thermal pad thickness when replacing pads on graphics cards, motherboards or SSDs. The flexible plastic tool supports measurements ranging from 0.5mm to 5mm, covering the thermal pad thicknesses most commonly found on graphics cards, motherboards and SSDs.
Alongside the TG PadMate, Thermal Grizzly is also launching the minus pad 8 Multipack-Set. The kit bundles the measuring tool with a selection of thermal pads in six different thicknesses, giving users a single package for thermal pad replacement and maintenance tasks.
The Delid-Heat-Mate is available now with an MSRP of €19.90, while the TG PadMate costs €2.90 on its own. The minus pad 8 Multipack-Set is priced at €39.90.
