Lineage M 2027 plan: faster class reboots, new content, and more solo dungeons
items.content:
NCSOFT has revealed its 2027 plans for Lineage M, including shorter (and, indeed, more frequent) class reboot cycles and more solo dungeons. It should come as good news to fans of the game who have been starved of attention this year, and the updates arrive as the mobile MMORP closes in on its 10th anniversary.
The company says its answer for the next decade is "being true to Lineage." For them, it means leveraging three keywords: "Pioneer," which means pushing the world beyond Aden; "Dynamic," which means faster growth; and "Lineage," means a return to relationship systems such as Blood Pledges.
Where it was shown
NCSOFT presented the plan at Lineage Festival: Invitation to Aden, held at KINTEX Exhibition Center 2 in Ilsan. The company calls it its first offline festival covering the entire Lineage IP, and the event drew 5,000 attendees per session. For a first attempt, that’s not bad at all but NC Senior Executive Vice President (CBO) Lee Sung-koo wondered out loud why they hadn’t done it sooner and promised next year's event will take place over a weekend, as opposed to another Wednesday.
Lee Sang-min, Head of Business Division for Lineage M, and Cho Jae-kyung, Development PD for Lineage M, ran the "Playlist M" session. It was set up as a talk concert, with classic Lineage BGM tracks introducing each segment.
What veterans voted for
Poll topicWinning choice
2027 update directionBrand-new content over renewing existing content
New class conceptGrowth class built for hunting and EXP gain
Most anticipated class rebootMagic Swordsman (out of five candidates)
Hunting groundsSolo growth dungeons
Cho explained that his team has listened to those who say they’ve explored every nook and cranny of Arden. They want fresh content, and Lee pledged to prepare new stuff more thoroughly in 2027.
2026 was a barren year for class releases, and no 2027 class release has yet to be confirmed. The reboot queue for existing classes still runs one to two years, so the poll was about gathering input for the next one. Lee added that all five nominated classes need reboots, not just the winner.
On hunting grounds, Cho promised a broader variety of solo dungeons next year. His reasoning was that most players don’t switch classes, so a new primary hunting ground is the simplest way to give them something different to aim for.
Reboots get a faster schedule
According to Cho, the team fell behind with class reboots because of business decisions and clashing development schedules. The previous pace was one class every three months, which raised expectations. The plan is to shorten the cycle in 2027 and maybe, just maybe, we’ll see a quarterly approach that overhauls several classes at once.
Details will follow, and the team says it will review changes carefully so players aren't overburdened. Lee noted that balancing a live-service game demands extreme caution and adds developer workload, but said the team will prepare to deliver the faster updates players want.
Further Lineage M details are expected at next week's broadcast, with a Q4 update to follow. Lineage Classic's Tria update lands Dec. 2.

items.title: Blizzard is making parts of Diablo 4’s nostalgia-fuelled Hell’s Legacy season permanent
items.content:
Diablo 4's Season of Hell's Legacy wasn't an average seasonal update. Blizzard used the season to celebrate the franchise's history, bringing back bosses, locations and rewards inspired by Diablo, Diablo II and Diablo III. Now, after overwhelming player demand, Blizzard has confirmed that several of the season's most popular features are becoming permanent additions to then game.
In a new blog post, Blizzard revealed that while the entirety of Season of Hell's Legacy won't carry over, a number of fan-favourite activities and rewards will remain available in both Eternal and Seasonal realms. Chief among them is the Prime Evil Council in Uber Tristram, which will now function as a permanent endgame boss activity. The Hell's Legacy Capstone Dungeons are also sticking around in Torment 10+, alongside the Diablo World Boss encounter.
Some of the season's biggest nods to earlier Diablo games are sticking around too. Larger Waking Nightmares Dungeons will continue to be available through Chronicle of Nightmares Dungeon Keys, while players running The Pit will occasionally encounter monster families from previous Diablo games. Blizzard is also keeping Deckard Cain's collection of books accessible in Tristram, giving players a permanent way to revisit some of the franchise's lore.
A handful of rewards and secrets are surviving the seasonal transition too. The Annihilus Seal and Hellfire Torch Charm will remain obtainable, and Cow Island isn't going anywhere either. Blizzard also noted that other frequently requested features from the season are currently being evaluated and could potentially return in reworked form in the future.

Pocket Mirror: GoldenerTraum Looks Lavish on the Switch
items.content:
Pocket Mirror: GoldenerTraum is one of those games that’s often considered most memorable for its visuals. Which tracks. While the original was an RPG Maker VX Ace title, it always looked stunning and the remaster ensured that element endured. It looked good when it showed up again on PCs in 2023. Yet somehow, now that we’ve got Pocket Mirror: Goldenertraum on the Switch as well, I find it somehow feels a little more lavish and even more at home on the system.
As a quick refresher, a young girl with amnesia finds herself in a strange place only remembering that she must hold tight to a golden pocket mirror with her. Her goal is to survive in order to find out the truth about her situation and perhaps even a means to safety. While the remaster is largely the same game, it does offer more insights into a certain character, a chapter select, and an additional ending to earn.
Images via AstralShift
Like other RPG Maker horror games, Pocket Mirror: Goldenertraum involves more exploration and puzzle solving, alongside intense visuals and descriptions, to tell its story and unsettle a player. It’s incredibly effective at this, and on the Switch it looks absolutely stunning in handheld mode. It really looks wonderful, and playing it in this way allows someone to really pause and take in the moment. Yes, if someone played it on a Steam Deck or handheld gaming PC, they also already had this sort of experience and moment. But for those new to it, it’s incredibly intricate and a great way to appreciate the spritework.
The things that do still present themselves as issues in the Switch release of Pocket Mirror: Goldenertraum come across more as gameplay design decisions that might’ve been a result of the time it was made and limitations of RPG Maker VX Ace. I would have liked more save points, for example, or a bit more guidance. (Though past horror games along this line like Corpse Party and The Aquarium Does Not Dance show that you can provide that without handholding.) The script isn’t as solid as the follow-up Little Goody Two Shoes. But then, considering the premise and certain revelations, it being obtuse ends up making a bit of sense too.
Images via AstralShift
But I think what I also appreciate a lot about the Switch release of Pocket Mirror: Goldenertraum is that it means another elaborate RPG Maker horror game is on the system. It sort of crept up on me, and perhaps others, but this really is a good device for playing these kinds of classic titles. I already mentioned how you can find Corpse Party and The Aquarium Does Not Dance here. Angels of Death, Ao Oni, Mad Father, The Witch’s House MV, and Ib are can be found on the system too. It’s a genuinely great library made even stronger by this AstralShift inclusion.
Pocket Mirror: Goldenertraum is a great addition to the Switch RPG Maker horror game library and looks beautiful on the system. It’s still a gorgeous and lavish game, and it feels especially pretty with this port. Its release also builds up an already admirable collection of games in this genre even more so.
Pocket Mirror: Goldenertraum is available on the Switch and PC.

New details have emerged regarding PlayStation’s Jak and Daxter film
items.content:
For years now there has been sporadic talk regarding a potential Jak and Daxter film adaptation, with claims from as far back as 2022 stating that Uncharted director Ruben Fleischer is tied to such a project. While official details have yet to be shared, a newly surfaced report appears to affirm that the film is still in the works, and will star Spider-Man’s own Tom Holland.
As discovered recently by one Reddit user, a Production Weekly issue from last year included a listing for the long-dormant Jak and Daxter film – confirming some previously-leaked details while simultaneously offering new information.
Production Weekly, for the uninitiated, is a long-running subscription service dedicated to offering up-to-date details on various film and TV projects in the works across the world.
According to this listing, the Jak & Daxter film is well underway with Ruben Fleischer (known best for the Uncharted film adaptation) serving as its director. Perhaps the most notable revelation from the report is the fact that Tom Holland is said to be starring in the film.
This isn’t the first time that Holland’s name has come up, with the Spider-Man actor expressing back in 2022 that “I would like to make a Jak and Daxter movie, and I would play Jak”. Though far from official at the time, it appears as though Holland may have gotten his way.
Prior to this recently-resurfaced report, known film insider DanielRPK took to social media to claim that Minecraft writers Gavin James and Neil Widener had been tasked with the writing for Jak and Daxter – though no details regarding Tom Holland’s involvement was shared at the time.
All-in-all, it appears as though the long-awaited Jak and Daxter film is indeed on its way, and unlike the Uncharted film before it, has not suffered from a rotating door of Directors. It will be interesting to see what direction the project takes, especially as Holland himself previously expressed desires for it to be “weird” and “dark.”

items.title: PUBG Mobile 4.7 Patch Notes: M134 and Flamethrower Buffed as Two Pending Bugs Are Finally Fixed
items.content:
PUBG Mobile has rolled out another round of fixes for its 4.7 Arctic Chronicles update, buffing two Metro Royale weapons against monsters and clearing two bugs it had flagged as pending for almost a week. The development team listed 15 changes in its latest notice on 24 November, covering the Arctic Chronicles mode, World of Wonder, Metro Royale and the lobby. It is the fourth fix list since version 4.7 went live on 12 November, following earlier rounds on 16, 18 and 20 November.
The change most players will notice is in Metro Royale, where the M134 and the Flamethrower now deal more damage to monsters. The rest of the list is mostly clean-up, from characters clipping into the Ancient Beast in the Prison area to the blurry graphics some players saw after the patch. PUBG Mobile did not say whether any of the changes need a new download, and its notice asks players to report remaining issues through customer service or its official community.
Every fix in PUBG Mobile’s 24 November update
PUBG Mobile grouped the changes by mode, and the list below follows the same order. Arctic Chronicles, the themed mode at the heart of version 4.7, received three fixes. Metro Royale had the longest section, with six changes including the weapon buff, while five general fixes cover finishes, events and the lobby.
Arctic Chronicles: fixed terrain that displayed incorrectly in some areas.
Arctic Chronicles: fixed the portal tunnel visual effect after entering a portal.
Arctic Chronicles: fixed characters clipping into the Ancient Beast’s shifting body in the Prison area.
World of Wonder: fixed some School template objects appearing in the backpack of other templates.
Metro Royale: the M134 and Flamethrower now deal more damage to monsters.
Metro Royale: fixed the incomplete description of the U-CH0 Season Commemoration Medal in Achievement Missions.
Metro Royale: fixed characters getting stuck underground at certain spawn points.
Metro Royale: switching weapons now interrupts the Stealth Syringe progress bar.
Metro Royale: fixed the wrong bonus description for the Reaper Scorpion Statue (Gold) collectible.
Metro Royale: fixed the mini-map showing the wrong range for the random High-Loot Zone.
General: improved the weapon switch animation for the Tidal Embrace M416 finish on the Smooth graphics setting.
General: fixed custom buttons and blurry graphics after the patch update.
General: fixed the S32 P90 finish icon not matching its in-match colour.
General: fixed Lucky Eggs that could not be gifted in the Chicko’s Loot event.
General: fixed the Lobby Team Code overlapping some buttons.
Dear players,
Thanks to your proactive feedback, we have recently resolved the following issues:
Arctic Chronicles
– Fixed a terrain display issue in certain areas.
– Fixed a display issue with the portal tunnel visual effect after entering a portal.
– Fixed an issue in the…
— PUBG MOBILE (@PUBGMOBILE) November 24, 2026
The pending fixes PUBG Mobile has now delivered
PUBG Mobile’s fix notices have carried a Pending Fix section since 18 November, and this round clears two of its oldest entries. The incomplete U-CH0 medal description and the S32 P90 icon that did not match its in-match colour were both listed as pending in the 18 November notice. Both were still waiting in the 20 November notice, which did fix a third item from that list, the held weapon finish displaying wrongly when players returned to the Metro Royale lobby.
One problem from the 18 November list has not yet appeared as fixed. Metro Royale containers that showed two Honors, only one of which could be picked up, were listed as pending at the time, and neither of the two later notices mentions them. Players who still run into it can report it, because PUBG Mobile keeps pointing players to its customer service and official community channels for feedback.
What else has changed since Arctic Chronicles launched
The 18 November round was the biggest so far. It made fishing available on the Rondo and Karakin maps, and it stopped players from dropping their Fishing Rod and Bait when defeated. It also doubled the drop rate for Legacy Armament Vouchers in the new Seal City PvE mode. PUBG Mobile said the double drop runs every Friday to Sunday until version 4.7 ends, starting with the weekend of 20 to 22 November.
Read together, the four notices give a good picture of how Arctic Chronicles plays. The mode is built around a huge Ancient Beast whose shifting body moves through the map, along with portals that players can enter and an Aurora Realm that defeated players pass through before spectating. Players can also summon an Aurora Horse, which the 20 November round made easier to call up after complaints that it sometimes needed several taps.
The 20 November round also removed an invisible wall on the Ancient Beast’s body that had been blocking shots, and fixed abnormal movement speed when players fired and peeked straight after sprinting in Classic Mode. The first round on 16 November dealt with abnormal rewards for some Brainrot characters in World of Wonder. Every notice so far has appeared on PUBG Mobile’s official X account, which also posted the original 4.7 preview before launch.
The update is available through the Google Play listing and PUBG Mobile’s official site. BGMI, Krafton’s separate version of the game, received the same Arctic Chronicles content in its own 4.7 update, as our BGMI 4.7 guide explains. Players on low-end phones also have a new option in PUBG Mobile Flash, the lighter version that launched on 13 November, as our report on PUBG Mobile Flash covers.
The competitive side of the game is heading into its biggest event of the year, and our PMGC 2026 Gauntlet guide has the teams and format. PMGC is PUBG Mobile’s annual world championship, and it brings together the top teams from each region’s qualifying events. For casual players, the next Seal City double drop weekend starts on Friday 27 November.
The post PUBG Mobile 4.7 Patch Notes: M134 and Flamethrower Buffed as Two Pending Bugs Are Finally Fixed appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: GTA 6’s ‘Woke’ Backlash Over Jason and Lucia Relationship
items.content:
The row over whether Grand Theft Auto VI has gone “woke” has spilled out of streams and X threads and into mainstream news. AFP’s wire story on 25 November asked whether the series had gone soft. CBC News then reported that some streamers find the game too woke, while WIRED ran a piece on 19 November about men online who are angry that the game rewards being a good partner. The complaints centre on Jason and Lucia’s relationship, a new system that scores how players behave, and the absence of sex workers for the first time since GTA III.
The backlash sits awkwardly next to the numbers. GTA VI made about .8 billion on its first day, as our report on its record launch revenue covers, and it holds a 99 Metascore, as our reviews roundup found. That gap between the loudest critics and the wider audience is exactly what has drawn reporters in.
Why some fans say GTA 6 has gone soft
Most of the anger is about what the game asks players to do between heists. Players are encouraged to look after the relationship by fixing up Jason and Lucia’s house, buying flowers and jewellery, and running errands such as picking up groceries for Lucia. Some anonymous X users have called the result “feminist slop”, while others have reached for a slur borrowed from manosphere forums, according to AFP. Several streamers have also complained that too much of the early story is made up of errand-style missions.
The second target is the behaviour system, which AFP describes as an honour system. Citing video game press reports, the agency said players earn focus and behaviour points for acts such as kindness to strangers, not littering and staying fit. The happiest ending reportedly needs a strong relationship and a professional criminal profile rather than a violent or psycho one, which critics argue is a strange fit for a series built on chaos.
Fans who miss the older games also point to the removal of sex workers, a feature the series had carried since GTA III in 2001, as our report on why Rockstar removed it explains. For many of the angriest players, that single change has become a symbol of everything they think the series has lost. Others simply argue that the game has become less of a sandbox and more of a guided story.
Rockstar’s second GTA VI trailer, which centred on Jason and Lucia. Video: Rockstar Games/YouTube
What Rockstar and researchers say about the change
Rockstar has framed the changes as a matter of story. The studio told AFP that GTA VI is about a couple in trouble and on the run together, and that its design choices were made to serve that story. Rockstar North’s Rob Nelson made a similar point before launch, saying the game offers optional ways to show empathy for players who want them, as our report on his comments and the criminal profile explains.
The researchers AFP spoke to were not convinced that the game had gone soft at all. Andrew Przybylski of the Oxford Internet Institute said he would not call it wholesome, describing it instead as a more complete and thoughtful story that is still transgressive. Douglas Gentile of Iowa State University said the game sits in a morally grey area that reflects everyday life.
The game is also far from sanitised, whatever its critics say. It still has strip clubs, which have been getting some streamers flagged on YouTube, as our report on the strip club warnings covers. The shootouts, robberies and police chases the series is known for are all still there, and nothing in the behaviour system stops players from causing chaos if they accept the consequences.
Why the GTA 6 culture war keeps growing
Part of the reason the argument keeps spreading is that it rewards everyone involved. Clips of streamers raging at a grocery errand travel well, and so do the replies mocking them, so every new round of outrage brings more attention to both camps. The mainstream coverage has largely framed the backlash as a loud complaint set against enormous sales, with CBC noting that the game has still made billions despite the pushback.
None of that is likely to settle the argument, because the two sides are judging different things. Critics are measuring GTA VI against what the series used to be, while most reviewers and buyers are judging the game Rockstar actually made. PlayStation has called it the biggest launch in its history, as our PlayStation launch record report covers.
Rockstar has not said it plans to change any of the relationship or behaviour systems, even as the argument has spread. Because the relationship is woven into the main story, any change would go far deeper than a settings menu. GTA VI is out on PS5 and Xbox Series X and S, according to Rockstar’s GTA VI site, and no PC version has been announced.
The post GTA 6’s ‘Woke’ Backlash Over Jason and Lucia Relationship appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Sony has obtained marketing rights for The Witcher 4, CD Projekt Red confirms
items.content:
Sony is not one to shy away from marketing deals, with the PlayStation console maker having most recently spent an unknown (though likely hefty) sum in order to obtain exclusive rights to advertise GTA VI across the world. This already seems to be paying off, with GTA VI breaking half a dozen different PlayStation records, and so it comes as little surprise that Sony has struck a marketing deal with CD Projekt Red for the much-anticipated Witcher 4.
As shared by the publication VGC, CD Projekt Red revealed during its latest earnings report that the company has penned an agreement with Sony for what seems to be a multi-year marketing deal, with CFO Piotr Nielubowicz telling investors:
“Just today, we signed new partnership agreements with Sony Interactive Entertainment covering the presence of our games on PlayStation and in PlayStation Plus subscriptions, as well as our collaboration during the upcoming Witcher 4 marketing campaign. This cooperation will support our business and financial outlook in this and future years.”
While The Witcher series remains in a league lower than that of GTA, it still represents one of the biggest and most hyped franchises out there, with TW3: Wild Hunt sitting in the top 10 best selling games of all time at 65 million copies.
This, in combination with the ongoing success of Cyberpunk 2077 (which alone has sold 40 million units since 2020) puts CDPR in the upper echelon of video game developers.
As such, it makes sense that Sony would want to associate itself with the company – especially as Rockstar is unlikely to have another new game coming out any time soon. It will be interesting to see how closely they try to tie The Witcher 4 into the PlayStation sphere.

items.title: Woman Asks Instagram How to Cash Out Her Boyfriend’s CS2 Skins, Gets Roasted Instead
items.content:
A screenshot of a woman asking Instagram how to cash out her boyfriend’s Counter-Strike 2 skins while he was away from his PC has gone viral, and every reply shown in the screenshot turned on her. The post shows a monitor filled with knives, gloves and rifle skins, alongside a request for help selling them because he would not do it himself. The caption says she wanted the money for a visit to a cosmetologist, which only made the reaction harsher.
The screenshot spread fast after a CS2 meme account shared it on X on 24 November. Much of the attention has come from the comments, and from the reminder of how much some CS2 inventories are now worth. It also raises a fair question that the replies mostly skipped over, which is whether anyone could actually do what she asked.
What the viral CS2 skins post showed
In the post, the woman says she has access to her boyfriend’s PC and asks how to cash out the items on the screen. She adds that he refuses to do it himself, and that she wants the money for a beauty appointment. The inventory in the photo is the kind that many CS2 players spend years building, with several knives and pairs of gloves sitting in the top rows.
The most popular reply told her to look after her partner’s things and “mind your own business”, and it drew thousands of likes. Another joked that if he found out, no cosmetologist would be able to help her. A third pointed out that turning skins into real money is far more of a hassle than she seemed to think, and advised her to leave them alone.
A girl tried to cash out her boyfriend’s skins while he wasn’t at his PC and asked for help on Instagram.
Comments cooked her instantly pic.twitter.com/LSDaHnrZzV
— Slamsa (@Slamsawtf) November 24, 2026
There is no way to confirm that the post is genuine, and the account that first posted it is not visible in the screenshot. The text also reads like a translation, so it may have started in another language before it reached X. Viral posts like this one are often jokes or bait, and it should be treated as an unverified screenshot rather than a real attempt to empty someone’s account.
Why selling someone else’s CS2 skins is harder than it looks
Sitting at someone’s PC is rarely enough to move their items. Players who use the Steam Guard Mobile Authenticator have to confirm every trade and Community Market listing in the Steam app on their phone. Without the phone, a trade or listing started on the PC simply waits for a confirmation that never comes.
Accounts without the authenticator face a different barrier. Steam’s trading and market restrictions put items on hold for up to 15 days when an account is not protected by the mobile app, and the owner can cancel anything still on hold. Those holds exist for exactly this kind of situation, where someone else has got hold of an account and tries to move its items.
CS2 also has a safety net that no other Steam game has yet. Under Trade Protection, every CS2 item received in a trade is protected for seven days, and the original owner can reverse all trades containing protected items from that period through their Trade History page. The items go back to their previous owners, although the account that reverses the trades is barred from trading and the Market for 30 days.
Even a successful sale on the Community Market would not produce cash. The Steam Subscriber Agreement says Steam Wallet funds have no cash value and cannot be exchanged for cash, so Market sales only add credit for spending on Steam. That is the hassle the third reply was hinting at, since Steam itself offers no way to turn skins into cash.
How CS2 players can protect their inventory at home
The simplest protection is the authenticator itself, because it ties every trade and listing to the owner’s phone. Locking a PC when stepping away, and logging out of Steam on shared computers, closes the gap that the viral post was supposedly trying to use. Players with valuable items should also check their Trade History regularly, since reversals are only possible within the seven-day window.
The value of those items is exactly why people pay attention to stories like this. Our guide to building a colour-themed CS2 inventory shows how quickly costs add up even on a budget, and knives and gloves sit at the very top of that range. Valve has also kept changing how items are sold in some countries, as our report on the X-Ray Scanner arriving for Swiss players explains.
Interest in skins tends to peak around the Majors, and the PGL Singapore Major is under way right now, as our Stage 1 Pick’Ems guide covers. Valve’s official Counter-Strike site lists every update to the game and its items. According to Steam Support, Counter-Strike 2 is currently the only game on Steam that supports Trade Protected items.

items.title: BGMI Air vs BGMI on the Same Phone: 60 FPS vs 40, Zero Ads and No 2.4GB Download
items.content:
BGMI Air’s open beta went live on the Google Play Store at 10am IST on 25 November, and by lunchtime X was full of posts claiming that the lighter version of Battlegrounds Mobile India lags badly and pushes ads at players. We installed it the same morning and played a full Classic match on Erangel to see how much of that holds up. Across roughly 14 minutes of recorded play, the ping readout never moved from 20ms, not a single ad appeared, and the game let us drop into a 100-player match without forcing any extra download first.
One phone and one match cannot settle the question for every device, of course, and Air makes some visible trade-offs to stay this small. To put the numbers in context, we then installed the main BGMI on the same phone, signed in with the same account and played it too. Below is everything we found, set against what KRAFTON has confirmed so far and what other early testers are reporting.
Watch our Hindi video: BGMI Air and BGMI side by side on the same phone, with live FPS counters.
Ping Stayed at 20ms for the Whole Erangel Match
The lag complaints were the main reason we wanted to test Air ourselves, so we kept an eye on the network readout in the bottom corner of the screen throughout. From the plane and the drop towards Georgopol, through a buggy ride across the map, to a firefight in which we knocked down an enemy, it read 20ms every time we checked, on Wi-Fi and on the India server. Going back through the recording afterwards, we found no rubber-banding and no frozen frames either.
Smoothness held up just as well. Our screen recording averaged about 58 frames per second over the session, which suggests the game was running close to 60 FPS for most of the match. A screen recorder is not a proper frame counter, so treat that figure as a strong hint rather than a benchmark. It is also worth saying that our test phone runs the main game too, which means this result tells you little about how Air behaves on a 2GB budget handset, the kind of device it was actually built for. That test is next on our list.
Not a Single Ad in 14 Minutes, Lobby Included
The ad worry appears to trace back to an Instagram story from the creator LetsGrow about irrelevant ads playing while the lobby sat idle, according to the esports account Esports360 (@Esports360igc). Esports360 then tried it in both BGMI and BGMI Air, leaving each game idle in the lobby for five to six minutes, and reported that no ad appeared in either.
Our session lines up with that. We spent time in the lobby, opened the Download Center, waited through matchmaking on the spawn island and played the match out, and at no point did a video or banner ad show up. Live service games can switch features on from the server whenever the developer chooses, so that could change before or after launch, but on the evidence so far the ad claims look unproven.
A 0.98GB Install, and a 216.2MB Lobby You Don’t Have to Download
Storage is where Air really separates itself from the main game. According to Digit, the open beta’s initial download on Android is 0.98GB, compared with roughly 1.5GB for regular BGMI. KRAFTON’s own Instagram post puts the minimum hardware at 1.5GB of RAM and an Adreno 306 GPU, while the Play Store listing asks for Android 5 or above.
Inside the game, most of that saving comes from a Download Center that splits the extras into optional packs. The Full Lobby pack, which restores the complete lobby with its social hub, perks and customisation screens, weighs 216.2MB, and we had downloaded just 0.2MB of it when we started our match. Alongside it sits a separate 291.2MB Recommended Resource Pack, made up of a Standard Definition Icon Pack (252.5MB), Classic map visual enhancements (22.1MB) and Basic Audio (16.7MB).
The Full Lobby pack is optional: we had 0.2MB of its 216.2MB when we played. Screenshot: TalkEsport.
That behaviour fits the promise of no forced packages before the first match, which KRAFTON made ahead of launch, as Digit reported. When we tapped an item that needed new files, the game asked before fetching anything, with a notice that the resource required an estimated 25.6MB and a choice to continue or cancel. We chose to grab about 39MB of extras over Wi-Fi at a reported 2,260KB/s, and the Download Center also notes that any download pauses on its own once a match begins.
Air asks before it downloads anything new. Screenshot: TalkEsport.
Air Exclusive Graphics, and the 90 FPS Question
Air also ships with a graphics preset of its own. For the whole match, the corner of the HUD showed Air Exclusive, and the lobby carries a dedicated Air Features button that explains the approach. In a screenshot of that screen shared on X by TechiBoy (@techiboy96), it promises strict control over file size with content downloaded as needed, a clean and minimal lobby with lightweight resources, and three graphics choices: Air Exclusive, which is marked as a beta, Super Smooth and Power Saving.
The BGMI Air lobby with its Air Features button. Screenshot: TalkEsport.
High refresh rates are the bigger open question. TechiBoy says 90 FPS and 120 FPS gameplay still requires the main BGMI, and the Free Press Journal reported the same limit. Air’s settings menu does list higher frame rate options, as our BGMI Air FPS guide explains, with the top two tied to supported devices. We did not test a 90Hz or 120Hz phone, so if high refresh play matters to you, the main game remains the safer choice until KRAFTON clarifies.
Same Phone, Same Account: BGMI Wanted 2.4GB Before We Could Play
The clearest difference showed up before either game reached a match. On first launch, the main BGMI asked us to choose a resource pack before anything else, either a Low-spec pack of 1,478.9MB or an HD pack of 2,399.2MB, and warned us not to close the game until the download finished. We picked HD, and at the 5 to 8MB/s our connection managed, it took roughly six minutes before the lobby opened. Air, by contrast, went straight into its tutorial, asked for one quick restart after a small update, and then let us start a match with almost nothing extra downloaded.
The lobbies tell a similar story. In BGMI, our character appeared in its outfit with a pet companion and the usual event panels around it, while in Air the same account loaded in a plain default look, which fits TechiBoy’s report that cosmetics currently use placeholders. Neither lobby showed us an ad.
40 FPS in BGMI, 60 FPS in Air on the Same Phone
The frame rate gap was the biggest surprise of the day. Counting the frames our screen recorder captured each second, the main game held at about 40 FPS for almost the entire match on its default Balanced graphics setting, while Air sat at about 60 FPS on its default Air Exclusive preset. We left both games exactly as they installed, without changing a single setting. Air did dip to around 40 FPS during the plane ride and parachute drop, but it climbed back to 60 once we landed. Ping sat mostly at 28ms in BGMI, with brief spikes to 36ms and 44ms, against a steady 20ms in Air, although ping depends as much on the network at that moment as on the game itself.
Two caveats are worth keeping in mind. A screen recorder is not a true frame counter, and BGMI may well run faster on this phone if you turn its graphics down yourself. Even so, on default settings Air delivered the smoother match straight out of the box, and from a distance the greenery, buildings and vehicles looked much the same in both, with Air’s textures only turning noticeably soft up close.
Same phone, same account: BGMI (top) at about 40 FPS, BGMI Air (bottom) at about 60 FPS. Screenshot: TalkEsport.
BGMI Air vs BGMI: The Numbers Side by Side
For anyone deciding which version to keep on their phone, here is how the two compare on what has been confirmed or reported so far, together with what we saw in our own session.
Where BGMI Air Still Feels Like a Beta
Air saves space by holding assets back, and you can see it. With the Full Lobby pack skipped, the lobby backdrop looked noticeably soft and blocky in places, and TechiBoy reports that outfits, gun skins and car skins currently use placeholder items. The first launch also walks every player through a tutorial before the lobby opens, which BGMI veterans will want to tap through quickly.
There is a gentle nudge to download more, too. A line at the bottom of the Recommended Resource Pack page says some rewards can only be collected once the recommended resources are in place, so players who want everything will still end up pulling in a few hundred megabytes over time.
The 291.2MB Recommended Resource Pack, with rewards tied to downloading it. Screenshot: TalkEsport.
None of this touched the match itself. Matchmaking took seconds, Erangel loaded without stutters, and the familiar rhythm of drop, loot, drive and fight felt the same as it does in the main game. The build we played was version 4.7.0.21787, with KRAFTON’s Ban Pan Security System 3.0 running its scan on the loading screen.
Our Take Before the 10 December Launch
On the strength of one full match in each game, BGMI Air is in better shape than the noise on X suggests. Ping stayed flat, ads never showed up, the small install let us play first and download later, and on our phone it ran smoother than the main game. The trade is a plainer lobby and, by most accounts, no high refresh support, which matters far less on the entry-level phones Air is aimed at.
The full game launches in India on 10 December on Android and iOS, according to Digit, after passing 14 million pre-registrations on Google Play, and you can log in with your existing BGMI ID. If you want to try it now, our step-by-step guide to the open beta download covers the Play Store route, and every update lands on our BGMI Air page. Our Hindi video puts both games side by side, and a budget-phone test is next.
The post BGMI Air vs BGMI on the Same Phone: 60 FPS vs 40, Zero Ads and No 2.4GB Download appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: LiberNovo Omni SE Chair Review
items.content:
Back in June, I reviewed the LiberNovo Omni Pro and walked away thoroughly impressed by its dynamic ergonomics, but the eye-watering £1,200 price tag was a massive hurdle. Enter the Omni SE, a stripped-down manual version that cuts the price down to just over £700 while keeping the core frame and dynamic support intact. On paper, shedding the motors, battery, and cooling fans to save nearly £500 sounds like the ideal compromise. But did LiberNovo cut the right corners to make this ergonomic design more accessible, or does the loss of premium materials spoil the experience?
Timestamps:
00:00 Intro
00:58 Price details
02:09 Differences vs the Pro
02:38 Back adjustment
03:30 Overall comfort
04:31 Arm rest discussion
05:48 Back support is great
06:26 The biggest downgrade?
07:47 Discussion vs Fractal Refine 2
08:25 Closing thoughts
Specifications:
Model: LiberNovo Omni SE Dynamic Ergonomic Chair.
Target Price: £786 (Bundle with StepSync footrest) / £79 standalone footrest add-on.
Backrest: Bionic FlexFit frame with 8 flexible panels and 16 spherical pivots.
Lumbar Adjustment: Manual precision screw dial (40mm depth travel).
Recline Mechanism: 5-position SynchroLink recline (105°, 115°, 125°, 135°, 160°).
Seat Cushion: Multi-density contoured foam (firmer rear support, softer front edge).
Armrests: Linked 4D dynamic armrests (recline in sync with the backrest).
Headrest: Detachable, multi-angle dynamic neck support.
Upholstery: Tensioned micro-linen fabric (Obsidian Black only).
Max Load Rating: 136 kg (300 lbs) BIFMA X5.1 certified.
Electronics: None (100% mechanical design).
Closing Thoughts
Ever since I reviewed the LiberNovo Omni Pro five months ago, it has remained my everyday chair whenever I am not testing another model for review. It is simply the most comfortable seat I have ever used, which made testing the Omni SE a matter of seeing just how much of that magic survives a massive £484 price drop.
The good news is that the core ergonomic experience is remarkably close to the flagship. The multi-density foam seat cushion retains the firmer foam at the rear for spinal support and softer foam near the front edge to avoid cutting off circulation to your legs. The neck support remains my absolute gold standard in the chair market, effortlessly adjustable and perfectly positioned whether sitting bolt upright or kicked all the way back in the 160-degree recline. I also remain a huge fan of the linked armrests; while they can occasionally shift if you bump them while standing up, their effortless fluidity means I actually use them across a wider variety of tasks. The optional £79 footrest is equally fantastic. Going fully manual means there are no batteries to recharge or motors to worry about down the road.
However, the corners that LiberNovo cut are hard to ignore. The manual lumbar wheel is effective at dialing in depth, but it is awkwardly small and pinched my fingers almost every time I reached behind to adjust it. The upholstery is also disappointing. Dropping the Pro's premium Danish Gabriel fabric for this Obsidian Black material results in a seat that feels cheaper and more plasticky. The fabric sits looser on the frame, breathes noticeably worse during warmer days, and the dark finish grabs onto skin oils and pet hair like a magnet.
Compared to something like the £500 Fractal Refine 2, which prioritized tank-like, pristine build quality over adaptable posture, the Omni SE is the opposite. It delivers world-class, dynamic ergonomic support, but encases it in materials that feel out of place on a chair costing over £700. If your singular priority is spinal comfort and versatile sitting positions, the Omni SE delivers nearly everything the £1,200 Pro model does for hundreds of pounds less. But if tactile material quality and aesthetics matter to you, the fabric downgrade is a tough pill to swallow.
You can buy the LiberNovo Omni SE for £786 (bundled with footrest) HERE.
Pros:
Delivers the same world-class dynamic ergonomic comfort as the £1,200 Omni Pro.
Nearly £500 cheaper than the motorized flagship model.
Multi-density foam cushion provides superb long-session comfort without pinching legs.
Industry-leading neck support that easily adapts to upright or reclined postures.
Fully mechanical design eliminates charging cables, batteries, and motor reliability concerns.
Fluid armrests dynamically shift in tandem with the backrest recline.
Cons:
Upholstery feels distinctly cheaper, looser, and less breathable than the Pro model.
Black fabric and plastic trim attract skin oils and pet hair aggressively.
Manual lumbar wheel is small and awkwardly placed, making it easy to pinch your fingers.
Single colorway option makes the chair look visually heavy.
KitGuru says: The LiberNovo Omni SE brings the phenomenal dynamic ergonomics of its £1,200 sibling down to a much more accessible price, but the compromised, plasticky fabrics hold it back from true greatness.

Square Enix is bringing cross-region Data Center travel to Final Fantasy XIV
items.content:
The back-end infrastructure of your average MMO is a bit of a double edged sword. While they allow for massive numbers of concurrent players populating a single world, such MMOs typically require the use of dozens of region-locked servers in order to maintain stability. In an interesting move, Square Enix have now announced that they will be enabling cross-region Data Center Travel in Final Fantasy XIV– albeit only temporarily for now.
In anticipation of Final Fantasy XIV’s upcoming patch 8.0, the team at Square Enix announced that they would be changing how their game servers operate, taking to their blog to write:
“To help alleviate server congestion following the release of Patch 8.0, we will be enabling cross-region Data Center Travel between the North American and European data centers during scheduled maintenance on Tuesday, December 1, 2026.”
Full details on the technical reasons behind this decision can be found HERE, but according to the team:
“We have received ongoing feedback from players wishing to travel between the North American and European data centers, and many players in both regions are able to communicate in English even when it is not their first language. Taking these factors into consideration, we have decided to temporarily open travel between these two data centers as part of our efforts to mitigate congestion.“
While it is somewhat disappointing to see cross-region support being a temporary addition, Square Enix did note that they will be listening to fan feedback and thus will “carefully evaluate the possibility of permanently enabling travel between the North American and European data centers, as well as opening travel between other physical data centers.”
In a world which has standardised cross-play, cross-saves and all other forms of multiplayer conveniences, it is encouraging to see the likes of FFXIV trying to make its own experience more seamless.

BGMI Air Supported Devices: Minimum Requirements and Phones That Can Run It
items.content:
BGMI Air needs only 1.5GB of RAM and an Adreno 306 GPU or better to run on Android, which puts it within reach of phones that cannot handle the full version of Battlegrounds Mobile India. On iPhone and iPad, you need iOS 13 or later.
KRAFTON India built BGMI Air for players with entry level phones and limited storage, and the game launches on 10 December 2026. This guide lists the confirmed BGMI Air requirements, which phones are likely to qualify and how you can check your own device before launch.
What are the BGMI Air minimum requirements?
KRAFTON has confirmed two hardware requirements for Android: at least 1.5GB of RAM and an Adreno 306 GPU or higher. It has not announced a minimum Android version. For Apple devices, the App Store listing specifies iOS 13 or later.
Compare that with the full BGMI, which now takes well over 10GB on many phones once all resource packs are downloaded. BGMI Air starts at around 1GB on Android, and extra content packs are optional, so you can remove them if your storage runs low.
Which Android phones support BGMI Air?
KRAFTON has not released an official list of supported phones. Any Android phone that meets both requirements, 1.5GB of RAM and an Adreno 306 or newer GPU, should be able to install and run the game.
The Adreno 306 is the graphics chip inside Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 410 and 412, entry level processors from 2014. That means almost every Qualcomm powered phone released since then clears the GPU requirement, including budget lines such as:
Below are popular phones in India that meet both requirements, grouped by type. Each one has at least 2GB of RAM in its base variant and an Adreno GPU at or above the Adreno 306 level.
Budget Snapdragon phones that support BGMI Air
Older low end phones that meet the requirements
BGMI Air is aimed at phones that struggle with the full game, and many older budget phones still clear the minimum bar. These models have Adreno GPUs above the 306 level and at least 2GB of RAM.
MediaTek and Exynos phones likely to support BGMI Air
Phones with MediaTek or Samsung Exynos processors use Mali GPUs instead of Adreno. KRAFTON has only named an Adreno chip, so these models are not confirmed, but their GPUs are far more powerful than the Adreno 306 and should run the game.
Very old or ultra budget phones with Unisoc processors and 1GB of RAM are the most likely to miss out. If your phone is not listed, check its RAM and processor against the requirements, or try the open beta.
Which iPhones and iPads support BGMI Air?
BGMI Air runs on any iPhone or iPad that can install iOS 13 or later. That covers iPhone 6s and iPhone SE (first generation) and every newer model, along with iPads that support iPadOS 13 or later.
The iOS download is larger at around 1.8GB, so make sure you have a few gigabytes free before installing, as updates and optional packs can add to that.
How to check if your phone supports BGMI Air
The quickest way to check is through the official store listing. If your device is not compatible, the store will tell you before you download.
Open the Google Play Store or Apple App Store on your phone
Search for BGMI Air or Battlegrounds Mobile India Air
Check whether the Install or Pre-register button is available
If you see a message saying your device is not compatible, your phone does not meet the requirements
On Android, check your RAM and processor under Settings, then About Phone
You can also join the BGMI Air open beta on Android to test the game on your phone before the full launch.
What FPS can you expect on supported phones?
Meeting the minimum requirements means BGMI Air will run, not that it will run at high frame rates. Phones near the 1.5GB RAM floor will usually be limited to the lower frame rate settings, while mid range phones can reach Extreme, which is 60 FPS. The full breakdown is in our guide to how much FPS BGMI Air supports.
If your phone already runs the full BGMI smoothly, you do not need BGMI Air, though it can still save storage. For players chasing the highest frame rates, the main game supports more devices at 90 and 120 FPS, as listed in our guide to BGMI 120 FPS supported devices.
Can you use your BGMI account on BGMI Air?
Yes. BGMI Air supports existing BGMI accounts, so your progress, items and friends carry over without a transfer. Players on BGMI Air can also play alongside players using the full BGMI.
BGMI Air passed 14 million pre-registrations on Google Play before launch, a figure KRAFTON highlighted in its Q3 2026 results. Official updates are posted on the Battlegrounds Mobile India website.

items.title: Another Big PS5 Game Will Be Delisted in the Coming Months
CDPR compares the jump between The Witcher 3 and 4 to GTA VI
items.content:
With Grand Theft Auto VI officially out and available for all (on console) to enjoy, the most-anticipated games list has been shifted, with CD Projekt Red’s The Witcher 4 likely now sitting at the top of most people’s wishlists. With more than a decade in between releases, CDPR have promised that – just as is the case with GTA VI – the jump in quality between The Witcher 3 and 4 will be substantial.
During CDPR’s latest earnings call, joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski was unsurprisingly asked about the recently-released juggernaut that is GTA VI. In tying it into the studio’s own output, one investor asked “How do you assess the scale of the technological and qualitative leap from GTA 5 to GTA 6? Do you believe a similar leap is possible with The Witcher 4?”
Rather humorously, Nowakowski began by stating: “First of all, obviously this is a call about us, not about Rockstar, but I do understand the connection here.”
In discussing this ‘connection’ the CEO continued, “We believe there's going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4 – I think so, yes. It's been 11 years, we are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game, so yes you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4.”
In looking at the entire Witcher trilogy, each successive game has been a significant improvement when compared to the last. That said, there are still plenty of avenues with which The Witcher 4 could improve over TW3 (and even Cyberpunk 2077), from world simulation to NPCs; combat; immersion and more.
All that being said, trying to compare anything to GTA VI is a bit of a losing battle, given that Rockstar was afforded a near-limitless amount of time and budget thanks to GTA V selling almost a quarter of a billion copies. Regardless, it is exciting to see the team pushing themselves in this regard.
KitGuru says: What do you think of CDPR’s comments? What areas would you like to see the team focus on most for The Witcher 4? Between it and Cyberpunk 2, which will offer a bigger leap across the board? Let us know down below.

MrBeast Gaming Overtakes IShowSpeed as GTA 6 Launch Week Views Hit 1.77 Billion
items.content:
MrBeast Gaming has overtaken IShowSpeed as the YouTube channel gaining the most views from Grand Theft Auto VI’s launch week. MrBeast’s gaming channel had added 269.9 million public views by 25 November, against 232.9 million for IShowSpeed, according to PUNKSQUAD’s GTA VI launch tracker. Speed led comfortably for the first few days, but a huge two-day surge early this week carried MrBeast Gaming past him.
The tracker follows 127 channels streaming the game, and together they have picked up 1.77 billion public views since 18 November, the day before launch. Those channels have a combined 1.15 billion subscribers, which gives a sense of how far GTA VI has spread across YouTube in a single week. The surge on YouTube follows a record on Twitch as well, as our report on the game’s 7.1 million peak viewers at launch covers.
How MrBeast Gaming overtook IShowSpeed
IShowSpeed made the much faster start of the two. His channel added 37.4 million views in the first daily snapshot after launch and another 61.3 million in the next, so he was close to 100 million before MrBeast Gaming had reached 30 million. By the snapshot on 22 November, Speed still led by 138.7 million to 94.7 million.
The gap then closed in just two days. MrBeast Gaming added 74.7 million views in the 23 November snapshot and 71.4 million in the next, the two biggest single-day gains of any channel on the list all week. That run took it from 94.7 million to 240.8 million and past Speed, who added 40.8 million and 35.4 million over the same two days.
The lead has kept growing since then, with 29.1 million more views for MrBeast Gaming in the 25 November snapshot against 18.0 million for Speed. MrBeast Gaming is the gaming offshoot of MrBeast, whose main channel is the most subscribed on YouTube. It now has 62.8 million subscribers of its own, almost level with Speed’s 63.3 million. The main channel has been setting records of its own this year too, as our report on his record-breaking grocery store challenge shows.
The rest of the GTA 6 YouTube top ten
Techno Gamerz sits third with 112.2 million, well clear of a tight group below him. IGN’s channel is fourth on 76.8 million, just ahead of Kai Cenat Live on 72.5 million, while DarkViperAU, best known for his GTA V speedruns and commentary, is sixth with 69.4 million. Kai Cenat’s GTA streams have made headlines of their own this month, as our report on his GTA marathon sets out.
Typical Gamer, YOLO AVENTURAS, Ludwig and Windah Basudara complete the top ten, each with more than 50 million. Spanish-language creators form the strongest group further down, with nine of the top 30 channels making videos in Spanish, including YOLO AVENTURAS, TheGrefg, JuegaGerman, VEGETTA777 and Auron. The top 30 also includes SQUEEZIE from France, Renato Garcia from Brazil and Windah Basudara from Indonesia, so the audience is spread well beyond English-language YouTube.
.@MrBeast goes No 1
GTA VI Launch – YouTube Net Public Views since 18 November 2026 (Top 125) #GTA6 #GTAIV
1. MrBeast Gaming | +240,798,649
2. @ishowspeedsui – IShowSpeed | +214,909,782
3. @technogamerzyt – Techno Gamerz | +112,153,095
4. Kai Cenat Live |… pic.twitter.com/7RxWLJ7D5P
— PUNKSQUAD (@PUNKSQUADcom) November 24, 2026
Rockstar Games sits 13th with its own channel on 35.0 million, although it was only added to the tracker on 21 November. MrBeast Gaming has gained almost eight times as much over the week, and the top two channels together account for more than a quarter of the 1.77 billion total. Creators, rather than the publisher, are doing most of the work of putting GTA VI in front of YouTube viewers.
What the 1.77 billion figure actually counts
The figures measure the change in each channel’s total public view count, not views on GTA VI videos alone. A channel that posted other videos during launch week gets credit for those views too, so the numbers show which channels gained the most attention rather than exactly how many people watched GTA VI. Channels added after 18 November are counted from the day they signed up, which is why Rockstar Games and Windah Basudara have no figures for the first days.
The snapshots are taken once a day, which can also make the figures lumpy. Techno Gamerz, for example, shows no gain in three of the seven daily snapshots, but jumps of 52.3 million on 21 November and more than 25 million on each of 23 and 24 November. Even with those limits, the tracker is one of the clearest side-by-side pictures of which creators are winning the GTA VI launch on YouTube.
The game itself keeps setting records away from YouTube as well. It became the biggest launch in PlayStation history in its first days, as our report on the PlayStation launch record covers, and our launch week recap rounds up every other milestone so far. GTA VI launched on 19 November on PS5 and Xbox Series X and S, according to Rockstar’s GTA VI site.
