items.title: Can you return to Jason’s Key Lento house in GTA 6?
items.content:
For the first 25% of the main story in Grand Theft Auto 6, you play as Jason, who’s living out of a house right on the coast in Key Lento. The house belongs to Brian Heder, Jason’s boss, but he’s allowed to stay there as long as he keeps working. The house itself is a bit of a work in progress, as Jason needs to do some chores before Lucia comes home. However, after some sweat is shed, Jason’s house in Key Lento looks pretty decent in GTA 6.
Following the events of Chapter 1, though, the house is in a much different state. If you’ve completed Chapter 1, then you might be wondering if the Key Lento house can be returned to, especially considering you had some money stashed away there. Below, you can see exactly what happens if you go back to the safehouse during Chapter 2 and beyond in GTA 6.
Warning: There are spoilers for the main story in GTA 6 below.
Key Takeaways
Jason’s safehouse in Key Lento is your main base of operations in Chapter 1
The house burns down following the events of Chapter 1, leaving it in a state of ruin
The area around the house in Key Lento is marked in red in Chapter 2 due to the police presence
Table of contents
Key Takeaways
How to return to Jason’s safehouse in GTA 6
What happens when you explore the burned down house in GTA 6?
How to return to Jason’s safehouse in GTA 6
During the events of Chapter 1, which concludes with Jason and Lucia fighting their way out of a hospital against Mendez’s men, the Key Lento house burns to the ground. The owners of the hard drive that Jason and Lucia stole want the item back, and they burn the house down in order to get it.
Naturally, this is a major blow, both to Jason and Lucia and to you as the player. GTA 6 emphasizes saving money in the house’s floorboard stash, so you might have saved a tidy sum of cash before the house burns down. However, following Chapter 1, the entire area around Jason’s safehouse is marked in red, which indicates a major police presence.
The location of Jason’s burned down house in Key Lento. Screenshot by esports.gg
This is basically the game’s way of telling you it’s not safe to return to the house. However, you can fully return to the Key Lento house when there are cops around it. You can also wait until the back half of GTA 6, when the police have left the area entirely, giving you free rein to explore the remains.
What happens when you explore the burned down house in GTA 6?
If you decide to return to the Key Lento house after it’s burned down, you’ll find some interesting Easter Eggs and items.
SPOILER…
You can go back to Jasons burned Safehouse and collect the old pictures and 5k pic.twitter.com/QjvnOCwIwO
— Jesse 🎱 (@DjoJesse) November 20, 2026
For starters, you can head back to the upper floor of the house and find your stash money totally intact. It’s marked as the “Rainy Day Fund,” and it’s located in the middle of the bedroom. You’ll also find photos in the stash that you can take. Unfortunately, your Rainy Day Fund only has $5,000 in it, even if you deposited more there during Chapter 1. If you deposited less, that exact amount will be in the stash.
As for what else is at the safehouse, if you head down the front steps and look underneath them, you’ll find Dolores, your snake, all tucked in a new home. Dolores managed to escape the fire and set up a new life for herself under the remains of the burned house. You’ll get different voicelines about seeing Dolores if you visit the house as Jason or Lucia. Dolores was Jason’s original pet, so he’ll be happier to see the snake than Lucia.
And that’s everything that you can see and do at Jason’s Key Lento house after it’s been burned down. It’s not much, but at least some of your stash stays intact, and Dolores made it out safely.

items.title: Xbox’s Project  Helix reportedly began life as a Steam-enabled gaming PC
items.content:
Just days after Xbox executives stressed that Project Helix should not be viewed as a gaming PC, a new report claims earlier plans for the system were far more ambitious. According to Windows Central, Microsoft originally envisioned Helix as a Steam-enabled PC-console hybrid that would also remove the paywall for online multiplayer.
According to Windows Central's Jez Corden, the original vision for Project Helix dates back to the leadership era of Phil Spencer and Sarah Bond. Sources familiar with Microsoft's plans claim the console was initially conceived as a full gaming PC capable of running Windows games and storefronts like Steam, while also retaining compatibility with Xbox's existing console library.
Rather than functioning as a traditional console, Helix was reportedly intended to work in a similar fashion to the recently announced Xbox Ally handheld. Users would boot into an Xbox-style full-screen interface but retain access to the Windows desktop underneath, allowing them to install additional storefronts and PC software.
One of the more surprising claims in the report concerns online multiplayer. According to Windows Central, Microsoft's original plans would have removed the requirement for an Xbox Game Pass Core subscription to access online multiplayer. The logic was simple enough: if Helix was effectively a PC, it would be difficult to justify charging players for multiplayer access while also giving them access to platforms like Steam, which don't impose additional online play fees.
The report also suggests that Microsoft's thinking may have changed since then. As we discussed last week, Xbox executives have recently been keen to frame Helix as a console that can play PC games rather than a gaming PC that happens to play Xbox titles. If Windows Central's sources are accurate, Helix may have started life as something much closer to a gaming PC than Xbox would like people to believe today.

Fans have brought multiplayer to The Last of Us Part II Remastered on PC
items.content:
A new fan-made multiplayer mod for The Last of Us Part II Remastered has launched on PC just months after Sony shut down a similar community project. Known as Twelve Weeks, the mod introduces 4v4 team-based multiplayer inspired by the Factions mode from the original game.
According to the mod's website (via DSOG), up to eight players face off in 4v4 matches as either the WLF or the Seraphites. Currently, there are two modes available: Supply Raid tasks teams with depleting enemy reinforcements, and Interrogation requires questioning downed foes to locate and raid their safe.
Twelve Weeks includes eight preset classes, alongside six custom loadout slots built around a 13-point system. Players can scavenge resources to craft items such as Molotovs, bombs, shivs and medkits, while earned parts can be spent on armour and weapon upgrades. The mod also adapts The Last of Us Part II's melee system, incorporating dodges, counters and a variety of melee weapons.
The mod's namesake comes from its twelve-week clan campaign system. Each match advances the in-game calendar by a day, with players gathering supplies to support survivors, unlock cosmetic rewards and complete missions. Twelve maps from Part II are currently supported, while players who own The Last of Us Part I can optionally import the Bookstore and Plaza maps through a dedicated launcher tool.
Online matchmaking is already available through in-game lobbies, complete with party queues, anti-cheat measures and servers located in Europe and North America. Private matches are not currently available, although the developers say they are planned for a future update.

GTA 6 gets its first post-launch patch
items.content:
GTA 6 has now been out for a few days and while the launch-day version was fairly strong for a game of this size, there were some lingering issues not squashed before release. Now, the very first patch is rolling out, aiming to fix up a few problems – including autosaves not working as intended.
Just a few days after launch, GTA 6 has received its first update on Xbox Series X|S and PS5. While Rockstar hasn't introduced any major gameplay changes, the update does fix several issues reported by players since launch. According to Rockstar's patch notes, the update fixes an issue that could prevent the game from autosaving correctly, as well as a few crash-causing bugs.
The full patch notes from Rockstar can be seen below:
Fixed several issues that caused the game to crash
Fixed an issue that resulted in the weather not changing for extended periods
Fixed an issue that resulted in the game not autosaving correctly
Fixed several issues that resulted in phone calls not triggering correctly including those that progressed the story or unlocked mission content
Fixed an issue that resulted in the player being unable to lose their Wanted Level
Fixed an issue that resulted in the player being unable to use the deadlift bar in the Gym
Fixed an issue that resulted in partners not handing over bags so that players could sell them to fences
There are still a few things I'd personally like to see Rockstar address in future updates after spending dozens of hours with the game over the past few days. For starters, I don't think players should be handed “psycho” points for defending themselves against NPCs who initiated a physical confrontation or pulled a weapon first.
My biggest gripe at the moment, however, is the vignette effect while driving. At night, the effect becomes incredibly aggressive, leaving a large portion of the screen shrouded in darkness around your vehicle. I find it more distracting than immersive, particularly on OLED displays where “true black” really means true black. Hopefully Rockstar gives players the option to tone it down in a future update.
I'd also like Rockstar to speed up vehicle entry animations in certain situations. When you're trying to escape the scene of a robbery, Jason and Lucia can sometimes take their sweet time getting into a car. I've ended up in more than a few unwanted police chases that probably could have been avoided if they'd stopped faffing about and got in the vehicle.

items.title: Halo fans finally get a look at the cancelled battle royale project
items.content:
Over the course of 2024 and 2025, we repeatedly heard reports of a Halo battle royale game in development at support studio Certain Affinity. The project, reportedly codenamed “Tatanka”, was eventually cancelled, although newly discovered concept art gives us a small peek at what was being planned.
As spotted by Insider Gaming, the artwork was recently shared to ArtStation by former Certain Affinity environment artist Jason Lavoie under the title “Cancelled Project – World Building”. While Lavoie never specifically names Tatanka or Halo, we can see some remnants of Halo's visual flavour throughout the artwork.
The pieces fit together reasonably well. Lavoie worked at Certain Affinity in 2020, around the same time Tatanka is believed to have entered development, and references working on an unannounced cancelled project. Previous reports have also linked Certain Affinity to the Halo battle royale project before it underwent several major changes behind the scenes.
The artwork itself showcases a range of environments, including rocky ravines, ancient structures, abandoned facilities and cave systems. Personally, I think some of these environments look closer to something I'd expect to see in Destiny rather than Halo, particularly the overgrown ruins, but nonetheless, this was concept art, and the art direction would have gone through revisions and refinement over the course of development. More often than not, environments seen in concept art aren't present in a final product.
Halo fans spent years hearing rumours about Tatanka without ever getting a proper look at the project itself. Even if these images date from a very early stage of development, they're the closest we've come to seeing what Tatanka actually looked like.

items.title: Nvidia Adds Roughly $1 Trillion in Value as Jensen Huang Returns as CEO
items.content:
Nvidia added roughly $1 trillion in market value in the first hour and a half of trading on Monday, after its board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive 11 days after he resigned. The shares were up 33.76% at $167.91 at 11:11am ET, which is 4:11pm UTC, according to Google Finance. That lifted the chipmaker’s market value to about $4.04 trillion, from roughly $3 trillion at Friday’s close of $125.53.
The jump reverses a large part of the slide that followed Huang’s exit on 12 November. Friday’s close left the stock within a dollar or so of its 52-week low of $124.50, and almost half below its 52-week high of $243.37. The board’s decision, announced before the US market opened, is covered in full in our report on Huang’s reinstatement.
How much Nvidia added in a morning
The shares opened at $167.04 and traded between $156.93 and $171.50 in the first part of the session. Volume had already passed 400 million shares by late morning, well above the stock’s average of about 225 million a day. With about 24.1 billion shares outstanding, each dollar on the share price is worth roughly $24 billion in market value.
On those numbers, the morning’s rise of more than $42 a share added about $1 trillion to Nvidia’s value. The figure will move through the day, but it is an unusually large one-day move even for a company of Nvidia’s size. It also suggests how much of Nvidia’s recent fall investors tied to the leadership crisis rather than to the business itself. The gain on Monday helped lift the wider US market at the open, according to our earlier report.
Why Nvidia’s board brought Jensen Huang back
The board’s change of heart took just six days. Nvidia’s 12 November announcement, also filed with the SEC as a Form 8-K exhibit, said Huang had resigned as president, chief executive and director with immediate effect. It named chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while the board began a search for a permanent successor, looking at internal and external candidates. Huang left after reports of extramarital affairs, including one with a businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for China, according to Reuters, and Beijing has denied the allegation.
As recently as 17 November, the board said it did not intend to bring him back, as our report on the board’s rejection covered. Monday’s filing with the SEC said the board voted unanimously for his return after “a series of discussions and meetings” with him. It said it had received input from “senior levels of the United States government” and was confident his return “poses no national security risk”.
Washington’s view had been far from settled a week earlier. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in mid-November that Nvidia needed “a dramatic shakeup” and an outside chief executive, as our Bessent report explains. Board chair Harvey Jones said on Monday that the board believes Huang “is the right person to lead NVIDIA”. Pressure from outside the company had been building too, with a petition calling for Huang’s return passing 175,000 signatures, as our petition report covered.
What changes at Nvidia with Huang’s return
Huang returns with more oversight around him than before. A committee made up solely of independent directors is still investigating the reports that he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, and the board said that investigation “will proceed to conclusion” with his cooperation. Nvidia is also hiring a new chief compliance officer, who will report to the board’s governance committee.
A separate National Security and Export Control Committee, also made up of independent directors, will oversee trade compliance and national security risks. Our report on that committee covers why it was set up. Kress returns to her role as chief financial officer, and Jones stays on as chair, a post Nvidia created when Huang stepped down.
For gamers, Nvidia is still best known for its GeForce graphics cards and drivers, even though AI data centres now bring in most of its revenue. The company shipped a driver hotfix for excessive SSD writes during Huang’s absence, as our GeForce hotfix report covered. Huang said he takes the role back “with the greatest humility and renewed commitment”. Nvidia publishes its filings and results on its investor relations site, and its shares were trading near $168 at 11:11am ET on Monday.

In the latest Deltarune development newsletter, Fox says Chapter 6 is now a “structurally complete draft” that can be played from start to finish. According to Fox, all maps, battles and story events are now in place, with the exception of one optional event that remains unfinished.
Fox says localisation work and preliminary testing should now begin. However, some scenes and presentation elements still require additional work before the chapter is ready to enter full testing. Despite describing Chapter 6 as a relatively short chapter, Fox says he has no intention of rushing it out the door.
Development of Chapter 7 has also begun. Team members who have completed their Chapter 6 work have already started moving onto the final chapter. Fox has also started sharing Chapter 7's story with the team, although he stopped reading before revealing the ending.
Deltarune is Toby Fox's follow-up to Undertale, releasing its story across multiple chapters rather than as a single game. Five chapters have been released so far, with Chapters 6 and 7 expected to complete the game.

Mark Darrah says BioWare was repeatedly forced to choose between bad options
items.content:
Former Dragon Age executive producer Mark Darrah has argued that many of BioWare's most controversial decisions were made under pressure to meet financial targets, likening EA's management style to repeatedly forcing studios to choose between bad options.
As spotted by PC Gamer, Darrah made the comments during a discussion with YouTuber Pembridge. While Darrah stopped short of saying EA directly forced BioWare into specific decisions, he argued that the publisher repeatedly pushed the studio into situations where none of the available options were particularly good.
To illustrate the point, Darrah recalled a description of EA's management style that had been shared with him by another developer:
“Someone, I won't name them just so I don't get them in trouble, once said that EA doesn't shoot you, it puts a gun on the table and then comes in everyday and asks you if you'll shoot yourself, and they just keep coming in over and over until eventually you just are like ‘Ugh, fine. Just stop bugging me about it, I'll do it.'”
Darrah went on to argue that decisions such as developing Dragon Age 2 on a compressed schedule, adopting the Frostbite engine and shipping Anthem were influenced by pressure to meet financial targets. While EA could claim those decisions ultimately belonged to BioWare, Darrah argues the alternatives facing the studio were hardly any better.
“EA can legitimately say ‘we didn't make BioWare do this, they chose to do this', but if you dig underneath that statement the reality is that the options on the table were all terrible. We chose the least terrible of the options.”

items.title: Unreal Engine 6 drops Blueprints as Epic doubles down on AI-assisted development
items.content:
One of Unreal Engine's most widely used features won't be making the jump to Unreal Engine 6. Epic Games has confirmed that Blueprints will be absent from both UE6 Early Access and the full UE6 release, with the company instead betting on Verse and AI-assisted conversion tools.
As spotted by PC Gamer, Epic's Marcus Wassmer confirmed the change in a recent Unreal Engine update. While Epic previously said Blueprints and the Actor Gameplay Framework would coexist with Unreal Engine 6 during the transition from UE5, that is no longer the plan. Instead, gameplay systems in UE6 will be built using the Verse programming language and the new Scene Graph framework.
Epic claims recent advances in AI have changed its approach. According to Wassmer, Epic now believes AI can handle much of the work involved in converting UE5 Blueprint projects to UE6. Epic also pointed to its ongoing AI-assisted efforts to convert Fortnite's Blueprint library to Verse as evidence that the process can work at scale.
The decision is unlikely to go down well with all developers. Blueprints have long served as a bridge between designers, artists and programmers, enabling non-coders to build gameplay systems through a visual scripting interface. Former Valve writer Chet Faliszek recently argued that tools like Blueprints create an important middle ground between purely technical development and traditional design work, warning that replacing them with either code or AI prompting could make game creation less accessible for some teams.
Epic has stressed that Blueprints are not being removed from Unreal Engine 5 and maintains that upgrading projects to UE6 will remain straightforward. Whether developers will be as enthusiastic about that approach as Epic remains to be seen.
KitGuru says: Blueprints became one of Unreal Engine's defining features for a reason. Do you think Epic is making the right call by betting so heavily on AI-assisted development?

Hizuki of the Ginza Patrol Is New Manga From Mission: Yozakura Family Creator
items.content:
Shueisha announced the new manga from Mission: Yozakura Family creator Hitsuji Gondaira is Hizuki of the Ginza Patrol. It is now running in Weekly Shonen Jump as a new series. The first chapter is live worldwide, with the English ones available on Manga Plus and Viz Media sites. This comes after the previous manga and its anime adaptation appeared worldwide.
Like the previous piece from the mangaka behind Mission: Yozakura Family, Hizuki of the Ginza Patrol is another action series from the creator that involves an individual dealing with serious threats. However, this one is a Meiji period piece set after the Boshin civil war. A hero from that fight named Osamu Hizuki decided that going forward, he’ll join the police force to protect people. He works alongside Rin Inokuma, one of the first female cops. This also means he’ll get involved in her quest to figure out the truth behind her mother’s death. While he seems a bit unorthodox, the first chapter shows he’s also incredibly observant, intelligent, kind, and strong.
While Mission: Yozakura Family is the most famous manga from creator Hitsuji Gondaira, we have seen other new series from the mangaka before. There were one-shots and a contribution to a One Piece short story compilation. However, since the previous Mission: Yozakura Family did run between 2019 and 2025 and ended up lasting 29 volumes, it has been a while since the mangaka prepared any new series.
The first chapter of the new Weekly Shonen Jump manga series Hizuki of the Ginza Patrol is available worldwide, and chapter 2 will appear in English on November 29, 2026. The Mission: Yozakura Family is available in English via Viz Media in North America, and the anime is on Hulu and Disney+.

items.title: Rob Run Implements Jail Time and Purchase Restrictions on Servers to Combat Cheaters
items.content:
Rob Run is taking a series of much-needed measures to combat the ever-increasing cheater population that has been plaguing the title since its early access launch, including server restrictions based on players’ accumulated jail time and in-game purchases.
Unless you’ve been living under a rock for the past couple of weeks, chances are you’ve probably heard of Rob Run, the brand-new crime extraction shooter from Kefir that went into early access on November 4, 2026. The title has drawn widespread praise from gamers, but due to it being a free-to-play title, it has fallen victim to one of the biggest problems facing modern multiplayer games: rampant cheating.
ROB RUN IS OUT NOW ON STEAM!
The wait is over.
ROB RUN has officially launched, and the streets of Looty Bay are waiting for new heroes. Not that anyone stays a hero around here for long.
Catch you on the wrong side of the law.https://t.co/NRVhwwcoSG
— ROBRUN (@ROBRUNGame) November 4, 2026
Prominent streamers like TheBurntPeanut, Cloakzy, and Hutch have reported running into multiple cheaters over the course of the past several days, with some clips showing players using aimbots, wallhacks, and item duplication glitches to wipe out their entire squads before they could even react.
Fortunately, the developers behind Rob Run seem to be aware of the issue, and they’ve been taking steps to address it before it gets any worse.
Through an update on November 23, 2026, Rob Run has deployed a patch that implements restrictions on servers based on players’ total accumulated jail time or in-game purchases.
“We’ve blocked more than 200,000 accounts so far,” a Rob Run community manager said in a statement on the game’s official Discord server. “However, we know that in a free-to-play game, a standard ban isn’t enough. Cheaters can quickly create a new account and jump right back in. To combat this, we’re exploring hardware bans. Because separate servers with stricter access requirements can be launched much faster, we plan to roll those out first.”
As confirmed by the developers, players will now require either a minimum amount of jail time or a certain total of in-game purchases to enter specific servers. Additionally, these restricted servers will have separate matchmaking from standard servers.
“Depending on the server, access will require either a minimum amount of jail time or a certain total of in-game purchases,” they continued. “Players on these restricted servers will be matchmade separately from standard servers, including in Looty Bay. We expect this to drastically reduce ban evasion and limit your encounters with cheaters.”
The approach isn’t without controversy, though. Players have expressed concerns that legitimate newcomers, or people who simply prefer not to spend money in the game, could get caught in the net and be stuck in lobbies filled with cheaters. Veteran players could also run into difficulties when introducing their friends to the game.
These measures are likely to come as part of a broader anti-cheat push that Kefir says will continue to evolve as the game moves toward its full release. How effective Rob Run’s latest update is in combating the cheater infestation in the title still remains to be seen.

items.title: Jensen Huang has been reinstated as Nvidia CEO: 'I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment'
Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
items.content:
Just a week on from Nvidia's board issuing a statement saying it ‘does not intend' to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, the company has changed its tune. Jensen is back as CEO as of today, following “input from senior levels of the United States government”.
In a statement issued today, NVIDIA confirmed that Huang has been reinstated with immediate effect after what the board described as a series of discussions and meetings with the company's founder, as well as “input from senior levels of the United States government”. The statement also says that there is “no national security risk” in reinstating Jensen.
Harvey C. Jones, who just last week said that the board ‘does not intend to' bring Jensen back, is now saying that “the board beleives Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interest of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers”. He adds that the board has “every confidence in Jensen”.
In his own statement, Jensen Huang said “I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution”.
Nvidia's investigation into claims that it was targeted by Chinese intelligence is still on-going, and the company's newly established Export oversight committee will remain in place.

When did FNCS start?
The inaugural Fortnite Champion Series (FNCS) began in August 2019 during Chapter 1 Season X. It featured a Trios format and a staggering $10 million prize pool on the heels of the Fortnite World Cup. This prize pool covered the game’s seven regions: Europe, NA East, NA West, Brazil, Asia, Middle East, and Oceania.

items.title: Jensen Huang Reinstated as CEO of NVIDIA
Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, 11 Days After His Resignation
items.content:
Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, 11 days after he resigned. The board voted unanimously for his return on 23 November, reversing its position from just days earlier that it did not intend to bring him back.
Nvidia shares jumped more than 25% in early trading after the announcement. Interim chief executive Colette Kress will return to her role as chief financial officer.
The board said it reached the decision after “a series of discussions and meetings” with Huang, after which it was satisfied with his “candor and ability to lead NVIDIA”. It also said it had received input from senior levels of the United States government and was confident that Huang’s return poses no national security risk.
Board chair Harvey Jones said Huang is “the right person to lead NVIDIA” and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of the company’s stockholders, employees, partners and customers. The announcement was published in Nvidia’s filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission.
Huang said he was “honored to return” to lead what he called one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. He described the current period as the beginning of a new industrial revolution.
A sharp reversal in a week
The return marks a complete turn from the board’s stance at Nvidia’s earnings call last week. Jones said then that the board did not intend to reinstate Huang, even after Huang said publicly that he would be honoured to return, a decision covered when Nvidia’s board rejected Huang’s offer to come back.
Pressure built quickly after that. A petition to reinstate Huang gathered more than 175,000 signatures, including thousands of people who said they worked at Nvidia. On 22 November, US President Donald Trump wrote on social media that he hoped the board would rehire Huang.
Why Jensen Huang left Nvidia
Huang resigned on 12 November after reports of inappropriate relationships, including one with a woman alleged to have links to Chinese intelligence. Reports also said he had a third relationship with a senior Nvidia employee who reported directly to him.
The national security questions led Nvidia’s board to set up a national security committee as Washington increased its scrutiny of the company’s chip exports. Monday’s statement said the board had received assurances from the US government on that point before voting to bring Huang back.
After his resignation, Kress served as interim chief executive while the board began a search for a permanent leader. That search has now ended, with the company thanking Kress for her service during the transition.
Huang cofounded Nvidia in 1993 and led it for more than three decades, turning a graphics chip maker for video games into the world’s dominant supplier of AI processors. His long run of bets on CUDA and Mellanox helped make Nvidia one of the most valuable companies in the world.
The share price surge on Monday also lifted the wider US market, with the S&P 500 opening sharply higher. Investors had treated Huang’s departure as one of the biggest risks to Nvidia’s roadmap, customer deals and relationships in Washington.
The post Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, 11 Days After His Resignation appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Fan-made MotorStorm PC port aims to revive Pacific Rift
items.content:
An unofficial PC port and fan remaster of the PS3 racing game MotorStorm: Pacific Rift is currently in development. Titled MotorStorm: Ashfall, the project aims to bring the off-road racer to PC with a range of enhancements, while also offering an alternative version powered by Driveclub's graphics technology.
Shared on Reddit by the developer (via DSOG), MotorStorm: Ashfall goes beyond a straight port by introducing features absent from the original release. Players will get Lua modding support, native settings, and expanded language options, as well as a first-person driving view, character customisation, and the ability to build their own lair.
Image credit: keku645
The project also includes an alternative version that uses Driveclub's graphics renderer to overhaul the visuals. This version brings Driveclub's lighting, skies, dynamic weather system, post-processing effects and select driving animations to Pacific Rift. It also adds rain accumulation on windscreens, with wipers clearing away water during races.
The developer also plans to bring tracks from MotorStorm: Monument Valley and Arctic Edge into the game, while adding new shaders, tessellation and dirt and mud buildup on vehicles as races progress. There is currently no release date for MotorStorm: Ashfall.

Review: Pet Shop After Dark Works on the Switch
items.content:
It’s no secret that Pet Shop After Dark is a horror puzzle game. Npckc makes that clear everywhere. The thing is that it is a ver unusual sort of title that worked amazingly well on PCs. The good news is that like the port of Doki Doki Literature Club and other games that can rely on getting into the nitty gritty of things, the Pet Shop After Dark Switch release still “works” and makes the adventure feel special.
Editor’s Note: There will be no spoilers for Pet Shop After Dark below.
A more recent concept in horror stories and creepypastas is that a person needs to follow a handful of set rules or instructions to safely inhabit a space, with disregarding them leading to possible disaster. Pet Shop After Dark begins with an individual arriving at a combination plant and pet shop to tend the flora and fauna while the owner is away. The rules are to water all the plants, feed all the pets, and keep the lights on.
You can probably guess where things are going.
Go Ad-Free With Siliconera+View the site with no ads, be able to provide direct feedback about what we cover, and be automatically entered into our monthly PC game giveaway.Join Siliconera+
Pet Shop After Dark is one of those games where the simplicity belies its true nature and what players are capable of as they play. The tasks are as easy as they sound, and things start out very minimalistic. You are in the pet shop. There are a handful of rooms. One features a bookcase, window, and sofa where the new employee can sleep. Another is an empty room with a bowl. One has a selection of cages and a tank. (The pets are shy! Don’t think about the fact that you can’t see them! Really!) The main room features instructions, plants, and another shelving unit. Tapping some objects let you interact with them. Following the rules nets you certain results.
I don’t want to spoil things, but the nature of Pet Shop After Dark means you need to do certain things in order to solve puzzles and accomplish actions. These are quite clever and involve interacting with everything you can when you get an opportunity and exploring. As you might guess, both with the lights on and off, since you can reveal certain things. This is a short game, one that shouldn’t take more than two hours. (I could see it maybe taking three if someone gets stumped about a next step.) But npckc did a great job of ensuring it feels the same and the puzzle execution works the way we would expect even on a console for the Switch Pet Shop After Dark release. (Though admittedly, it did take me two shifts in the shop to realize how to interact with certain things.)
Images via npckc
Pet Shop After Dark also serves as a perfect example of a game being able to properly convey certain emotions, concepts, and challenges even with a minimalistic presentation. It’s a short adventure. There aren’t a lot of embellishments when it comes to character and environmental design. It’s incredibly stylized and doesn’t use cheap tricks to unnerve a player. It’s just clever!
I will caution folks, however. This is a clever, short game that makes you think and is unnerving, but I wouldn’t consider it as scary or unsettling as Doki Doki Literature Club. It’s a more novel approach to what someone is capable of when designing a thinky thriller.
Pet Shop After Dark remains as strong on the Switch as the horror game did on the PC. Considering how it works, that’s reassuring! It’s still quite effective and tells a good story, and npckc kept it as clever as before.
Pet Shop After Dark is available on the Switch, PS5, Xbox Series X, and PC.

Free OLEDTextFix utility tackles text color fringing on OLED monitors
items.content:
A new free, open-source utility called OLEDTextFix has been released to reduce coloured text fringing on OLED monitors. Rather than tweaking system fonts, the tool uses GPU-based processing to correct issues caused by the unconventional subpixel layouts found on many QD-OLED and WOLED displays.
According to the project's GitHub (via Wccftech) OLEDTextFix works by applying a transparent GPU-rendered overlay across the desktop, aligning text rendering more closely with the physical subpixel layout of the display. The utility includes presets for nine QD-OLED panel classes, alongside RWBG and RGWB WOLED profiles, as well as “Sharp”, “Balanced” and “Smooth” filter modes.
According to the developer's testing, OLEDTextFix can reduce visible colour fringing on QD-OLED panels by between 58% and 71% against dark backgrounds. Those figures come from image-processing simulations rather than independent testing, however. Improvements on WOLED panels are expected to be less dramatic, and early feedback from users has been mixed.
The utility supports Windows 10 version 2004 and newer, as well as Windows 11, using a DirectX 11-compatible GPU. It can also automatically pause when launching fullscreen games. However, the desktop-overlay approach comes with some trade-offs. The developer notes that OLEDTextFix can introduce roughly one frame of latency and reported GPU power consumption increasing by around 40-50W on a Radeon RX 6900 XT during testing.
Experimental HDR and Auto Color Management support have also been added following feedback from users, although HDR functionality remains disabled by default and has yet to undergo extensive testing.
KitGuru says: Text fringing remains one of the few lingering annoyances with certain OLED monitor panels. It'll be interesting to see whether OLEDTextFix becomes the workaround that OLED users actually stick with.

Viral Claim Says GTA 6 Profiles Players for Insurers and Employers, but There Is No Proof
items.content:
A viral claim that Grand Theft Auto VI builds psychological profiles of players and sells them to insurers, lenders and employers has spread across social media, but no evidence has been published to support it. The claim comes from an anonymous account on X that says it belongs to a former senior engine engineer at Rockstar North.
Rockstar Games and its parent company Take-Two Interactive have not commented on the allegations. No documents, network data or technical proof have been shared, and several details in the claim do not match public records about Take-Two.
What the viral GTA 6 data claim says
The post, written in Chinese and shared on 20 November, claims GTA 6 sends gameplay telemetry to an internal Take-Two system called “Lens”. According to the account, Lens records how players use their controllers, including button timing, stick movement and DualSense trigger pressure.
The account claims Lens then scores each player for impulse control, risk tolerance, aggression and spending habits, and links that score to the player’s console account and IP address. It says the profiles go to a Take-Two subsidiary named Vantage Analytics, which allegedly licenses the models to insurance companies, a credit risk firm, a hiring platform and an advertising broker.
Rockstar Games 周三解雇了我。第二天 GTA 6 就发售了
我是 Rockstar North 的高级引擎工程师，从事 RAGE 性能优化。三个月前，我在遥测模块里发现了一条本不该存在的数据管道，而且我能证明它流向了哪里
此刻每一份正在运行的 GTA 6… pic.twitter.com/TGxZ8LTl6A
— make claude (@make_claude) November 20, 2026
The poster says Rockstar fired them a day before the game’s 19 November launch. The account also shared what it described as a termination email from Take-Two’s legal team, accusing the engineer of stealing data and trying to sell Vantage’s model design for $15 million.
Why the GTA 6 profiling claim lacks proof
The account is anonymous, and reports say it was only created in August. It has not shared internal documents, network captures, server addresses or any other technical evidence that would show such data leaving the game.
Searches of Take-Two’s filings with the US Securities and Exchange Commission have found no subsidiary called Vantage Analytics among the roughly 145 companies the publisher lists. Fact checkers have also questioned whether the termination email is genuine.
One technical detail in the claim also appears to be wrong. The DualSense controller reports how far a trigger is pulled, not how much force a player applies, which undercuts the idea that the game measures trigger pressure.
What Take-Two’s privacy policy actually says
Take-Two does collect data from its games, and its privacy policy states that it can draw “profile inferences” to build a personalised profile of a player. The policy also says the company sells or shares unique identifiers and IP addresses with third party advertising providers.
Players in many regions can opt out of that sharing through the policy’s privacy controls. The policy does not mention insurers, lenders or employers, and nothing in it describes the scoring of personality traits that the viral post claims.
GTA 6 does track player behaviour inside the game through its Criminal Profile system, which records how violent a player is and affects how the world reacts to them. Rockstar has described that system as part of the story and gameplay, and Rockstar’s comments on empathy and the Criminal Profile give no indication it is shared outside the game.
Why the claim spread so quickly
The claim landed in the busiest week in GTA history, as millions of players started the game and Take-Two’s market value jumped on launch day. Concerns about how games collect data are common, and specific names such as “Lens” and “Vantage Analytics” made the post sound credible to many readers.
Until the account shares verifiable evidence, or Rockstar or Take-Two respond, the claim remains unproven. Players who are concerned about data collection can review and change their settings through Take-Two’s privacy page and their console’s privacy options.

items.title: GTA VI is the latest game to be ‘review-bombed’ online
items.content:
After 13 years of hype and anticipation, Rockstar’s Grand Theft Auto VI is finally here. While sentiment amongst critics could not have been more positive with a near-perfect score of 99, ‘fans’ of the franchise have expressed far more contentious opinions with regards to Rockstar’s magnum opus – with a review-bombing campaign putting the title at just 5.6 out of 10 on Metacritic.
In today’s day and age, video games are not just video games, but are in fact simply a cog in a larger online culture war. Unfortunately – though unsurprisingly – Rockstar’s all-encompassing GTA VI has become the latest victim in this unrelenting back-and-forth.
In going to the aggregate review site Metacritic, the user score for Grand Theft Auto VI is currently sitting at a surprisingly low rating of 5.6 out of 10 across 97 thousand reviews. When compared to its critic score (which puts GTA VI as the highest rated game of all time), a 5.6 out of 10 places GTA VI as the 142nd best-game of 2026 – below even the likes of Bungie’s much-maligned Marathon.
In reading these reviews, it’s clear that much of the criticism comes from an angle of bad faith, being brought down by 10s of thousands of 0s and 1s. Of course, Metacritic is a public platform and so anyone can leave a review.
In looking at its reception across the Xbox and PlayStation storefronts however (in which you have to buy the game to leave a rating) GTA VI is performing far more favourably, currently sitting at a 4.8 / 5 on PlayStation (across 270,000 reviews) and 4.7 / 5 on Xbox.
GTA VI is far from the first game to be review-bombed on Metacritic and it certainly won’t be the last. Considering the fact that the game has already sold over 32 million copies in pre-orders alone, Rockstar / Take-Two are unlikely to be bothered by the 40,000 negative reviews online.

GTA 6 60 FPS Glitch on Xbox: How It Works and the Catch
items.content:
The GTA 6 60 FPS glitch lets Xbox Series X players unlock the game’s 30 FPS cap through the console’s Quick Resume feature. Reddit user Meowwie64 shared the method, which needs a 120Hz display and a few changes to the refresh rate. The trick comes with problems. Frame rates sit closer to 40 FPS than 60 FPS in normal play, and gameplay animations run much faster than intended. Rockstar Games has not added an official 60 FPS mode.
Below are the exact steps and the drawbacks reported so far.
GTA 6 60 FPS Glitch: What Players Found
GTA 6 runs with a 30 FPS target on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The game launched on Xbox Series X|S on November 19, 2026.
Meowwie64 posted the workaround on Reddit. The player said the method comes from an odd glitch in the Xbox Quick Resume feature, and it does not involve editing any game files. The post lists Game Version 01.002.001 as the tested build. The player was unsure whether it still works on later versions.
GTA VI FPS Unlock Glitch
byu/Meowwie64 inGTA6unmoderated
The original post covers the Xbox Series X. The player could not test the Series S. Later footage shared by Fuzion Xbox Testing shows the glitch running on both the Series X and the Series S.
How to Unlock 60 FPS in GTA 6 on Xbox
You need an Xbox Series X and a display that supports 120Hz. Follow these steps:
Open the Xbox display settings and set the refresh rate to 60Hz.
Launch GTA 6.
Wait until the six stars appear in the intro sequence.
Change the display setting back to 120Hz.
Open the Xbox Guide and start another game from scratch. Do not quit GTA 6.
Switch back to GTA 6 through Quick Resume.
If the glitch works, GTA 6 runs with an unlocked frame rate.
Drawbacks of the GTA 6 FPS Unlock
An unlocked frame rate does not mean a stable 60 FPS. Players who tried the trick reported about 40 FPS in regular gameplay and 35 to 40 FPS on a highway drive. It says 60 FPS or more appears only in scenes with very little graphical load. The frame rate also changes with what happens on screen.
Game animation and movement appear tied to the frame rate. Characters and other gameplay elements, including the in-game clock, run faster than intended. Some animations reportedly play at twice their normal speed.
Cutscenes appear unaffected. Players with a compatible display can turn on Variable Refresh Rate (VRR) to smooth out frame rate swings. VRR does not fix the fast animations.
Risks and Rockstar’s Position
GTA 6 was not built to run this way on Xbox Series X|S. Players could run into crashes or bugs. It also mentions console overheating, but calls that unlikely.
Rockstar Games has not released an official 60 FPS performance mode for GTA 6. Even the PS5 Pro cannot handle the game’s complex simulation at 60 FPS. The glitch is also reported not to work on PS5.
Nobody knows if the workaround will survive future updates. Rockstar will probably fix it in an upcoming patch. Rockstar has not commented on the glitch.

items.title: SOL: enchant Episode 2 opens Hellond with guild-summoned bosses on Nov. 25
items.content:
SOL: enchant's Episode 2 update later this week adds the Hellond region and a Lancer-only Class Change, along with the game's first new server, Infinity. Developers laid out the thinking behind the major update in an interview with Inven Global. It’s the biggest patch since late August and arrives on Wednesday.
ReleaseDate
Episode 2 update (Hellond region, Lancer Class Change)Wednesday, Nov. 25
Infinity serverDec. 2
The interview featured Director Gyeong-myeong Kang, Planning Team Lead Jae-ho Hwang, and Business Division Director Jang-hwan Kim. The biggest change for anyone who’s been playing the game for a few months is a boss system that no longer runs on a fixed clock.
Hellond: a magic city built to feel unlike Caltheon
Hellond is set in a magic city, though all that’s available at launch is its entrance, with the team opting for a phased rollout. Kang said broader playable areas and more content will follow soon. How different is it to the existing Caltheon region? The monsters are said to be tough, there are new progression targets, while extra quests are designed to educate players on the region's lore. Essentially, you’ll do more than just hunt monsters.
Kang said the team wanted a clean break from the old map. "We wanted players to feel from the moment they step into Hellond that they have arrived somewhere completely different from Caltheon."
Hwang added that the Episode 2 title, Infinity, reflects hopes that growth and challenge continue without end.
Bosses on your schedule
Earlier bosses in SOL: enchant spawned at set times, which meant raiding on the clock, something that Hellond changes. Kang explained that "Hellond allows guild members to directly summon bosses and challenge them together whenever they choose."
The team also built a route for players outside the big raiding guilds. Event monsters will appear in general fields during boss spawn hours, so solo hunters and neutral guilds can still chase special rewards if they wish. Bandit raids are also new, while lighter encounters will be scattered across the field while details are tuned.
How tough is it?
Not all of Hellond sits above the current top-tier hunting grounds. According to Kang, the entrance is tuned for players who already hunt in upper zones such as Caltheon North Gate. Things get harder the deeper you go, and Hwang described a mid-region benchmark comparable to Floor 3 of the game's existing tower content, with harder spots beyond it for players who farm that floor comfortably.
Average monster stats are higher, so EXP and Nine (the game's currency) gains should be good. Kang said Sky Island and the tower content have limited entry time, so the team kept their reward value intact rather than letting Hellond overshadow them.
What else ships with Episode 2
Class Change arrives on Wednesday but only for Lancer. An earlier developer note set that scope and said transfers between other classes are planned later, without a schedule. Revealed Lancer footage shows basic attacks hitting multiple enemies and a survival skill that uses two potions at once.
A Restoration Ticket also covers one piece of Rare-grade or higher weapon or armor lost to failed enhancement. Divine Accessories are excluded, and restored gear comes back Bound, so it can't be traded.
Ahead of launch, players have been weighing Lancer's playstyle and wondering what gear Hellond will demand. Hwang's answer is that the entrance is tuned to be reachable.
Writer's take
Letting guilds summon bosses is an interesting change, and it introduces a degree of flexibility that was previously missing, while removing the late-night spawn grind. We support it. The event monsters, meanwhile, give solo players a seat at the table. Also, pairing a fresh Infinity server with reworked pain points could even bring back lapsed players.
Episode 2 hits Nov. 25, and the Infinity server opens its doors Dec. 2. Developers have said Hellond's deeper areas will arrive in later updates.

items.title: CS2 Singapore Major 2026 Starts Today: Stage 1 Teams, Schedule, and Where to Watch
items.content:
As we stand less than a day away from the start of the CS2 Singapore Major 2026 Stage 1, anticipation within the community is at an all-time high. The teams are gearing up to battle it out on LAN for a shot at securing their Stage 2 spot and a chance at a share of the $1,250,000 prize pool.
For the unaware, the CS2 Singapore Major 2026 Stage 1 will kick off on Monday, November 23, 2026, at roughly 8:00 PM PST. The first stage of the event will see sixteen elite CS2 teams go head-to-head in a Swiss-system format, where three wins will secure advancement to Stage 2, while three losses mean elimination from the event.
All matches will be played as best-of-1s, with the exception of the advancement and elimination matches, which will be best-of-3s. GTA 6 update 01.002.002 is rolling out now on PS5 and Xbox, and it is the first patch since the game launched on November 19. Rockstar Games is releasing it in phases worldwide. A dataminer reported that 33% of players can already download it. The update is 603 MB on PS5 and 1.6 GB on Xbox. Rockstar has not published official patch notes yet.
This article explains the update size, the rollout, the version history, and the status of the GTA 6 patch notes.
GTA 6 Update 01.002.002 Release Date and Size
Rockstar started rolling out GTA 6 update 01.002.002 on November 23, 2026. It is the first update since the game’s release, which came 4 days earlier.
According to dataminer, the size is 603 MB. It added that nobody has confirmed whether that figure applies to both platforms.
GTA 6 – Update 01.002.002
33% of Users : Now Available.
66% of Users : in 3h
All Users : in 6h
Update Size : 603 MB pic.twitter.com/bQ2frBuBfd
— PlayStation Game Size (@PlaystationSize) November 23, 2026
The download size is 603.8 MB on PS5 and 1.6 GB on Xbox. That means Xbox players need to free up more space for this patch.
GTA 6 Update Rollout Status
The update is releasing in phases around the world. It is unclear whether the phases follow regions. Around 33% of players can already download it.
Players who do not see the update yet should check their console’s download queue. Turning on automatic updates also helps. Rockstar used a staggered release for its earlier updates too, so a delay is not unusual.

No official GTA 6 patch notes exist for this version at the time of writing.
Reports suggest that the update addresses the money glitch that went viral and the bugs players have reported. Until Rockstar shares the notes, what the patch changes stays unknown.
Rockstar also skipped patch notes for the two updates that came before launch.
GTA 6 Update History
Rockstar has now released 3 updates for the game. Two of them arrived before launch. Version 01.002.002 is the first one after that.
Version 01.002.000 was a mandatory download that players had to install before playing. Version 01.002.001 was much smaller. The newest patch is almost the same size as 01.002.001 on both platforms.

items.content:
First released back in 2017, the Nioh series has managed to make a name for itself by offering a blend of FromSoftware-esque gameplay principles alongside the more fast-paced action-focused mentality of Team Ninja’s past offerings. The formula has proven to be a success, with Nioh spawning two sequels in 2020 and 2026 respectively. As was the case with the past two titles, Nioh 3 appears set to breakaway from its PlayStation exclusivity, with a ‘complete edition’ having now popped up on various game rating boards.
As reported by the publication Insider-Gaming, a listing for Nioh 3: Complete Edition has popped up on the Korean and Japanese game rating boards. While little can be gleaned from the rating itself, this does follow a similar trend to the past two titles in the series.
As mentioned, all three Nioh titles released as PlayStation console exclusives. That said, unlike the first two (which were published by PlayStation themselves globally), Nioh 3 was published by Koei Tecmo and thus released simultaneously on both PS5 and PC back in February of this year.
Given this, it is possible that the complete edition will find its way onto Xbox at some point (likely around February of 2027 – one year on from its initial launch).
On the flipside, it is also possible that said Complete Edition will still be limited to just PS5 and PC, bundling in the base game with its two DLCs (the latter of which is scheduled to launch in February of next year).
While sentiment surrounding Nioh 3 is somewhat mixed – especially compared to the first two entries – having any of the Nioh games on Xbox would be a boon to the platform. We will have to wait and see exactly what Koei Tecmo is planning.

items.title: Elvish Yadav and Jonathan Gaming Fans Clash on X
items.content:
In another surprising development in the GodLike Esports vs Team Apex Gaming saga, Elvish Yadav and Jonathan Gaming fans have found themselves in a clash on X. The clash started in the aftermath of the rumour suggesting Elvish Yadav could join GodLike Esports as a co-owner took the community by the storm.
As the GodLike x Elvish Yadav rumour started gaining traction, a post comparing the brand value of both influencers further fuelled the clash. Fans of both creators rushed to support their favourite.
Post Comparing Elvish Yadav and Jonathan Gaming’s Brand Value Fuels Fan Clash
What fuelled the clash was a post by a user that compared the brand value both influencers bring in. The post stated that Jonathan was associated with brands like Red Bull, Kick, Realme, OnePlus, Samsung, Rooter, and more. On the other hand, Elvish Yadav is associated with brands like Dream11, 1xBet, etc., which are gambling apps. At the end, the post read that Jonathan has built his name through gaming, esports, and mainstream tech brands, whereas Elvish Yadav has built his name through entertainment and reality TV.
One important point to note is that Elvish Yadav has partnered with multiple more brands than what the post has stated. He has also worked with brands like Mamaearth, OZiva, Plix, Bella Vita Luxury, and more.
Fans started flaming on this post to support their influencer. Elvish Yadav fans did not take this comparison lightly at all. Many replied with warnings, asking not to mess with them, some mocked the comparison and pointed towards the struggles he has overcome in his journey. On the other hand, Jonathan Gaming supporters stood by the post, arguing that his credentials come from esports.
The timing has also added fuel to the fire. Jonathan left GodLike Esports in April 2026 and launched Team Apex Gaming, and the ongoing dispute between him and GodLike owner Kronten has kept the community on edge for weeks.
It is important to remember that the GodLike x Elvish Yadav collaboration is still a rumour. At the time of writing, neither Elvish Yadav nor GodLike Esports has made an official announcement, so it should be taken with a pinch of salt.

items.title: Leaks from 2023 claim Rockstar’s next game will be a sequel to LA Noire
items.content:
Despite being known primarily as the GTA and Red Dead Redemption studio, Rockstar Games were once far more varied when it comes to the games they released, having produced classics such as Bully (Canis Canem Edit); Midnight Club and most recently LA Noire. With regards to the latter, it appears as though Rockstar are planning to develop a sequel, with leakers claiming it could arrive as early as 2030.
With Grand Theft Auto VI finally out and available for all to play, some fans have been going back into the internet archives to see which of the game’s many pre-release leaks proved to be true.
As discovered by Reddit users, a leak from back in 2023 seems to have hit the nail on its head when it came to story elements related to GTA VI, lending legitimacy to its report.
Interestingly, as part of this original post, the leaker also offered early details on what Rockstar would be working on next after GTA VI, claiming back in 2023 that a sequel to LA Noire had been greenlit.
Details on this sequel are understandably rather light, but according to the post, LA Noire 2 is in the works. That being said, it is unlikely to be called LA Noire 2 as according to the leaker, the sequel will instead be set in another California city: San Francisco.
Said to be “in the very early stages of development” (at least back in 2023) with a target release year of 2030, the sequel will reportedly revolve around the infamous Zodiac killer – a mysterious serial killer who operated back during the late 1960s and was known best for releasing a number of cryptic messages pertaining to the killings. To this day, the identity of the killer has not been discovered, making for a rather enticing story.
Beyond this, the leaker claimed that SF: Noire (or whatever it ends up being called) will once again make use of advanced facial scanning with desires to “be the best looking game ever made”. Considering just how advanced GTA VI is already, a more concentrated and focused game such as this could easily yield some of the best-looking facial animations we’ve seen to date.
All that said, GTA VI still has plenty of life ahead of it, from the inevitable PC release to the much anticipated online mode, and so it is likely that 2030 is no longer the target year. We will have to wait and see.

ATLUS claims fans won’t have to “wait as long” for future instalments after Persona 6
items.content:
The wait for Persona 6 has been rather arduous, with the last mainline entry having been released over a decade ago at this point. With marketing for its sequel finally having begun to be spun up as part of the franchise’s 30th anniversary, SEGA / ATLUS are claiming that players won’t “have to wait as long for the next instalment as we have in the past.”
As part of the franchise’s 30th anniversary celebrations, SEGA has been publishing various interviews and ‘inside stories’ pertaining to the JRPG series’ past, present and future. The full story can be found HERE, and goes into specifics regarding the turning point that was Persona 3, the franchise’s expansion beyond video games and much more.
In looking towards the future however, SEGA / ATLUS offered some encouraging words, with series producer and director Kazuhisa Wada teasing their mindset going into Persona 6 and beyond, writing:
“Persona 6 is not the end. We are working on various things to ensure that you don't have to wait as long for the next installment as we have in the past. And in order to make Persona an even bigger IP, we are constantly thinking about creative ideas and developments that will not disappoint your expectations. Please look forward to what's to come from Persona.”
Since the arrival of Persona 3 in 2006, each successive mainline entry has taken longer and longer to come to fruition, with Persona 4 arriving just two years later, followed by Persona 5 eight years on – and P6 taking at least a further ten years (possibly longer depending on when it finally arrives).
Of course, across each entry we’ve seen a rise in the number of spin-offs produced, with Persona 4 receiving four spin-offs and the expanded P4: Golden. Persona 5 meanwhile has had a total of 5 spin-offs and its own expanded P5: Royal. Combine this with various remasters, remakes and even free-to-play mobile offerings, and fans have not been hurting for new Persona content.
That said, nothing beats a brand new mainline Persona game, and so it is encouraging to see the team at ATLUS / SEGA keeping such notions in mind when it comes to future releases.

ESGAMING EDGEFLOW targets GPU cooling with an angled side intake
items.content:
ESGAMING has announced the EDGEFLOW, a dual-chamber PC case with an angled side intake designed to feed fresh air towards the graphics card. It comes with three preinstalled ARGB PWM fan modules, supports BTF motherboards and has room for graphics cards up to 435mm long.
The front and left side use tempered glass, giving a clear view of the build. Alongside that glass sits a metal mesh panel angled at 60 degrees. ESGAMING calls this its 3D airflow design, with the fan module behind the angled panel directing air towards the GPU and the rear module exhausting warm air.
The supplied cooling consists of two 360mm fan modules and a 240mm module at the rear. The larger modules sit at the side and bottom of the case, as shown in the product images. All three support PWM speed control and ARGB lighting. There is also support for a 360mm radiator in the roof if you plan to use liquid cooling.
Some of the more practical details concern getting components into the case. The front and side panels come off without tools, while the fan bracket behind the angled panel can be removed completely. That lets you fit fans outside the chassis, with more room to work around the screws and cables.
Motherboard support covers ATX, Micro-ATX and Mini-ITX, along with BTF boards in ATX and Micro-ATX sizes. The latter put their connections on the back of the motherboard, allowing the wiring to run behind the tray.
ESGAMING lists 435mm of graphics card clearance and includes a GPU support bracket. CPU air coolers can be up to 175mm tall, giving builders room to consider a substantial tower cooler as well as the option of a top-mounted radiator.
Behind the motherboard tray, the second chamber provides up to 65mm of cable routing space. Two rubber grommets and three Velcro straps are included to help organise the wiring. The drive cage swings open, providing access for fitting or replacing drives without having to work around a fixed cage.
There are also foam pads on the PSU shroud. ESGAMING says these increase grip between the power supply and the shroud and help reduce vibration and noise.
The front connections run down the side of the front panel. They comprise one USB Type-C port rated at up to 20Gbps, one USB 3.0 port and a combined headphone and microphone jack, alongside the power and reset buttons.
The EDGEFLOW will be offered in black and white through ESGAMING's authorised distributors. The announcement does not include pricing or a firm date for retail availability.
KitGuru says Being able to remove the fan bracket and swing the drive cage out of the way should help when working inside the EDGEFLOW. The supplied fans also give buyers a starting point for cooling without immediately adding more to the shopping list. What we'd want to establish in testing is how well that arrangement cools the graphics card without becoming intrusive under load. Pricing is still missing, so it's too early to judge value.

items.title: Fate/Prototype: Fragments of Sky Silver Tells Another Side of Type Moon’s Story
items.content:
We’re enjoying a wealth of Type Moon and Fate/ series media in the 2020s. The original Fate/stay Night is available worldwide. There was no doubt we’d get the Fate/Extra Record game. Crunchyroll is bringing Witch on the Holy Night to theaters outside Japan. And now Yen Press is further assisting in piecing together the history of the series with an English release of the Fate/Prototype: Fragments of Sky Silver manga. It’s another fascinating exploration of relationships between Masters and Servants and the motivations that drive people to compete in a Holy Grail War.
The history of Fate/Prototype is an interesting one. As the “prototype” part of it suggests, Kinoko Nasu originally had this as the original Fate/stay Night story. But since then, we’ve seen it get its own due with things like this Fate/Prototype: Fragments of Sky Silver manga that sets the stage for the First Tokyo Holy Grail War and the background for the Sajou sisters Manaka and Ayaka. (We’ve only seen Ayaka’s proper follow-up story and start in Japan via a Carnival Phantasm short.) This means what we have here is more of a proper introduction to this additional storyline and major players in it.
Things begin with Manaka summoning her Servant for the Tokyo Holy Grail War. She doesn’t seem particularly enthused about the prospect, given she’s doing that under the orders of her father. Likewise, there are hints she is an especially accomplished mage even at her age due to how she’s referencing the whole ritual and idea of only engaging in these sorts of summonings at that time. She comes across as passive throughout. However, we do see a sudden surge of passion arise once she uses the artifact her father’s brought, a sword, to guarantee a Saber-class servant.
Image via Type Moon and Yen Press
What’s interesting in this first volume of the Fate/Prototype: Fragments of Sky Silver manga is seeing the differing perspectives of the new Masters and Servants. With Manaka, she seems like something of a concerning and unusual case case. It almost seems like she’s only doing this for the sake of the family and their pursuit of power and “The Root.” She comes across as apathetic until she sees Saber and decides he is her “prince.” Seiji Jinga, in contrast, seems more driven and perhaps even fanatical about his pursuit of power, but seems as taken with his Servant Assassin as Manaka. With Tatsumi Kitano and Berserker, we get a young man who read what turned out to be a spell from his grandpa’s journal and ended up as a competitor by accident alongside Berserker, acting as a shocked bystander perspective completely flummoxed by the situation. Seeing these emotions develop between Masters and Servants and situations arise so quickly establishes identities and perspectives in a swift, but helpful, manner.
Go Ad-Free With Siliconera+View the site with no ads, be able to provide direct feedback about what we cover, and be automatically entered into our monthly PC game giveaway.Join Siliconera+
Spoilers aside, what makes this first volume and additional Fate/ story even more compelling is the hints at what people are willing to do and why as the first volume of the Fate/Prototype: Fragments of Sky Silver manga comes to a close. Since it does jump between pairings and perspectives, we start to gain more insights as we see duos pop up again. The ones between Manaka and Saber, as you might imagine from them being the “main” characters, show the most development. At the outset, she’s this passive, almost blank individual who is difficult to read. Then, once she gets her “prince,” we start to see a total shift and increasing levels of passion and devotion. But by the end, there’s something else there that suggests she’s someone to absolutely watch.
Given Fate/Prototype: Fragments of Sky Silver first came out in Japan back in September 2024, I’m honestly just heartened to see Yen Press did license and release it worldwide. It’s a fascinating look at new Master and Servant relationships and another take on a Holy Grail War. Especially considering what the Fate/ series has become now. Though, to be honest, I also can’t help but hope this renewed interest in a Fate/Prototype project could perhaps even one day lead to a more proper anime adaptation or retelling of Ayaka’s story.
Volume 1 of Fate/Prototype: Fragments of Sky Silver is available in English, and Yen Press hasn’t set a date for the second volume of the manga.

items.content:
The Brawl Stars Championship (BSC) returns for the 2027 season with extra regional tournaments and more opportunities for lower-seeded teams to join tier 1 competition.
The circuit includes two huge LAN events: Brawl Cup and World Finals 2027. Esports teams will compete through two seasonal splits to qualify for these offline internationals.
Read on for all the details on the Brawl Stars esports 2027 season: the competitive format, basic schedule, and LAN locations.
Key takeaways
Brawl Stars Championship 2027 features regional Invitationals as a new series of offline tournaments.
Two seasonal Splits are qualification series for Brawl Cup and Brawl Stars World Finals.
Brawl Stars esports season 2027 starts on Jan. 16–17.
South Korea hosts the Brawl Cup 2027.
The World Finals 2027 takes place in Paris, France.
The Challengers circuit comes with the opportunity for the top two teams to battle for BSC spots.
Table of contents
Key takeaways

FAQs about Brawl Stars Championship 2027
Roadmap of the Brawl Stars season 2027
Brawl Stars Championship 2027 was revealed during the World Finals 2026. The trailer highlights the main circuit format and the Challengers series.
BSC 2027: The main competitive series
All the strongest Brawl Stars esports teams compete in the main Brawl Stars Championship 2027 series. The schedule includes the following events.
Regional Invitationals: From Jan. 16 to Jan. 17.
Spring Split: February, March, and April.
Brawl Cup 2027: In South Korea.
Fall Split: August, September, and October.
Brawl Stars World Finals 2027: In Paris, France.
The lower-tier Brawl Stars Challengers series generally mirrors this format, while also having pre-LAN Regional Finals. These tournaments are battles for two spots at the Brawl Cup and World Finals: between the bottom two BSC and top two Challengers teams.
Brawl Stars esports 2027 season roadmap (Image credit: Supercell)
Brawl Stars Invitationals to kick off the 2027 Championship
BSC 2027 introduces a new series of regional tournaments — Brawl Stars Invitationals. They take place in four regions over one weekend, from Jan. 16 to Jan. 17, 2027.
The Invitationals are offline events.
East Asia Invitational: In Tokyo, Japan.
EMEA Invitational: In Frankfurt, Germany.
South America Invitational: In São Paulo, Brazil.
North America Invitational: In Dallas, USA.
There are tournaments for the 7th–12th teams on the regional leaderboard. Those who finish in the top 2 advance to the Top Level competition.

Spring Split and Brawl Cup 2027 in South Korea
Starting in February 2027, all the top dogs in Brawl Stars esports join the Championship. Eight Top Level teams compete throughout the Spring Split, with matches happening every week, up to April.
Scheme of seasonal Splits during the Brawl Stars Championship 2027 (Image credit: Supercell)
Brawl Cup 2027 is a LAN event to conclude the BSC Spring Split. This tournament takes place in South Korea.
The official reveal of the Brawl Cup 2027 location: South Korea (Image credit: Supercell)
Fall Split and Brawl Stars World Finals 2027 in Paris, France
The Fall Split follows the general format from Spring: weekly matches between the eight Top Level teams, from August to October.
As for the LAN conclusion, it’s the World Finals 2027. The main Brawl Stars esports event of the year takes place in Paris, France.
The official reveal of the Brawl Stars World Finals 2027 location: Paris, France (Image credit: Supercell)
Challengers series: Regional Finals to advance to BSC
The lower-tier competition in Brawl Stars happens within the Challengers circuit. While the series itself is not new, Challengers teams receive a fresh promotion opportunity in 2027.
At the end of both Splits, the top two Challengers teams advance to the Regional Final.
The bottom two Top Level teams fall to the Regional Finals, too.
Via these tournaments, Challengers can advance to the main BSC series — if they defeat the Top Level opponents.
Brawl Stars Regional Finals is a clash of Challengers and BSC teams for two spots in the Top Level league (Image credit: Supercell)
The tradition of viewership rewards continues for Brawl Stars season 2027. Additionally, Supercell promises a new tournament platform, new merch available at LAN events, and more partner clubs in the mix.
Brawl Stars Championship 2027 (Image credit: Supercell)
FAQs about Brawl Stars Championship 2027
What are the main new features of the Brawl Stars esports season 2027?
The addition of Brawl Stars Invitationals, weekly matches during the season Splits, and the BSC promotion opportunity for lower-tier Challengers teams are the main new features of season 2027.
When does the Brawl Stars Championship 2027 start?
The 2027 competitive season in Brawl Stars starts on the weekend of Jan. 16–17, with the regional Invitational tournaments.
Which teams play at the Brawl Stars Invitationals?
Brawl Stars esports teams with the regional leaderboard placements 7th–12th compete in the early-season Invitationals. The top two advance to the main Top Level series.
Where do the LAN Brawl Stars events take place in 2027, Brawl Cup and World Finals?
Locations for LAN Brawl Stars esports events are South Korea for the Brawl Cup and Paris, France, for the World Finals 2027.
What are the Regional Finals in the Brawl Stars 2027 season?
The Regional Finals are clashes of the top two teams from the lower-tier Challengers series and the bottom two teams from the higher-tier BSC league. The rewards are two spots at the upcoming Brawl Stars LAN events and Top Level seasonal Splits.

items.title: Usagi Shima: Bunny Island Feels Better on PC
items.content:
When Usagi Shima originally appeared on mobile devices, it acted as a Neko Atsume sort of game where you’d set items out for bunnies and decorate a space, leave the app, then come back to see which rabbits showed up and collect ‘em all. There were some more hands-on elements, such as minigames and feeding the critters to bolster relationships with them and little types of facilities to place. But it still felt pretty hands-off. The new PC version of Usagi Shima: Bunny Island feels a little different due to some adjustments in the way it works and how rabbits show up, leading to a game that feels a little stronger than it did before.
As I mentioned before, the concept behind Usagi Shima is simple. Place items. Wait for bunnies to appear. Take photos for their profile and care for them so they’ll like you. Get currency to buy more items as a result, which means more rabbits. However, a number of elements in this PC version of Usagi Shima make enjoying that element a little easier. It’s no longer an idle sort of game where you go away and come back. You don’t need to close it, then come back later. They’ll show up and move around your island as you play during a session. It’s also possible to choose how time flows, so you aren’t stuck with a real-time connection that penalizes you for doing things like working or studying. Also, minigames are optional, which is handy if you don’t enjoy some of them and makes bunny care a bit faster if that’s not why you’re playing.
The decorating and designing element is also so much easier in Usagi Shima: Bunny Island on a PC than in the original mobile release. This is due to a number of elements. A big one is the new perspective. Constantly playing in landscape mode gives you a greater sense of space when tailoring your item to your wants and needs. The lack of microtransactions also is a big help with picking up certain cosmetics. But what I really appreciate is the mouse controls. I did really enjoy the mobile app. However, so many times I found things didn’t look exactly how I wanted with regards to placement since I played on my phone. That isn’t an issue here.
Images via Studio Rabbiko
But what I really like is how Usagi Shima on PC offers more customization items for my laptop in general because I played it. It can run as a screensaver. The photos I take can be wallpapers. It feels like even though it isn’t the sort of idle game it once was, it still maintains some of that due to how it can run as a relaxing sort of background that I cultivate and customize when I play.
There are merits to the mobile version of Usagi Shima: Bunny Island, but I think I prefer the PC release now. It’s so much easier to play it. The customization elements also make setting up my island less troublesome. Also, when I’m taking these screenshots, I have a better use for them than a bunch of photos on my phone that I end up forgetting are even there.
Usagi Shima: Bunny Island is available on the PC via Steam and mobile devices.
