items.title: SilverStone launches 1350W HELA 1350Rz Platinum ATX 3.1 PSU
items.content:
SilverStone has expanded its Hela PSU lineup with the Hela 1350Rz, a 1350W unit carrying 80 Plus Platinum certification and ATX 3.1 compliance.
According to Cowcotland, the new HELA 1350Rz is a fully modular unit designed for high-end systems with demanding power requirements. Alongside its dual 12V-2×6 connectors, the power supply includes three EPS 4+4 CPU power connectors and delivers its full rated output through a single 12V rail rated at 112.5A.
SilverStone has equipped the PSU with Japanese capacitors and a 135mm FDB cooling fan featuring a semi-passive mode that keeps the fan switched off at lower loads. The company quotes efficiency figures ranging from 89% to 92% depending on load, putting the unit in line with its 80 Plus Platinum certification.
The HELA 1350Rz uses SilverStone's third-generation modular cable interface, with shared ports for EPS and PCIe connections. SilverStone also claims a sensing wire integrated into the motherboard cable can improve voltage regulation by up to 2%. Protection features include OCP, OPP, OVP, SCP and OTP safeguards.
KitGuru says: The market for 1350W power supplies is relatively niche, but Platinum-rated efficiency and dual 12V-2×6 connectors should make the HELA 1350Rz a suitable option for enthusiasts building high-end systems. Would you consider a 1350W PSU for your next build?

Debian launches Gaming Hardware Team to improve support for handhelds and consoles
items.content:
The Debian project has launched a new Gaming Hardware Team tasked with improving support for handheld PCs, consoles and other gaming hardware. The initiative will focus on testing hardware, documenting compatibility issues and exploring potential fixes, all while maintaining Debian's long-standing focus on stability.
While Linux distributions like Bazzite and CachyOS have become popular among gamers and handheld PC enthusiasts, Debian has traditionally favoured stability over rapid hardware support. With Linux gaming continuing to gain momentum thanks to devices like the Steam Deck and newer SteamOS-powered systems, Debian now appears keen to improve its standing among gaming users.
According to Debian project maintainer Karamtoth (via GamingOnLinux), the new team will test a wide range of hardware spanning handheld gaming PCs, emulation devices and home consoles. The goal is to identify bugs, document compatibility issues and investigate patches that could improve hardware support across Debian systems. Karamtoth also noted that the project may look at ways to better support newer gaming hardware without compromising Debian's reputation for stability.
Better hardware support would make Debian a more practical option for gamers running newer hardware, while any improvements could also benefit downstream distributions built on Debian packages. Alongside the announcement, the project has launched a dedicated wiki page where users can test Debian on their own gaming devices and submit compatibility reports to help guide future development.
KitGuru says: Debian's conservative update cycle has always prioritised rock-solid stability over day-one hardware support, so forming a dedicated team for handhelds and modern components makes plenty of sense. Would you consider running Debian on a gaming PC or handheld?

KitGuru Games: History Will Vindicate Black Ops 7
items.content:
Call of Duty Black Ops 7 came out at the exact wrong time. Being the second game in a back-to-back release for Treyarch’s Black Ops series, 2025’s COD entry was carrying a couple suitcases worth of baggage from Black Ops 6 while bumping into its own roadblocks in the form of Battlefield 6 – a supposed return to its roots for COD’s long-standing rival. Combine this with general fatigue, a wealth of other games to play and a heavy focus on memeing its – admittedly terrible – campaign, and it comes as little surprise that Black Ops 7 came and went with little fanfare outside of its core audience. In fact, some have deemed it to be one of the worst Call of Duty games of all time. With 2026’s Modern Warfare 4 officially out and BO7 having reached its end-of-life however, I can say with great confidence that Black Ops 7 is in fact one of the best.
First thing’s first, let's get this out of the way: the main campaign for Black Ops 7 was bad…really bad. Even beyond its always-online requirements and the inability to pause when playing solo, the narrative of Black Ops 7 felt rushed, its level design uninspired and the open-combat missions were boring. Topping things off were these Destiny-esque boss fights which, while mostly visually pleasing, carried little in the way of mechanical depth; leading to basically no impactful moments.
This is where Black Ops 7 has gotten most of its negative reception from, and in this regard, the critics were correct. That being said, COD’s campaigns serve primarily as flavor text for the rest of the experience, being played once at launch and likely never again. To supplement this terrible campaign, Treyarch / Activision gave players an entirely new mode which in my opinion managed to become one of the best new things to come out of COD in many years: Endgame.
Upon completion of the campaign (and made available separately shortly following launch), players would be dropped into the open world map of Avalon to take on all manner of enemies, contracts, assignments and more in what was a PvE pseudo-extraction shooter.
Though somewhat light in content at launch, through Seasonal updates Endgame would wind up becoming a fun and highly replayable sandbox experience featuring its own progression system; unique exotic rewards; operator abilities; and massive PvE boss fights from giant robots to zombie-dinosaurs; secret German superweapons; a Dune-esque sandworm and more – requiring much of the lobby to work together for mutual benefits.
While I will typically enjoy the average Call of Duty campaign (getting my 5ish hours worth of entertainment from it), Endgame offered me dozens of hours of entertainment in a mode which allowed for a combination of mindless fun, high stakes and a sense of community through cooperation. When all was said and done, Endgame alone had enough going for it to be worthy of a separate game in and of itself. If having a bad campaign was the sacrifice required for Endgame to come to reality, then I’m glad Treyarch went the route that they did (even if the campaign is what caused so much ire towards BO7 critically).
Treyarch also took some major risks when it came to Black Ops 7’s multiplayer. After years of skill-based matchmaking determining every single game, with disbanding lobbies making it so even the fun matches were short-lived, Treyarch introduced its ‘Open matchmaking’ for Black Ops 7.
While not quite the free-for-all seen with the golden era of COD, this new system put a greater emphasis on connection quality and player variety. Combined with the return of persistent lobbies, and BO7 on the backend was closer to the OG call of Duties than it had been in years. This was unfortunately a bit of a double-edged sword however.
Given that BO7 sold relatively poorly (for a COD title anyways), most of those who purchased the game landed closer to the hardcore side of things; ultimately making the reduction of SBMM a more prohibitive experience for some casuals. Still, after years of begging for no more skill based matchmaking, Black Ops 7 actually listened – and whether it be due to BO7’s sales, internal data or other ancillary factors – Activision is unlikely to embrace such a notion once again for quite some time.
Zombies however is where the game truly shined. Having always been the unsung hero of the Black Ops series, this latest iteration of Treyarch’s horde survival shooter offered an abundance of both quality and quantity; so much so that in my opinion it reigns as the best iteration of COD Zombies we’ve ever seen…perhaps with the sole exception of 2015’s Call of Duty Black Ops 3.
Narratively speaking, it brought back the OG crew (Richtofen, Takeo, Dempsey and Nikolai) in a new form while building on the Requiem team from BO6 (Maya, Weaver, Carver and Grey). While a tough act to balance 8 different playable characters, each with their own backstories; motivations and ideals, the narrative team managed to make each operator unique, interesting and memorable – supplemented by plenty of character quotes and conversions during gameplay.
Speaking of gameplay, this is where BO7 Zombies thrived. I have spoken at length over the years regarding COD’s tight and satisfying gunplay. Though a somewhat controversial mechanic for those on the multiplayer side of things, omni-movement and wallhopping in particular played like absolute butter in the zombies mode.
Maintaining awareness of the enemies constantly trying to surround you while being cognizant of the map design and its hazards lent itself to a gameplay loop which was not only immensely satisfying but near-infinitely replayable. Combine this with an expansion of the augment system first introduced in BO6 and the sense of progression and power felt throughout a match was in many ways unmatched.
This also lent itself to a great deal of customisation on a gameplay front. As a fan of the fast-paced and ever-moving nature of combat in games such as the DOOM series, being able to tailor my perk upgrades in a way which allowed for a focus on movement and momentum through Stamin-Up, PHD Flopper; melee macchiato and the like meant that each player’s personal preference could be customised and accounted for – whether you are more of a camper, a trainer or something in between.
To be honest, given the sheer variety of core mechanics on offer, Treyarch could’ve dropped me into a plain and flat endless desert and I still would have had dozens of hours worth of fun just running in circles while demolishing the undead. Fortunately, the team chose not to settle on their laurels and instead offered a suite of maps which many would agree are comparable to some of the franchise’s best.
Throughout its year of support, Black Ops 7 Zombies saw the addition of 6 main maps:
Ashes of the Damned
A massive BO2 Tranzit inspired map featuring a variety of points of interests, dangerous fog-laden roads and a wonder-vehicle in the form of Tessie for extra navigation
Astra Malorum
A gorgeous facility set on a skull shaped meteor revolving around the rings of Saturn
Paradox Junction
A Nuketown remake featuring a unique time-travel mechanic which sent you between a pre-and-post-nuked version of the map
Totenreich
A Norse fishing village / secret facility which included both mythical ice giants and huge robotic experiments
Kowakujo
A feudal Japanese castle surrounded by Volcanoes and an eye-searing amount of lava
Rex Infernus
A broken nexus in the middle of the Dark Ether featuring plenty of verticality aided by a unique grapple hook for fast and fun navigation
Beyond their aesthetics, each map featured highly unique wonder weapons (ranging from the LGM1 which literally shot UFOs at enemies; to the Nekomancer – a spiritual talking cat which shoots powered hairballs and can be used as a melee weapon to scratch zombies – a gross skull spider which both kills enemies while healing you, among others).
The latter half of these maps also introduced unique and themed equipment such as the Manekineko cat grenade; the anti-gravity Glocke Drop and the aforementioned ‘Void Claw’ grapple hook – making each map both visually and mechanically distinct.
Of course, a Zombies map wouldn’t be a zombies map without its Easter Eggs, and in this regards Black Ops 7 was a true return to form. Alongside their narrative implications, each of these 6 experiences showed off Treyarch’s creativity when it came to puzzle solving, technical depth, mechanical variety and visual splendor; concluding with massive boss fights which put the campaign’s Destiny-esque encounters to shame.
From massive ice giants to floating gelatinous blobs; a fire breathing dragon; a racist, confederate-aligned human-scorpion hybrid and an ever-shifting rock monster set on the low-gravity atmosphere of Mars – each of these encounters both surprised and delighted players when they finally unlocked the boss fights after what was sometimes 24+ hours worth of community-led Easter Egg hunting. Treyarch truly put their all into these final encounters, and it showed.
It doesn’t end there however. Alongside these 6 core maps, BO7 Zombies brought back survival maps for the first time since Black Ops 2. Being selectively cut out versions of the larger experiences, those who wanted to simply shoot zombies, power up and shoot more zombies could do so across a total of 8 additional survival maps. Even within these, the team made sure to make each one feel somewhat distinct with different special enemies, elites and other ancillary mechanics.
My personal favourite has been Mars, owing to its low-gravity nature making the likes of rocket launchers and explosives immensely satisfying to use while simultaneously altering the movement mechanics for both you and the zombies – though each survival experience has its own merits.
Somehow, all this is still the tip of the iceberg, as Black Ops 7 Zombies also introduced one of its most innovative features in the entirety of the mode’s existence: Cursed. Functioning somewhat like the collectible skulls from Halo, upon the completion of a main map’s Easter Egg, players would unlock the ability to earn various cursed relics, each of which could alter the gameplay mechanics in both minor and major ways.
Unlike the skulls in Halo however, unlocking each of these individual relics required an easter egg hunt in and of itself, which concluded with its own unique set of challenges – leading to further community involvement throughout the year.
In its base form, the cursed mode presented itself more closely to that of classic zombies, meaning you would start with the basic 1911 pistol and little else. The points system was also altered, functioning more like OG zombies and allowing for a greater variety of strategic options during the early game. This, in combination with the 30 different cursed relics available meant you could then tailor the experience to be as close to ‘classic’ zombies as possible, or could make it a wholly different experience.
One of my favourite relics was the ‘Samantha’s Drawing’ which turned the mode into a gun game of sorts, where-in each round would see your weapons swapped out for a randomly selected alternative. It’s chaotic, but extremely fun. Another one of my go-tos is the Mannequin Turret relic, which removes all starting armour making the early-mid rounds much more tense.
Additionally, upping the number of relics equipped would then come with its own suite of boons, with Tier 1 of cursed giving you Golden armour (which auto-regenerates), Tier 2 adding in an extra rarity upgrade and Tier 3 allowing you to pack-a-punch your weapon up to 4 times – boosting your capabilities beyond what was previously possible.
Last but certainly not least, the final Season of BO7 brought in what is known as a Super Easter Egg.
After completing the main quests on each of the 6 major maps, players would find one more final easter egg added to each experience, which upon completion would culminate in a rather intense boss rush. Completing the boss rush would then introduce one last cursed relic: Mr Peeks Mayhem; giving you the benefits of all three tiers of cursed (alongside other bonuses) without the downsides – a final reward for all those who remained committed to the mode.
I haven’t even mentioned the literal hundreds of different camos and cosmetics which could be earned through other various challenges…but I feel like I’ve said enough at this point.
With the sheer amount of quality content on offer in Black Ops 7 across its multiplayer, Endgame and especially Zombies, I am almost embarrassed to admit that I put in over 1000 hours into the game – more than every other Call of Duty I’ve ever played combined. Even so, there is still plenty for me to unlock and experience, from cursed relics, to the boss rush mode, mastery camos or even just playing the main easter eggs with different characters in order to learn their perspectives on the unfolding narrative.
Black Ops 7 is now my ‘forever’ game, and I could easily see myself putting in another 1000 hours into it in the coming years. Over the past year, I’ve heard some people unironically claim that BO7 is the worst Call of Duty of all time, because it's cool to hate on COD. In my subjective and objective opinion however, Black Ops 7 is in fact the best. Given time, I believe history will prove this to be the case.
KitGuru says: Did you give Black Ops 7 a shot? Were you aware of all the strides made with Treyarch’s latest iteration? Which mode in COD do you care about the most? Let us know down below.
The post KitGuru Games: History Will Vindicate Black Ops 7 first appeared on KitGuru.

Mark's enthusiasm for computers dampened at an early age by the rubber-keyed Sinclair Spectrum 48K and feelings of Commodore 64 envy. However, in the mid-80s, hope in a digital future was rekindled by the purchase of an Atari 520 STe. Since that time Mark has used a multitude of computers for fun and professional endeavors. He often owned both Macs and PCs but went cold on the former after OS9 was killed off, and warmed to the latter with the introduction of Windows XP.

Early work years were spent in artwork and reprographics but in the late noughties, Mark started to blog about computers, Taiwanese food culture, and guitar design. This activity led to a full-time position writing about breaking PC tech news for HEXUS, for the best part of a decade. When HEXUS was abruptly closed, Mark helped with the foundation of Club386, before finding a new home at Tom's Hardware.

When not wearing through the keycap legends on his PC keyboards, Mark can be found wandering the computer malls of Taiwan's neon-lit conurbations and enjoying local and international cuisine.

Thunder Frogs are a pretty cool brawler. They fight as one, covering a decently big area with their basic attack and dealing significant damage. Sure, the colorful magic frogs are just a totally fun addition to your personal Brawl Stars roster!
Playing Thunder Frogs comes with downsides. It’s not that easy to establish their most effective traps. Teamplay and a creative approach are required. In a way, the game continues the recent tradition of unique kits that reward thinking outside the box.
In this Brawl Stars guide, we discuss essential details of Thunder Frogs’ abilities, highlight the best build ideas, and explain free unlock.
Key takeaways
Thunder Frogs is a Legendary Artillery brawler.
Their Basic Attack requires placing two frogs on the map to create a triangle and damage every opponent inside.
With their Super, Thunder Frogs can leap towards their victims for area damage or run from danger.
The best build for this brawler boosts the offense. The alternative is healing abilities: for Thunder Frogs and teammates.
As a Legendary brawler, Thunder Frogs costs 3,800 Credits. Patient players can earn this currency in-game for free.

Thunder Frogs and Ziggy’s magic show
Zap, Zee, and Volt knocked on Ziggy’s door when he looked for assistance during his magic performances. The three frogs did not impress Ziggy at all, so they needed to reveal their true power — people in Star Park adore these cute little creatures!
Ziggy granted Zap, Zee, and Volt his own magic hat, so that the frogs can create thunder out of blue air. They leap onto each other to wear the hat, conquer the audience’s heart with their smiles, and then … electrocute those who dare to stand against Thunder Frogs in a Brawl Stars match.

How to play Thunder Frogs in Brawl Stars: Abilities guide
The froggies are very unusual with their Brawl Stars kit. They are not your straightforward shooters, melee fighters, or even traditional Artillery brawlers. In a way, Thunder Frogs remind Bolt — with how strongly you need to change your approach to the game to be effective on this character pick.
Basic Attack, Triangle Trick: You need to show where two frogs should jump — They form a triangle that damages with a powerful electricity strike.
In the heat of the fight, it may not be too easy to form that triangle. Thunder Frogs remain vulnerable in the process. The opponents can move away.
The best approach is to find a moment when your teammates attack and keep the opponents busy fighting. In this case, you have time and safety to use the thunder magic. Melee allies can be especially helpful for this trick.
Triangle Trick: Thunder Frogs’ Basic Attack in Brawl Stars (Image credit: Supercell, screenshot via esports.gg)
Super, Frogzilla: Three froggies unite and form one really big frog. They jump to deal area damage on landing. With one use of their Super, Thunder Frogs can jump three times.
The Super requires caution. You may need to save the final jump to escape from danger. However, if you feel that the damage is enough, you may decide to land the fatal blow, or killing leap.
Frogzilla: Thunder Frogs’ Super in Brawl Stars (Image credit: Supercell, screenshot via esports.gg)
The best build for Thunder Frogs
The brawler offers two build approaches. You can focus on offense or choose some support features.
Offense feels like the best build for Thunder Frogs in Brawl Stars matches.
Star Power 2, Swamp Stomps: The triangle’s edges slow opponents down. Fleeing from the thunder magic becomes more difficult.
Gadget 1, Double Jumpers: You can launch two frogs with one attack, making it easier to form the triangle during a battle.
As for Gears, Shield can add extra protection for slow basic attack execution. Speed is a nice power-up to improve Thunder Frogs’ mobility, for both offense and defense.
Thunder Frogs with their Gadgets and Star Powers in Brawl Stars (Image credit: Supercell, screenshot via esports.gg)
The alternative choices add healing features to Thunder Frogs’ Brawl Stars kit. With Star Power 1, Leech Landing, Thunder Frogs heal themselves from the damage dealt by the Super leaps. After activating Gadget 2, Soothing Shock, the next basic attack heals teammates.
These are also good picks. However, Brawl Stars has more effective support healers if you like this role. Leech Landing, or self-healing during Super can be helpful if you like taking big risks in the game.

Is Thunder Frogs a difficult brawler to play?
Thunder Frogs are on the more difficult side of the roster. Their Basic Attack requires precision, good timing, and safe positioning.
Can Thunder Frogs deal big damage?
Yes, Thunder Frogs are very good at damage-dealing, including Basic and Super Attacks. Their weak side is vulnerability during the Basic Attack execution.
Do Thunder Frogs have a good Super?
The Super Attack of Thunder Frogs is very good. It’s simple to use and highly damaging.

Star Power 2, Swamp Stomps, and Gadget 1, Double Jumpers. are arguably the best build for Thunder Frogs. They improve your offensive playstyle.

You need to accumulate 3,800 Credits from various in-game drops and rewards. Then, you need to select Thunder Frogs as your next Legendary brawler — this may take time if you have many brawlers to unlock.

items.title: Review: Virtue and a Sledgehammer Supports Humanity and Rejects AI
items.content:
Deconstructeam games tend to feel poignant and offer a significant message in addition to telling a good story. We saw it happen with The Red Strings Club and The Cosmic Wheel Sisterhood. Virtue and a Sledgehammer, its latest game with Selkie Harbour, maintains that trend by offering commentary on family, relationships, community, technology, and AI combined with a walking sim that involves taking a sledgehammer to that which is inhuman. It’s a stark, violent adventure that makes you think and explores humanity, and one that might feel off-putting or due to some subject matter and protagonist reactions.
Pratelle and her sister Nina grew up in the town of Virtud with their mother Merche. Virtue and a Sledgehammer begins with Pratelle returning with what looks to be the corpse of her mom in the trunk of her car. From there, Deconstructeam and Selkie Harbour hit us with her asking “us” a critical question while holding a sledgehammer with Nina and Merche nearby. “How far would you go to keep a family member from doing something terrible?” After this preamble, we’re warned that we’ll witness a lot of violence and love. We then see Pratelle holding the sledgehammer in her hands as words on a computer describe flesh as a prison and say they’ve never been happier. It’s then that we can smash and strike and receive the mission. Find Nina and confront her.
While Virtue and a Sledgehammer’s name and some trailers showing Pratelle destroying buildings, furniture, and robots might suggest a beat’em up, this is more a visual novel and walking sim with opportunities to unleash our rage and frustration through destruction. Is that decision right? Seeing the facsimiles of humanity that all these robotic replicas with the memories and programmed personality traits of former Virtud residents exhibit is designed to make us consider that. Perhaps its finally giving people the rest and respect they deserve. No more replicas spouting inane commentary stolen from actual humans, plagiarizing their identities. As Pratelle puts it early on, “This isn’t a person; it’s a talking microwave.”
What makes it difficult is the way these AIs can copy the humans they replaced. They might beg for their lives. They may not fight back. They could even make points about how certain health or mental things that held them back before no longer do. Once they start to realize what Pratelle is trying, they might even try to do the very human thing of sacrificing themselves to hold her back so someone can go and warn the others so they can prepare, get to safety, or even escape. But then, we also run into ones that retain the same cruel or even despicable personality traits as the originals, which opens up another philosophical puzzle. Do we allow that hatred to continue? And there are even ones that do seem very much the “talking microwave” Pratelle describes, spouting nonsense and looking quite artificial.
In addition to telling some of the story through these possible smash’em up moments and AI robot interactions, another major element of Virtue is a Sledgehammer is Pratelle finding robot parts with certain highlighted colors. Say you smash enough pieces with a red highlight. Doing that helps to unlock flashbacks. These offer insights into what happened to with her sister and to her family. Again, they can feel as raw, devastating, and harrowing as the interactions and questions posed as we tear down what remains of the town.
While so much of Virtue and a Sledgehammer shows Pratelle dealing with cold, inhuman, fake replicas of actual individuals, I do think it makes the moments we see in those flashbacks and story segments hit even harder. It’s a very human story. We’re going into it seeing Nina as a villain due to her actions that resulted in the AI town, but these paint Pratelle as equally flawed. Even knowing and seeing what Nina’s done, we get moments where her sister wonders about and blames herself. And seeing those moments, including ones interspersed with the technological elements and robots that use those people’s digitized selves… I sometimes found it heartbreaking.
Images via Deconstructeam and Selkie Harbour
Especially since Virtue and a Sledgehammer also can feel like it touches on the evolution of AI-induced psychosis. As Pratelle goes through town, it made me feel like we were seeing people who embraced the technology and were brainwashed into seeing a reality that wasn’t there. There are these shades of delusion. Especially seeing people prioritize that tech over actual people in front of them. Seeing that, especially if someone’s seen that in people around them in their lives, hits so hard.
I will note that Virtue and a Sledgehammer is quite short. This works in its favor. There are some moments that can get a bit tedious as Pratelle ventures through Virtud on her mission due to things like layout and walking speed. Coupled with the weight of what’s happening and raw subject matter, I think lasting longer than four hours would do it a disservice. What’s here is the perfect length to convey Deconstructeam and Selkie Harbour’s messages properly.
Virtue and a Sledgehammer explores what it means to be human, the relationships that shape our lives, the anguish of grief, and how horrifying AI replicants could be. It feels like a very human cautionary tale. It may even hit so close to home that it’s difficult to play. But I’d say it’s quite an important experience as a result.
Virtue and a Sledgehammer is available on PCs.

Jowi Morales is a writer and journalist covering the tech beat since 2021. However, he’s been interested in technology far earlier than that. He started discovering desktop computers when his father brought home a Windows 95 PC, but his first real experience working under the hood of the PC was when the old computer’s hard drive was filled to the brim in the year 2000. He deleted the Windows folder to attempt to rectify the situation, which led to his dad buying a new desktop PC. Since then, he learned a lot more about computers, and he’s always been the go-to tech expert for his family and friends.

Jowi primarily uses a Windows workstation and an Android phone, but he also bought into the Apple ecosystem with the 6th-gen iPad, iPhone 14 Pro Max, and the M1 MacBook Air. Today, Jowi covers hardware and software from Redmond and Cupertino, while also looking at the tech industry in general.

Aside from covering technology, Jowi is an avid photographer and writes about automobiles, aviation, and tanks. You can find his bylines at MakeUseOf, SlashGear, and, of course, Tom’s Hardware.

items.title: Aion 2 to Get Global Market With November 25 Update
items.content:
Aion 2 players will soon be able to trade items with players from other servers, NC has confirmed.
In a recent Aion 2 update notice, the Korean devs behind the title have confirmed that the World Market and World Exchange will be added to the MMORPG with its November 25 patch.
Once the feature is implemented, players will be able to trade items directly with other servers, as long as they are in the same faction and region.
Aion 2 Global Market Restrictions
The Aion 2 Global Market will see a number of additional restrictions compared to the regular marketplace:
A 20% sales tax will apply to items sold through the World Market and World Exchange.
The World Market and World Exchange (Quna) will each have a limit of 10 sale listings per day.
The World Market and World Exchange will be available to Membership users only.
Note that the existing Server Market and Server Exchange continue to remain in the game, so you’ll still be able to buy and sell items there.
The changes to the Aion 2 market come after repeated community complaints about the price difference of items across servers. Additionally, the price tags on the crafting and gathering items such as Wrathful Minds and Pure Odyles were especially inflated in some servers.
A number of players believed that the elevated prices of these items on some servers were due to bots and RMT-ers. NC has yet to comment on that issue, although they have publicly acknowledged the presence of bots in Aion 2 in the past. The company continues to suspend accounts suspected of RMT-ing and botting in occasional ban waves.
Not much else is known about the contents of the next Aion 2 update at the time of writing. Detailed patch notes for the November 25 update are expected to be revealed on the same day.

items.title: GTA 6 Just Made $3.79 Billion in One Day, and No Movie, Album, or Game Has Ever Come Close
items.content:
Rockstar Games has once again made its mark on history with the launch of its newest title, Grand Theft Auto VI. According to Rockstar and its parent company Take-Two, the open-world action-adventure title brought in a whopping $3.79 billion on its opening day, making it “the biggest entertainment launch in history.”
The aforementioned figure covers worldwide retail sales through the November 19 launch day, with pre-sales included.
Rockstar confirmed that most of the revenue GTA 6 has made until now had already been locked in before players ever reached Vice City. As per the company, approximately 32.5 million units were sold ahead of the game’s release, which goes on to show the amount of anticipation built among gamers over the past 13 years.
Despite only a day having passed since its launch, the revenue that GTA 6 has managed to generate so far has already exceeded the estimated development budget that went into the game. While the development costs haven’t been officially shared by Rockstar, some reports indicate that the company spent close to $2 billion developing this game.
GTA 6 Shatters GTA 5’s Record
Previously, the title of the best-selling video game of all time in the first 24 hours since its launch belonged to GTA 5, which earned an estimated $800 million when it debuted in 2013. With the release of GTA 6, Rockstar has broken its own record by a wide margin, with first-day revenue almost five times that of its predecessor.
That puts a video game ahead of the biggest cinema openings and music tours, which have traditionally set the bar for entertainment launches.
GTA 6 Rating
Aside from the revenue, GTA 6 also managed to earn a near-perfect 99 score on Metacritic. To date, only a few titles, including Baldur’s Gate 3 and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, have managed to reach a 99 score on the platform. The user scores for GTA 6, however, are rather varied. At the time of writing, GTA has a 5.6 user rating on Metacritic over nearly 55,000 ratings.
Still, a single video game release outperforming any piece of media film, television, or music has produced in a day is certainly surprising to see. Take-Two’s bet on a long, expensive development cycle appears to have paid off.
That being said, there’s still a much bigger test that lies ahead of GTA 6. First-day numbers are primarily driven by preorders and the hype surrounding a game’s launch, while the game’s actual content will fuel its sales in the weeks and months to come. If it manages to maintain its early momentum, and if the PC release isn’t delayed significantly, GTA 6 could easily become the highest-earning entertainment product of all time.
The post GTA 6 Just Made $3.79 Billion in One Day, and No Movie, Album, or Game Has Ever Come Close appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Razer Kraken Kitty V3 Feels Like a Logical Next Step
items.content:
We see tech companies release upgrades to devices as time passes. Sometimes they make sense. Other times, it might not make as much sense. The Razer Kraken Kitty V3 falls into the latter, thankfully, but at the same time is the sort of upgrade that might not be necessary if someone already owns a previous V2 iteration or intends to only use the headset around the house due to decisions the company made.
To start, a lot of the Razer Kraken Kitty V3 specs aren’t all that dissimilar from the V2 model. They have the same frequency response (20 Hz – 20 kHz), impedance (32 Ω), and 40mm Razer TriForce drivers. Both offer support for 7.1 surround sound. Each offer noise canceling, to ensure you’re hearing what you need to and can focus. Both have the reactive lighting for the cat ears and earcups that you can set up to correspond to emotes and alerts when connected to a PC, if you set it up. They also both have the unidirectional Hyperclear Cardioid mic attached to them, each with the same 100 Hz – 10 kHz frequency response. They even feel like they’re about the same weight, though to be fair I am comparing mine to Pompompurin ones with extra rubbery ears adding to the weight a bit.
Photos by Siliconera
However, there are a few performance changes that you might pick up on if you really pay attention. They’re very minor. I only noticed because I sometimes podcast and often take part in meetings and calls that require a headset. The V2 has -42 dBV / Pa mic sensitivity, while the V3 is at -38 dBV / Pa, 1 kHz. The general sensitivity is also 92.5 dB SPL / mW @ 1kHz for the V2 and 106 dB SPL / mW @ 1kHz for the V3. But these are things you might not super notice.
More noticeable, and appreciated, are the changes that are more obvious with the Razer Kraken Kitty V3 design. The inner earcups are wider and longer, and they fit more comfortably on on my ears. It’s not a huge difference! But I did feel a bit more comfortable.
Also nice is the way controls work now. On the V3 model, there’s a dial for the volume, one button to mute and unmute the mic, and a third one that basically feels there for the new cosplay mode. (More on that in a bit.) The previous model had buttons to make it louder and quieter and the mic button. I prefer the dial, as it’s easier to adjust to exactly the level I need and to feel at a glance when I reach for the controls.
Photos by Siliconera
This version of the Kraken Kitty feels updated for modern platforms and requirements. The V2 used a USB-A cable that was about two meters long. It’s a good length, but I had to rely on adapters to use it with my laptop and other devices. The V3 has a USB-C by default. It feels like more of an acceptance of what we all need and use now, which is handy for compatibility purposes. (The cable is still two meters too, which is fine since that’s a good length.)
Okay, so finally, there’s the new Razer Kraken Kitty V3 cosplay mode. This is a cosmetic feature. If you have a USB-C compatible power bank and plug the wired cable for the headset into it. Remember that button I mentioned earlier for Chroma functions? That lets you choose what the light pattern looks like for the ears and earcups if you are using the headset as a fashion accessory. Since the cable is a good length, you could easily hide the power bank in a backpack, purse, or even pocket. You don’t get the same responses and reactions as if you were using the headset while streaming. However, it does light up. Given how many anime characters out there have been seen in cat ear headsets, it could work in a number of situations.
Photo by Siliconera
The Razer Kraken Kitty V3 can feel like a more subtle incremental upgrade, but there are a few helpful adjustments. The USB-C support off the bat is great, and I preferred the volume dial to buttons for sound control. The quality from the V2 is still here and sometimes feels slightly better. The cosplay mode support is the biggest addition, and people who do consider these fashion or cosplay accessories in addition to practical peripherals might like that. It’s a situation where the V3 will be preferred if you don’t already own a Kraken Kitty, but those with a V2 they love could be fine waiting.
The Razer Kraken Kitty V3 and V3 Pro are available now.

items.title: Top 5 Players to Watch at PGL Major Singapore 2026
items.content:
The highly anticipated PGL Singapore Major is right around the corner as every team enters the final stage of their practice session. Several teams have made an argument for themselves to stand out as the favorites in Singapore, with individual players playing an important part. As the second half of the season has progressed, so has the debate over who is the best player in the world, and everyone making a case for themselves must deliver on the big stage should they bag the title before the season concludes.
In this article, we will try to see the hottest hands in Counter-Strike 2 going into the 2026 PGL Singapore Major.
1. Mathieu “ZywOo” Herbaut – Team Vitality
ZyWoo is the best player in the world, be it his rifle work or his fabled AWPing; he is the player everyone watches out for when facing Vitality’s star-studded lineup. Sure, Vitality has struggled to close out matches in tournaments leading up to the Major, but ZyWoo remains a strong performer who can turn the tide of the game at any moment. Should Vitality lift the trophy, it can be assumed that this will be because of ZyWoo.
2. Ilya “m0NESY” Osipov – Team Falcons
m0NESY is the only esports player in Forbes Russia’s list of the 30 most valuable personal brands of Russian athletes. Image credit: BLAST RIVALS
Team Falcons are a shadow of the team that won the Major in June, but m0NESY’s individual brilliance has saved them time and time again in big events. As the Falcons as a team continue to struggle, m0NESY’s consistency against big teams has proven that he can do it under any circumstances. Top events are where he shines, and even when his team fails to keep up, m0NESY will be coming in with hot hands and a point to prove.
3. Danil “donk” Kryshkovets – Team Spirit
Donk has been the best pure rifler in the world since his tier-1 debut, but Team Spirit has failed to keep up with his extraordinary standards. Despite significant changes made to the team, the CIS side’s last significant honor came in Paris, where it won the Esports World Cup 2026. Driving Spirit to its second Major would take an unthinkable amount of effort from their young gun, but the team’s recent performances cast doubt on whether he could bag his second Major MVP.
4. Kaike “KSCERATO” Cerato – FURIA
The Brazilian starboy has turned into a lethal force under the guidance of FalleN as FURIA continues to challenge for every trophy. While his name is rarely mentioned in the conversation for the best player in the world, KSCERATO’s performances have been instrumental in FURIA becoming a top 5 team in the world. If FURIA are to win the tournament, KSCERATO should bring his A-game to keep up with ZywOo and m0NESY.
5. Ihor “w0nderful” Zhdanov – Natus Vincere
NAVI have lost their edge as tournament favorites, but their recent form has once again got the world talking. w0nderful’s AWPing may have gone under the radar for many, but he has started to pick up significant momentum. For now, it is difficult to imagine NAVI bagging this Major, but they will cause damage with w0nderful’s AWP spearheading their offense while bolstering their defense. Whether his recent form will reach Singapore is a debate for another day.
As Counter-Strike has evolved over the years, teamwork has always been at the center of the game, and no matter how brilliant an individual player is, it is a team that wins trophies. While these individuals will stand out among their peers, not having the necessary supporting cast around them would not be enough to get them firing on all cylinders. All the big names have made the race for Major MVP highly confusing yet interesting as we enjoy the month-long festival of Counter-Strike.

items.title: NVIDIA GeForce Hotfix 621.35 Fixes SSD Writes
items.content:
NVIDIA GeForce Hotfix 621.35 is now available to fix a driver bug that caused excessive SSD writes on Windows PCs. NVIDIA released the hotfix on November 20 after users reported the problem on drivers 621.14 and 621.24. In some cases, the drivers wrote up to 30GB per hour to the system drive while the PC sat idle.
Below, you will find what caused the issue, what the hotfix changes, who should install it, and the risks NVIDIA lists.
NVIDIA GeForce Hotfix 621.35 Release and Fix
NVIDIA released GeForce Hotfix 621.35 to stop the unnecessary writes. The company’s release notes acknowledge that excessive writes to the file nvlog.nvlgstg may occur in the background. NVIDIA tracks the issue under bug ID 7116722.
NVIDIA GeForce Hotfix Driver v621.35 is now available. This update resolves the following:
Excessive writes to file nvlog.nvlgstg may occur in background
Click below to learn more: https://t.co/1oI8isbzD9
Download from: https://t.co/AHyk9uLTHY
— NVIDIA Customer Care (@nvidiacc) November 20, 2026
The hotfix is built on driver 621.24. The problem affected driver versions 621.14 and 621.24. Not every system was hit by it.
What Caused the Excessive SSD Writes
User reports and technical analyses point to the NVDisplay.Container.exe background service. It belongs to the NVIDIA Display Container LS service.
The service kept overwriting a binary log file named nvlog.nvlgstg on the main system drive. This happened even when the PC was doing nothing. The file sits in the NVIDIA Corporation folder inside ProgramData.
The file was not simply extended over time. It was repeatedly shortened and rewritten. That means the write volume may also depend on how large the file had grown.
How Much Data the Bug Wrote
In the worst reported cases, the drivers wrote up to 30GB per hour while idle. Constant writes like this add wear to an SSD and can shorten its lifespan.
Driver 621.01 behaved very differently. It wrote roughly 2MB every 5 minutes during idle periods. Driver 617.42 also does not show the same behavior.
Who Should Install the Hotfix
Users on driver 621.14 or 621.24 are advised to install the hotfix. NVIDIA does not push it through the normal update channel. You need to download the standalone installer from NVIDIA’s Customer Care support page.
Before the hotfix, one workaround was to roll back to driver 621.01.
Why NVIDIA Hotfix Drivers Are Not Automatic
NVIDIA says hotfix drivers skip full Windows Hardware Quality Labs certification. This lets the company reach affected users faster.
The company also describes these drivers as beta and optional. They are provided as-is and go through a much shorter QA process. That is why they are not delivered automatically.
The NVIDIA bug mirrors a separate problem AMD faced earlier in November. AMD responded with its optional Adrenalin Edition 26.11.1 driver, which curbs excessive idle activity on the system drive.

GTA 6 PS5 Crash Reported With Error CE-108255-1
items.content:
The GTA 6 PS5 crash is hitting some players who see error code CE-108255-1 and get sent back to the home screen. Reports say the game closes after a few minutes of play, during certain missions, or at launch. Reinstalling, rebuilding the database, and resetting the console have not fixed it for some players. Some suspect overheating, but no one has confirmed a cause.
Below, you can read what the error code means and which fixes are worth trying first.
GTA 6 PS5 Crash: What Players Report
Some PS5 owners say GTA 6 closes after a few minutes of play. The game then returns them to the home screen with error CE-108255-1. Grand Theft Auto VI has been out since November 19, 2026.
Reports on timing vary. Some players crash after 15 to 20 minutes. Others crash during the opening cutscene or Lucia’s prison sequence. Crashes are happening on the loading screen too, and some players cannot launch the game at all.
Because of how intensive Grand Theft Auto VI is, it's exposing a lot of PS5s that weren't truly stable. pic.twitter.com/2xXzBgllJE
— Charlie (@ghost_motley) November 19, 2026
Players say system updates, cache clears, and factory resets have not helped. Several users also said that the rest of their game library runs fine.
Some players also say autosave does not always protect progress when the console freezes or reboots.
What PS5 Error CE-108255-1 Means
PlayStation lists CE-108255-1 as an error with the game or application. The code does not indicate overheating, cooling failure, or any other hardware fault. It can be an unexpected app closure.
A game closing to the home screen is not the same as a console shutting off. A full shutdown points more strongly to a thermal or power problem.
PlayStation‘s own steps for this code are simple. Start the PS5 in Safe Mode and choose Rebuild Database. If the error returns, back up your data, reset the console, and install the game again.
Is Overheating Behind the GTA 6 PS5 Crash?
Some players blame dust buildup or worn liquid metal in older consoles. Players with newly bought consoles report the same error. Also, there is no confirmed evidence linking the crashes to cooling.
The liquid metal idea has a history. Sony uses liquid metal between the chip and the heatsink. Alderon Games founder Matthew Cassells earlier linked some PS5 unexpected shutdowns to liquid metal moving out of place. He reportedly estimated that 2% to 3% of Path of Titans players hit the issue. That figure has not been independently verified.
However, those reports describe full console shutdowns. They do not describe CE-108255-1 crashes in GTA 6.
A Redditor said that Sony support called the issue software-related. That is a single account, and Sony has made no public statement.
GTA 6 is also a heavy game. Some reports describe a 30 FPS target on current consoles. A heavy workload may expose weak units, but it does not follow that the game damages healthy hardware.
How to Fix GTA 6 Crashing on PS5
No confirmed fix exists yet. These steps are worth trying before you assume a hardware fault:
Install the latest PS5 system software. The update 14.23, which is 1.267GB, is needed to play GTA 6.
Install the latest game updates.
Check airflow around the console and clear dust from accessible vents.
Rebuild the database in Safe Mode.
Run another demanding game to see whether the crashes happen only in GTA 6.
Seek professional diagnosis if the console shuts down fully, runs unusually loud, or shows heat-related behavior.
Do not open the console or try to reapply liquid metal without qualified help.
As of publication, neither Rockstar nor Sony has announced a fix. A software cause would likely mean a patch, while a hardware cause would mean a repair.

items.title: Team SouL’s Coach Ayogi to Miss PMGC 2026
items.content:
In a major blow to Team SouL, coach Rahul “Ayogi” will be missing out on PUBG Mobile Global Championship 2026 (PMGC 2026) due to passport-related issues. S8UL Esports’ Animesh “Thug” Agarwal recently addressed the situation during a livestream. He revealed that Ayogi’s passport will not be ready before the tournament due to some personal reasons. He also clarified that the organisation cannot resolve.
Team SouL’s Coach Ayogi to Miss PMGC 2026 Due To Passport-related Issues
There were reports that Ayogi won’t be travelling to Turkiye with Team SouL for PMGC 2026 due to some passport issues. When Thug recently went live on his YouTube channel, fans requested more details about the Ayogi’s situation. Responding to this, Thug reiterated that Ayogi does not have a passport and revealed that his passport is not going to come through before PMGC 2026 due to some personal reasons. “It’s nothing new. We knew he was not going. And it is not on the org to sort that thing out. We cannot sort that thing out because we don’t even know (the reason). But there are some issues with his passport, so that’s why he can’t come. End of story.”
Following this, a viewer asked Thug whether Ayogi would never go to international tournaments with Team SouL due to his passport issues. “Why would he never come? We’ll do it, it will take time, but it’s not happening right now,” he responded.
Another viewer asked Thug why they did not create Ayogi’s passport beforehand. Thug explained, “The passport can’t be made because of his personal reasons, you understand? Meaning there’s some complication. He would know better, but whatever we know, we’ve shared the information. So there is no point talking about it.”
Team SouL has a lot of experienced esports individuals associated with it, including Naman “MortaL” Mathur, Aman Jain, Siddhant “Sid” Joshi, and more. When a viewer asked if someone will accompany Team Soul to guide them at PMGC 2026. Thug positively responded that there are a lot of individuals to guide the team.
Thug reiterated that the entire team already knew about Ayogi’s passport issue. “However much you all are stressing about it, the players are not. Everyone is very chill about it. Frankly, I’m telling you, everyone is very chill about it.”
With all the players having secured their Turkish visas, Team SouL will be competing at PMGC 2026 with its full roster. However, the team will have to travel without its coach, Ayogi, due to his passport issues. Ayogi played a crucial role in Team SouL’s BMSD 2026 victory, and it will be interesting to see how the team performs at the international tournament without him.

Elvish Yadav to Join GodLike Esports? Rumours Suggest
items.content:
The rumours surrounding CarryMinati joining GodLike Esports were not even completely settled and a new rumour took the gaming and esports community by storm. The latest speculation suggests that renowned internet personality Elvish Yadav could join GodLike Esports in a co-founder role.
Is Elvish Yadav joining GodLike Esports?
The rumour suggesting Elvish Yadav could join GodLike Esports has overshadowed the previous rumours, with all eyes now being on Elvish Yadav. However, neither party has made any official announcement or confirmation, nor has any credible personality specified it.
The rumour started to emerge after some members of GodLike Esports, who reportedly weren’t following him earlier, started following Elvish Yadav. What further fueled the speculation were the comments made by GodLike Esports’ content creator Ankit “AnkiiiBOT” Pandey and S8UL Esports’ Animesh “Thug” Agarwal and Siddhant “Sid” Joshi.
What Thug, Sid, and AnkiiiBOT Have Said
Talking about CarryMinati potentially joining GodLike Esports, in a livestream, AnkiiiBOT expressed uncertainty over whether the mystery content creator joining the organization was actually CarryMinati. He hinted that the mystery creator did not come from an esports or streaming background and was more inclined towards vlogging content.
Sid and Thug, who belong to a rival organization, praised GodLike Esports. Both said, “GodLike is cooking!” Sid further explained, “The things we know… GodLike is doing some industry shattering, breaking, f***ing things. Very hyped to see it. I know they are rivals and everything, but it’s always good to see rivals also grow to that level because it benefits the industry.”
AnkiiiBOT’s statement confirms that the mystery creator does not come from an esports background, so it makes the CarryMinati speculation less likely. Furthermore, the way Sid and Thug praised GodLike Esports, it hints that the mystery creator is not someone from the industry, but is a very big personality. Considering these developments, Elvish Yadav is now being linked to the organisation. However, there’s no official confirmation, and the possibility remains speculation.
With over 21 million followers on Instagram, Elvish Yadav has a massive fan following. Bringing such a big personality into the gaming and esports industry would mean a lot for the industry and could help it grow further. However, it remains to be seen whether the rumours turn out to be true.

Day 2 (November 20): Day 2 will take place on 20 November, where two teams from Pool 2 plus 10 teams from the previous day (#3 to #12 teams from Day 1) will play six games, and the top 2 teams will qualify for the Grand Finals, and the rest of the teams will move to Day 3.
Day 3 (November 21): Day 3 will be played on 21 November, featuring 2 teams from Pool plus the bottom 10 teams from Day 2. After six games, the top 2 teams will qualify for the Grand Finals, while the bottom 10 teams move to Day 4.
Day 4 (November 22): Day 4 will take place on 22 November, where 2 teams from Pool 4 and the bottom 10 teams of the previous day will play six games, and the top 2 teams again qualify for the Grand Finals. The remaining team will be relegated to the Last Chance Stage.

Is Niko Bellic in GTA 6? Return, mission, and voice actor explained
items.content:
If you’re wondering if Niko Bellic returns in Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6), then read on for spoilers about the GTA 4 protagonist. We also go over Niko Bellic’s GTA 6 voice actor.
Key takeaways
Yes, Niko Bellic is in GTA 6. He appears during the Taking Liberties mission in the final chapter of the game’s story.
Niko Bellic looks older in GTA 6 compared to GTA 4. He now has gray hair and wears a jacket, jeans, black turtleneck, and gold chain.
Michael Hollick returns as Niko Bellic’s voice actor in GTA 6.
Niko Bellic is listed as “The Hitman” in GTA 6’s credits.
Table of contents
Niko Bellic in GTA 6
GTA 6 Niko Bellic returns
GTA 6 Niko Bellic voice actor
GTA 6 Niko Bellic FAQs
Niko speaks with Giorgio in GTA 6 (Image credit: Shirrako)
Niko Bellic in GTA 6
Is Niko Bellic in GTA 6? The answer is yes. The character from GTA 4 appears in the fifth chapter of GTA 6. To be specific, he’s in a cutscene during the Taking Liberties mission.
The other main GTA 6 story missions that follow that are VC Baby, Doggie Bag, Operation Savage, Glory Protective Custody, and The End of the Road.
Niko appears older in GTA 6 (Image credit: Shirrako)
GTA 6 Niko Bellic returns
After stepping out of the elevator, Jason, Lucia, and Giorgio enter a dark room accented with red lights. Sitting at a desk with his feet up is none other than an older version of Niko Bellic.
He explains to Giorgio why he’s there in the first place. A two-billion-dollar shipment went wrong, and after missing too many shipments, the cartel decided to take another route.
Giorgio’s not having it, but Niko Bellic is not impressed. Instead, he reveals that he hasn’t killed anybody since 2012. Giorgio panics and promises that he won’t mess up the next shipment. However, Niko Bellic knocks him to the ground and points a gun at him. He then looks at Jason before walking away.
Jason, Lucia, and Giorgio then try to work out what to do about the expensive shipment.
GTA 6 Niko Bellic voice actor
Michael Hollick returns as the voice actor for Niko Bellic in GTA 6. Hollick previously voiced the character back in GTA 4 in 2008.
Interestingly, Hollick is listed as “The Hitman” in the GTA 6 credits instead of Niko Bellic.
Niko in a GTA 6 cutscene (Image credit: Shirrako)
GTA 6 Niko Bellic FAQs
Is Niko Bellic in GTA 6?
Yes, Niko Bellic returns as a character in a cameo in GTA 6.
Who is the GTA 6 Niko Bellic voice actor?
Michael Hollick voices Niko Bellic in GTA 6. He previously voiced the character in GTA 4.
Where can you find Niko Bellic in GTA 6?
You encounter Niko Bellic during the Taking Liberties mission in Chapter 5: Top of the World, Ma. This mission happens after the Bird in the Hand one.
What is Niko Bellic called in GTA 6 credits?
Michael Hollick is credited as “The Hitman” in GTA 6. However, the character he plays is Niko Bellic.
Does Niko Bellic look different in GTA 6?
Yes, Niko Bellic looks older in GTA 6. He has gray hair and sports a jacket, turtleneck, and gold chain.
Is Niko Bellic playable in GTA 6?
No, Niko Bellic is not playable in GTA 6 as he only appears in a cutscene involving Giorgio, Jason, and Lucia.

items.title: All Casino locations in GTA 6 & how to gamble
items.content:
There are dozens and dozens of possible side activities and different locations to see on the map of Leonida in Grand Theft Auto 6. From robbing banks to racing in mud to performing base jumps off buildings, it’s truly staggering what you can do right from the start of the game. However, one of the most memorable side activities across the entire GTA franchise has been gambling at casinos, so you might be curious about where to find locations to bet your money in GTA 6.
Well, we have good news and bad news about the casinos in GTA 6. The good news is there are multiple casinos in Leonida, but the bad news is that you might not be able to use them to gamble for a while. We’ll explain more in the guide below.
Key Takeaways
There are multiple casinos that you can visit in Leonida in GTA 6
Casinos are fully-fleshed out locations on the outside, with names, parking lots, and more
Casinos aren’t as in-depth as other pieces of side content in the game
Table of contents
Key Takeaways
All Casino locations in GTA 6
Vice City Casino
Merlin’s Palace Casino
How to enter and gamble at the casinos in GTA 6
All Casino locations in GTA 6
There are two total casino locations in GTA 6, and they are actually fairly close to one another on the map. The first casino is simply called the “Vice City Casino,” and it’s located in southern Leonard County, east of Bellville and south of Waning Sands. The second casino is called Merlin’s Palace Casino, and it’s located in northwest Vice-Dale County, just south of Balsero and north of Salton.
You can see exact map screenshot locations for both casinos below.
Vice City Casino
The Vice City Casino location. Screenshot by esports.gg
Merlin’s Palace Casino
The Merlin’s Palace Casino location. Screenshot by esports.gg
How to enter and gamble at the casinos in GTA 6
If you’ve driven past these casinos during your time with GTA 6 so far, you might have attempted to enter them so you could throw some money at a craps or poker table. However, you were undoubtedly met with closed doors and no feasible way to get inside the casinos.
We can confirm that both the Vice City Casino and the Merlin’s Palace Casino are both fully closed to players during the entirety of GTA 6. Even at the end of the game in Chapters 4 and 5, you will never receive access to the casinos. It’s unclear what Rockstar Games’ plans are for the casinos, but we would imagine that the developers are waiting for GTA Online to be released to make full use of them.
In front of the Merlin’s Palace Casino in Vice City. Screenshot by esports.gg
This means that there is currently no way to gamble or play casino games in GTA 6. You won’t even be able to play poker or blackjack at a dive bar or other location. However, you can gamble on yourself in other mini-games, such as pool, street races, and time trials.
Hopefully, the doors to both casinos open up soon in GTA 6, but for right now, they remain closed to the public.

GTA 6 sold 32M copies at launch, earning more than $3.7B
items.content:
It looks like Take Two was eager to get the word out on GTA 6's performance just ahead of the game's first full weekend on the market. Following analyst predictions that the game earned over $2.5B at launch, the publisher has now revealed the official numbers, with the game earning over $3.79 billion in just its first few days.
Analysts had predicted around 25M copies sold for the game ahead of the weekend but Take-Two has now confirmed that the game sold over 32M copies in pre-orders alone, setting new records not just for gaming, but for the entertainment industry as a whole. By this time next week, that number could be much bigger, as word of mouth about the game continues to spread.
GTA 6 officially launched on November 19th, more than 13 years after the release of GTA V. For now, the new game is a single-player only experience, exclusively available on Xbox Series X/S and PS5 consoles. However, a PC version is due out in the future, and the new version of GTA Online should be coming next year too.
The game launched to universally positive reviews, earning a rare 99 overall rating on Metacritic, based on over 100 different scored reviews from gaming outlets across the world. The only other game to achieve a similar rating is the original version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, although that was achieved with fewer total reviews.
Speaking on the record-setting launch, Rockstar president, Sam Houser, said “we are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn't be more excited to share this moment with you”.
Now that the main game is out on consoles, hopefully we won't have to wait too long for updates on the pending PC version of the game, and the return of GTA Online.

items.title: Chiikawa Shows the Value of Unanswered Questions
items.content:
When it comes to storytelling, it’s only natural to want things to wrap up with no loose ends. Indeed, there are virtual cottage industries out there dedicated to taking movies, comics, and games to task for leaving questions unanswered. It’s especially the case for stories that might appeal to children. In those cases very few difficult questions are ever asked and when they are, clear answers are typically provided. After all, if we’re trying to teach lessons then it’s probably best not to be too mysterious about it, right? Even media aimed at adults tends to take this approach if it’s seeking mainstream success.
Chiikawa: Something Small and Cute has become a massive success for its creator Nagano. It started off as little more than some amusing doodles posted on the artist’s X account but now has a successful anime, hit movie, and more merch than you can shake a stick at. The anime is now even being officially released in English on the official Chiikawa YouTube channel. As each new comic page was posted, a world started to take shape. Soon there were more characters, more details in the setting, and longer stories that spanned multiple pages.
Through several years’ worth of comic pages, we now know quite a lot about Chiikawa, their friends Hachiware and Usagi, various other denizens, and the magical yet occasionally dark world they all reside in. For as much as we’ve learned however, there are still many things we don’t know. Some things just happen for the amusement of the situation and probably aren’t meant to be taken too seriously. Why does whistle ramune candy sprout from nowhere sometimes? What’s up with that rice cooker embedded in the ground in the forest? Where does Kuri-Manju put all those calories?
Other mysteries might one day have the truth behind them revealed, but Nagano has them on a slow burn. What exactly happened between Momonga and Deka Tsuyo? Where does Usagi actually live? Why do some chiikawas become chimeras, and what does that really mean? What’s the deal with the armored Yoroi-sans? They’re all compelling things to think about, and every so often Nagano throws a little nugget of information out there to get the fans talking all over again.
Chiikawa also raises a lot of questions that are never going to be answered because it’s more interesting to let the fans consider them and make up their own minds. Indeed, one such question sits right at the center of this year’s number one hit movie in Japan, Chiikawa the Movie: The Secret of the Mermaid Island. It adapts one of the more complex comic arcs and the moral problem it puts forward is a big part of why the movie has become so successful. Its refusal to give the viewer relief with a clean answer to the problem resulted in something truly fascinating.
By leaving so much unexplained, Chiikawa allows the fans to try to fill in the gaps. It makes people think more about the world and its characters, and when it flirts with more challenging problems it generates some real discussion. Even younger kids enjoy talking about these mysteries. Perhaps more stories should be willing to leave those lingering questions and allow the audience to put in some work of its own.

items.content:
In Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6), Mandy is a supporting non-playable character (NPC). Played by actress Lexie Shoaibi, Mandy appears early on in GTA 6 when you’re going about as Jason Duval.
Key takeaways
Mandy is an NPC in GTA 6. She’s also one of Brian Heder’s tenants and encounters Jason early on in the game.
Mandy appears in the Pipework mission where Jason visits her home to collect overdue rent and fix her sink.
GTA 6 players shared clips of Mandy flirting with Jason and took note of the severed finger in her sink.
Actress and model Lexie Shoaibi plays Mandy in GTA 6.
Table of contents
GTA 6 Mandy scene and mission
Is Mandy a serial killer in GTA 6?
GTA 6 Mandy actress
GTA 6 Mandy FAQs
GTA 6 Mandy scene and mission
Mandy is one of Brian Heder’s tenants in GTA 6. Jason encounters her in the first chapter’s Pipework mission. During that mission, Jason visits her place to collect overdue rent and fix her sink. While Jason fixes her sink, Mandy flirts with him. However, Jason doesn’t reciprocate her advances.
This Mandy and Jason scene soon attracted the attention of many players, making Mandy one of GTA 6’s most discussed supporting characters.
Mandy flirts with Jason in GTA 6, but Jason is committed to Lucia (Image credit: Rockstar Games)
Is Mandy a serial killer in GTA 6?
Mandy went viral because GTA 6 players shared clips and screenshots of her interactions with Jason on social media. Alongside her flirtatious behavior, players focused on the severed finger that Jason found in her blocked sink. This discovery raised eyebrows and led to theories about Mandy being a serial killer.
At the time of writing and publishing this article, Rockstar Games has neither confirmed nor denied the serial killer Mandy theory.
Mandy’s actress posing in front of a GTA 6 mural (Image credit: Lexie Shoaibi)
GTA 6 Mandy actress
Lexie Shoaibi plays Mandy in GTA 6. The actress and model confirmed her involvement via an Instagram post on Nov. 19.
“Okay, now that Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally out, I can share with you guys a secret, which is that I’m in it!” Shoaibi said. “I play Mandy. I do her voice over and I do her motion capture. And she’s a lot of fun. So if you play the game, let me know if you find me.”
GTA 6 Mandy FAQs
Who plays Mandy in GTA 6?
Lexie Shoaibi did Mandy’s voice acting and motion capture in GTA 6. She confirmed her involvement in the game through an Instagram post.
Is Mandy a serial killer in GTA 6?
Rockstar Games has not confirmed whether or not Mandy is a serial killer in GTA 6. The theory started after Jason’s discovery of a severed finger in Mandy’s blocked sink.
Where is Mandy’s house in GTA 6?
In GTA 6, Mandy’s place is close to Jason’s house in Key Lento. Drive or walk northeast a bit to find it. It’s specially located on Peach Palm Drive. The outside of Mandy’s place is teal and located next to a yellow house.
Where can you find Mandy in GTA 6?
You encounter Mandy at her home during the Pipework mission in the first chapter of GTA 6. Jason visits her to collect overdue rent and fix her sink.
What is Mandy’s full name in GTA 6?
Mandy just goes by her first name in GTA 6. At the time of writing and publishing this article, Rockstar Games has not revealed her full name.
What happens in the Mandy mission in GTA 6?
In GTA 6, Mandy flirts with Jason while he tries to collect her overdue rent and fix her sink. Jason doesn’t return her advances because he’s committed to Lucia. Jason later discovers what appears to be a severed finger in Mandy’s sink. Mandy then quickly takes it away.
Can you play as Mandy in GTA 6?
No, you cannot play as Mandy in GTA 6 because she’s an NPC.
Does Mandy appear in GTA 6 trailers?
No. Rockstar Games did not feature Mandy in GTA 6’s pre-release trailers.

items.title: Esportes da Sorte investigation involves €360.4 million in frozen assets
items.content:
Brazilian authorities have frozen approximately €360.4 million in assets connected to Esportes da Sorte amid an investigation, according to the Ministry of Justice and Public Security.
Operation Cashout press conference (Image credit: Brazil’s Ministry of Finance)
Brazil launches Operation Cash Out
According to Brazil’s Ministry of Justice and Public Security, the Federal Police conducted an investigation into illegal gambling. Called Operation Cash Out, the investigation launched on November 18, 2026 with the goal of dismantling a suspected illegal operation in Pernambuco involving gambling, betting, money laundering, currency evasion, and tax evasion, the noticed revealed.
Companies linked to the group allegedly operated betting services before obtaining authorization and transferred more than €500 million abroad. The Federal Revenue Service and Federal Public Prosecutor’s Office executed 59 search and seizure warrants as well, the post added.
A slide from the Operation Cashout press conference (Image credit: Brazil’s Ministry of Finance)
Esportes da Sorte investigation
According to Brazilian news outlet G1, Darwin Henrique da Silva Filho, the owner of Esportes da Sorte, was one of the operation’s targets.
The Federal Revenue Service noted the alleged use of shell companies, national and foreign corporate structures, and financial mechanisms to hide financial transactions and the origin of funds.
The Federal Revenue Service also alleged that the group used individual taxpayer identification numbers, known as Cadastro de Pessoas Físicas (CPF) numbers in Brazil, belonging to deceased people and minors. Cadastro Nacional da Pessoa Jurídica (CNPJ) numbers, which are Brazilian corporate taxpayer registration numbers, were used as well.
As of November 20, 2026, Esportes da Sorte and Darwin Filho’s lawyers have not responded to G1’s requests for comment.

items.title: Valve’s latest Steam Machine update doesn’t inspire confidence for 2TB buyers
items.content:
Valve has shared a fresh update on Steam Machine availability, and the outlook for the flagship 2TB model appears increasingly uncertain. While reservations for the 512GB model have now been fulfilled, Valve says demand for the 2TB version exceeds current production plans, prompting the company to close the waitlist and warn that customers currently in the queue are no longer guaranteed a unit.
In a new update posted this week, Valve confirmed that the 512GB Steam Machine has now moved to a normal add-to-cart status, with all existing reservations fulfilled. Customers can purchase the system directly while stock remains available. However, Valve says that once current inventory is exhausted, the model will simply switch to an out-of-stock status rather than reopening reservations or creating a new waitlist, suggesting future production remains uncertain.
The update paints a far less encouraging picture for the 2TB model. Valve says it has now sent purchase invitations to all existing reservation holders, but the company continues to face hardware supply constraints, particularly around memory and storage components. According to Valve, the number of customers currently on the 2TB waitlist exceeds the number of units it expects to produce under current conditions.
As a result, Valve has closed the waitlist for additional signups. Those already in the queue will retain their place, but the company cautions that no one on the waitlist is guaranteed to receive a unit. Customers are free to switch to the 512GB model instead, although doing so means giving up their existing waitlist position.
Perhaps most concerningly, Valve admits it currently doesn't know how many additional Steam Machine systems it will be able to manufacture, or what future pricing may look like. The company cites unprecedented increases in memory and storage costs, with the 2TB model expected to remain particularly constrained.
Valve says it expects to have more information to share in January. Until then, customers still holding out for a 2TB Steam Machine face an increasingly uncertain wait, with Valve unable to guarantee that everyone currently in the queue will eventually receive a system.

GTA 6 estimated to have sold 25M copies within days
items.content:
Grand Theft Auto 6 may have sold almost 25 million copies within its first 24 hours on sale, according to new estimates from Sensor Tower. The firm believes Rockstar's latest blockbuster generated approximately $2.36 billion in revenue on launch day alone.
Sensor Tower estimates that GTA 6 sold around 24.58 million copies on launch day, generating approximately $2.36 billion in revenue. Take-Two has yet to release any official sales figures, making these estimates the clearest picture we have so far of the game's launch performance.
Prior to launch, analysts estimated roughly 16 million pre-orders worth around $1.8 billion in revenue. If both estimates are accurate, it suggests millions of players held off on pre-ordering and instead purchased the game after release.
Sensor Tower also estimates that around 75% of sales came from PlayStation 5, amounting to roughly 18.4 million copies, while Xbox Series X/S accounted for the remaining 6.15 million sales.
Grand Theft Auto V generated around $815 million in revenue during its first 24 hours back in 2013, before going on to surpass $1 billion within three days. If Sensor Tower's latest estimates are even close to accurate, GTA 6 has comfortably surpassed that record.
Take-Two has yet to release any official launch statistics, but publishers often wait until a game's first full launch weekend has concluded before revealing major sales milestones, so we may not have long to wait before learning how close these estimates are to the real numbers.

items.title: How to get the unique shotgun Smuggler Gorse early in GTA 6
items.content:
You can never have enough guns in Grand Theft Auto, and GTA 6 is no exception. Here’s how you can get the Unique shotgun, the Smuggler Gorse, as early as Chapter 1!
Where to find the Smuggler Gorse in GTA 6
The Assassin Nipper can be found in a shipwreck on an island in the Permit Keys. You can find it near the Mile Zero Air Station in the south-west portion of the GTA 6 map.
You can get the Smuggler Gorse as early as Chapter 1 playing as Jason. Here’s how.
Head over to Southwind. You can Set Destination anywhere in the area, then drive or hail a RydeMe to it.
From here, choose whether you want to go by sea or air. The area enclosed in red in the image below has a dock with boats on it, and a helipad right under with a helicopter free for the taking.
Head to the area marked by the red square to get to the island marked by the player icon. (Image credit: esports.gg)
Head to the middle portion of a long island in the northern part of Permit Keys, as shown in the image above.
Image credit: esports.gg
Locate the Shipwreck on the island and look around. Use Focus (L3 + R3) to help with this. The wreck is located right before the sand turns into vegetation when going north on the island.
You’ll find the Smuggler Gorse on the ground next to the wreck, along with a Cigar for your troubles. Make sure to save your game after!
OPTIONAL: While you have the helicopter, you can opt to go get the silenced unique pistol Assassin Nipper, located near this area.
Smuggler Gorse stats in GTA 6
The Smuggler Gorse is a Longarm, specifically a Stubby Shotgun. This could be one of your first shotguns, depending on how early you go for the trek.
Type: Stubby Shotgun
Damage: 7.5
Accuracy: 3.8
Handling: 6.2
Range: 2.0
Mag Size: 5
Fire Style: Pump Action
Brand: Fortune & Son
Caliber: 12-Gauge
