items.title: The TenZ Gamble: Why T1’s 2027 Roster Could Struggle
items.content:
T1’s 2027 VALORANT roster is complete, but three questions hang over it before its first match: who plays which role, which language the team calls in, and whether it can finally win a VCT Pacific league stage. The club confirmed Tyson “TenZ” Ngo on 12 November, ending a retirement that began in September 2024. TenZ replied to the announcement with “I’m back”. Austin “crashies” Roberts had joined a day earlier, and Gustavo “Sacy” Rossi was named head coach on 13 November.
The expected starting five is Kim “stax” Gu-taek, Yu “BuZz” Byung-chul, Ham “iZu” Woo-joo, TenZ and crashies. So “sungmin” Seong-min, previously head coach of T1’s academy side, returns as coach. The team is expected to debut at Red Bull Home Ground in December.
T1 rebuilt its staff after releasing KDG on 2 November
T1 cleared most of its staff on 2 November. Head coach Kim “KDG” Dong-gun and assistant coach Lee “CheongGak” Il-ho left, along with players Meteor, Munchkin and DH. T1 credited KDG with taking the team to its first Champions playoffs. Sacy, a Champions and Masters winner as a player, has never coached a team before. Two new players and a new head coach will start their preparation at the same time.
TenZ and stax both played controller in their last seasons
TenZ built his reputation on duelists, but he moved to controller in his final season with Sentinels. Since retiring, he has played only two professional series, for Sentinels’ academy team in May 2025. stax played controller for T1 in 2026, iZu played initiator and BuZz was the primary duelist. crashies has played both initiator and sentinel.
That leaves two recent controller players for a role most compositions fill once. If TenZ plays controller, stax has to move to another role. If TenZ returns to duelist, he shares the role with BuZz. crashies is the most flexible of the five, and T1 has not said how it will split the roles.
T1 adds its first English speakers in VCT Pacific
TenZ and crashies are the first non Korean players on T1’s main roster since the team joined VCT Pacific. The squad has three Korean speakers and two English speakers, with a Brazilian head coach. Mixed Pacific teams usually call in English, and crashies has already played in North America and Europe. T1 has not said which language the team will use.
Gen.G faced a language gap in 2023, when its Korean roster worked with Australian head coach Chris “Elmapuddy” Tebbit. The team missed Champions that year and released five players and two coaches. Elmapuddy later said the language barrier limited his impact. T1’s Korean coach sungmin could ease the same problem between Sacy and the Korean players.
VCT Pacific rules also limit how T1 can change the roster. Teams based in Korea must keep at least three Korean players, and TenZ and crashies fill both import slots. Replacing either import would mean releasing one first.
T1 has reached finals but never won a Pacific league stage
T1 won Masters Bangkok in 2025, its biggest international title. It finished second at Pacific Kickoff in 2025 and 2026, third in Stage 2 and fifth to sixth at Champions 2026. T1 has never won a Pacific league stage. TenZ said on 16 November that VALORANT should copy League of Legends’ pro view feature, his first public comment on the game since the signing.
After Red Bull Home Ground in December, T1 plays VCT Pacific Kickoff in Bangkok in January 2027. It reached the Kickoff final in each of the last two seasons. The TenZ signing was one of the biggest moves in the 2027 transfer window.
The post The TenZ Gamble: Why T1’s 2027 Roster Could Struggle appeared first on TalkEsport.

TCL CSOT targets Q4 2027 IJP OLED production with new 500Hz OLED prototype
items.content:
TCL CSOT has unveiled a new wave of inkjet-printed (IJP) OLED prototypes and display technologies at DTC2026. Among the prototypes on show was a 27-inch QHD 500Hz IJP OLED gaming monitor, while the company also confirmed that its next-generation IJP OLED production line remains on track for mass production in Q4 2027.
Equipment installation for TCL CSOT's next-generation IJP OLED production line began on 31st October, with mass production and shipments currently scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2027. The company used DTC2026 to showcase what that future might look like, demonstrating a 27-inch QHD gaming monitor capable of running at up to 500Hz. Built on an oxide backplane, the display incorporates real-time in-panel compensation technology designed to maintain image uniformity without requiring periodic powered-off compensation cycles. TCL CSOT claims the panel can achieve response times of less than 1ms.
Image Credit: TCL CSOT
Beyond the 500Hz gaming monitor, TCL CSOT also displayed a range of experimental OLED concepts aimed at different device categories. Other prototypes on display included a 14-inch ultra-thin notebook display measuring less than 0.66mm thick and weighing under 66g, a 6.36-inch blue phosphorescent OLED mobile panel designed to improve power efficiency, a 10.95-inch OLED tablet display featuring 360-degree privacy protection, and a 115-inch 16K light-field television capable of glasses-free 3D viewing.
Inkjet-printed OLED technology is viewed as one potential route to reducing OLED manufacturing costs by improving material utilisation and simplifying production. While commercial products based on TCL CSOT's latest generation of IJP OLED technology are still some way off, the company's Q4 2027 production target offers one of the clearest indications yet of when large-scale manufacturing could begin.
KitGuru says: Inkjet-printed OLEDs promise to reduce manufacturing costs, but given that we'll have to wait until Q4 2027 for mass production to start, it seems it will still take some time before we see these OLEDs cost the same as an IPS or VA display.

items.title: The Elder Scrolls Online returns to Skyrim with Winterhold expansion
items.content:
Zenimax has officially confirmed that Winterhold will be the next major zone coming to The Elder Scrolls Online, with the region set to arrive as part of Season Three in early 2027. While details remain scarce for now, players at least know where ESO's next major zone will be set.
For many Elder Scrolls fans, Winterhold is one of Skyrim's most recognisable locations thanks to its icy coastline and the famous College of Winterhold. However, because The Elder Scrolls Online takes place centuries before the events of The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim, players will get to see a very different version of Winterhold when it arrives next year.
This won't be ESO's first visit to Skyrim. The game's Greymoor expansion proved popular among players when it introduced Western Skyrim and Blackreach back in 2020, tapping into the nostalgia surrounding Bethesda's hugely successful RPG. A return to Skyrim with an entirely new zone could once again prove attractive to lapsed players looking for a reason to jump back into Tamriel.
Unfortunately, Zenimax isn't revealing much else just yet. The studio says Winterhold will be fully showcased during a special livestream planned for January 2027, with additional details expected in the annual community letter due next month.
KitGuru says: Skyrim remains the most recognisable setting in the Elder Scrolls universe for many players, so another return to the province feels like a smart move. Now we just need to find out what's actually happening in Winterhold.

items.title: Firaxis is finally bringing XCOM back
items.content:
It has been a decade since XCOM 2, and while Firaxis has yet to officially announce a new game in the series, a new report this week claims that the next XCOM strategy game is indeed in the works, although it appears to be hitting some bumps in development.
XCOM 2 launched in 2016 and remains one of the most highly regarded strategy games of the last decade. Since then, Firaxis has focused on other projects, including Marvel's Midnight Suns and Civilization VII. According to a new report from Bloomberg's Jason Schreier, a new XCOM game is now in development, although the project reportedly missed a significant internal milestone earlier this year.
While news of a new XCOM game is certainly exciting, it unfortunately comes attached to some less positive developments. Firaxis has reportedly laid off around 60 employees, roughly a third of its workforce, as part of a restructuring effort. Studio head Heather Hazen is also set to depart, with parent company Take-Two stating that Firaxis is refocusing on its core strength of developing strategy games.
Despite the cuts, the report claims development on the next XCOM will continue. However, with the project already facing reported development difficulties and Firaxis now undergoing significant restructuring, it remains unclear when the game might be ready for a public unveiling.
KitGuru says: XCOM 2 is still one of the best strategy games released in the last decade, so it's difficult not to get excited by news that the series is finally making a return. Let's just hope the current upheaval at Firaxis doesn't derail it.

Razer goes carbon fibre with new Viper V4 Pro and DeathAdder V4 Pro variants
items.content:
Razer has unveiled carbon fibre versions of its flagship Viper V4 Pro and DeathAdder V4 Pro gaming mice. Rather than simply applying a new finish, the company has rebuilt the shell using genuine woven carbon fibre, resulting in lighter mice that Razer says are also significantly stronger than their standard plastic counterparts.
According to Razer, the woven carbon fibre shell is up to 53% stronger than ABS plastic while helping reduce overall weight. The Viper V4 Pro Carbon Fiber Edition weighs 47g, while the DeathAdder V4 Pro Carbon Fiber Edition comes in at 49g. Both retain the same shapes as the existing Viper V4 Pro and DeathAdder V4 Pro models, with Razer focusing on durability and weight reduction rather than redesigning the mice themselves.
Razer says the shells are produced using a 2×2 twill carbon fibre weave before being hot-pressed and cured under heat and pressure. The shells are then CNC machined to shape and finished with a clear UV-cured coating, allowing the carbon fibre pattern to remain visible rather than being covered by paint.
Beyond the new shell material, both mice continue to use Razer's Focus Pro 50K Optical Sensor Gen-3, HyperSpeed Wireless Gen-2 and fourth-generation optical switches. Battery life is rated at up to 180 hours. The Razer Viper V4 Pro Carbon Fiber Edition and DeathAdder V4 Pro Carbon Fiber Edition will be available from 17th November, priced at £249.99/$249.99.
KitGuru says: The carbon fibre shell is a more meaningful change than the average special edition peripheral, but £250 is still a lot of money for a gaming mouse.

items.content:
Travis Scott, Nike and Rockstar Games are releasing a pack of three Air Force 1 Low ’07 sneakers tied to Grand Theft Auto VI. Each pair is expected to cost $130. Release listings first gave 19 November, the day GTA 6 launches, before the date moved to 21 November. Nike and Rockstar have not officially confirmed the price, the date or where the shoes will be sold.
Scott shared the first images of the collaboration on Instagram in early November. He posed with the shoes beside a pink vintage car, with the caption “As a kid it was a game now it’s reality”. Scott also features on GTA VI: The Album with the track “RHYNO”, part of the game’s 34 song soundtrack.
The three GTA 6 Air Force 1 Low colourways
The pack comes in three colourways: white, black, and a black pair covered in multicoloured stars. The star pair carries the style code JJ7603-900 and the colour name Multi Color/Pale Ivory/Black/Bold Berry/Fire Pink. Images of all three leaked in the first week of November, before Scott confirmed the project himself.
Each shoe swaps the usual “AIR” lettering on the midsole for “GTA”. The designs also carry Scott’s reverse Swoosh, a feature of his earlier Nike collaborations. The star pattern refers to the wanted level system used across the GTA series, and the black pair shows a full six star wanted level.
Nike has not published a product page or said which apps and stores will carry the pack. Nike has sold earlier Travis Scott collaborations through its SNKRS app, Scott’s Cactus Jack website and selected retailers. Those releases usually sold out quickly and appeared on resale sites at higher prices within hours.

Nvidia creates export oversight committee following leadership shake-up
items.content:
Nvidia has had a turbulent few weeks following the departure of founder and long-time CEO Jensen Huang. Now, the company has announced another change behind the scenes, establishing a new National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee amid ongoing scrutiny of AI chip exports and Nvidia's compliance with US export regulations.
According to Nvidia, the new committee will provide board-level oversight of the company's national security policies, export control compliance efforts and global trade risk management programmes. Nvidia's existing National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team will report directly to the committee, as well as interim CEO Colette Kress for day-to-day operations.
The committee will be chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson, alongside fellow board members Stephen C. Neal and John O. Dabiri. Nvidia says the group will meet at least quarterly and will work with independent legal, national security and trade compliance experts. Nvidia says the committee will help oversee efforts to strengthen the company's national security and trade compliance programmes while maintaining closer engagement with government stakeholders.
The announcement comes shortly after Nvidia confirmed that Jensen Huang and company representatives had agreed to appear before Congress as part of an ongoing inquiry related to AI chip exports. While Nvidia has not directly linked the new committee to those proceedings, the announcement comes as the company faces increased scrutiny over AI chip exports. The company is also due to hold its quarterly earnings call later today, marking the first such call in Nvidia's history without Huang at the helm.
KitGuru says: Board committees rarely make headlines, but this one arrives at a particularly interesting moment for Nvidia.

items.title: Introducing Hounded: Crafting the dog adventure coming to PS5 in 2027
items.content:
Hey PlayStation community! We’ve been keeping a secret under wraps at Imprnt Studios and Silver Lining Interactive, and we can finally let the dog out of the bag: Hounded is heading to PS5 in 2027. Get ready to step into the paws of a brave (and incredibly adorable) Border Collie, Duke, as you help him search for his lost master in an epic journey across the conflict-torn world of Anglodia.
Hounded has been in development for just over two years, and in that time we’ve been hard at work developing our very own Motion Matching system for our main character. Along with this exciting announcement, we wanted to show you what making our passion project actually looks like behind the scenes. So, we put together our very first dev diary with a full look into how the sausage (or kibble?) gets made.
Have you ever wondered how you make a dog communicate through animation? Or what a realistic quadruped animation made from scratch looks like before it lands on your screen? We’re tackling all of that and more, while introducing the little guy who started this entire journey: Duke. Check it out.
Play Video
A dog story – who is Duke?
Duke is a young, clumsy, yet loyal Border Collie. He lives in the world of Anglodia – a flintlock fantasy inspired Britain in the late 18th century. It is a beautiful and mythical land filled with mysterious technology that is coming apart at the seams under tyrannical rule. However, Duke’s interests lie outside of politics and the brewing rebellion against the crown… His master, Artemys Fletcher – a secretive key player in the resistance, has vanished. Duke’s home has been torn apart by the regime and the only thing that matters now is finding his master.
Building a border collie from the paws up
Here’s the thing about four-legged protagonists: you can’t just reskin a two-legged skeleton and call it a day. In our earliest test builds, Duke moved like a clunky wooden table with paws. It felt terrible—Border Collies have this iconic, low-slung energy that looks like they are about to run at all times. To bring this into reality in Unreal Engine, we decided to animate all of Duke’s movement by hand, using a handcrafted Motion Matching system. Eventually, we were able to set it up so that it pulls from a library of animations based on real-world references, selects the most appropriate animation for the movement, and smooths out the whole process (for the dev team and for the players).
What does the dog say?
Giving Duke a good expressive range has easily been one of the biggest creative mountains our narrative and animation teams had to climb. While humans rely on words, smirks, and raised eyebrows, Duke has muzzle twitches, ear pivots, and whiskers. We spent a while studying canine expressions and famous animated dogs (shout out to Dug) to make sure Duke could hold his own in cinematic story moments. Every movement, every sad face, and every happy snout you will see in the game is handcrafted by our incredible animation team.
More than just a good boy – Magic of The Tide
As adorable as he looks, Duke is far from an ordinary dog. Beneath the soil of Anglodia hums an ancient, strange magic known as The Tide, and Duke is one of its wielders. He possesses unlockable abilities that no other hound has, such as the Power Bark (smash through obstacles in your way) and Power Howl (electrically charge the mysterious technology you find in the world). He can even pierce the veil to perceive ghostly echoes trapped in time, known as Imprints, reliving moments that unfolded hours before he arrived. What will he discover, and will it help him find Fletcher?
Wishlist on PS5 today
Seeing our game come to life on PlayStation 5 is a dream come true for the whole team—you can add it to your wishlist on your console today. We’ve still got miles to run before 2027, but we wanted to put Duke on your radar early. Take the dev diary for a walk, tell us what you think of Duke, and give your own pets a solid scratch behind the ears from everyone on the crew today.

items.title: DLSS 4.5 updates arrive for EVE Vanguard, Teardown and more
items.content:
EVE Vanguard's new 24/7 alpha has launched with support for DLSS 4.5, making it the headline addition among the latest wave of RTX-enhanced games and applications. Assetto Corsa Rally, Lightyear Frontier, Blender 5.3 and Teardown are also receiving DLSS-related updates.
EVE Vanguard is now playable through the EVE launcher via a Founder Pack ahead of its planned Steam release in 2027. From day one, the alpha includes support for DLSS 4.5 Super Resolution, Multi Frame Generation, DLAA and Reflex, so the final release version of the game should also ship with all of those features in place too.
Elsewhere, Assetto Corsa Rally is set to receive an upgrade from its existing DLSS 4 implementation to DLSS 4.5, bringing improved image quality alongside support for Dynamic Multi Frame Generation. Meanwhile, Lightyear Frontier has officially launched version 1.0 after several years in Early Access, adding support for DLSS 4.5 Super Resolution and DLAA.
Beyond gaming, Blender 5.3 now supports DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction for viewport denoising, helping creators preview scenes in greater detail before committing to final renders. The release also adds native support for RTX Spark devices. Meanwhile, Tuxedo Labs' Teardown, the voxel-based destruction sandbox known for its fully destructible environments and creative heist gameplay, has been updated with Nvidia's latest DLSS Super Resolution model, while DLAA remains available for users prioritising image quality over frame rates.
KitGuru says: EVE Vanguard looks like the strongest addition in this week's DLSS update list, although Blender users may end up benefiting just as much from the arrival of DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction.

The Blood of Dawnwalker gets New Game+ in Update 1.2
items.content:
The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting another major update, with Update 1.2 introducing New Game+ for players who have already completed the game's story. The new mode allows players to begin a fresh playthrough while retaining their character progression, skills and inventory. Update 1.2 also raises the level cap and introduces new rewards for returning players.
New Game+ unlocks after completing the Epilogue and can be started from the main menu using an existing save file. Players will retain their character level, abilities and inventory, while the level cap has been increased to 100. The update also removes zone scaling, allowing players to explore different regions more freely after completing the prologue. To keep things challenging, enemy levels have been rebalanced around player progression, while damage values have been increased for combat encounters.
The update also introduces new versions of existing armour, swords and accessories for New Game+ playthroughs. These items feature updated stats while retaining the same appearance as their original versions. New item frames and labels have been added to help distinguish upgraded gear, while legendary New Game+ items receive a unique red border.
Update 1.2 also includes a number of smaller fixes and balancing changes. The game's soundtrack has been expanded for Eclipse Edition owners with additional music tracks, while terrain geometry fixes aim to improve movement during exploration and combat. Enemy health values between levels 17 and 30 have also been adjusted, alongside changes to how frequently enemies use abilities during battle.
KitGuru says: If you're going to add New Game+, this is probably the way to do it. A higher level cap and new gear gives players something to chase, rather than simply replaying the story with an overpowered character.

items.title: GTA 6’s Leonida’s Weather Teases Six New Screenshots, Shows How Wild Its Weather Gets
items.content:
The Weather Channel spent Monday afternoon, US time, forecasting a state that does not exist. Three days before Grand Theft Auto VI launches on 19 November, the American TV network posted a six-part forecast for Leonida, the fictional version of Florida where the game is set. Each post came with a new screenshot supplied by Rockstar Games, and the opening post had passed 5.2 million views on X by Tuesday evening in India.
Nobody knows weather like we do. That’s why @rockstargames gave us an exclusive look at the forecast for Leonida and the dynamic weather in GTAVI.
“Grand Theft Auto VI takes place in Leonida – a fictional world inspired by modern-day Florida, a landscape with one of the most…
— The Weather Channel (@weatherchannel) November 16, 2026
The Weather Channel’s GTA VI forecast thread on X, posted on 16 November 2026 in the US.
The partnership is a marketing stunt, but the choice of subject is deliberate. Weather has been one of the systems Rockstar has talked about most in the run-up to launch, and the thread came with a statement from Owen Shepherd, Rockstar’s VP of Art for Light and Rendering. “We had to completely reimagine our in-game weather systems to feel more localized, persistent, and above all dynamic,” he said, describing skies that range “from clear blue skies to towering vertiginous cumulonimbus clouds”.
Shepherd also explained why Leonida needed that work in the first place. He called it “a fictional world inspired by modern-day Florida, a landscape with one of the most unpredictable weather systems in the US”. That makes it worth looking at the six forecasts closely, both for what they show about the game and for how they compare with the real Florida.
Six forecasts from a state that does not exist
The forecasts are written in The Weather Channel’s familiar on-air voice, but every detail points back to the game. The first warns that heavy rain is making visibility poor across “many places in the Keys”, and adds that local authorities have installed reflectors on some roads. It finishes with a joke about getting your headlights fixed at Coastal Auto Care, which appears to be one of Leonida’s in-game businesses.
Heavy rain cuts visibility in the Leonida Keys. Image: Rockstar Games via The Weather Channel
The second forecast moves inland, to the swamps of Pelican Valley. “The water is murky at the best of times but this storm’s made it nearly impossible to spot the big nibblers,” the post reads. That line is a nod to the alligators Rockstar has already confirmed among the animals of Leonida, and the screenshot shows a storm front rolling across flooded grassland.
A storm over the swamps of Pelican Valley. Image: Rockstar Games via The Weather Channel
The third shot is the most cinematic of the set. Guests booked into a South Ocean Beach hotel are told their expensive view “might be hidden behind a wall of sea fog coming in off the ocean”. The image shows a bank of fog swallowing the lower floors of a high-rise skyline while traffic keeps moving over the causeways, with patches of blue sky still showing above the cloud.
Sea fog over the hotels of South Ocean Beach. Image: Rockstar Games via The Weather Channel
The fourth forecast, and our lead image, is the stormiest. Anyone heading to the Rusty Anchor for a drink “might need a bigger boat”, because a tropical storm is making the water very choppy. In the shot, lightning drops out of a storm cell over the bay while lights stay on along the shore, jet skis bob beside a wooden pier and a few people stand on the dock watching.
The fifth forecast is the calmest of the six, and it swaps storms for stillness. High humidity covers the waters of Gambit Bay in low-lying mist, “making for a tranquil start to hunting season”. The hunting line fits what Rockstar has said about wildlife so far, since some animals in Leonida are classed as Rare, Discoverable and Legendary and can be tracked.
Low-lying mist at Gambit Bay at the start of hunting season. Image: Rockstar Games via The Weather Channel
The last post covers the morning commute from Key Lento, which is “spicy” thanks to more rain and wind. Its screenshot may be the most revealing of all, because it shows a wet highway under a purple storm sky with green road signs for North Catalan Key and Hamlet. One sign even copies the Toll-By-Plate system used on real Florida toll roads, which shows how closely Rockstar has modelled the state’s everyday details.
Rain and wind on the morning commute from Key Lento. Image: Rockstar Games via The Weather Channel
What Rockstar changed in GTA VI’s weather system
Shepherd’s three words, localised, persistent and dynamic, match what Rockstar has described in earlier interviews. In previous Grand Theft Auto games, one weather state largely covered the whole map at once. As we reported when Rockstar first outlined the GTA 6 weather system, Leonida instead lets one part of the map sit in sunshine while another takes a downpour.
Game Informer’s reporting in September added more detail. Players can watch rain fall in the distance, travel into that area after the shower has passed and find puddles and wet surfaces waiting for them. Clouds move across the map, rainbows can appear after rainfall, and Rockstar has confirmed both hurricanes and tropical storms, as we covered in our round-up of GTA 6’s biggest new details.
The new screenshots show those ideas in practice rather than in a description. The Rusty Anchor storm is a single cell over the water, not a blanket of rain across the whole bay. The South Ocean Beach fog sits low enough to hide the lower floors of the towers while the sky stays bright above it. The Gambit Bay mist, meanwhile, clings to one stretch of ground while the trees behind it stay clear.
Shepherd’s job title is a clue to how closely the two subjects are linked. Weather in a game like this is as much a lighting problem as a physics one, because fog, cloud and rain all change how light reaches every surface in the scene. Rockstar has confirmed GTA VI runs at 30fps on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, with PS5 Pro getting exclusive ray-traced shadows, as we reported when the console frame rates were confirmed.
Persistence is the harder part to judge from still images. Wet roads, standing water and the spray behind cars all appear in the Keys and Key Lento shots, but a screenshot cannot show how long that water stays after the rain stops. Players will only be able to test that once they reach Leonida, and Rockstar has given no figures for how often hurricanes appear or what they do to the map.
How close Leonida’s weather is to the real Florida
Rockstar picked the right state for this kind of system. According to the National Weather Service office in Melbourne, July is the busiest month for lightning across Florida. It says the highest flash rates over the peninsula come from “the collision of the two sea breezes” that form along the Atlantic and Gulf coasts.
The NWS office in Tampa Bay says Southwest Florida’s rainy season runs from 15 May to 15 October. Late May and June bring the most severe storms, with hail, damaging winds and waterspouts common, before the season peaks from July to early September. The Rusty Anchor storm, with lightning striking over open water, looks a lot like that summer pattern.
Fog is a different story, and here Rockstar has taken a little artistic licence. The NWS office in Miami says South Florida’s main fog season runs from late autumn to early spring. It adds that fog usually forms over the Everglades and the southwest coast, which makes the swampy mist of Pelican Valley and Gambit Bay the most true-to-life shots in the set. A sea fog bank rolling into a Miami-style beach is rarer, although the office notes that warm, moist air off the Atlantic can bring fog when it moves over cooler land in spring.
Hurricanes need the least explanation for anyone who follows Florida’s weather. The National Hurricane Center lists the official Atlantic hurricane season as 1 June to 30 November, with a peak on 10 September. GTA VI arrives in the final two weeks of the real season, which suits a game whose tropical storm screenshot has just been forecast by a real weather network.
The Weather Channel thread is also the latest in a run of tie-ins outside gaming before launch, after the Miami Heat released limited-edition GTA 6 jerseys earlier this month. Rockstar’s own GTA VI page lists the game for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, with no PC version announced, as our GTA 6 guide sets out. In India, the game unlocks at midnight on 19 November, as our GTA 6 release time guide explains.
The post GTA 6’s Leonida’s Weather Teases Six New Screenshots, Shows How Wild Its Weather Gets appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: First details on MLB The Show 27
items.content:
Before we dive into new information on MLB The Show 27, let’s take a look back.
As we reflect on 2026, two things stand out above everything else: the incredible passion and support of the MLB The Show community, and our need to better communicate and react to community feedback going forward. Whether you’ve been playing for decades or joined us for the first time this year, you’ve helped make this another special chapter in our franchise’s history.
Community stats from MLB The Show 26
While we’re proud of what our team accomplished this year, we recognize that the heart of MLB The Show has always been its community. Since launch, you’ve hit an astonishing:
1,058,402,460 home runs
55,168,197 triples
1,639,448,296 singles
You’ve also drawn 123,300,616 walks and racked up a staggering 2,130,551,161 strikeouts. It seems we have some work to do on our collective plate discipline and pitch recognition!
But it’s not all strikeouts. You’ve also recorded 18,666,758 Perfect-Perfect hits and scored an incredible 2,506,757,548 runs.
And if those numbers weren’t impressive enough, the community collectively spent the equivalent of 31,541 years playing MLB The Show this year.
This year was not without some issues and hopefully over the next few months we’ll show you how we’ve made improvements in a host of areas.Your stories, feedback, creativity, and passion remind us why we do what we do. We don’t take your time, trust, or support for granted, and we’re incredibly fortunate to have a community that cares so deeply about the game.
From all of us at San Diego Studio, thank you for another unforgettable year. We’re excited about what lies ahead and look forward to continuing this journey together.
Get ready for MLB The Show 27
So, what lies ahead? We’re eager to share the exciting new features and improvements coming to MLB The Show 27, but it’s still a little too early to reveal what’s in store. However, there’s one announcement we can’t wait to make: The Tech Test is officially returning for MLB The Show 27.
Tech Tests are invaluable to the development process. They help our team identify bugs, evaluate performance, and gather meaningful feedback from the community before the game officially launches.
Now, you might be wondering: If Tech Tests are so important, why haven’t we held one since MLB The Show 23? That’s a fair question.
Game development is challenging, and each year brings its own set of difficult decisions and competing priorities. Some of those decisions resulted in us not holding Tech Tests for the past few years. We appreciate your patience, passion, and continued support, and we’re looking forward to having you be part of the process again. We will provide more details on the Tech Test in the new year.
Now & Later Packs return, so keep playing MLB The Show 26
There is still more ahead for MLB The Show 26, and the time you spend playing can give you a head start in MLB The Show 27. Now & Later packs are coming back.
Now & Later Packs contain items you can use now in MLB The Show 26, with the added bonus of allowing you to redeem The Show Packs “later” in MLB The Show 27 at no additional cost.
Each Now & Later Pack you earn playing Diamond Dynasty Content in MLB The Show 26 on console will give out a Now & Later voucher that will automatically be redeemed into The Show Packs when logging into MLB The Show 27 on console during its standard release. Make sure you log into ‘27 with the same account you used to earn Now & Later Packs in ‘26.
While that’s all for today, in the meantime, get a head start and start earning those Now & Later Packs in MLB The Show 26.
We look forward to sharing more soon and are excited about what’s to come in 2027. In the meantime, for the latest MLB The Show news, head to TheShow.com, sign up for The Scouting Report, and follow our official social channels.

items.title: Ian Buck Kicks Off NVIDIA’s Week at SC26 as Science Enters the Age of Agents
items.content:
NVIDIA’s Ian Buck kicked off the company’s week at SC26 in Chicago on Monday with new tools for AI agents, software that can plan experiments, run code and check results on researchers’ own systems.
In NVIDIA’s special address, Buck announced Nemotron for Science, the Rubin HPC GPU and an expanded Vera CPU platform for high-performance computing. He also detailed a new collaboration in quantum computing with IBM and Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory.
“The frontier of computing and the new scientific stack is going to be simulation, as always, but combined with AI and the future of quantum,” said Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA.
Buck opened the talk by looking back to his first public talk on CUDA, at an SC06 tutorial in Tampa, Florida, 20 years ago. NVIDIA now offers more than 1,000 CUDA-X libraries, he said.
Open Models for Science Agents
“[Agents] have been just a game changer in how we interface with our supercomputers, with our devices, our instruments and how we can do the research,” Buck said.
Simulation remains the foundation of scientific computing, “which will always be on the top,” Buck said, with AI, quantum and now agents working alongside it.
Nemotron for Science combines the Nemotron 3.5 Super VL open model with a new open chemistry dataset and post-training recipes for life sciences and chemistry, Buck explained. Researchers can run it locally on a DGX Spark, a workstation or their own supercomputer.
At Argonne National Laboratory, Buck said, an agent built with the toolkit took a single prompt, planned and tested hypotheses, chose which simulations to run and identified two new binding sites.
“You own your data. You own the model,” Buck said.
Buck highlighted other agents already in use:
GROMACS: An agent from KTH Royal Institute of Technology repairs broken GROMACS setups on its own. In one overnight run on a single DGX Spark, it fixed 81% of test cases.
SETI Institute: At the Allen Telescope Array, an agent took a one-line prompt to plot a methanol line. Buck explained that it then retuned for Doppler shift on its own [NGC 869 vs. 896, check slide].
Nsight AI Porting Agent: NVIDIA’s new agent ported a routine from the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model to GPUs, Buck said, speeding it up more than 5x using about 150 million tokens.
CPUs for the Agent Loop
Agents lean on CPUs to run tool calls between model steps, Buck explained.
“That’s exactly what agents need,” he said. “They need a CPU that can run, evaluate, run the tool, perform the operations, gather the results.”
DKRZ, the German Climate Computing Center, has selected Vera CPUs for its HLRE-5 supercomputer, expected in early 2028. Buck said it joins Vera systems already announced at Texas Advanced Computing Center.
A New GPU for Science
Rubin HPC is a new GPU in the Vera Rubin platform, built for science, engineering, analytics and AI, Buck said.
It supports precisions from FP64 to FP4, adds sparse-data acceleration and connects over seventh-generation NVIDIA NVLink. With more than 50,000 CUDA cores, it has about three times as many as Hopper, Buck said. It is expected in 2028.
Quantum Error Correction
Buck said a simulation on Jülich’s JUPITER supercomputer showed that a technique called magic state cultivation can cut the operations needed for one logical step tenfold. The work is being added to CUDA-Q.
NVIDIA, IBM and Fermilab announced plans today for a quantum computing co-design platform to support error-correction and applications research. NVIDIA and IBM are pairing NVIDIA DGX B200 systems with IBM quantum computers, including those powered by IBM Quantum Nighthawk.
Buck also introduced a new breakthrough for quantum decoding. The goal, Buck explained, is to cut decoding latency from about 300 microseconds to 10. A new CUDA-Q decoding algorithm, TCBP-JOBS, cuts error-correction research computation from 12 weeks to 45 minutes, he said.
Networking
Buck also showed one of the first deployments of NVIDIA Photonics co-packaged optics switches, at Lambda. He said they are 15x more reliable on bit errors and link flaps.
See notice regarding software product information.

items.title: Phison showcases 28GB/s PCIe Gen6 storage controller at SC26
items.content:
Phison has unveiled a trio of new storage technologies at SC26, headlined by its upcoming X3 (PS5303) enterprise SSD controller. Designed for PCIe Gen6, the controller is targeting up to 28GB/s sequential throughput and 6.8 million IOPS, potentially delivering close to twice the performance of current PCIe Gen5 enterprise SSDs.
The new controller supports a PCIe Gen6 x4, NVMe 2.3 interface and forms part of Phison's wider push into next-generation datacentre infrastructure. Alongside the controller, the company is also developing supporting PCIe Gen6 components such as redrivers and retimers designed to maintain signal integrity at higher transfer speeds. Phison says its PS7161 has become the first PCIe 6.0 redriver to appear on the PCI-SIG Integrators List.
Phison also used SC26 to highlight its Computational Storage architecture. Rather than moving large datasets between storage, memory and CPUs for processing, the technology brings compute resources directly to where the data resides. According to the company, this approach can reduce data transfers by between 10x and 100x in suitable workloads while freeing up host CPU resources. The architecture incorporates an integrated NPU delivering 36,800 DMIPS of compute performance, paired with 64GB of memory and support for frameworks like PyTorch, vLLM and OpenVINO.
The third announcement centres around Phison's Mixed Media architecture, which combines high-endurance pSLC flash and high-capacity QLC flash within a single SSD. The goal is to eliminate the need for dedicated cache drives while allowing performance and capacity to scale together. Phison also claims the design improves resilience by distributing cache resources across multiple drives, reducing the impact of individual drive failures while maintaining compatibility with standard NVMe infrastructure.
There is no word on when we might see any of this in consumer level drives, or even enterprise hardware, but we expect that will start to change in 2027.
KitGuru says: PCIe Gen6 SSDs may still be some way from widespread deployment, but Phison's 28GB/s throughput target gives us a clear indication of the performance level being aimed for here.

JioBLAST’s First VCT Qualifier Opens With Self-Hosted Matches and a Last-Minute Bracket Change
items.content:
The VCT 2027 Kickoff Open Qualifiers for South Asia began on 17 November, and the first day of JioBLAST’s first Valorant Champions Tour event drew complaints from players before many of the opening matches had finished. Teams said they were left to set up their own match lobbies, and one player said a new schedule and bracket arrived on Discord an hour before his team was due to play. JioBLAST, the Indian venture that pairs Jio with BLAST, had not commented publicly on the complaints by the evening.
What you said here is one thing, and there’s one more thing I’d like to add.
Since I’m also playing in this VCT Qualifier, I honestly can’t get my head around the fact that the admins/management released the schedule and match timings last night, around 11 PM–12 AM on the 16th… https://t.co/LwX4ivTRe6
— Hassan Aseel Rasheed (@Asitte_) November 17, 2026
Hassan Aseel Rasheed’s post on X about the VCT South Asia qualifier schedule, 17 November 2026.
Riot Games named JioBLAST as the organiser in early November, after NODWIN Gaming ran South Asia’s Challengers circuit in 2026. As our guide to the South Asia Open Qualifiers explained, the Swiss stage runs from 17 to 20 November and sends eight teams to a double-elimination playoff from 23 to 29 November. Only two teams will go on to Kickoff APAC, and the playoffs will be broadcast.
What players say went wrong on the first day of the qualifier
The loudest complaint came from a post by an Indian esports news account on X, published at 1:25 pm Indian time, shortly before the first matches were due to start. It said there were “no mods, no admins” to oversee the opening matches, and that teams had been asked to contact each other, set up their games and play. By the evening, the post had passed 25,000 views, far more than JioBLAST’s own post announcing the qualifier the day before.
A more detailed account came from inside the event. Hassan Aseel “Asitte” Rasheed, a Maldivian player who was named Best Esports PC Player of the Year at awards backed by Ooredoo Maldives in 2023, said he was playing in the qualifier himself. In his post on X, he said the schedule and match timings were released at around 11 pm to midnight on 16 November, with matches due to start from 2 pm Indian time the next day.
“That was fine, even though it wasn’t a full 24 hours’ notice,” Rasheed wrote. On 17 November, however, he said teams were told on Discord, an hour before their scheduled matches, that a new schedule and new brackets had been released. “It now seems like we have to play a BO3 today,” he added, and said many teams were raising the same issue in Discord voice chats and channels.
Rasheed tagged JioBLAST, Riot’s VALORANT India and South Asia account and a Riot staff member in his post, and later tagged Riot Games and VALORANT as well. Rushindra Sinha, whose Global Esports left Valorant and esports in October, also replied to the original complaint. “Idk how I’d feel if we had to play like this,” he wrote.
Why self-hosted early rounds are normal but late bracket changes are not
Not everyone agreed that the self-hosted matches were a scandal in themselves. Purab Jyoti Kashyap, a Valorant community figure in India, wrote on X that the round of 256 and round of 128 are usually hosted this way. He added that teams could not “expect admins to host 128 matches simultaneously”, and pointed out that “it’s a BO1 format”. Another reply made the same point, saying open qualifiers in every region had been run like this until the later stages.
That is how many large online qualifiers work. Teams in the early rounds create a custom lobby, play their match and report the score, while admins handle disputes and take closer control once the field shrinks. With an opening round that Kashyap put at 128 matches, a dedicated admin for every lobby would be unusual for any organiser.
Kashyap still said JioBLAST’s communication “could definitely be better”, and he added that it had “changed the bracket twice within 24 hours”. The two accounts also differ on match length, with Kashyap describing a best-of-one format and Rasheed saying his team now faced a best-of-three. JioBLAST had not posted a revised schedule or bracket on its X account at the time of writing.
Two Kickoff APAC places for South Asia’s Valorant teams
The stakes explain why a late schedule change lands badly. Under Riot’s new VCT 2027 system, the two South Asian qualifiers join a four-team Kickoff Last Chance Qualifier with Oceania’s playoff winner and Southeast Asia’s runner-up. The winner of that event takes the final Open place at VCT Pacific Kickoff in Bangkok, where the top three teams reach Masters Seoul.
The field includes established names chasing that route. GodLike were reported to be building a return roster around RvK for these qualifiers, and Helix Esports announced its own line-up on the day the event began. For smaller teams across the region, including Rasheed’s in the Maldives, this is the first chance of the 2027 season to reach the Pacific stage.
South Asia’s tournament operations have faced scrutiny before. In May, ARISE Esports alleged that a team in VCSA 2026 was allowed to keep playing after one of its players received a Riot ban for cheating. Riot has also shown it will step in during Open Qualifiers, as it did when it disqualified Team BONK and ordered replays in the EMEA Kickoff qualifier on 8 November.
The Swiss stage continues until 20 November, with the remaining rounds set to decide which eight teams reach the playoffs. Those playoffs begin on 23 November and will be shown live on the official JioBLAST and VALORANT YouTube channels and on JioTV. The two teams that come through will then represent South Asia at Kickoff APAC.

items.title: Nvidia Board Creates National Security Committee as Washington Presses for Answers on China Chips
items.content:
Nvidia’s board has set up a new committee to watch over the company’s national security work and export controls, five days after Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive. The National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee was announced on 17 November, the same day Nvidia reports its third-quarter results, the first under interim chief executive Colette Kress. In its announcement, Nvidia said the new standing committee will be responsible for board-level oversight of “national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management”.
The NVIDIA Board of Directors has established the National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee. Read the release: https://t.co/uIeCqHURiI
— NVIDIA Newsroom (@nvidianewsroom) November 17, 2026
Nvidia’s newsroom announced the committee on X on 17 November 2026.
The timing is hard to separate from the pressure building in Washington. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has demanded answers from Nvidia’s board within 10 days, as we reported when he called for a “dramatic shakeup” at the company. A day before the committee was announced, the Commerce and Justice departments said in a rare joint statement that they had been investigating the Singapore cloud company Megaspeed since 2024.
Who sits on Nvidia’s new national security committee
Director Suzanne Nora Johnson, a former vice chairman of Goldman Sachs, will chair the committee. The other two members are Stephen Neal, chairman emeritus and senior counsel at the law firm Cooley, and John O. Dabiri, a professor of aeronautics and mechanical engineering at Caltech. All three are listed on Nvidia’s board of directors page, which now names Harvey Jones as chair.
Judging by those biographies, none of the three comes from a national security or export control background. The board appears to know it, because the committee will hire “independent, outside experts” in law, national security and trade compliance to support its work. It will meet at least four times a year, including sessions with management and private sessions without them.
The change to reporting lines may matter more than the committee itself. Nvidia’s existing National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team will now report directly to the committee, as well as to Kress on day-to-day operations. That gives the board a direct line to the teams that handle export compliance, rather than hearing from them only through management.
Why the board is acting on export controls now
Questions about the board’s oversight of export controls did not start with Huang’s exit. In a letter dated 1 June, Senator Elizabeth Warren asked Nvidia whether the board was providing meaningful oversight of export control compliance. She addressed it to general counsel Tim Teter and to director Brooke Seawell, who chairs the audit committee, and cited several criminal cases over Nvidia chips allegedly diverted to China.
One of those cases, brought in March 2026, charged three people, including a Super Micro Computer co-founder, over roughly $510 million of servers with restricted Nvidia products headed for China. Warren asked whether the audit committee had carried out any independent review of Nvidia’s export control programmes after that indictment. The new committee now gives that question a dedicated home on the board.
The scandal around Megaspeed then pushed the issue to the top of the agenda. Huang resigned on 12 November as president, chief executive and director, and Jones became the board’s first-ever chair on the same day. The board had already opened an independent investigation on 8 November, overseen by a committee of independent directors with outside counsel, after reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort.
“NVIDIA recognizes that advanced silicon technologies and the emergence of artificial and superintelligence present unprecedented challenges for national security,” Jones said in the announcement. He added that Nvidia is “committed to working constructively with government and industry partners” to build a framework that protects national security while supporting innovation. The announcement did not say when the committee will hold its first meeting.
What Nvidia’s announcement leaves out
The release does not mention Huang, Megaspeed or the government investigations by name. It also does not name the outside experts the committee will hire, or say whether the board plans to add a director with national security experience. The board itself is under closer watch, as our report on director Mark Stevens’ share sales before Huang’s exit showed.
The committee also arrives without any announced change in who runs Nvidia’s compliance work. The same National Security and Global Trade Compliance teams remain in place, and the board says it will work to “enhance” them rather than replace them. For investors weighing the company Huang built, the first test comes within hours.
Nvidia will report its results for the third quarter of fiscal 2027 at about 1:20 pm Pacific time on 17 November, with an earnings call at 2 pm. In India, that is 2:50 am and 3:30 am on 18 November. It will be Kress’s first earnings call as interim chief executive since Huang’s resignation.

Legacy CS2 Orgs Could Quit If They Miss Majors, Warns TechGirl, as Sticker Money Dries Up
items.content:
Counter-Strike’s biggest names could start walking away from the game if they keep missing Majors, according to presenter and podcaster Sam “TechGirl” Wright. Speaking on the latest episode of Feed the Trolls, her show with Duncan “Thorin” Shields, she said she thinks “a lot of these legacy orgs eventually pull out of Counter-Strike if they’re not making the Major”. The warning lands a week before the PGL Major Singapore begins on 24 November, with fnatic, NRG, paiN and TYLOO all missing from the 32-team field.
Wright’s point is about money as much as prestige. Since Valve rebuilt the Major sticker system in May, an organisation’s income from the biggest event of the season depends far more on how far it goes. Teams that do not qualify get nothing at all, and for clubs with large wage bills and few other reliable revenue streams, that gap is getting harder to absorb.
Feed the Trolls Ep 86, with TechGirl, Thorin and Ne0kai, published on 16 November 2026. The sticker discussion starts at 32:28.
How Valve’s sticker changes squeezed CS2 teams
For years, Major stickers were sold in capsules, and organisations and players negotiated their own splits in their contracts. Valve scrapped capsules for the IEM Cologne Major in May 2026 and moved to a Major Shop, where fans buy the exact stickers they want with tokens. Half of all sales still go to the tournament organiser, the teams and the players. What changed is that Valve now sets each team’s royalty rate by its seeding before the Major and its final placing after it, as Counter-Strike’s official account announced at the time.
The gap between the top and bottom of that scale is wide. The Major champion receives 2.85% of token sales, while the bottom-placed teams receive 0.72%, and each team’s share is now split evenly between the organisation and its five players. On every $100 million of sales, that leaves a champion’s organisation with about $1.43 million and a first-stage casualty’s with about $360,000. At Cologne, the bottom rate went to Gaimin Gladiators and SINNERS, whose organisations each took just 0.36%.
Some team owners warned about this months ago. M80 chief executive Marco Mereu said in June that the change “could cause teams to refocus on other events besides the Majors” as they look for income. Reports since then have described sales slowing sharply after the Cologne launch, and Valve skipped its usual end-of-event sticker sale for the first time. For organisations that relied on a healthy sticker cheque even after an early exit, the budget maths has changed, and missing the Major altogether now leaves an even bigger gap against rivals who go deep.
The FiRe CEO who says the sticker problem will be fixed
Wright also took aim at one organiser in particular. On the podcast, she said that “apparently” the chief executive of FiReSPORTS had claimed the sticker situation would be fixed after Singapore. “How convenient that leads into his Majors,” she added. FiReSPORTS, the Argentine company behind FiReLEAGUE, will host the first Major of 2027 in Buenos Aires, before Perfect World stages the second in Shanghai.
The chief executive in question is Rodrigo Figueroa Reyes, and his own words were slightly different. In an interview with Dust2 Brasil on 5 November, he said he thinks Valve “will adjust the sticker issue now in Singapore”. He added that his event will have “the same values as before” by the time teams arrive in Buenos Aires. He also said FiReSPORTS has a direct line to Valve and expects PGL owner Silviu Stroie, who has a close relationship with the developer, to help push for changes.
Neither Valve nor PGL has announced any change to the sticker system for Singapore, and Valve has not released the event’s stickers yet. The Singapore Major already has its own complications, too. Four betting-backed teams were forced to play under different names because of local gambling laws, and others such as BC.Game rely on a regional exception to field their rosters.
Which legacy orgs are on the outside of the Singapore Major
The Singapore field shows why the warning resonates with fans. Fnatic lost the Stake Ranked final 3-2 to Eternal Fire, NRG were knocked out of the FiRe Last Chance quarter-finals by Wildcard, paiN exited Gamers Club Masters early, and TYLOO withdrew from an event in Lisbon. Several of those clubs have been regulars at Majors in recent years. Qualification now runs through Valve’s Regional Standings, and the episode spent a section on how teams can plan their calendars around those points.
Some famous names did make it to Singapore, even if not all of them took the direct route. American side 100 Thieves reached Stage 1 after what the episode’s chapter list calls a “VRS-maxxed” season, while Astralis and Natus Vincere start in Stage 2. The full bracket, from Stage 1 to the playoffs at the Singapore Indoor Stadium from 10 to 13 December, is on our PGL Major Singapore wiki page.
The post Legacy CS2 Orgs Could Quit If They Miss Majors, Warns TechGirl, as Sticker Money Dries Up appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: IEM Beijing locked in through 2028 as EFG signs 3-year deal with city esports body
items.content:
Under a three-year framework deal that ESL FACEIT Group (EFG) concluded with the Beijing Esports Industry Development Association, Intel Extreme Masters (IEM) Beijing will be held each year as a Counter-Strike 2 (CS2) tournament between 2026 and 2028. The deal was rubber stamped at a ceremony during IEM Beijing 2026, Insider Gaming detailed.
The Bloomage Biotech Biohyalux ECM Arena in Wukesong, Haidian District, successfully hosted IEM Beijing 2026 earlier this month, which MOUZ won. The Association, which is supervised by the Beijing Municipal Bureau of Press and Publication, will now start working closely with EFG and local authorities on a long-term support structure. The aim is for broadcasters, sponsors, and Chinese esports clubs to get the commercial safety net they crave.
Marc Winther, Director of Esports Counter-Strike 2 at EFG, hailed the deal as a flagship event for domestic fans. He also said the arrangement offers teams and partners in the area a stable footing for expansion.
The numbers behind the deal
Looking at the figures, it’s no surprise that EFG wanted to hang around: the 2026 edition prompted almost 60,000 fans to turn up across six days of competition, which EFG calls the biggest standalone IEM held in Asia ever. It also revived IEM's 360-degree arena stage for the first time since 2022, when the IEM Rio Major took place.
IEM Beijing 2026Detail
DatesNov. 2 to 8
Teams16
Prize pool$1.25M
Attendance59,000+
ChampionMOUZ
A Chinese CS2 audience that keeps growing
The commitment follows a run of strong domestic numbers. IEM's standalone Chinese debut was in Beijing in 2019. IEM Chengdu in 2025 sold out with more than 35,000 attendees and 770,000 peak online viewers. Research firm Niko Partners estimates CS2 pulled 137.5 million viewers on Chinese livestreaming platforms in June 2026, up 50 percent month on month, making it the second most-watched shooter in the territory.
Three years of municipal backing is a different proposition entirely from a one-off stop. Teams and sponsors now have a known destination they can plan around, while local fans are guaranteed top tier for the next three years at least. The 2026 edition has set a high bar for the next two.
MOUZ made the first edition under the deal count
MOUZ deservedly lifted the trophy and collected $360,000 without dropping a map, dismantling The MongolZ 3-0 in the grand final, and taking Mirage 13-5, Dust2 13-6, and Inferno 13-4. Across the event, they went 11-0 in maps.
xertioN was named MVP with a 1.28 HLTV rating. Seven players earned EVP honors, including four MOUZ players,: NAVI's w0nderful and b1t, and The MongolZ's Techno. MOUZ took five individual awards in total.
The circuit now turns to the PGL Singapore Major 2026, which starts Nov. 24. The next IEM Beijing is expected in 2027, though EFG hasn't yet revealed dates for it.

GTA 6 Launch Day Marathons: List of Biggest Streamers to Watch
items.content:
After years of trailers, leaks, and two delays, the global launch of Grand Theft Auto VI is finally upon us. As we stand only a few hours away from the release of what is arguably the most anticipated video game of all time, the excitement is palpable among gamers throughout the globe. Fans have already started taking days off work and clearing their schedule as they get ready for a return to Vice City.
For the unaware, GTA 6 is all set to launch on the PlayStation 5 and the Xbox Series X|S on November 19, 2026. This means PC gamers might have to sit this one out for now, as no release date for the game has been given on PC at the time of writing.
But if you’re on PC, or you don’t have a next-gen console, don’t worry. You can still be part of the launch-day celebrations, as several prominent streamers are set to broadcast their playthroughs from the moment servers open, and that means you can watch the game without owning it.
Major streamers from throughout the world have already started organizing GTA 6 marathons on the game’s launch day, with many planning to stay live for 12, 24, or even more hours as they explore Leonida.
In this article, we’ll go through the biggest GTA 6 launch day marathons you need to be aware of if you’re planning to catch the gameplay live alongside thousands of other gamers.
GTA 6 Launch Day Marathons List: Best Streamers to Watch
Here are some of the biggest names in the streaming world who have confirmed GTA 6 marathons right from the launch day:
1. Kai Cenat (Twitch / YouTube)
The clear frontrunner for the biggest individual stream is Kai Cenat. Kai has spent weeks preparing for a massive GTA 6 launch-day stream with a five-game GTA marathon (III through V) that he completed in roughly 130 hours. For GTA 6 he has confirmed a full playthrough aiming for 100% completion while also sharing a trailer for it on this X handle.
GTA 6 FULL PLAY THROUGH
NOVEMBER 18TH 8PM EST pic.twitter.com/W6rhy1JhTn
— Kai Cenat (@KaiCenat) November 16, 2026
2. IShowSpeed (YouTube)
Although Speed has confirmed that he won’t be doing a continuous 24-hour marathon for GTA 6, he will be doing roughly 12-hour streams every day, starting November 18 at 9 PM ET. He further said that he will focus on enjoyment and exploration rather than rushing the story.
IShowSpeed says he WON'T be Marathoning GTA 6 but will still stream the game for 12 hours a day so he can Take his time and Enjoy the Game!
"I waited my whole life to play this game. Why would I wanna rush it?" pic.twitter.com/2CLYsuoJtr
— Speedy Updates (@SpeedUpdates1) November 16, 2026
3. Official YouTube 24-Hour Launch Stream
YouTube itself is running a massive coordinated event to prepare for the GTA 6 launch in partnership with Rockstar. The pre-show will take place on November 18 at 11 PM ET, hosted by RDCWorld, while the main stream will go on for 24 hours starting at midnight ET on November 19.
Featured creators include Caylus, Zhong & Kat, Jelly, Rivers, Jake Baldino, Cinna, Payal Gaming, and a lot more content creators from over a dozen countries. This is the closest thing to an “official” day-one marathon that fans will be able to witness, so you won’t want to miss it.
4. Lacy + CORE Group (Twitch)
Nick “Lacy” is organizing a week-long 24/7-style GTA 6 marathon with Clix, Marlon, JasonTheWeen, and Stable Ronaldo. The group is setting up in a Miami mansion, and it’s certain to be one of the more ambitious collaborative efforts during launch week.
5. DarkViperAU (Twitch)
DarkViperAU, one of the most well-known names in the GTA speedrunning community, is organizing a GTA 6 launch-day livestream of his own. He has also confirmed that the stream will be packed with exciting giveaways for fans to participate in.
Note that the game unlocks at midnight local time, so New Zealand and Australian streamers will be the first to go live.
From the hype surrounding the launch of GTA 6, day one of its release might just be one of the biggest streaming moments of the decade, if not ever.

Star Wars: Galactic Racer to receive 4-player local splitscreen in Early 2027
items.content:
Having launched back in October, the team at Fuse Games recently-revealed that the well-regarded arcadey roguelite racing game ‘Star Wars: Galactic Racer’ had hit a major milestone, officially surpassing 1.5 million players. Teasing at the time that “we can't wait to share more about the future of STAR WARS: Galactic Racer with you” it appears as though they could indeed not wait – having now confirmed that Galactic Racer will be getting local 4-player splitscreen support early next year.
Taking to BlueSky to make the announcement, the Galactic racer team offered an unexpected update, writing: “We’ve heard you! Local split-screen multiplayer racing is coming in early 2027.”
While in and of itself a welcome announcement, the local multiplayer update will be made available alongside a brand new mode, confirming that “a dedicated team at Fuse Games has been working hard to develop a new mode: Free Play,” with it being described as follows: “Choose your vehicle, character, planet, and track to race alone or with up to 3 other players in local splitscreen action.”
Local splitscreen has become an increasingly rare feature in games nowadays, both due to the rise in online gaming as well as the general computational cost of rendering a scene out multiple times. As such, it is a welcome surprise to see Galactic Racer set to receive such a feature. Here’s to hoping they are able to maintain a smooth 60fps on consoles.

ESL FACEIT Group (EFG) has announced on X that Intel Extreme Masters will return to Beijing in 2027 and 2028.
EFG and the Beijing Esports Industry Development Association signed a 3-year framework cooperation agreement. It brings IEM to Beijing every year from 2026 to 2028. EFG says the deal establishes the Chinese capital as Counter-Strike’s new home in Asia.
Today we're thrilled to announce that #IEM will be returning to Beijing for three consecutive years from 2026 to 2028! pic.twitter.com/KSOTrdiHKs
— ESL Counter-Strike (@ESLCS) November 17, 2026
The 2027 and 2028 dates are listed below:
Marc Winther, Director of Esports Counter-Strike 2 at EFG, commented on the news. He said Chinese fans “have always brought incredible passion to IEM.”
What the 3-Year Agreement Covers
The two sides signed the agreement at a ceremony during IEM Beijing 2026. The tournament took place from November 2 to 8 at the Bloomage Biotech·Biohyalux ECM Arena in Wukesong, Haidian District.
The Association will work with EFG to provide long-term support for the event. Relevant Beijing municipal authorities will also back the tournament.
EFG’s announcement described the return of IEM to Beijing for 3 straight years as a step in the city’s journey toward becoming an international esports hub.
IEM Beijing 2026 Recap
IEM Beijing 2026 was the first IEM Beijing since 2019. ESL held it instead of another Chengdu event, after Chengdu hosted IEM in 2024 and 2025.
The tournament featured 16 Counter-Strike 2 teams and a total prize pool of $1.25 million. It was an ESL Pro Tour Masters event and counted toward ESL Grand Slam VII.
The format used 2 double-elimination groups of 8 teams. The winner of each group went straight to the semifinals. Second and third place moved to the quarterfinals. All matches were best-of-3 except the best-of-5 final.
MOUZ won the title with a grand final victory over The MongolZ. The winner’s prize was $125,000, along with a $235,000 club reward.
IEM’s History in China
IEM Beijing 2019 was the first standalone IEM event in China. Astralis won that tournament, and 100 Thieves finished second. A second event, IEM Beijing-Haidian, ran online in 2020.
IEM Chengdu 2025 drew more than 35,000 fans to a sold-out venue, according to EFG. The company also reported a peak online audience of over 770,000 viewers.

Escape From Tarkov has been a decades long project, with the hardcore extraction shooter first being made available through an alpha back in 2016. After almost 10 years in ‘early access’ the PC exclusive finally hit 1.0 late last year. While a console version of the game is in the works, it will understandably take some time, with the team at Battlestate Games claiming that an official announcement is slated for some time next year.
Prior to the 1.0 release of Escape From Tarkov, Battlestate Games head Nikita Buyanov claimed that early work was going ahead on porting the hardcore shooter to consoles, with the team looking for a partner to helm the project.
Following up on this announcement from 2025, Buyanov took part in an interview with the publication Insider-Gaming, offering an update on the current state of the port.
According to Buyanov: “We are really close to [finding a development partner]” adding that “the console version, it won’t be ready next year, for sure. But for next year will be the announcement, 100%, I believe that. I guess the announcement will be early next year; I believe so.”
Given that Battlestate Games have acknowledged that a console port is in the works, it technically has already been announced. That said, what Buyanov is likely referring to here is a proper unveiling with details on who is in charge of the port alongside other ancillary details.
Being a PC-focused title, it will be interesting to see what concessions and alterations will need to be made in order to facilitate a satisfying and smooth experience on consoles. If nothing else, UI elements such as menus and player inventories will likely need to be retooled for controllers. Time will tell.

Asus has announced the ROG Harpe II Ace Mini, a compact wireless gaming mouse developed in collaboration with Valorant world champion Max “Demon1” Mazanov. Weighing just 47g, the new mouse is aimed at players who favour claw and fingertip grips, with Asus also releasing a special Demon1 Edition alongside the standard models.
The ROG Harpe II Ace Mini uses a bio-based nylon shell designed to balance low weight with durability, helping Asus keep the mouse down to just 47g. The mouse features a semi-symmetrical shape and will be available in black, white, blue and red colour options.
Inside, Asus has equipped the Harpe II Ace Mini with its ROG AimPoint Pro 65K optical sensor and ROG 100M optical microswitches, rated for up to 100 million clicks. Connectivity includes wired USB, Bluetooth 5.1 and 2.4G wireless modes, while second-generation ROG SpeedNova technology enables polling rates of up to 8000Hz in both wired and wireless operation.
Players can configure settings through Gear Link directly within a web browser without installing background software, and Asus also includes a dedicated carry case. Alongside the standard models, the ROG Harpe II Ace Mini Demon1 Edition features a light purple finish, Demon1 branding and matching accessories, including a custom receiver, carry case and sticker set.

GTA 6 New Zealand Release Time Revealed: Check Here
items.content:
GTA 6 New Zealand release time is 12:00 AM NZDT on Thursday, November 19, 2026. Rockstar Games confirmed a rolling midnight launch, so New Zealand gets Grand Theft Auto VI first on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. That moment equals 11:00 UTC on November 18, which is 4:30 PM IST in India. Players in other countries unlock the game at their own local midnight.
Below, you will find the New Zealand unlock time in major time zones, how the rolling launch works, and the GTA 6 preload details.
GTA 6 New Zealand Release Time and Date
The launch begins at 12:00 AM NZDT in New Zealand and moves across the globe as each country reaches midnight on November 19. The game releases on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.
The New Zealand PlayStation Store lists the unlock as November 18 at 11:00 AM UTC, which is midnight in Auckland on November 19. New Zealand Daylight Time is UTC+13.
For most of the world, the first unlock happens on November 18. Players elsewhere still wait for their own local midnight.
New Zealand Unlock Time in Other Time Zones
This table shows the New Zealand unlock converted to other time zones. It does not show when players in those regions can start playing.
Indian players reach their own midnight on November 19, later than New Zealand. The 4:30 PM IST time marks only the moment New Zealand unlocks.
How the GTA 6 Rolling Midnight Launch Works
GTA 6 does not unlock at one moment worldwide. Each country gets the game at 12:00 AM local time on November 19. Rockstar applies this rule to both PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.
Regional store listings show Mexico and Central America unlocking last, at 6:00 UTC on November 19. That is about 19 hours after New Zealand.
GTA 6 Preload Details
The GTA 6 preload is already live. On PS5, digital preload began at midnight local time on November 10, 2026. On Xbox Series X|S, it began globally at 12 AM GMT on November 10. Rockstar first announced November 12 as the preload date and later moved it to November 10.
The game is a download of over 200GB. Players who preloaded can launch the game once their region unlocks.
What About the New Zealand Trick?
Some guides describe a “New Zealand trick” that involves changing a console’s region and time to New Zealand to play early. Neither Rockstar nor PlayStation has announced that it works.

AnkiiiBot Defends Aadi Over Team SouL Targeting Controversy
items.content:
Nebula Esports, led by former IGL Aditya “Aadi” Dawar, targeted Team SouL in the last match of Battlegrounds Mobile India Showdown 2026 (BMSD 2026). Although he explained his reason behind his actions, the criticism did not seem to stop. BGMI caster Ankit “AnkiiiBOT” Pandey recently shared his two cents on the controversy.
AnkiiiBot Asserts Targeting Is a Part of The Game
In a recent livestream, in the context of Nebula Esports (former roster) targeting Team SouL, AnkiiiBot asserted that there’s nothing wrong with it and that it is a part of the game. “I don’t know, man. Why do people take this stuff so personally? Targeting and all is part of the game, period.”
Further clarifying his stance, AnkiiiBot added that Aadi doesn’t need to explain why he targeted someone. “It’s a game. You felt like doing it, you did it.”
He staunchly added that there is no official rule against targeting another team, and if someone has a problem, they can get a rule written down by Krafton itself saying that you can’t target. However, he was quick to clarify that he was not isolating this event, but he is talking about all the ‘targeting’ controversies that have emerged over the past few years. “I’m not saying this just about this particular matter. There have been plenty of instances like this, whether it was regarding Hector or some other team.”
AnkiiiBot Recalls RevenantXSpark and GodLike Esports Targeting Controversy in BMPS 2026 and BGIS 2026
AnkiiiBot recalled a similar instance that happened with RevenantXSpark and GodLike Esports in BGMI Pro Series 2026 (BMPS 2026) and Battlegrounds Mobile India Series (BGIS 2026). He asserted that it is a sensible thing to do against a strong team because naturally they would want to eliminate the strongest competition from the lobby. “Why wouldn’t they? You’re a strong team. They would want you out of the tournament. They wouldn’t want you to win a trophy.” He added, “So what’s the big deal? In the next tournament (BMPS 2026), you targeted them, you even won, and that was that. The tournament was settled.”
Sharing his personal opinion, AnkiiiBot said, “Everyone should just do whatever they want.”
Targeting another team has always been viewed as an unethical practice in BGMI esports. However, in a competitive tournament, eliminating your biggest opponent can be a sensible decision, especially when that team poses a major threat to your chances of winning. It can even be one of the most strategic moves a team makes during a match. As long as there is no official rule against it, targeting remains a part of the game, and teams are free to make such decisions based on their strategies.
