items.title: How the World’s Most Advanced AI Infrastructure Supply Chain Invents the Future
items.content:
Deb Shoquist leads operations at NVIDIA, overseeing the supply chain and manufacturing behind its AI platforms. That description sums up the job, but it doesn’t begin to encompass what Shoquist has made possible over decades.
Shoquist, her team and their global network of manufacturing partners enable NVIDIA to introduce world-leading technologies year-round.
Much of the team’s success comes down to her deep relationships with some of the world’s most accomplished manufacturers, including TSMC, Foxconn, Wistron, SPIL, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Unimicron, Lumentum, Coherent and Amkor. TSMC has partnered with NVIDIA since 1998. SPIL and KYEC were assembling and testing its chips more than two decades ago.
For Shoquist, those relationships grow stronger through each challenge solved together on the factory floor, as every generation of technology demands more from the people and tools behind it.
Ask her about the global network she relies on, and she starts with the people. There’s the supplier in Taiwan so eager to get production moving that he calls her at 3 a.m. with a fix to the latest problem. There are the factory workers in Vietnam whose only ask of her are more tools to get more work done. She remembers the partners that supported NVIDIA when it was small, and the work they’ve done to help each other grow.
Shoquist meets with key suppliers quarterly and spends six weeks each year on the road visiting partners in Taiwan, China, Korea, Vietnam and the U.S., where conversations move from meeting rooms to factory floors.
Recently, she paused her travels to accept the 2026 Dr. Lisa Su Woman of Innovation Award — and to share how she finds the right people and companies to imagine and produce at massive scale technology that has never been built before.
Foxconn
Q: How would you describe your job to someone outside NVIDIA?
A: At the most basic level, our job is to convert designs into the physical world. Our design team creates a blueprint, and our job is to transition it into a reliable, high-performance supply chain.
A matchmaker is probably the best analogy. You have to find the partner that matches your ramp style and has the technology that can meet the needs of very precise designs. The supplier has to be financially strong enough to invest in our ramps. They have to be highly technical. And they have to be willing to do something that has never been done before.
If you don’t have all three, you can’t create products at the volume and speed that we need. You need those three legs, and in some cases, if you only have two, you have to invest in the company to make them a partner.
Q: What’s an example of that in practice ?
A: Amphenol’s cable cartridge is the most complex interconnect assembly they have ever built. When I recently visited the Vietnam factory, now in full production, I was struck by the level of precision required to build a product of this complexity.
In this large cable cartridge, there are 1,500 small cable legs. Each one requires a very precise assembly to yield a quality level of less than 1 DPPM, or defect part per million. Amphenol built over a hundred automated lines to produce this product at the speed and scale we require. That takes know-how and technology, but it also takes heart, willingness and dedication.
Creating anything of that complexity and precision with a supplier forges the partnership. The partners NVIDIA maintains are the ones who supported us when we were small, and yet are willing to scale with us today.
Q: What changed as NVIDIA went from selling chips to building systems and platforms?
A: When we were primarily a chip manufacturer, we were small, and the semiconductor industry was at scale. In that environment, it was about picking the best technology match for the products we envisioned.
As we became a data center systems company, we needed more partners. But we’ve also now entered into new technology areas where the scale of the supply base is still developing.
For example, our optical component partners have the technology and the willingness, but they don’t yet have the scale or capital to build fabs for the volume we need. To grow, we needed to support and invest, like we did with Coherent and Lumentum.
Beyond that, with products like CPO (co-packaged optics), we’re creating entirely new supply chains with scale partners that are new to the optics world. Leading the integration of talent across the supply chain is the key to driving this incredible technology to high volume quickly.
Wistron
Q: You clearly enjoy spending time with supply partners, and in particular on the factory floor. What have you learned there over time that can’t be learned anywhere else?
A: Over 20 years, you meet many individuals key to the success of your supply. You meet not only the CEOs, but also the people that are running the production floor. These are the people that really know the problems of manufacturing.
If you don’t have a tight working relationship with the people deeper in the organization, then it’s hard to have an open dialogue about any challenges. But when you have tight relationships, they want to help you, and they feel comfortable enough telling you, “I need better technical support on the floor. I need more quality engineers. We need a better design. We need to automate this. We need more buffers of material.”
That’s what 20 years of working with our suppliers has taught us. It’s year after year of learning from people, getting to know people deeper in the organization and creating the trust where they can tell us what we need to do to be successful with them.
Q: Demand for NVIDIA technology is already massive and growing. Your job is to make sure NVIDIA’s volume can keep up. How do you make it happen?
A: It goes back to relationships. When you decide that you’re going to push a line hard to increase volume, you have to have the relationships. You have to know their processes in detail. You have to know their people in detail, and they have to trust you. Only then are you in a position to ask them for special favors, because you can do it surgically, and your ask is credible and reasonable.
And when you’re successful together, they’re happy, you’re happy, and the appreciation for the partnership deepens. We all appreciate those that make us successful.
Coherent
Q: How do you prioritize resources across the supply chain?
A: You need to first understand what the most critical components are, and protect and prioritize production around them. We need wafers like we need air. And the critical component is the TSMC chip. As it comes out of assembly every week, we decide what factory gets what chip.
Every week, we look at factory performance. If a particular factory yield is low, if their time of ownership is not at the level we want, they don’t get more chips that week.
We keep track of every chip, from the identification number on the die all the way to the customer invoice. If you want to be our supplier, you have to support that traceability process. With that process, we took the time it takes from chip out at TSMC to system out at Foxconn and Wistron from five to two weeks when supply and demand requires it.
Think of the supply chain as a large circulatory system with pathways everywhere — and when you need to accelerate any branch of it, you have the power to do that. We have the capability to do that. It’s empowering and exciting.
Amphenol
Q: What’s an example of a time things didn’t go as planned? How did you, the team and your partners find a way forward?
A: We were getting ready to go to volume production with Foxconn and Wistron for the compute board of NVIDIA GB200. The last step in the process was a test managed by an automated handler — a completely new approach for us, developed to meet the demands of high-volume throughput for these complicated products. During the initial ramp, the throughput was significantly below plan.
The operations director of Taiwan manufacturing made the call that to protect the product and shipments, he needed to disable the entire process and return to manual test loading. Our manufacturers backed him without question and brought in the necessary manpower to meet the immediate needs, literally hundreds of operators. That kept production moving, but would not solve the throughput requirement of full production.
As with any operations problem, the root cause had many elements to it: test tray assembly, test tray design, automation hardware design, automation control software, product yield. From all viewpoints, it was a difficult problem to resolve quickly.
That’s when we executed the NVIDIA swarm. Teams from NVIDIA design engineering, operations industrial, and product and test engineering, as well as from Foxconn automation engineering, flooded the line with talent to redesign and reactivate the line before the scale ramp hit.
This is not an unusual occurrence when there is a problem in operations. All teams at NVIDIA are street fighters — action-oriented, and know no organizational boundaries. We say that “the mission is the boss,” but we also live “the mission is the boss.”
Q: What makes this work so exciting for you?
A: Operations is a very empowering place to be at NVIDIA. Our team is designing and implementing changes to the supply chain constantly to meet the strong demand of our new products. The challenges are understandably high, but we’re always given the resources we need to be successful. The only thing between our goals and our success is our own creativity. That is exhilarating.

items.title: What Makes The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time So Great Anyway?
items.content: Spend even a little time online in gaming circles, and you'll inevitably come across claims that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is one of the greatest games ever made. Those claims resurfaced with greater frequency with the announcement of the Nintendo Switch 2 Ocarina of Time remake and subsequent warm reception from critics. The reaction from those I know who played for the first time and enjoyed it has generally been "yes, it really is one of the greats." What there's been less of, however, is a concerted effort to explain what exactly makes it deserving of that praise. Make no mistake, it does deserve it — and not just for reasons of nostalgia. That’s because Ocarina of Time anticipated some of gaming's biggest trends, and now that those trends have spiralled out of control, the remake serves as a blueprint for good game design moving forward.

Toshiba TV becomes Official Premium Partner of MLBB’s first MCT SEA in Bangkok
items.content:
MOONTON Games took the opportunity at the tournament's Group draw to reveal that Toshiba TV is now the Official Premium Partner of the first Mobile Legends: Bang Bang Southeast Asia Championship Tour (MCT SEA). It represents new territory for the telly maker, which has never before worked with the MLBB developer on such a large regional esports event. The in-person tournament runs in Bangkok, Thailand, from Dec. 9 to 13 with a $50,000 prize pool.
What Toshiba gets on screen
The activation runs under a campaign called "Set the Game On.” It will cover tournament broadcasts, retail stores, social media, and even online shopping. Toshiba branding will sit alongside Turtle Cam and Turtle Slain. In addition, Toshiba TV will have its own presence at the celebration for the Grand Final.
The TV maker, of course, has a product to push: its flagship RGB Mini LED ZXS. The R650 Mini LED, an e-commerce exclusive in Southeast Asia, will tie the campaign to local online retail.
Does the deal make sense? Toshiba TV's Regional Marketing Manager (ASEAN), Ken Lim, noted that MLBB is a mobile game but insisted that more fans are following it on larger screens. "We want Toshiba TV to become part of that shared viewing experience," he said. What’s more, MLBB's biggest moments, such as a Turtle fight deciding a series, will be replayed on living-room screens and watch-party projectors. According to Toshiba, that’s where its sets really belong.
So although Toshiba hasn’t worked on such a big regional esports before, it has worked with MLBB, sponsoring small community events like a Philippines watch party for the M5 World Championship.
Who's in the draw
MOONTON's Group Draw results confirm several matchups so far:
Group B and Group C: Thailand's Bacon Time and Tenacity, the MLBB Super League (MSL) Thailand Season 2 runner-up and third-place teams, will start in Groups B and C
Group D: Team Falcons Academy, the MLBB Development League (MDL) Philippines Season 8 champions, face BIGETRON ACADEMY, MDL Indonesia's unbeaten champions
Group D: SRG Academy, the MLBB Academy League (MAL) Malaysia champions, complete the group
Fans without a ticket to the arena can join MLBB Friend Fest, a free community hub at ICONSIAM that covers both the MCT SEA and the M8 World Championship Wild Card periods. As well as live match screenings, it offers watch parties, community tournaments, merchandise, sponsor activations, and food and beverage stalls.
Why the road to M8 raises the stakes
Though the $50,000 prize pool is modest, a place at the world championship is also at stake and, for most teams, is probably the bigger pull. The top two teams go directly to the M8 Main Stage in Istanbul, Türkiye, while third and fourth place drop into the M8 Wild Card, also in Bangkok.
Manurung Martinus Haposan, Head of Esports Business Development, Indonesia, at MOONTON Games, said the tour "creates a meaningful new platform for emerging teams to compete beyond their home markets." He called Toshiba's arrival "a strong validation of that opportunity."
The M8 link, meanwhile, gives the sponsorship more reach. Visa has a three-year deal as Global Payment Partner for the M8 through M10 World Championships, and Infinix is the official gaming phone partner for the domestic leagues that feed MCT SEA. Toshiba is the only commercial partner MOONTON has named specifically for the MCT SEA itself.
MCT SEA opens with the group stage at ICONSIAM in Bangkok on Dec. 9, and the Grand Final follows on Dec. 13.

items.title: From underdog to champion: Myyz wins TFT Enchanted Wilds Tactician’s Crown!
items.content:
The winner of the Teamfight Tactics (TFT) Set 18: Enchanted Wilds Tactician’s Crown is Myyz! Read on for Myyz’s journey to the top what he said about his well-earned victory.
Myyz winning the Enchanted Wilds Tactician’s Crown (Image credit: Riot Games)
Myyz wins TFT Enchanted Wilds Tactician’s Crown
Over the weekend, 40 TFT players duked it out in hopes of claiming the lion’s share of $470,000 USD and making esports history. After Day 1’s matches, only 32 players remained in the competition. They then fought until only eight players claimed spots in the Day 3 Grand Final.
Played under the checkmate format, the TFT Set 18 Tactician’s Crown Grand Final required players to reach 20 points before securing a first-place finish to take home the gold. The competition was intense, as by Game 7, almost every player entered checkmate. Then, a Game 8 came about for the first time ever in TFT Grand Finals history.
It was a Riftbeast showdown between Maris and Myyz, and the latter player came out on top!
Myyz versus Maris in Game 8 of the TFT Set 18 Tactician’s Crown Grand Finals (Image credit: Riot Games)
Myyz makes esports history at TFT Set 18 Tactician’s Crown
In that moment, Myyz went from a relatively unfamiliar name on the international stage to a Tactician’s Crown champion. Previously, he only participated in the TFT Open Championship 2026 Fall: Super Server event and its Regional Finals.
The player took home $150,000 USD and dedicated his victory to China’s (CN) competitive scene.
“I must take this [championship] for CN,” Myyz said in the post-match interview. He then thanked his biggest supporters. “I want to thank all of my fans, all of my teammates, and especially my mother. I could not have done this without your support. Thank you, everyone.”
TFT Enchanted Wilds Tactician’s Crown results (Image credit: Riot Games)
TFT Set 18 Tactician’s Crown results
Here are all of the results for the TFT Enchanted Wilds Tactician’s Crown Grand Finals. While Myyz earned 36 points in total, TLG diaomei scored 41 while Dishsoap and Chunington tied at 39 points each. CangShan, Maris, Baizhi, and oskuu followed with 38, 35, 31, and 29 points, respectively.
In terms of the most popular compositions, Brambleback Riftbeast was seen in 13 matches in total. This was followed by Malphite AP Flex, Primal Flex, Yunara/Karma Reroll, ad Ahri Zyra Flex.
The most popular compositions (Image credit: Riot Games / BarryBadden / Ziziziziie)
That’s all for now. Did you enjoy the TFT esports action? Stick around on esports.gg for more TFT news, interviews, and updates!

Xbox really doesn’t want you thinking of Project Helix as a gaming PC
items.content:
Xbox has shared fresh details on its next-generation console, Project Helix, but Microsoft is keen to make one thing clear. Despite repeated promises that the system will play PC games, the company does not want players thinking of Helix as a gaming PC.
In Microsoft's newly released digital Xbox magazine, Vice President of Next Generation Jason Ronald again confirmed that Project Helix will be able to play PC games. However, he was keen to draw a distinction between a console that can access PC games and a gaming PC that can play Xbox titles.
“We're very clear on the design goal,” Ronald said. “Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games.”
Ronald added that Project Helix is being designed to remove many of the barriers that have traditionally separated console and PC gaming. Players will be able to bring four generations of Xbox games and progression forward, while Microsoft also aims to remove the “arbitrary constraints” between console and PC titles.
The Xbox executive also reiterated the importance of preserving the console experience. While Helix will offer additional settings and performance options for enthusiasts, Microsoft still wants the experience to remain as straightforward as a traditional console.
“When I think about what makes a console magical, it's that it just makes my games instantly accessible and ready to play in an instant,” Ronald explained. “I don't have to worry about updating my operating system, updating drivers, configuring different settings – things like that. The hardware and the experience is entirely designed around playing games.”
Project Helix increasingly sounds like a hybrid between a traditional console and a gaming PC, offering access to both Xbox and PC libraries while introducing more extensive performance and graphics options. However, Xbox leadership clearly wants the console experience itself to remain at the centre of the platform's identity.
KitGuru says: Microsoft really doesn't want people thinking of Helix as an Xbox PC, even though that appears to be the core of the sales pitch. It wouldn't be the first time we've seen confusing messaging from the Xbox higher-ups though, and it likely won't be the last.

Halo: Campaign Evolved begins expanding beyond the campaign with Firefight
items.content:
Halo: Campaign Evolved launched earlier this year with a visual overhaul for the original Halo campaign, but many fans were disappointed by the lack of multiplayer content. That is finally set to change, with Halo Studios announcing plans to add Firefight later this Winter.
Firefight is Halo's long-running co-op survival mode, first introduced in Halo 3: ODST in 2009. The mode typically tasks up to four players with surviving increasingly difficult waves of enemies and has appeared in multiple Halo titles over the years, including Halo: Reach, Halo 5 and Halo Infinite.
The new Firefight mode for Halo: Campaign Evolved will support up to four players and will exist separately from the campaign itself. Halo Studios has not announced a release date just yet, but more details are set to be shared during Halo Fest, taking place between December 12th and December 13th.
The announcement is somewhat surprising given the uncertainty surrounding the franchise over the past year. Microsoft recently conducted another round of layoffs affecting Halo Studios, formerly known as 343 Industries. At the same time, stewardship of the Halo franchise has shifted to Activision, which is now set to oversee development of future Halo games.
The addition of Firefight also raises questions about whether other multiplayer content could eventually make its way into Halo: Campaign Evolved. The remaster launched without classic multiplayer modes outside of campaign co-op, leaving many players to return to Halo: The Master Chief Collection or Halo Infinite for their multiplayer fix. While Firefight isn't a full replacement for traditional Halo multiplayer, it does represent the first significant step towards bringing more of the complete Halo experience to Campaign Evolved.
KitGuru says: Firefight feels like an obvious addition for Halo: Campaign Evolved. The bigger question now is whether Halo Studios is willing to go further and bring back some form of classic Halo PvP as well.

items.title: NBA 2K27 Joins GTA+ From 27 November With a Vice City Bonus Pack
items.content:
Rockstar Games is adding NBA 2K27 Standard Edition to GTA+ from 27 November, letting members on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S play it at no extra cost. The game stays in the GTA+ library until 15 January 2027. During that period, members can also buy NBA 2K27 Standard Edition at 20% off on the platform linked to their membership. Rockstar has not said whether the discount applies to the Deluxe or Ultra editions.
From 17 December, members can also download an NBA 2K27 GTA+ Bonus Pack. The pack stays available until 31 March 2027. It contains MyCAREER clothing styled after Vice City, along with boosts for use in matches. Rockstar has not said whether players keep the items if their GTA+ membership lapses.
What the NBA 2K27 GTA+ Bonus Pack includes
The bonus pack is aimed at players of MyCAREER, the mode in which players create and develop their own basketball player. Rockstar listed four items in the pack:
Vice City styled blue Boat Hat (MyCAREER)
Vice City styled Oversized T Shirt (MyCAREER)
30 Skill Boosts, lasting five games
15 Gatorade Boosts, lasting five games
The offer runs on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S only. Rockstar has not said whether the pack will be available on PC or Nintendo Switch 2, where NBA 2K27 is also sold. It has also not said whether the 20% discount stacks with other store sales running at the same time.
GTA VI rewards in NBA MyCareer pic.twitter.com/gNPF8KuCIl
— GTA News RockstarINTEL.com (@GTAonlineNews) November 16, 2026
The three parts of the offer run on different dates, and the bonus pack stays available for more than two months after the free play period ends.
NBA 2K27 is sold in three editions. The Standard Edition costs $69.99, the Deluxe Edition $99.99 and the Ultra Edition $149.99. The 20% GTA+ discount applies to the Standard Edition, which would bring its US price to about $56. Prices in other regions have not been listed for the offer.
NBA 2K27 joins GTA+ during the GTA 6 launch period
The offer starts eight days after Grand Theft Auto VI launches on 19 November. GTA 6 players who bought the digital edition before 20 November receive one month of GTA+ at no extra cost. That free month would cover the start of the NBA 2K27 period for many new members. GTA+ costs $7.99 a month in the US, a price Rockstar set in 2024.
NBA 2K27 released on 4 September on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2 and PC, priced at $69.99 for the Standard Edition. 2K and Rockstar are both owned by Take-Two Interactive. GTA+ previously added NBA 2K26 in March 2026, the first game in the service that was not made by Rockstar. Its library otherwise contains Rockstar titles such as Red Dead Redemption and Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy.
Take-Two has not said whether more of its games will join GTA+ after NBA 2K27. Rockstar has also not said whether GTA 6 itself will receive GTA+ benefits, or how the service will work alongside the game after it unlocks in each region. The first GTA 6 patch, update 01.002.001, is already rolling out ahead of launch.

LoL 2027: Kleptomancy is back, new Titanborn tank Keystone
items.content:
The League of Legends dev team has confirmed the return of the Kleptomancy Keystone, along with the addition of a tank-focused one, Titanborn. Here’s everything we know about Keystones in LoL 2027.
LoL 2027 Keystones
These two Runes will be added in January “for the short-term health of League” and might be carried over onto New Dawn. New items, and an overhaul to the on-hit system will also be added alongside these.
Kleptomancy is back!
Gangplank mains, this one is for you! Kleptomancy is returning in 2027, but it won’t be exactly the same one you all knew and loved.
Kleptomancy is back! (Image credit: Riot Games)
The new Kleptomancy features a new unique loot reward which can give you a small discount to items in the store. Combined with Cashback, which lives in the same Inspiration Tree as Kleptomancy, you can earn an edge over your lane opponent simply from the discounts.
From the short preview in the dev update video, we can see that the Mana Potion and extra gold are still part of the possible loot you can get.
Head of League Studio Andrei “Meddler” van Roon described the new Kleptomancy as a “greedy Keystone” to out-econ your opponent.
New Titanborn Keystone
Titanborn is a new Tank-focused Keystone grants ramping armor and magic resist while in champion combat. At max stacks, you become Titanic, granting increased size and periodically causes your next attack to unleash a shockwave for extra damage and slow to enemies. We can expect this to be in the Resolve tree.
A Titanic Malphite. (Image credit: Riot Games)
This sounds kind of similar to Aftershock, but we don’t have to say goodbye to that Keystone. So this wouldn’t be the same case as Stormraider’s Surge replacing Phase Rush.
The difference lies in use case: Titanborn is meant for longer trades and fights, while Aftershock gives all value up-front for a short amount of time.
The Kleptomancy and Titanborn Keystones go live on January 2027.

The next new item is Gravescourge. This is a new Lethality item that summons Mistwraiths to chase down nearby enemies. Twin Shadows, anybody?
Gravescourge summons three Mistwraiths to slow enemies. (Image credit: Riot Games)
Finally, Fatetaker is a new on-hit item that grants attack speed, armor, and a three-hit passive. It will also get the slow that was previously part of Blade of the Ruined King (since that is being removed, see below) with no cooldown.
Fatetaker slows enemies and steals their soul on a three-hit passive. (Image credit: Riot Games)
Item changes in League of Legends 2027
The dev update told us that they will be overhauling the on-hit item system to “give on-hit users more options,” but we didn’t get any more details than that.
We do know how some items are being changed, though:
Wit’s End will be a “go-to movespeed item” against AP enemies.
Blade of the Ruined King‘s percent health damage will be buffed, but the slow will be removed (and placed onto Fatetaker, see above)
Terminus might shed its defensive stats for more offensive stats.
Riftmaker stats and unique passives will be modified.
Serpent’s Fang will be less about shield mitigation and be tweaked to deal more damage to shielded enemies.
These item changes go live on January 2027.

items.title: Petition to Reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO Passes 175,000 Signatures
items.content:
An online petition calling on Nvidia’s board to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive has passed 175,000 signatures. About 8,800 of the signatories say they work at Nvidia, a figure that has not been independently verified. The campaign, called “Stand With Jensen”, later showed more than 178,000 names on 16 November. Nvidia has not commented on the petition, and its site states that neither Nvidia nor Huang endorses it.
The petition takes the form of an open letter to Nvidia’s board. It asks the board to reinstate Huang while an independent investigation establishes the facts, to give him a fair hearing and to explain its decision publicly. Huang resigned on 12 November after admitting to an extramarital relationship, ending 33 years as chief executive. Chief financial officer Colette Kress became interim chief executive.
Huang’s resignation followed weeks of scrutiny over his personal relationships. He admitted to being unfaithful to his wife, Lori Huang, in a letter to staff on 8 November. Questions had already been raised about his meetings with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore data centre company Megaspeed. Two sources later said he had a relationship with a second Nvidia employee, a claim Nvidia declined to address. The board opened an independent investigation, which is still under way.
Elon Musk and tech executives among Stand With Jensen signatories
Tesla and SpaceX chief executive Elon Musk said on X on 13 November that he was signing the petition. Epic Games chief executive Tim Sweeney, Replit chief executive Amjad Masad, Uber cofounder Travis Kalanick and Shopify chief executive Tobias Lütke are also listed among the signatories. Musk had earlier said that hiring Huang “would be an honour”.
Not every name on the list is genuine. Some people listed as signatories said they never signed it. The organisers said on X that they were “actively working” to remove fake signatures. They have not said how they verify that a signatory works at Nvidia, and the 8,800 figure relies on what each person entered when signing.
The petition grew quickly over the weekend after Huang stepped down. It passed 100,000 signatures within days of going live. The campaign site counter showed 135,468 signatures on 15 November, before the total moved past 175,000 the following day. The organisers have not said who set up the campaign or whether they plan to deliver the letter to Nvidia’s board in person.
Nvidia board faces pressure over Jensen Huang’s return
Huang has discussed a possible return with close confidants, although he has not commented publicly. US President Donald Trump said he would not mind seeing Huang return. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent took the opposite view, saying Nvidia needs an outside chief executive. Nvidia has said its search for a permanent chief executive is in its early stages.
Nvidia shares recovered some of their early losses on 16 November after Trump’s remarks but remained more than 1% lower during trading. The company is due to report its third quarter results on 17 November. It will be Kress’s first earnings call as interim chief executive. The board has not said whether it will respond to the petition.

items.title: How Long Is GTA 6? New Estimate Puts the Main Story Below Rockstar’s 80 Hours
items.content:
A new estimate of how long Grand Theft Auto VI takes to finish emerged days before its 19 November launch, and it is shorter than the figure many players expected. The estimate covers the main story, the number of missions and the time needed to unlock every trophy. A person with knowledge of the game gave the figures. Rockstar Games has not confirmed them, and it has not published an official completion time.
Until now, the only number in circulation came from Rockstar itself. Studio head Rob Nelson said his own playthrough took about 80 hours. That figure spread online as the length of the main story. Nelson said, however, that his run also covered “optional goals with narrative ramifications”, side tasks whose outcomes affect the story.
How long the GTA 6 main story takes
The main story of GTA 6 takes about 50 hours to complete. The campaign is said to contain nearly 100 missions spread across five chapters. The estimate covers the main missions featuring Jason and Lucia, the game’s two lead characters. It does not include side activities, optional missions or time spent exploring the state of Leonida.
Unlocking every trophy or achievement is expected to take 200 hours or more. Playtime will also vary with how quickly each player moves through missions. Rockstar has not said how many missions the game contains or how the story is divided. The full list of GTA 6 trophies appeared before launch, giving players an early view of what a full completion requires.
Why the 50 hour and 80 hour figures differ
The two figures are not in conflict. A player who follows only the main missions would finish in less time than Nelson, while one who also completes the optional story goals would take closer to his 80 hours. A full completion run, covering every activity and collectible, would take longer than both. Rockstar has not said how much optional content the game holds.
How GTA 6 compares with GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2
A 50 hour campaign would make GTA 6 the longest main story in the series. Player data on the HowLongToBeat website puts the main story of GTA 5 at about 32 hours. Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar’s last major release in 2018, takes about 50 hours for its main story on the same site. GTA 6 would therefore sit close to Red Dead Redemption 2 rather than GTA 5.
The main story figure counts only the missions needed to reach the credits. A second figure adds side missions and extras, while a third covers full completion of every activity. GTA 6 times will be added once players begin submitting them after launch, and Rockstar has spent more than a decade on the game after it refused to make a smaller follow up to GTA 5.
Players will be able to test the estimates from 19 November, when GTA 6 launches on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. The game unlocks at different times in each region. Rockstar has not said whether it will release completion statistics after launch.

items.title: Lambda Boosts AI Factory Resiliency and Efficiency With NVIDIA Photonics
items.content:
To train an AI model, thousands of GPUs have to work together, requiring a network that’s fast, efficient and resilient.
Lambda is tackling the network piece of the puzzle with NVIDIA Photonics co-packaged optics (CPO) switches. The cloud provider is using the switches to connect NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks with more than 10,000 GPUs, delivering lower power, higher resiliency and longer mean time between interruptions (MTBI) to an AI factory at scale.
“Networking has to keep pace with the demands of increasingly large AI clusters,” said Dave Ward, president of cloud services at Lambda. “Bringing co-packaged optics into a deployment of this scale is an important step toward building the infrastructure needed to support the next generation of AI.”
Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26
In the company’s tests using the switches, network latency — the time needed for moving data — dropped by about 4% at rack scale and by up to about 10% at pod scale. Across rack, scalable unit and pod configurations, the network maintains the same throughput as conventional pluggable optics.
Delivering Power Efficiency and Resiliency at Scale
Improving power efficiency and resiliency matters because the network sits at the center of AI factory productivity.
In a large training job, one interrupted link can stall thousands of GPUs. With agentic inference, one network disruption can introduce cascading latency effects on many agents. Every interruption costs time, and every watt spent on networking is a watt not available for compute.
NVIDIA Photonics addresses both power efficiency and resiliency. By replacing pluggable transceivers with co-packaged optical engines on the switch package, it delivers up to 5x better power efficiency and up to 15x higher reliability than conventional pluggable optics. It also uses 4x fewer lasers, which means fewer components that can fail.
Cooler Optics, Replaceable Light Sources Increase Resiliency
Lambda’s deployment uses NVIDIA Photonics switches, each with 144 ports running at 800Gb/s. Liquid cooling carries heat away from the switch chip and optical engines.
The company reports a median optics temperature of 36°C, compared with 51°C for conventional pluggable optics, and its tests find more stable signal integrity.
NVIDIA Photonics also brings the electrical-to-optical conversion closer to the switch chip. Each switch has 18 removable external light sources, which supply light to the optical engines. Optical engines sit alongside the chip on the same package and convert electrical signals into light that carries data over fiber between parts of the cluster.
Technicians can replace the light-source modules in the field, unlike traditional pluggable optics, which require replacing the entire module if a laser fails.
Co-packaging shortens the electrical path from inches to millimeters, which reduces signal loss. It also removes the need for retimer chips, cutting both power draw and the number of parts in the signal path.

items.title: NVIDIA Expands Slurm to Bring Quantum Computing Into Supercomputing
items.content:
Quantum processor deployments at supercomputing centers have grown nearly sevenfold over the past five years, with nearly 30 supercomputing centers around the world now in the process of deploying over 50 quantum processors.
Many of these centers use Slurm to run scientific supercomputing workloads, so expanding its support for quantum processors builds on familiar workflows and tools, enabling computational chemists, nuclear physicists and materials scientists to bring quantum computing into their research domains without friction.
In a new release, Slurm builds on previous work with IBM, Pasqal and the wider quantum computing community to allow QPU builders to create a single interface to their hardware for every supercomputing center, through a simple file. This makes it easier than ever for HPC centers and QPU builders to integrate and serve their hardware.
The expansion is already being adopted by Alice & Bob, IBM, IQM, Pasqal, Quantinuum and MQSC and supports the widely used QRMI and QDMI interfaces.
Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26
Beating the Bottleneck
Until now, integrating a QPU into a supercomputing center meant a new software challenge for every new QPU or supercomputing center. By building on existing quantum-HPC interfaces such as QRMI and QDMI, the Slurm expansion allows QPU builders to reuse their integrations across all their deployments. It also means that supercomputing centers can add new quantum processors to their existing scheduling and resource-management workflows without developing bespoke QPU-specific solutions.
For quantum computing to advance science, it needs to be used by scientists. Now scientists can run quantum-classical applications developed with platforms such as NVIDIA CUDA-Q with Slurm coordinating access to all the processing they need.
Slurm 26.11 will be available later this month.
Orchestrating Resources in an Open Quantum-GPU Platform
The Slurm expansion adds a community-developed orchestration layer to NVIDIA’s open platform for quantum-GPU supercomputing, which centers around the CUDA-Q open platform for hybrid quantum-classical computing. At SC26, new releases expand all aspects of the platform:
CUDA-Q QEC allows researchers developing quantum error correction to rapidly prototype and test new ideas, including with a new decoder server. A new TCBP-JOBS decoder is 13,000x faster than the industry standard.
CUDA-Q gets an expanded layer of fault-tolerant primitives that application builders can use to realistically compile their ideas. Fermilab has already used CUDA-Q to perform studies in three weeks that would normally have taken five months.
CUDA-Q Algorithms provides reusable components for builders of quantum applications, including new capabilities in helping design the loading data into quantum circuits and tools specifically for chemistry and materials applications
CUDA-Q Pulse gives quantum hardware builders a layer for shaping the ‘pulses’ needed to control qubits on a QPU, including tools to GPU accelerate their generation.
The quantum ecosystem around the world is continuing to build with this platform. Quantum Motion integrated its QUICHE chemistry framework with CUDA-Q. Altera and Oxford Quantum Circuits designed an FPGA-based controller connecting qubit control and readout to GPUs through NVQLink.
At supercomputing scale, QunaSys used cuQuantum and 1,024 NVIDIA Hopper GPUs on ABCI-Q to simulate more than 300 million quantum operations, reaching chemical accuracy for a four-hydrogen-atom model. NVIDIA researchers used JUPITER to simulate 104 qubits under realistic noise, testing fault-tolerant designs before they’re built.

NVIDIA Sweeps MLPerf Training and Endpoints as Vera Rubin Debuts With Leading Performance
items.content:
In its MLPerf benchmarks debut, with results released today, the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform delivers leading performance across training, post-training and agentic inference.
NVIDIA swept every MLPerf Training v6.1 benchmark and, in its first MLPerf Endpoints submission, delivered more than 10x generational gains in throughput per watt for agentic AI — measuring how much agentic work a system delivers with each watt of power.
These results are just the beginning. Vera Rubin performance will keep climbing through continuous optimization of NVIDIA’s CUDA-powered software stack, so the infrastructure that customers invest in today delivers more value over time.
NVIDIA Sweeps MLPerf Training v6.1
AI agents are now everywhere, writing code, running business workflows, answering customer questions and, as this week’s SC26 conference highlights, advancing scientific research.
Faster training means smarter agents can reach users sooner, drug discovery models can keep pace with new lab data and fraud-detection models can adapt to new threats faster.
MLPerf Training measures how fast a system can train a range of AI models to a target level of accuracy.
The NVIDIA platform was the only one with results on every benchmark this round, spanning large language models, image generation, recommender systems and reinforcement learning post-training. In its debut, Vera Rubin NVL72 delivered up to 2x more performance per GPU than the highly optimized NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 system — early results that show the pace of generation-over-generation innovation.
MLPerfTraining v6.1 results retrieved from www.mlcommons.org on Nov 16, 2026, from the following entries: 6.1-0116 , 6.1-0030, 6.1-0135, 6.1-0020, 6.1-0049, 6.1-0123, 6.1-0138, 6.1-0073, 6.1-0124, 6.1-0129 and 6.1-0038. The MLPerf name and logo are trademarks of MLCommons Association in the United States and other countries. All rights reserved. Unauthorized use is strictly prohibited. See www.mlcommons.org for more information.
NVIDIA also demonstrated performance at scale. On the DeepSeek-V3 benchmark, Vera Rubin NVL72 scaled from 256 to 1,024 GPUs with about 97% efficiency: quadrupling the GPUs cut time to train from 16 minutes to about four.
NVIDIA also ran the benchmark on 10,240 GPUs with GB300 systems, representing the largest scale in this round. Microsoft Azure matched that scale with 10,240 NVIDIA GPUs with GB200 systems.
Results at this scale matter because adding GPUs only speeds up training if they can work together efficiently. NVIDIA NVLink scale-up networking connects the GPUs within each system so they act as one, while NVIDIA Quantum-X800 InfiniBand and Spectrum-X Ethernet scale-out networking link those systems across the data center. Combined with optimized software, this keeps thousands of GPUs working in concert, helping developers build more intelligent models while cutting training times.
NVIDIA Vera Rubin Leads Agentic Inference on MLPerf Endpoints
An AI agent for travel that plans and books a whole trip — or an IT agent that finds and fixes a problem before anyone files a ticket — may reason, call tools and check its work many times to finish a single task.
Each of those steps generates tokens. Because AI data centers are limited by power, the more tokens a system can generate each second for every watt of power, the more agents it can serve and the more value it creates.
MLPerf Endpoints tests systems on real agentic coding and enterprise workflows, and checks that the agents still complete their tasks correctly. NVIDIA Vera Rubin leads across all of its agentic benchmarks.
For example, in a provisional result for Kimi K3, a large open model built for agentic workflows, Vera Rubin NVL72 systems deliver more than 10x the throughput per watt of NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 at the same response speed.
MLPerf® Endpoints v1.0, Kimi K3, Standardized division, Available category, published November 9, 2026. NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, 32 accelerators, result 1.0.1.kimi-k3.agentic_combined.1p, run 9: concurrency = 1,024 queries, TTFT P90 = 4,673.9 ms, system TPS= 41,414.2 tokens/sec, E2E average interactivity = 50.4 tokens/sec per user, operating power = 100.89 kW. NVIDIA GB300 NVL72, 48 accelerators, result1.0.0.kimi-k3.agentic_combined.1, run 6: concurrency = 48 queries, TTFT P90 = 2,305.1 ms, system TPS= 2,210.4 tokens/sec, E2E average interactivity = 56.2 tokens/sec per user, operating power = 60 kW. GB300 results verified by MLCommons Association. For the provisional Vera Rubin results: pending MLCommons Association verification, results are subject to change pending peer review. The MLPerf name and logo are registered and unregistered trademarks of MLCommons Association in the United States and other countries. All rights reserved. Unauthorized use is strictly prohibited. See www.mlcommons.org for more information.
Every AI service has to balance serving many users at once against responding quickly to each one. Vera Rubin shifts that entire curve, serving more users while responding faster.
Leadership Across Benchmarks and Workloads
NVIDIA partners participated extensively in MLPerf Training, with submissions from 20 organizations: ASUS, Azure, Cisco, CoreWeave, Crusoe, Dell Technologies, Firmus, Giga Computing, Google Cloud, HPE, Inventec, Krai, Lambda, Nebius, Oracle, Quanta Cloud Technology (QCT), Supermicro, TTA and the University of Florida.
Their submissions show how NVIDIA’s programmable platform, with open source libraries and frameworks, lets a vast ecosystem of partners innovate and optimize AI training performance.
The lead extends beyond MLPerf.
Vera Rubin also delivers leading performance on independent benchmarks including SemiAnalysis AgentX and Artificial Analysis AgentPerf, showcasing how the same NVIDIA infrastructure can productively run everything from pretraining and post-training to agentic inference, as well as workloads beyond AI, such as the high-performance computing showcased at SC26 this week.

items.title: NVIDIA CUDA-X Libraries Give Agents the Tools to Accelerate Scientific Discovery
items.content:
With expanded NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries, including cuPhoton, cuPotential and cuSpa, researchers can sift through vast amounts of data to accelerate research, from astrophysics and materials science to single-cell biology.
The speedups are helping scientists analyze larger datasets and model more complex systems.
The new libraries give AI agents the tools to help researchers make discoveries faster than ever.
Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26
Bringing Black Holes Into Focus
Seeing a black hole takes a telescope the size of Earth. The Event Horizon Telescope links radio dishes worldwide, generating petabytes of data that can take months to process.
With NVIDIA cuPhoton.xBeam, a module within the cuPhoton Toolkit, black hole observations from the Event Horizon Telescope can now be correlated orders of magnitude faster than ever. Analysis that once took over a month now takes eight minutes.
By combining global radio dishes into Earth-sized aperture, cuPhoton delivers unprecedented astronomical imaging resolution. cuPhoton successfully correlated observations of powerful black hole jets J1924 and 3C279 in the night sky — making it a reality to reconstruct a Messier 87* black hole galaxy in real time.
The entire pipeline, from data loading and processing to visualization, runs on distributed multi-GPU systems or a compact NVIDIA DGX Spark system, helping scientists study how gas spirals inward under a black hole’s powerful gravitational pull.
Steering Fusion Simulations
Sustaining plasma at millions of degrees is essential to achieving stable, continuous fusion energy. But simulating its behavior is costly: on petascale systems, a single time step can take days, with simulations running for weeks. Experiments also generate data faster than traditional pipelines can process it, often leaving scientists waiting until experiments end to analyze results.
Pacific Fusion researchers used NVIDIA cuPhoton.xLens module to extract insights while plasma simulations run, helping them visualize what’s happening as results emerge.
The NVIDIA cuPhoton.xLens module extracts insights while plasma simulations run, helping researchers understand what’s happening as results emerge. Researchers can couple the entire pipeline with an NVIDIA Nemotron-powered agent running locally on the same system, enabling interactive analysis that can help steer simulations in real time to inform fusion reactor target and chamber design.
Exploring Potential Medicines
Molecular simulations help scientists evaluate drug designs before costly laboratory experiments. NVIDIA cuPotential, built on work by researchers at Simons Foundation’s Flatiron Institute and D. E. Shaw Research, accelerates existing simulation software by up to 3x while improving calculation stability and accuracy. It expedites synthetic data creation for generative AI models, finding previously unknown molecular binding sites and calculating the strength of molecular interactions.
NVIDIA is working with Schrödinger and the AMBER, NAMD, GROMACS, LAMMPS and Open Molecular Software Foundation communities to bring cuPotential acceleration to molecular dynamics engines and workflows.
Cadence, Fathom Therapeutics, Topos Bio, Genesis Molecular AI and Terray Therapeutics are adopting it for drug discovery.
Accelerating Materials Research
Daviator, a collection of batched GPU kernels for the widely used Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package, is coming to NVIDIA ALCHEMI — delivering quantum-mechanical calculations up to 22x faster and at up to 75% lower cost. With Daviator, researchers building simulation models can now use GPU acceleration across atomistic systems of all sizes to generate the millions of calculations of atomic interactions needed for model training and inference, including for small systems that previously ran faster on CPUs.
At Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, the NVIDIA DAQIRI networking library connects a high-speed electron microscopy detector to GPU processing, moving analysis into the experiment itself. Researchers can identify useful signals, discover previously unknown regions of interest and decide what to measure next while measurements are being taken.
The workflow supports atomic-resolution materials studies that can distinguish elements, laying the groundwork for future automated experiments.
Revealing Biology at Scale
The newly open source cuSpa accelerates cell polygon calculations, enabling developers to generate massive spatial graphs for next-generation patient and cancer models at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, with a 900x speedup compared with using CPUs.
Codeveloped with scverse, the rapids-singlecell framework accelerates single-cell analysis — and is now available in a single, agent-ready container. Using the tool, Therna Biosciences processed data 200x faster for therapeutic design. 10x Genomics integrated rapids-singlecell in its new Sentira platform, helping academic researchers, biopharma teams and foundation model builders accelerate the path from large-scale spatial data to biological insights.
And the NVIDIA GPU-accelerated HMMER library, also open source, accelerates the annotation of predicted protein sequences, supporting data preparation for biological foundation models. At Basecamp Research, benchmark searches ran up to 84x faster than with standard HMMER, reducing the time required to annotate the large biological datasets used to train the company’s therapeutic design models.

items.title: CUDA at 20: How the Platform Transformed Scientific Computing
items.content:
This week at SC26, NVIDIA is marking two decades of CUDA by honoring the researchers, developers and engineers who helped make GPU computing a foundation for modern science and AI.
CUDA’s 20th anniversary presents an occasion to reflect across computing eras, from the people who wrote the very first CUDA programs to the AI developers building on their work today.
At the platform’s core is this developer community whose experiments, tools and persistence expanded what accelerated computing could do.
From SC06 to SC26
NVIDIA announced CUDA in November 2006 and brought it to the scientific community at SC06, giving scientists and developers a familiar, high-level programming model for using GPUs. It fundamentally extended accelerated computing beyond graphics use cases to accelerate demanding applications for science, simulation and more.
In the two decades since, developers have used CUDA to advance Nobel Prize-winning AI research, accelerate scientific applications on supercomputers and support visual effects in Oscar-winning films.
Today, more than 11 million developers build on CUDA across the computing stack.
Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26
Honoring the Architects of Progress
Now, at SC26, NVIDIA is looking back at some of the CUDA luminaries who’ve spearheaded breakthroughs in science and AI:
At the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, biophysicist Klaus Schulten’s team helped connect GPU computing with molecular biology through Nanoscale Molecular Dynamics and Visual Molecular Dynamics, tools for molecular simulation and visualization. In 2013, researchers at Illinois, the University of Pittsburgh and Vanderbilt University used CUDA-accelerated tools to help resolve the HIV capsid’s atomic structure. They combined experiments with simulations on Blue Waters, one of the world’s most powerful supercomputers at the time.
In a critical breakthrough in AI, University of Toronto researchers Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever and Geoffrey Hinton used CUDA to train AlexNet on just two NVIDIA GPUs. Their image-recognition system won the 2012 ImageNet competition, helping demonstrate the potential of GPU computing for deep learning.
That connection between computing and scientific discovery is seen with AlphaFold, which predicts protein structures. Demis Hassabis and John Jumper shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for protein structure prediction. Their team’s publicly released AlphaFold 2 software uses CUDA for GPU execution.
These are just a few of many examples that show how one generation’s work creates opportunities for the next. With 1,000+ NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries, developers are now reshaping industries and giving machines the power to see, learn and reason — from discovering new medicines and designing next-generation factories to advancing autonomous vehicles, modeling financial markets and unlocking quantum computing — and more.
Start building with the CUDA Toolkit and visit the 20-Year CUDA Celebration Event Wall at NVIDIA’s booth at SC26.

items.title: NVIDIA Announces Rubin HPC — A New GPU to Accelerate Agents for Science, Engineering and Analytics
items.content:
Announced today at SC26, NVIDIA Rubin HPC is a new GPU in the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform designed to accelerate simulation and data processing for science, engineering and analytics workflows.
As agents help scientists and engineers explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs, they rely on simulations to test those ideas and guide their next steps. Rubin HPC will accelerate those simulations, shortening the path from exploration to scientific discovery and industrial design.
The Rubin HPC GPU features a record number of CUDA cores — more than 50,000 on a single GPU — as well as a sparse data acceleration capability that keeps those cores fed with data, and accelerates GPU-to-GPU connectivity with seventh-generation NVIDIA NVLink interconnect technology.
Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26
Scientists and engineers rely on simulation to understand complex systems before committing to experiments or physical prototypes. Working with agents, these teams can explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs. This increases demand for the GPU-accelerated simulations needed to evaluate those ideas and guide next steps.
“For agents tackling science and engineering, faster simulation means faster discovery,” said Ian Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. “Rubin HPC accelerates the simulations agents use to test ideas and guide their next steps, helping scientists and engineers explore more possibilities and bring breakthroughs closer.”
Turning Faster Computation Into Faster Discovery
Across climate models, engineering simulations, genomic analysis and financial risk, scientific computing workloads take a similar shape: an application reaches into an immense dataset, gathers a handful of scattered values, calculates a result and repeats this on an enormous scale.
To help address the challenge, Rubin HPC will offer a balanced design, scaling data movement and compute together rather than increasing compute alone.
That balance is what optimizes Rubin HPC for scientific computing. It keeps the GPU’s record number of CUDA cores supplied with data, so they spend their time computing rather than waiting. This accelerates recurring patterns of every simulation workload — from sparse matrix operations to stencil computations to sorting and reductions.
These patterns are prevalent across data analytics, science and engineering workloads, which is why a purpose-built GPU delivering the broadest acceleration can help unlock cross-industry breakthroughs.
NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries offer a growing set of optimized implementations of complex algorithms for agents to use, including those most relevant to simulation and analytics. Used together with Rubin HPC, the libraries can give agents the fastest glide path to reasoning outcomes.
And faster agent-invoked simulations mean faster feedback — shortening the loop of hypothesis, simulation and refinement, so researchers and engineers can choose next steps sooner and point lab work at the most promising candidates.
Rubin HPC is expected to be available in 2028.

items.title: GTA 6 Boxed Copy Codes Can Be Read Through Sealed Cases, Buyers Say
items.content:
Buyers say the download code inside some boxed copies of Grand Theft Auto VI can be read without opening the box. A video posted on X on 13 November showed a person shining a bright torch through the side of a sealed case at an angle. The full redeem code became visible through the cover. Rockstar Games has not commented on the claims, and it has not said how many copies could be affected.
The boxed edition of GTA 6 contains no disc, only a code for the PlayStation Store or the Microsoft Store. In the affected copies, the code is printed directly on the inside of the cover. Rockstar did not use a separate paper insert or a scratch panel to hide it. Anyone who reads the code from a sealed box on a shop shelf could redeem it before the buyer does.
Which GTA 6 boxes appear to be affected
Buyers on the ResetEra forum said the issue appears limited to copies sold in regions that use the PEGI age rating system. Copies sold in the US carry a printed backing behind the code that hides it from the outside. Some testers were unable to repeat the trick with their own boxes. That suggests the problem may depend on the region or the print run, although this has not been confirmed.
There have been no confirmed cases of codes being stolen this way. The claims came a few days after other buyers said their boxes arrived with no code at all, or with a code that had already been redeemed. Neither Rockstar nor Take-Two Interactive has said whether the two issues are linked. Sony’s GTA VI code support page tells buyers with a damaged or missing code to “contact the retailer for help”.
Why the GTA 6 boxed edition has no disc
Rockstar chose to ship the boxed edition of GTA 6 with a code instead of a game disc. The company has not explained the decision in detail. Earlier leaks of footage and trailers had raised concerns that boxed copies sold early by retailers could spread story details before launch. A code also means the box itself holds no part of the game, so a buyer cannot install anything until the code is redeemed online.
My box came with blank code
by
u/asindragon in
GTA6unmoderated
The format has drawn complaints from collectors and from players with slow internet connections. The game requires a large download before it can be played, and the box offers no way to install it offline. Buyers in Japan have also found that codes in boxed copies there carry a 170 day expiry date. Rockstar has not said whether the same limit applies in other regions.
A fan account on X claimed that one Best Buy customer who found no code in his box was refused a replacement copy. That claim has not been confirmed, and Best Buy has not commented. Buyers who open a box and find a code that has already been used have no disc to fall back on. Rockstar has not said how it will handle refunds or replacements for any affected copies.
GTA 6 codes and launch timing
Boxed copies reached shops on 12 November so that buyers could redeem their codes and start the preload before release. Owners of digital and boxed copies can download the game early, but nobody can start playing it before launch. GTA 6 releases on 19 November on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, with unlock times that vary by region. Rockstar has not said whether it will change the packaging for later print runs.

GTA 6 Update 01.002.001 Size, Rollout Time, and More
items.content:
The GTA 6 update 01.002.001 is now rolling out on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, three days before the game’s November 19 launch. Rockstar Games released the patch on November 16. It is the second update since pre-loading began on November 10. The file is 602.5 MB on PS5 and about 1.6 GB on Xbox. Rockstar has not shared patch notes yet.
This article covers the update size, the PS5 rollout schedule, how to check for the patch, and what is still unknown.
GTA 6 Update 01.002.001 Size and Release Date
The new GTA 6 update takes the game to version 01.002.001. Rockstar pushed it live on November 16 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.
The PS5 version is 602.5 MB. The Xbox version is about 1.6 GB, according to dataminers. That makes the Xbox download roughly 1 GB larger than the PS5 one.
The update is not reaching every PS5 player at once. Sony is releasing it in waves, so some players can download it now while others must wait.
GTA 6 PS5 Update Rollout Schedule
Dataminers shared a rollout schedule for the GTA 6 PS5 update. It has three waves, each 12 hours apart. All PS5 players should have access by 2 AM PT on November 17.
GTA 6 – Update 01.002.001
33% of Users : Now Available.
66% of Users : in 12h
All Users : in 24h
Update Size : 602 MB pic.twitter.com/ZznlUAm8DP
— PlayStation Game Size (@PlaystationSize) November 16, 2026
In simple terms, a third of players get the patch first. Two-thirds can download it 12 hours later. Everyone gets it within 24 hours of the first wave. The IST column is a time conversion of the UTC schedule.
How to Check for the GTA 6 Update on PS5
If you have already pre-loaded GTA 6, you can check for the patch by hand. Follow these steps:
Highlight GTA 6 on the PS5 home screen.
Press the Options button on your controller.
Select Check for Update.
If your console says the game is up to date but shows version 01.002.000, check again after the next wave.
The second patch is also live on Xbox Series X|S. Dataminers put the Xbox GTA 6 update at around 1.6 GB.
It is unclear why the Xbox file is larger. Neither Rockstar nor the platform holders have explained the gap. It is also unknown whether both consoles get the same changes or whether the difference comes from how each platform handles game files.
Are There Any Patch Notes?
No. Rockstar has not released GTA 6 patch notes for update 01.002.001. The version number and file size are known, but the company has not said what changed since the previous patch.
What Happened With the First GTA 6 Patch
Rockstar released the first pre-launch patch, version 01.002.000, on November 13. It was about 1 GB on PS5. Rockstar did not publish patch notes for that update either.
Rockstar has not said whether another patch will arrive on launch day. It has also not said whether the two existing patches are enough for players to start the game right away.
GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Players who finished the GTA 6 pre-load should check for pending downloads before then. Installing the latest update early may help avoid an extra download when the game becomes playable.

items.title: The CS2 Mayonnaise Team: How Hellmann’s Became FURIA’s Most Famous Sponsor
items.content:
FURIA’s 3-0 win over Spirit in the BLAST Rivals Season 2 final on 15 November came with a nickname attached. “mayonnaise team just 3-0’d spirit lmao,” the Counter-Strike meme account cs2lmfao wrote on X after the final, a nod to the Hellmann’s name printed across the front of the Brazilian side’s jerseys. The joke works because of everything around it. In a CS2 scene where crypto casinos and bookmakers own teams outright and fill shirt sleeves, one of the strongest sides in the world is now known for a mayonnaise sponsor.
mayonnaise team just 3-0’d spirit lmao https://t.co/4WSOR8Udus
— (◣ _ ◢) (@cs2lmfao) November 15, 2026
cs2lmfao’s post on X after FURIA’s BLAST Rivals final, 15 November 2026
The partnership is a lot older than the meme, though. Hellmann’s, the Unilever mayonnaise brand that started in a New York deli in 1913, signed with FURIA in August 2024 and put its logo on the club’s uniforms. The two sides renewed the partnership in March 2026 with a fan promotion built around IEM Rio. FURIA’s run to the BLAST Rivals Season 2 title simply put the logo in front of more people than ever.
How Hellmann’s ended up on FURIA’s jerseys
Hellmann’s first worked with FURIA at Casa FURIA, the club’s fan event, in 2022, before signing a full partnership in August 2024. That deal covered the logo on FURIA’s uniforms, joint content and activations around events such as IEM Cologne, CBLOL and the Esports World Cup, according to MKT Esportivo. André Akkari, FURIA’s co-founder and co-CEO, said at the time that the partnership “not only validates our organisation as the leader in Latin America in the sector”.
For Hellmann’s, the reason was the size and age of FURIA’s audience. Unilever told Máquina do Esporte in September 2024 that Hellmann’s wanted to rejuvenate and widen its consumer base. The same plan took in NBA-themed sauce squeezes in Brazil and deals as the official sauce brand at the Allianz Parque and Mineirão football stadiums. “We made a very conscious choice with the NBA and FURIA, which have very large and loyal fan bases,” said Carolina Riotto, then Unilever’s food marketing director.
FURIA still carries betting money, and Brazil’s ban is closing in
The mayonnaise jokes leave out part of the picture. FURIA signed a two-year deal with the bookmaker BetBoom on 2 October 2025, which put the BetBoom logo on its CS2 jersey and made FalleN a brand ambassador. The club has also partnered with PokerStars in the past, and Akkari is himself a professional poker player. Hellmann’s sits on the same shirt as betting money, rather than in place of it.
That mix of sponsors matters more in Brazil now than it did a year ago. President Lula signed Provisional Measure 1,394 on 25 September, outlawing fixed-odds betting and betting sponsorship aimed at Brazilians. As our report on how Brazil’s betting ban hits CS2 showed, Keyd Stars paused its team, and FURIA had not commented on its BetBoom contract. Congress extended the measure on 9 November and now has until 4 March 2027 to vote on it, according to the Congress record.
The PGL Major Singapore adds a second test. PGL has confirmed that BC.Game, 1win, BetBoom and PARIVISION will play the Major as GOSH, THE ONE, BB Team and PVISION, because the companies behind them are not licensed under Singapore’s Gambling Control Act 2022. Reports before that confirmation said gambling logos and stickers would also be barred at the event. Our breakdown of the PGL Major Singapore name changes covers the four teams affected.
From Hungry Games to IEM Rio, why the mayo team label sticks
A sauce brand faces none of those limits, either at home in Brazil or at a Major in Singapore. That gives Hellmann’s something many betting sponsors have lost this year, a logo that can appear anywhere FURIA plays. The brand has also used the deal for more than a shirt patch.
In April 2025, Hellmann’s launched Hungry Games, a platform built with FURIA that used AI and facial recognition to spot signs of fatigue and irritability in players, then signal when they should eat. In a test with FURIA players and creators, one player in each pair ate snacks while the other played hungry, and the brand said the fed players won more often. Pedro Lopes, FURIA’s marketing director, said the club “always looks to create connections that go beyond the obvious”.
The March 2026 renewal turned the deal into fan access. Under the “Showmatch Irresistível” promotion, fans who bought a flavoured Hellmann’s squeeze could compete for eight places in a showmatch with FalleN and molodoy. The match was set for the Intel stand during the IEM Rio finals, from 17 to 19 April, with a stream on MadHouse TV. Riotto, by then CMO of Unilever Alimentos in Brazil, said the aim was to “go beyond sponsorship and create real connections between the gaming community and its idols”.
The timing of this run suits both sides as well. FalleN, FURIA’s in-game leader and one of the two pros in that showmatch, announced his retirement on stage at IEM Rio, saying he will stop playing at the end of 2026. That makes the Major in Singapore one of his last events as a player. FURIA, whose official store sells the club’s jerseys, goes into the PGL Major as BLAST Rivals champion after beating Legacy, Vitality, Falcons and Spirit. The Major starts on 24 November, and its playoffs run from 10 to 13 December at the Singapore Indoor Stadium.
The post The CS2 Mayonnaise Team: How Hellmann’s Became FURIA’s Most Famous Sponsor appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: SteamOS patch notes hint at Nvidia GPU support progress
items.content:
SteamOS 3.10 contains another sign that Valve's plans for Nvidia GPU support are beginning to take shape. Alongside the usual Steam Deck fixes and improvements, the latest SteamOS preview update also includes a dedicated Nvidia Graphics section, a noteworthy addition for an operating system historically associated almost exclusively with AMD graphics hardware.
Earlier this year, Valve confirmed that it was working directly with both Intel and Nvidia to expand SteamOS support beyond AMD hardware. At the time, Valve's Pierre-Loup Griffais said Intel had been doing “a lot of hard work” on SteamOS support, while Valve was also collaborating “very closely” with Nvidia behind the scenes.
The new SteamOS 3.10 preview update offers perhaps the clearest public sign of that work to date. The patch notes include Nvidia-specific stability and performance improvements, support for Mesh Shaders on Turing GPUs and newer, as well as fixes for rendering corruption in games like Shadow of the Tomb Raider and The Surge 2.
The significance of those changes extends beyond Steam Deck owners. SteamOS has traditionally been associated with AMD hardware, both because of the Steam Deck and AMD's long-standing support for Linux gaming. Broader Nvidia compatibility would make SteamOS a far more viable alternative for desktop PC gamers running GeForce RTX graphics cards. Valve still hasn't announced a timeline for wider Nvidia support, but the appearance of dedicated Nvidia features and fixes in official SteamOS patch notes suggests that good progress is being made currently.
KitGuru says: SteamOS support for Nvidia graphics has been discussed for a while now, but we're finally starting to see some tangible signs of progress. The bigger question is when Nvidia support will become mature enough for RTX owners to seriously consider SteamOS as a Windows alternative.

items.title: Rumour: Persona 6 Blowout Primed for The Game Awards
Kaashvi Hits Back at Pages Sending Her Hate: ‘I’ll Have My Say When I’m Ready’
items.content:
Kaashvi Hiranandani, the gaming creator known online as Kaash Plays, has told the pages criticising her that she will not defend herself until she is ready. “To the pages calling me out and sending me hate, go ahead and villainize me with whatever little context you have,” she wrote on X on 16 November. She added that she was not going to answer “a story you don’t even know in its entirety”, and that some of her critics would later “realise how unfairly you’ve judged me and the situation”. The post had passed 8,500 views and nearly 400 likes within half an hour.
to the pages calling me out and sending me hate, go ahead and villainize me with whatever little context you have. I'm not going to defend myself against a story you don't even know in its entirety. I'll have my say when I'm ready. some of you will realise then how unfairly…
— Kaash (@KaashviH) November 16, 2026
Kaashvi Hiranandani’s post on X, 16 November 2026
Kaashvi did not name the pages or say which story she meant. Her post came at the end of a weekend that tied her name to ScoutOP’s run on Bigg Boss 20 once again. It happened first on the show itself, and then in a viral clip from her own YouTube channel. She also did not say when she plans to speak, and neither Scout’s team nor Bigg Boss has commented on her post.
How Scout’s Bigg Boss 20 run put Kaashvi in the spotlight
Tanmay “Scout” Singh entered the Bigg Boss 20 house in September as the first Indian esports star on the show, and his closeness to fellow contestant Love Gill soon became one of the season’s talking points. On 25 October, Kaashvi entered the house and asked Scout to set boundaries with Love, whom she accused of emotional manipulation. Love denied it, and her team said the next day that she saw Scout as a brother.
Kaashvi apologised on Instagram on 26 October after viewers said she had painted Love unfairly on national television. She said that “some of the words I used were insensitive towards other people involved”, and that she never meant to direct hate at Love. On 6 November, she told viewers on a livestream that she would support Scout “wholeheartedly”, calling it “my last act for him” and “the last dance”. Many fans read that as a break-up, although neither of them has announced one.
Scout’s own time in the house has not been quiet either. He reportedly received four punishments after pushing Yung DSA earlier this month, and after a tough Weekend Ka Vaar on 31 October, his team wrote on Instagram that “storms don’t define legends” but reveal them. The post went up on Scout’s official Instagram account while he was inside the house, and it did not name anyone.
A fiancée reveal and a Samay Raina roast in the same weekend
The latest attention began on the Weekend Ka Vaar episode that aired on Sunday, 15 November. When host Salman Khan asked whether he was worried about what was happening outside the house, Scout said Kaashvi was not just his girlfriend. “I had never told anyone until now, but she is my fiancée,” he said in Hindi, according to Aaj Tak, and he denied having romantic feelings for Love Gill.
Scout added that he feels guilty if anything he does upsets Kaashvi even slightly, and that she has done a lot for him over the past five to six years. His mother also shared an audio note on social media saying that edited promos can give the wrong impression. TalkEsport found no public response from Kaashvi to the fiancée remark itself.
A day later, a clip from Kaashvi’s vlog “I GOT ROASTED BY SAMAY RAINA” spread online. It was filmed behind the scenes of the BGMI 4.7 promo in which Samay Raina plays a bus conductor. In it, the comedian jokes about Scout and Love Gill, including a jibe about loyalty, while Kaashvi laughs. Many fans praised the pair’s chemistry in the comments, and Kaashvi has not said whether her post on X was about the clip.
What Kaashvi has not said yet
Kaashvi’s post reads less like a statement and more like a request for time. She has not confirmed the state of her relationship with Scout, the fiancée claim or what she meant by a story people do not know “in its entirety”. That leaves fans with Scout’s words on television and her own clips, and very little from her about what has happened off camera.
Kaashvi has a large following of her own, built through her Kaash Plays channel on YouTube, where the Samay Raina vlog was posted. So far, she has said only that she will have her say “when I’m ready”. Scout was still in the Bigg Boss 20 house as of the Weekend Ka Vaar episode on 15 November.

Intel details Diamond Rapids Xeon and GPU D-series accelerators
items.content:
Intel has shared new details on its upcoming Diamond Rapids Xeon processors and GPU D-series accelerators at SC26. The updates provide a closer look at Intel's next-generation server CPU and GPU hardware, including significantly higher core counts, increased memory bandwidth and large-memory accelerator configurations aimed at AI and HPC workloads.
Diamond Rapids will succeed the current Xeon 6 platform, with configurations offering up to 256 performance cores alongside support for Intel's Advanced Performance Extensions (APX), AVX 10.2 and enhanced Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The next-gen Xeon chips will also offer up to 1.6TB/s of memory bandwidth and as much as 1.28GB of last-level cache.
Intel also shared new details on its upcoming GPU D-series accelerators. The GPU D-series is aimed at AI inference and scientific computing workloads, with support for formats ranging from FP4 and MXFP4 through to FP64. Intel says top-end configurations will feature up to 480GB of LPDDR5X memory while retaining a standard PCIe form factor and air-cooled design.
On the software side, Intel reiterated its commitment to open development tools and existing HPC ecosystems. The company also reaffirmed support for oneAPI, Intel MPI, Fortran and its wider compiler toolchain, with an emphasis on integrating AI workloads into existing HPC environments without forcing developers to abandon established codebases.
