items.title: TFT Set 19 Prismatic Tour hits high note with musical traits and champions
items.content:
Teamfight Tactics (TFT) Set 19 is Prismatic Tour! Ahead of the Dev Drop, esports.gg previewed TFT Set 19, and we can now reveal more details about Prismatic Tour’s champions, traits, music genres, and more.
TFT Set 19 release date
TFT Set 19, also known as Prismatic Tour, releases on Dec. 2 on PC and mobile. This launch features 94 champions and more than 20 music genres.
Official TFT Set 19 release date (Image credit: Riot Games)
TFT Set 19 Prismatic Tour unlocks
Prismatic Tour features the unlock mechanic from Lore & Legends, allowing you to add unlockable units to your champion pool. For example, you can field three Heartsteel champions to unlock Alune. Those who love Smeech and wish to experience the Jazz trait, meanwhile, can unlock him by having eight active traits.
“Take Smeech, for example, our legendary Jazz Renegade, swinging all the way over from our Arcane set in fedora-clad style. To unlock this smeechy smeecher, you’ll need to have eight or more traits active,” head of gameplay Alex “Riot Bluevelvet” Cole explained. “While difficult, it’s something you’ll want to do to maximize the Jazz trait, which is back from Set 10 to give stats based on your total active traits.”
Smeech in TFT Set 19 (Image credit: Riot Games)
Players who wish to experience the unlock mechanic at its fullest can try for an all-Yordle Hyperpop roster as well. While most TFT Set 19 traits have about two unlockable units, Hyperpop has all unlockables save for the 1-cost Ziggs.
Each member of the Hyperpop lineup helps unlock the next one until acquiring Ziggs, Kobuko, Tristana, and Lulu. Then, you can 3-star all these Yordles to unlock Teemo. Rerolling and increasing the star level of these Hyperpop champions also contributes to the Hype Meter for loot.
Hyperpop units in Prismatic Tour (Image credit: Riot Games)
TFT Set 19 traits and champions
The Gu Feng trait is another one that’s centered around the unlock mechanic. It begins with the 4-cost Xayah, who can deal damage to unlock Wukong. You can then deal more damage and pay 45 gold to unlock Janna and Lee Sin. Doing this leads to Gu Feng 4, allowing you to select either the Scroll of Heavenly Prayer or Scroll of the Beast.
While the Scroll of Heavenly Prayer can turn into a random recommended item that becomes radiant at level 10, the Scroll of the Beast grants a ton of attack damage, ability power, and mana regeneration. The latter scroll also summons the beast itself, who devours you if you lose two player combats in a row. Hitting level 10 does let you appease his appetite and grant you the ability to unlock level 11 for the win, thankfully.
Mel and Rell are soul-linked in TFT Set 19 (Image credit: Riot Games)
TFT Set 19 stars Mel and Rell combo, Ionic Spark, K/DA, and more
In addition to the Jazz, Hyperpop, and Gu Feng traits, esports.gg had a look at the R&M trait. This one features Mel and Rell as a musical duo. While the 4-cost Arcanist Mel is all about soft sounds, the 5-cost Rell brings about harsh, metal sounds. Together, they make a great combo in the late game where Rell tanks Mel’s damage and Mel heals Rell by dealing damage to enemies.
Another trait to note is Ionic Spark, which includes 10 units. This trait gives bandmates loot that can either give personalized offensive buffs or restore health and grant attack speed. You can unlock Tibbers via Annie, use Aurora and Jinx as late-game carries, and even have Shyvana as a tank to get more loot. Gwen, the 5-cost unit, is great at dishing out damage on the frontline while providing durability for allies.
Gwen has the Ionic Spark trait in TFT Set 19: Prismatic Tour (Image credit: Riot Games)
Don’t forget about the K/DA trait, either. This one unlocks higher breakpoints through star levels. For example, activating POP/STARS results in reduced mana costs, DRUM GO DUM grants a shield, VILLAIN grants more attack speed, and I’LL SHOW YOU boosts all prior effects. As for FIRESTARTER, a new track at 16 stars, it burns down a significant percentage of maximum health over time.
Reaching 22 stars results in K/DA’s prismatic breakpoint as well, allowing you to attack enemies with Evelynn and Akali. Since Akali is also part of True Damage, she has two separate unlockable 5-costs.
True Damage Akali artwork (Image credit: Riot Games)
More TFT Set 19 traits and champions
Speaking of True Damage, this trait lets you stack Bling and convert that to loot. You can flip between the A-Side or B-Side depending on your playstyle. While the A-Side grants bonus true damage, the B-Side lets you gain Bling on loss streaks.
As for Illbeats, it lets you raise the sliders to determine stats. The four adjustable sliders are health, attack damage, ability power, and the chance to drop gold on kill.
Other traits in TFT Set 19 include ones like the aforementioned Heartsteel one plus Pentakill, Beach Pop, and Classical.
The Illbeats trait lets you adjust sliders, and each slider has 10 levels (Image credit: Riot Games)
TFT Set 19 Solo Artists
TFT Set 19 features Solo Artists, too, which are threat-like units with their own unique, one-off origins. They have their music split into layers that can take over some trait genres.
“For example, Miss Fortune is a 5-cost who brings her 8-bit cash-out fantasy from Set 10 into the Prismatic Tour as a team-wide quest to continually break high scores by dealing more and more damage,” game designer Riot Fystai explained.
“Adding Miss Fortune and her brick-breaker cannons to your board will bring the classic 8-bit drum layer to your track,” music designer Jin Qin added. “If you start her up, she’ll also add another chord layer as she takes over as one of your team’s primary carries. Three-star her, and we’ll add all the layers, giving you the full 8-bit track.”
Malzahar, whose only trait is Composer, meanwhile, lets you collect instruments of each cost to unlock Baron Nashor. This 7-cost unit summons an orchestra and a Rift Herald. Other Solo Artists include Nunu, Nidalee, Zeri, and Seraphine.
Collect enough instruments as Malzahar to unlock the One Monster Band, Baron Nashor (Image credit: Riot Games)
TFT Tour Collection and cosmetics galore
Outside of the action, TFT players can decorate a room with Prismatic Tour items. Completing the Tour Collection results in portals, little legends, and more rewards.
The Ionic Spark arena in Set 19 (Image credit: Riot Games)
In terms of other cosmetics, they include the Ionic Spark arena, Ionic Spark Briar and Aurora chibis, special Choncc and Pengu little legends in honor of TFT Vegas Open 2026, and more.
Exalted Ionic Spark Gwen in Prismatic Tour (Image credit: Riot Games)
That’s all for now. Are you excited about TFT Set 19: Prismatic Tour? Stick around on esports.gg for more TFT news and updates!

items.title: NYT Connections Hints Today (#1253)—Answers for Sunday, November 15
Zombies Aren’t Real Lets You Stop an Outbreak in Real Cities, and Steam Players Love It
items.content:
Zombies Aren’t Real, a top-down strategy game about stopping a zombie outbreak in real cities, has made a strong start on Steam since its release at the end of last week. The Early Access game from Jogamedev, the studio behind Spellmasons, launched on 13 November and holds an Overwhelmingly Positive rating, with 96% of 611 user reviews recommending it on its Steam page. It reached an all-time peak of 5,782 concurrent players on 14 November, according to SteamDB, and was still above 5,300 players when TalkEsport checked. It costs $9.99, with a 10% launch discount until 20 November.
The idea is simple to explain and hard to master. You look down on a real city from above before an infection breaks out, spend limited resources on defences, and then try to contain the horde while saving as many civilians as you can. Every mission is scored on lives saved, which turns each decision about where to place troops into a question of who you can afford to leave outside the line.
You defend real cities, and the map can be your own
The most distinctive feature is where the outbreaks happen. Missions take place in large real-world cities built by the developer, and the game already supports custom maps through Steam Workshop. Jogamedev says custom maps can pull in public geographic data for zip codes worldwide, so players are not limited to the cities that ship with the game.
The first Workshop campaigns show where the developer’s head is. The four maps listed so far, all made by the developer, are Sighișoara in Romania, Auckland in New Zealand, and Nördlingen and Wemding in Bavaria. Sighișoara and Nördlingen are both famous for their surviving medieval town walls, which makes them obvious places to hold back a horde. Workshop pages for the game are available on its Steam Workshop hub.
For players in India, the zip code support is the most interesting part. If postal codes outside the US and Europe work as the store page suggests, Indian players could build and defend maps of their own neighbourhoods. The developer has not shown an Indian city yet, and TalkEsport has not tested how well the map data works for Indian postal codes.
Snipers, mortars and gunship helicopters, but civilians come first
Your tools are a mix of ground forces and air support. The Steam page lists snipers, turrets, mortar squads and garrisons on the ground, with bombers and gatling gun helicopters available as air strikes. Those strikes have to be aimed carefully, because the game counts civilian casualties as well as zombie kills, and players can also place safe zones and gates to protect people from the spread.
The game supports online co-op for two players, as well as Steam Achievements, leaderboards and a level editor. It is a 2D game, and the minimum specification asks for a four-core 3GHz processor, 8GB of RAM and a graphics card on the level of a GeForce GTX 750 Ti or Radeon R7 260X. It needs just 2GB of storage, and the developer recommends the Low graphics setting for smoother play on older PCs.
Interface text is available only in English at launch, with no full audio or subtitles in other languages listed. That may limit its reach in some markets, although the minimal 2D presentation means there is little dialogue to translate. Steam does not yet list a Steam Deck rating, so the store’s new frame rate data for Deck games is not available for it either.
Version 1.0 is due in early 2027, and the price may rise
Jogamedev says it released the game in Early Access because interest was strong, and that it already offers a few hours of play. The studio plans to add more troops, vehicles, aircraft and upgrades before version 1.0, which it is targeting for the first quarter of 2027. It also warns that the price may go up at 1.0, because the full game will have more content.
Jogamedev’s earlier games sit alongside this one on Steam. A bundle collects its catalogue, Spellmasons, Some of You May Die and Zombies Aren’t Real, and a $4.99 Supporter Pack is available for players who want to back development. Zombies Aren’t Real joins other small Steam successes this month, including Punch The Walls, in a November crowded by major releases led by GTA 6. Anyone tempted has until 20 November to buy it at the launch discount of 10%.
The post Zombies Aren’t Real Lets You Stop an Outbreak in Real Cities, and Steam Players Love It appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Is Minecraft 2 Real? Mojang Just Laid Out Very Different Plans
items.content:
Early today several reports emerged of Mojang, building a full-scale “Minecraft 2”, the studio’s own plans, which was published the same day, point somewhere else entirely. The post from Chaos Crave on Sunday said the sequel is being built “from the ground up on a brand-new engine” for PC, PlayStation 6 and the next Xbox. It credited unnamed “insiders” with details such as realistic water physics, dynamic weather disasters and travel between dimensions without loading screens.
The rumour spread quickly because it promises something many players have wanted for years. Minecraft has sold more than 425 million copies, according to Xbox, and Xbox chief executive Asha Sharma said in September that over 300,000 people play it for the first time every day. A clean-slate sequel would be one of the biggest announcements in gaming, which is exactly why the lack of a named source matters.
The post does not link to a report, name a publication or identify the insiders behind it. That is unusual for a claim of this size, because a genuine leak about Microsoft’s biggest game would normally come with at least one named outlet or reporter attached. Until that changes, the story is an unverified claim rather than a report.
The platforms named in the post raise questions of their own. Sony has not announced the PlayStation 6, and its chief executive said in May that the console’s release date and price had not been decided. Microsoft’s next console, Project Helix, will only reach developers as alpha hardware from 2027, and Xbox described it this weekend as a console that can also play PC games.
Mojang laid out its own plans the same weekend, and a sequel was not in them
Xbox’s 25th anniversary magazine, released on 15 November and free to read on Xbox Wire, includes a long feature on what comes next for Minecraft. It quotes Kayleen Walters, president of Xbox’s XP division and former president of Mojang, at length. Her account centres on extending the current game rather than replacing it.
The biggest piece of that plan is the Sift, a new dimension that Mojang announced at Minecraft Live on 26 September. It debuted in Minecraft Dungeons II, which launched in September, and arrives in the main game on Minecraft Java and Bedrock next year. The first Dungeons found around 30 million players, Walters said, which showed Mojang there was appetite for Minecraft in other genres. Walters said Mojang wanted “the most significant addition to the Minecraft universe in 15 years” to debut somewhere players had to go and experience for themselves.
Walters also stressed continuity with what players already have. Minecraft runs on roughly 20 platforms, and she said Mojang treats every player “as equally important, whatever platform they play on”. She described long-running save files as “digital heirlooms”, adding that everything Mojang ships “has to be safe for a world someone has been building since yesterday or for decades”.
Physics and a new dimension are already coming, just not as a new game
Some of what the rumour describes is already happening inside the existing game. Walters said the Sulfur Cube, a recent mob, began with the question “What if we put physics in Minecraft?”, which she called a bold question to ask of a 17-year-old game. The Sift adds the first new dimension since the End arrived in 2011, and TalkEsport’s guide to reaching the Sift covers how players can explore it early.
Mojang also has new leadership at the top of the studio. Maria Angelidou-Smith became chief executive of Mojang and Minecraft in October, and told the magazine she wants to help Minecraft reach new generations “while protecting what makes it so special”. None of that rules out a sequel at some point, but nothing Mojang has said publicly points to one being in development.
The magazine also shows how far Minecraft now reaches beyond the game itself, which is where much of Mojang’s new investment is going. Walters pointed to A Minecraft Movie as proof that new players can arrive through a film, a theme park or a classroom rather than the game. A Minecraft World theme park land is due to open at Chessington World of Adventures Resort near London in 2027, with what Xbox calls the world’s first Minecraft-themed hotel.
The post Is Minecraft 2 Real? Mojang Just Laid Out Very Different Plans appeared first on TalkEsport.

Jensen Huang Is Weighing a Return as Nvidia CEO
items.content:
Jensen Huang is considering a return as Nvidia’s chief executive, only days after he resigned, the Financial Times reported on Sunday. Citing people familiar with the matter, the newspaper said Huang has discussed the possibility of coming back with confidants. One of his allies is reportedly assembling a group of Silicon Valley executives, described as a “war room”, to lobby Nvidia’s board for his reinstatement and to seek support from the White House. TalkEsport has not seen a public response to the report from Huang or Nvidia, and the FT’s sources were not named.
The FT report lands at an awkward moment for the company. Huang stepped down on 12 November after reports about his relationship with Alice Huang, the former Megaspeed executive at the centre of a chip export scandal. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been running Nvidia on an interim basis since then, according to the company’s announcement. The board has said it is choosing a search firm and has not formally approached any candidates for the permanent job. The FT’s own summary says tech supporters are now lobbying the chipmaker’s board to reinstate its former chief executive.
Allies want the board and the White House on side
The campaign for Huang’s return was already loud before Sunday’s report. Elon Musk said last week that he was signing a petition to reinstate him, and the Stand with Jensen petition has circulated widely since. Musk has also said that hiring Huang himself “would be an honour”, a sign of how much of his standing in the industry has survived the scandal. Ruby on Rails creator David Heinemeier Hansson added his voice on Sunday, writing that “we need @JensenHuang back at NVIDIA” because “the free world depends on it”.
Some of Nvidia’s investors have been pushing in the same direction. Altimeter Capital’s Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management’s Gavin Baker wrote to the board asking it to keep Huang’s return on the table and avoid a rushed replacement. Inside the company, 88% of Nvidia staff who answered a Blind survey before his resignation said he should stay.
What the FT describes goes further than public support. An organised group of executives lobbying the board, and asking the White House to back them, would turn a petition into a direct pressure campaign. Accounts of the FT story published so far do not name the ally behind the “war room” or the executives involved, or say whether the White House has responded.
Washington and the board’s own investigation stand in the way
The biggest obstacle to a comeback is already out in the open. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday that Nvidia needs “a dramatic shakeup” and should hire an outside chief executive. He also wants answers from the board within 10 days on whether the company pushed “seemingly illicit” chip sales to China, a window that runs to around 25 November.
The board also has unfinished business of its own to deal with. Its independent members have hired Wachtell Lipton and former federal prosecutor Joon Kim to investigate Huang’s conduct, according to the board’s statement. That review has not reported, and reinstating Huang before it does would expose the board to the charge that it ignored its own process.
Only the board can appoint a chief executive, whatever executives, investors or the White House say. Huang co-founded Nvidia and remains one of its largest individual shareholders, but he does not control the company. A comeback would depend on directors deciding that the scandal matters less than the risk of losing him, at the same moment the Treasury is telling them the opposite.
Tuesday’s results are the next test
The report could hardly have come at a more sensitive time for Nvidia. The company reports its third-quarter results on Tuesday, 17 November, with Kress now running the company as interim chief executive. The call will be the first chance for analysts to question the company since Huang left, and the leadership search, the board’s investigation and the chip sales Bessent raised are all live issues.
The questions about Huang’s conduct have also grown since he quit. Reuters reported that he told Nvidia’s general counsel his dealings with Alice Huang and Megaspeed were standard business. In Washington, lawmakers are advancing new chip export bills after reports that Megaspeed arranged nearly $12 billion of advanced chips for Chinese companies. Megaspeed denies diverting chips to China, and Nvidia has said it complies with US export law.
The post Jensen Huang Is Weighing a Return as Nvidia CEO appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Worlds 2026 Final just recorded its lowest peak in 6 years at 3.98 million
items.content:
The Worlds 2026 final drew the smallest peak audience for a League of Legends World Championship since 2020. Bilibili Gaming’s 3-1 win over Gen.G at the Barclays Center in New York peaked at 3.98 million viewers, according to Esports Charts, whose figures leave out Chinese streaming platforms. That is roughly 2.8 million fewer than last year’s final and about 3 million below the record of 6.94 million set in 2024. The drop came on the night BLG won their first world title, and it has a few clear explanations.
Esports Charts counts official broadcasts and co-streams together, which is why individual streamers matter so much to these totals. It first reported a 3.9 million peak for the final on Saturday night, then put the figure at 3.98 million the next day. Its numbers show the audience building through the series, from 3.1 million during game one to 3.49 million in game three, before the peak in the deciding fourth game. The figure ties 2019’s final between FunPlus Phoenix and G2 Esports, which also peaked at 3.98 million.
Every Worlds final above 5 million peak viewers had T1 in it
The clearest pattern in the data is T1. Faker’s team played in every Worlds final from 2022 to 2025, and those four finals are the only ones to have passed 5 million peak viewers. The team also reached the 2016 and 2017 finals as SK Telecom T1, when Worlds audiences were far smaller across the board. This year, BLG knocked T1 out 3-1 in the semi-finals, ending their hopes of a fourth straight title before the final in Brooklyn.
The weaker numbers were already visible before the final began. Esports Charts compared peaks before each grand final, and 2026 stood at 3.6 million, against 3.9 million in 2025, 4.9 million in 2024 and 4.3 million in 2023. That 3.6 million peak came from T1’s semi-final against BLG, so the biggest audience of the tournament still belonged to a T1 series even after they were gone.
Gen.G bring a loyal Korean following, and BLG won First Stand earlier this year, but neither has T1’s global pull. TalkEsport’s Worlds 2026 hub shows how open the bracket was, with LYON and Karmine Corp also reaching the knockouts. A final between two strong teams without the sport’s biggest star was unlikely to match the T1 years, however good the series turned out to be.
The final started at 3 AM in China and 4 AM in Korea, and Chinese viewers are not counted
The start time made the problem worse for Asian fans in particular. The final began at 2 PM Eastern time on Saturday, which was 3 AM in China, as BLG’s own match post confirmed, and 4 AM in South Korea. In Vietnam, home of the night’s second-biggest co-stream, it started at 2 AM, while fans in India had to stay up until 12:30 AM, as TalkEsport’s grand final guide set out.
There is also a large audience that these charts never see. Esports Charts excludes Chinese platforms, and the final featured a Chinese champion owned by Bilibili, one of China’s biggest video sites. The real global audience was higher than 3.98 million, but no independent figure covers Chinese viewing, so the reported peak reflects only the rest of the world.
YouTube beat Twitch, and Caedrel was the biggest single channel
The platform split shows where the remaining viewers went. YouTube peaked at 1.75 million and Twitch at 1.44 million during the final, according to Esports Charts’ platform breakdown. Co-streamer Caedrel led all individual channels with more than 580,000 viewers, ahead of Vietnamese caster Hoàng Luân on 211,000 and lshooooo on 125,000. Kick also carried the official broadcast, but the breakdown did not list a separate peak for it.
Those co-stream numbers point to where League’s audience lives. A Vietnamese channel was the second-biggest stream of the night despite the 2 AM start, which suggests the market is still there when the schedule allows it. Esports Charts tracks the full year on its League of Legends stats page, where 3.98 million now stands as the top peak of 2026.
Next year’s location should suit those fans much better. Riot has confirmed that Worlds 2027 will be held in Japan and South Korea, putting the event back in East Asian time zones for the first time since the 2025 tournament in China. The Swiss stage will be played in Nagoya, the first time Worlds has visited Japan, and the whole knockout stage will be held in Korea.
The post Worlds 2026 Final just recorded its lowest peak in 6 years at 3.98 million appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Project Helix Is a Console First, Not a PC, XBOX Says
TenZ Wants VALORANT to Copy League’s Pro View After Knight’s Worlds-Winning POV: ‘Can Learn a Lot’
items.content:
TenZ wants VALORANT esports to copy one of League of Legends’ simplest ideas. On Sunday, the T1 star quoted a LoL Esports post that shared the full pro view of Knight’s game from Bilibili Gaming’s title-winning Worlds 2026 final. “It would be so cool seeing something like this in VALORANT, can learn a lot from watching someone’s POV,” TenZ wrote. His post came only days after T1 signed him to return to professional play in VCT Pacific for the 2027 season.
It would be so cool seeing something like this in VALORANT, can learn a lot from watching someone’s POV https://t.co/WkG03IjJdK
— TenZ (@TenZOfficial) November 15, 2026
The LoL Esports post invited fans to “check out the FULL PRO VIEW of Knight’s Worlds-winning game 4 against GEN”. The video runs for almost 43 minutes and shows only what BLG’s mid laner saw on his own screen, from his camera movement to his ability usage and minimap checks. BLG beat Gen.G 3-1 at the Barclays Center in New York on Saturday to win the title, and game four was the one that sealed the organisation’s first world title.
TenZ wants the one thing League fans already get after a Worlds final
LoL Esports shares pro view footage like this so fans can follow a single player instead of the main broadcast. The value is in the details that a broadcast misses, because an observer has to switch between ten players and cannot stay with one for long. A full game from one player’s screen shows every decision that player makes, including the quiet ones between fights.
VALORANT’s official broadcasts are built around a different approach. VCT coverage on VALORANT Esports follows an observer feed that cuts between players as rounds develop, and most player perspective content comes from clips or from players’ own streams. Riot has not announced a pro view series for VCT, and TenZ framed the idea as something he would like to see rather than something that already exists.
His point is easy to understand for anyone who has tried to learn the game from a broadcast. In a tactical shooter, the most useful lessons often happen before a fight starts, in where a player holds their crosshair, when they check a corner and how they time their utility. An observer usually cuts away from those moments to follow the action elsewhere, which is exactly the detail a full POV would keep.
Knight was a fitting choice for the clip. BLG’s mid laner was central to a run in which the team swept Dplus KIA 3-0 in the quarter-finals and beat T1 3-1 in the semi-finals before the final. BLG had already won First Stand in March, and the Worlds title completed the biggest season in the organisation’s history.
Why a full POV could matter even more in VALORANT
The case for it is arguably stronger in VALORANT than in League. A full round-by-round view would show how a professional handles economy decisions, mid-round calls and repositioning after a teammate dies, none of which fit neatly into a highlight clip. It would also give coaches and amateur teams a free study tool built from the highest level of play.
There are open questions that Riot would have to answer before anything like this could happen. Teams may not want every rotation and setup from an international match available for rivals to study in full, although broadcasts already show much of it. Riot would also need to decide which matches, which players and which platforms would carry the footage, and VCT has not said whether it is considering any of that.
TenZ has a better claim than most to ask. He built much of his following by streaming his own play, and fans have spent years studying his aim and movement from his own point of view. His post was a short reply rather than a campaign, but it put a simple idea in front of one of the biggest audiences in VALORANT.
TenZ now plays for T1, the team BLG knocked out of Worlds
There is an extra twist in who TenZ was praising. Knight’s BLG beat T1 3-1 in the Worlds semi-finals, ending the League side’s run of three straight titles, and TenZ now plays VALORANT for the same organisation. T1 officially signed him on 12 November, ending a retirement from pro play that began in September 2024. The club’s announcement called him “a living legend of VALORANT” and declared that “the KING is back”, while TenZ replied with a simple “I’m back”.
T1 has built one of the most talked-about rosters of the VCT 2027 off-season around him, with crashies also joining, as TalkEsport’s tracker of the biggest player transfers shows. If Riot ever does add pro view footage to VCT, TenZ’s own games in VCT Pacific would be among the most watched. T1 announced crashies on 11 November, a day before it confirmed TenZ.
The move had been building for months before T1 made it official. TenZ first joined T1 as an influencer in May, before the club confirmed him as a player for 2027. Fellow signing crashies called his own return “back where it all started”, because T1 was his first VALORANT team in 2020. Sacy has also been reported as the team’s new head coach, although T1 has not confirmed that yet. VCT Pacific 2027 will be TenZ’s first season of professional play since he retired in September 2024.

items.title: Punch The Walls Lets You Fist-Fight Your Way Out of Prison for $2.99, and Steam Look-Alikes Are Already Queuing Up
items.content:
Punch The Walls is a $2.99 Steam game in which you escape a concrete prison cell by punching through the walls with your bare hands. Developer BoomGames released it on 6 November, and its Steam page shows a Very Positive rating, with 80% of 324 user reviews recommending it at the time of writing. Its loop fits in one line: punch, collect the rubble, sell it, upgrade, and punch harder. At least three similar wall-breaking games are now listed on Steam as upcoming releases, and one of them may even have come first.
The Punch The Walls trailer, released by the game’s official YouTube channel ahead of its 6 November Steam launch.
You start with your fists, and the walls pay for every upgrade
You wake up locked in a concrete cell with no visible way out, and your fists are the only tool you have. Every punch breaks part of a voxel wall into cubes, which you vacuum up and feed into a shredder that turns them into cash. That money buys stronger, faster punches with more reach, as well as a better vacuum and an upgraded shredder, so each wall you break pays for the next one. The rubble is physics-based too, so broken cubes tumble and pile up on the floor until you clear them.
The tools grow more destructive as you dig. Steam’s feature list includes charged punches, dynamite and C4 for harder rock, and the punches and vacuum both have their own upgrade paths. There are eight rock types to break, and buried gold, watches and crowns add a reason to tunnel in every direction rather than straight for an exit.
There is a light mystery on top of the mining. Each prison is procedurally generated, and notes left behind by earlier prisoners hold the code to the door. That gives each run a reason to explore rather than simply dig, because the way out is written down somewhere inside the walls.
It costs $2.99, runs on old hardware and also works on a Mac
The low price is only part of its appeal. The minimum Windows specification asks for an Intel Core i5-4590 or AMD Ryzen 3 1200, 4GB of RAM and a GeForce GTX 750 Ti or Radeon R7 260X. That puts it within reach of PCs that are more than a decade old. It needs just 1GB of storage, and BoomGames also lists a macOS version for Apple M1 or quad-core Intel Macs with 8GB of RAM.
Interface text is available in English and 11 other languages, although there is no full voice audio to localise. Steam tags place it among incremental, destruction and physics games, with mining, voxel and escape room labels alongside them. The game is single-player only, and its tags lean towards relaxed, casual play rather than a stiff challenge.
Steam itself has been adding tools that help players judge small games like this one before they buy. Valve now shows real average frame rates for thousands of Steam Deck games, and desktop PCs are due to follow. Punch The Walls’ store page does not yet list a Steam Deck rating, so for now the gameplay footage on its official YouTube channel is the best guide for handheld players.
Look-alikes are already lining up on Steam
A successful idea on Steam rarely stays unique for long, and Punch The Walls is no exception. Wall Punch: Escape The Walls Simulator, from Thinflow Games, describes punching your way out of prison, growing stronger and using collected stones to upgrade. Break the Walls, from Smobu, swaps the cell for a sealed concrete bunker and adds online co-op for up to four players, with rubble turned into cash for better tools.
The third, Escape the Walls from Pandorio Games, is a first-person incremental game that also starts you with only your fists. Its Steam app number is lower than Punch The Walls’, and because Steam generally assigns those numbers in order, its store page appears to have been created first. Wall Punch and Break the Walls both carry higher numbers, which suggests they were registered after BoomGames’ game. None of the three store pages mentions Punch The Walls by name.
Copycat releases have become a familiar part of the store, as TalkEsport found when it looked at Valve’s stance on AI slop and clones. Punch The Walls also lands in a crowded month, with GTA 6 and the rest of November’s major releases competing for players’ time. All three look-alike games are still listed as coming soon on their Steam pages.
The post Punch The Walls Lets You Fist-Fight Your Way Out of Prison for $2.99, and Steam Look-Alikes Are Already Queuing Up appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: TSG Pros Eliminated From FFWS 2026 Global Finals, Two Points Short of Last Chance
items.content:
TSG Pros have been eliminated from the Free Fire World Series (FFWS) 2026 Global Finals in Bangkok. The Indian side finished 21st of 24 teams in Knockout Stage Phase 1 with 315 points when the stage ended on 15 November. Stellar Esport took 20th place, the last spot in the Last Chance stage, with 317 points. TSG Pros missed that place by two points.
TSG Pros scored 71 points in their final session, their best return of the stage. It was not enough to close the gap left by a slow first week. Garena’s format sends the bottom four teams home after Phase 1, so TSG Pros leave with ParadoX Gaming, Total Winner Esports and Pirate Esports. The organisation has not commented on the result.
TSG Pros’ session-by-session scores at FFWS 2026 Global Finals
TSG Pros played six sessions across two weeks in Group A, alongside Stellar Esport, Total Winner Esports, Buriram United Esports, ONIC Olympus and GunDynasty. They opened with 34 points on 6 November and finished the first day bottom of the overall table. They had 122 points and sat 21st at the end of Week 1 of the knockout stage, 30 points behind GunDynasty in 20th.
Week 2 brought 193 points from three sessions, against 122 in the first week. GunDynasty, who were docked 15 points after the opening day for deliberately dying to the zone, climbed to 14th with 411 points. Horaa Esports finished 19th on 334, taking the other Last Chance place.
Team Apex Gaming carry India’s hopes after TSG Pros exit
TSG Pros qualified as India’s third seed after finishing third at the TEZ FFMIC 2026 Fall in Noida in September. They topped out on 146 points in the regular FFMIC table, five behind Resurrection on 151. Team Apex Gaming won the FFMIC 2026 Fall title with a final-match Booyah in Champion Rush.
Team Apex Gaming finished 18th with 360 points and stayed in the main draw. Defending champions Buriram United Esports topped the overall FFWS 2026 Global Finals standings with 546 points and 10 Booyahs. Knockout Stage Phase 2 runs from 19 to 22 November, and the Last Chance stage is on 27 November. The Global Finals carry a $1,200,000 prize pool, and Garena has not yet published the payout for teams eliminated in Phase 1.

items.title: Xbox at 25 in Charts: Every Console Launched in November, and Series X|S Needs Until 2028 to Beat the 360
items.content:
Xbox turned 25 on 15 November, a quarter of a century after the original console went on sale in North America alongside Halo: Combat Evolved. Microsoft marked the date with a 116-page anniversary magazine and a numbered limited-edition console, while Geoff Keighley congratulated “everyone who helped build Xbox over the past quarter century”. TalkEsport went through that magazine page by page and checked Microsoft’s own launch records to build the charts and timeline below. Several of the details, from a staff-only launch console to the original plan for a 20-year lifespan, come straight from Xbox’s own pages rather than from older histories.
The numbers also show a pattern that is easy to miss. All four of its home consoles launched in North America in November, within 12 days of each other on the calendar, and Xbox Live arrived exactly one year after the first console. The record for the longest-serving Xbox generation still belongs to the Xbox 360, and the current Series X|S needs two more years to take it.
Every Xbox launched in November, and the Xbox 360 still holds the longevity record
Microsoft’s launch announcements put the Xbox 360’s North American release at 22 November 2005 and Xbox One’s at 22 November 2013. Series X|S followed on 10 November 2020, while the original Xbox had gone on sale on 15 November 2001. Xbox Live arrived in stores on 15 November 2002, one year to the day after the console it ran on. No other month appears anywhere in that list, so every Xbox has launched in the run-up to the holiday shopping season.
TalkEsport then measured how long each console stayed the newest Xbox, counting from its North American launch to its successor’s. The original Xbox lasted 1,468 days, just over four years, before the Xbox 360 replaced it. The 360 then held the top spot for exactly eight years, or 2,922 days, while Xbox One managed 2,545 days, almost seven years.
Series X|S turned six on 10 November, and by Xbox’s 25th birthday it had been the newest Xbox for 2,196 days, still 726 days short of the 360. If Microsoft’s next console does not reach shops before 11 November 2028, Series X|S will become the longest-serving Xbox generation. Xbox has said alpha hardware for Project Helix will reach developers from 2027, but it has not given the console a release date.
25 milestones from 25 years, with details from Xbox’s own anniversary magazine
The table lists 25 milestones in order, with the source for each one. Most come from Microsoft’s own announcements or from the anniversary magazine, which was written by the Xbox Wire team with editors from across Xbox and is free to read on Xbox Wire. Where the magazine gives a year but no exact date, the table uses the year.
A few of those entries tell a bigger story than a single table row allows. Before any customer had an Xbox, Microsoft gave its own launch staff a Launch Team Edition, a translucent green console with two green Duke controllers and a message to the team on the logo panel. Europe got a limited green Xbox for the console’s first birthday in 2003, and the Halo: Combat Evolved Special Edition followed in North America in 2004. Xbox names the Halo edition as one of the inspirations for this year’s X25 Limited Edition, of which only 25,000 numbered units are being made.
Achievements have an origin story of their own. Scott Henson, a founding Xbox team member who wrote the original concept document, told the magazine that co-creator J Allard pitched a “Scrapbook” for players’ online identity between 2001 and 2003, long before the technology existed. Henson also said the original vision for Xbox was a 20-year one, which makes the 25th anniversary feel, in his words, “a little surreal”. Achievements finally arrived with the Xbox 360 in 2005 and spread to most other gaming platforms within a few years.
Some of the firsts on the list are easy to forget after 25 years. Xbox says the original console was the first with a built-in hard drive and broadband from day one, and that the Xbox 360 became the first console with a local Netflix app in 2008. Backward compatibility mattered enough after its 2015 announcement that the team behind it renamed itself Game Preservation. Its programme lead, Peggy Lo, has worked at Xbox since the console launched in 2001.
The next 25 years start with Helix alpha kits in 2027
Xbox chief executive Asha Sharma used the magazine’s opening letter to say the company should be proud of its history but not “trapped by it”. The next chapter is Project Helix, which Jason Ronald, Xbox’s vice president of next generation, describes in the magazine as a console that plays PC games rather than a PC. The magazine also says the current component crisis has become a primary driver of how that hardware is being designed.
Alpha versions of the hardware will ship to developers from 2027, according to Xbox’s GDC announcement in March. Microsoft has not said when the console will launch or what it will cost, although a report last month suggested the Project Helix price could reach $1,800. Every Xbox console so far has gone on sale in November.
The post Xbox at 25 in Charts: Every Console Launched in November, and Series X|S Needs Until 2028 to Beat the 360 appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Megaspeed Says Alice Huang Left in August 2025, Two Months After Singapore Police Took Her Passport
items.content:
Megaspeed, the Singapore cloud company at the centre of the Nvidia scandal, says Alice Huang left the business on 30 August 2025 and “currently has no role with the company”. In a statement on Sunday, reported by The National, the company said it had “retained external legal counsel to conduct a thorough internal investigation”. It also said it “conducts legitimate and lawful business”, and that media reports about it were not backed by verifiable evidence. The exit date Megaspeed has now given, however, falls more than two months after Singapore police impounded her passport during their investigation into the company.
Alice Huang is the businesswoman whose relationship with Jensen Huang preceded his resignation as Nvidia’s chief executive on 12 November. US investigators reportedly suspect her of gathering information for China, which Beijing denies, and no charges against her have been reported. Megaspeed has denied diverting Nvidia chips to China, and the statement does not say what she did at the company before she left.
Megaspeed’s exit date lands in the middle of Singapore’s investigation
Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs set out its own timeline on 12 November, which TalkEsport covered in detail. Police and Singapore Customs opened an investigation into Megaspeed in February 2025, over possible false declarations in server purchases. On 24 June 2025, the US Bureau of Industry and Security carried out a post-shipment check at the company with Alice Huang present, and police interviewed her and impounded her passport that same day.
Megaspeed’s date of 30 August 2025 comes 67 days after that interview, at a time when police were still holding her passport. Police only returned it on 26 February 2026, and she left Singapore that day. By then, police had concluded that she gave them information she knew to be inaccurate, and she was given a stern warning and barred from re-entering the country, according to the ministry’s statement.
The timing also matters for the chip deals. The Wall Street Journal reported that Megaspeed arranged nearly $12 billion of advanced chips for Chinese companies between March 2024 and June 2025, a story that has pushed Congress towards new export bills. Megaspeed’s own date puts her departure about two months after the end of the period the Journal examined.
Three accounts of her role at Megaspeed do not line up
Megaspeed’s statement is the third version of her role to emerge. She was listed as managing director when the company took its current name in March 2023, according to Singapore’s ministry. Reuters reported last week that media reports put the end of that eight-month tenure in October 2023, in a factbox republished by The Standard. Tan, who now signs Megaspeed’s statements as chairman and chief executive, became a director in November 2023, according to the same factbox.
Singapore’s ministry, however, described her as Megaspeed’s “then-CEO, Chairperson, and one of the key controllers”, without giving dates. It also said police concluded that the inaccurate information she gave was meant to “downplay her role in Megaspeed”. Megaspeed’s new statement adds a third date, August 2025, and the company has not explained how it fits with either account.
An internal review joins US and Singapore probes that are still open
Sunday’s statement builds on one Megaspeed posted on its website on 12 November. In that statement, Tan said the company had cooperated with Bureau of Industry and Security inspections and had hired a US law firm to count its GPUs and check its export compliance. Neither statement names the lawyers involved, and Megaspeed has not said when the internal investigation will finish or whether it will publish the findings.
Singapore’s investigation into Megaspeed and six other people is continuing, and the ministry said it had received “limited information or assistance” from the US. It added that Supermicro, a US server supplier relevant to the case, had provided limited cooperation. In March, US prosecutors charged three men, including a co-founder of a US server maker, in a separate case. It concerns servers worth about $2.5 billion bought by a Southeast Asian company, at least $510 million of which were allegedly diverted to China. The Justice Department did not name that buyer, and nothing in its announcement links the case to Megaspeed.
Nvidia now faces questions about Megaspeed from Washington as well as from investors. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has given the board 10 days to answer his questions about whether the company pushed questionable chip sales, and he wants an outside chief executive. Interim chief executive Colette Kress will lead the company’s first earnings call since Huang’s resignation, when Nvidia reports third-quarter results on Tuesday, 17 November.
The post Megaspeed Says Alice Huang Left in August 2025, Two Months After Singapore Police Took Her Passport appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Project Helix Is ‘Not a PC’, Xbox Says, and the Component Crisis Is Now Shaping the Next Xbox
items.content:
Xbox has given its clearest description yet of Project Helix, calling its next console “a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC”. It is “not a PC that can also play console games”, said Jason Ronald, Xbox’s vice president of next generation, in a 25th anniversary magazine Xbox released on 15 November. The magazine came out on the day the original console turned 25, and its Helix feature makes a notable admission. The current component crisis, which is pushing up the price of almost anything with a plug, has changed how the next Xbox is being built.
The magazine was put together by the team behind Xbox Wire, and it is free to read in a digital edition on Xbox Wire, while printed copies were handed out at Xbox FanFest in Seattle. Its Project Helix feature runs across eight pages and includes a tour of the labs where the console is being designed. Most of what follows comes from Ronald’s interview in those pages, which goes well beyond what Xbox said when it revealed Helix at GDC in March.
Xbox’s next-gen chief says Helix is a console first, and PC tinkering is optional
Ronald described Helix as “the ultimate gaming machine” that removes “the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games”. In his words, players should be able to bring “four generations” of Xbox games and progress with them and have them available instantly, extending the backward compatibility programme Xbox began in 2015. He also said a console should spare players the chores of PC gaming, adding that he does not want to worry about “updating drivers” or configuring settings before he can play.
That focus on simplicity does not mean locking out enthusiasts who like to tinker. “If you’re a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it,” Ronald said. He also wants progress to follow players between devices, so that someone 25 hours into an 80-hour RPG can switch screens and “instantly resume from where I was”. That builds on Xbox Play Anywhere, which already carries purchases and saves between Xbox consoles and Windows PCs.
The clearest preview of how Helix will work is already on sale. Ronald called the ROG Xbox Ally handheld “a precursor to what we’re doing with Helix”, and said player feedback on its Xbox mode had “fundamentally informed and altered our plans”. That feedback covered playing libraries from several storefronts and showing PC and console games together in one library, although Ronald did not say which PC stores Helix will support.
The component crisis is now shaping Helix, and neural rendering is Xbox’s answer
The most revealing passage in the feature concerns the cost of building it. Consoles have historically been the cheapest way into gaming, the magazine notes, but the component crisis is a factor the team could not have foreseen when Helix began, and meeting that challenge has become “a primary driver” of its innovation. “It’s definitely a challenging time,” Ronald said, but he also called it “one of the most exciting times”, because Xbox has to “invent entirely new technology” to keep advancing the state of the art while still making things “accessible and affordable”. Memory prices have been at the centre of that squeeze, and TalkEsport’s investigation into the RAM price lawsuit explains why they have climbed so far.
Ronald’s answer is neural rendering, which he described as “an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that”. He also played down the usual spec-sheet race, saying the next generation is not defined by “8K, or 240 hertz”, but by gameplay innovation and new kinds of games. He expects “more innovation over the next three to five years” than in the previous decade.
Xbox has still not announced a price, and the cost question has followed Helix for months. A report last month suggested the Project Helix price could reach $1,800, and earlier reporting claimed Xbox may skip a disc drive. Neither claim has been confirmed by Microsoft, and the magazine does not mention a price or a release date.
Alpha kits arrive in 2027, and Xbox One is the lesson Ronald keeps returning to
The hardware details Xbox has confirmed still come from March. At GDC, Ronald said Helix uses a custom AMD system-on-chip co-designed for the next generation of DirectX and FSR, with “an order of magnitude leap” in ray tracing, according to Xbox’s GDC post. Xbox plans to ship alpha versions of the hardware to developers beginning in 2027.
Ronald also used the magazine to name the generation Xbox does not want to repeat. “With Xbox One, I think we got so focused on expanding our aperture that we lost sight of what truly is magical,” he said, describing that as players, developers and the games they love. He said the first next-generation conversations were held with Xbox’s own studios, before the team travelled to meet developers and players around the world.
The anniversary has come with hardware for the current generation too. Xbox is selling the Series X25 Limited Edition in translucent green, colour-matched to one of the original Xbox’s best-loved colourways. Only 25,000 of those consoles are being sold, and each one is individually numbered.
The post Project Helix Is ‘Not a PC’, Xbox Says, and the Component Crisis Is Now Shaping the Next Xbox appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Mass Effect Fans Send Protest Cupcakes To EA In Tribute To Movement That Successfully Altered Mass Effect 3 Ending
Samsung, SK hynix, and Micron Fail to Get DRAM Antitrust Suit Dismissed
Lawsuit citing ‘Hawks Flying in Formation’ against Samsung, SK hynix and Micron on RAM cartel, accepted
items.content:
A federal judge in California has ruled that a lawsuit accusing Samsung, SK hynix and Micron of conspiring to starve the world of ordinary RAM can go ahead. On 14 November, US District Judge Noël Wise denied the three companies’ joint motion to dismiss Garciaguirre v. Samsung Electronics, a proposed class action filed in the Northern District of California in June.
The complaint claims the three, which together took more than 91% of global DRAM revenue, coordinated production cuts and then used the AI boom as cover to keep conventional memory scarce. None of it has been proven, and the companies say they acted independently.
The ruling matters well beyond one courtroom in San Jose. Memory is the common thread in almost every bad price story gamers have read this year, from the cancelled 24GB RTX 5080 to Radeon supply cuts in China and Valve’s $879 Steam Machine. According to the complaint, conventional DRAM contract prices rose 171.8% in the year to the third quarter of 2025, then climbed about 50% in the fourth quarter and 95% in the first quarter of 2026. If the plaintiffs are right, at least part of that increase was manufactured rather than inevitable.
The case was filed on 25 June by 17 plaintiffs, 14 individuals and three small PC businesses from five states, represented by the antitrust firm Bathaee Dunne. They sue as indirect purchasers, meaning people who bought products containing DRAM rather than the chips themselves, and SK hynix’s own US share prospectus describes the suit in exactly those terms. The claims rest on Section 1 of the Sherman Act and a range of state antitrust and consumer protection laws. The plaintiffs want an injunction, treble damages and a court order ending what they call an engineered shortage.
So how do you cut RAM supply without switching a single machine off?
Nobody in this case is accused of padlocking a factory. DRAM supply is set months in advance by wafer starts, the number of silicon wafers fed into a fab each month. Trimming them by a few per cent only shows up as fewer chips much later. Speed of migration is the second dial, because every move to a denser process packs more bits onto each wafer. Slow that migration or delay a new fab, and bit growth stalls without any announcement that sounds like a cut.
The third dial is the one at the heart of this case. Every DRAM wafer can become high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for AI accelerators, DDR5 for servers and PCs, LPDDR for phones, GDDR6 or GDDR7 for graphics cards and consoles, or older DDR4. HBM is far hungrier for wafers than any of the others. Micron said in its June 2024 earnings remarks that HBM3E consumes approximately three times the wafer supply of DDR5 for the same number of bits. It added that the HBM ramp “will constrain industry supply growth in non-HBM products”.
That is why a memory maker can run its fabs flat out and still ship far fewer gigabytes of the memory you actually buy. Micron told investors in September 2024 that its rising HBM mix “is reducing DRAM supply allocated to traditional products”. The fourth dial is allocation, deciding which customers get chips under long-term contracts and which are left to the spot market. According to the complaint, all three companies began vetting customers in January 2026, with one industry executive quoted as saying they “asked us about who we will supply to”.
Pricing works on two speeds, which is why allocation matters so much. Most DRAM is sold at quarterly contract prices negotiated with big buyers such as PC makers, phone brands and cloud companies, while a smaller spot market serves module makers and resellers. When supply tightens, spot prices react first and hardest, and they reach DIY builders through retail RAM kits within weeks. Contract prices follow as deals are renegotiated, which is how console makers and laptop brands feel it, and why almost nobody in this lawsuit bought a DRAM chip on its own.
Memory has always been cyclical, which is what makes the timeline so contested. Prices were falling hard in late 2022 after the pandemic buying spree, and the complaint alleges the three makers coordinated production cuts between 26 October 2022 and 7 April 2023. It then points to the shift towards HBM from March 2023, a joint wind-down of DDR4 and DDR3 in 2024 and 2025, and a refusal to expand conventional capacity even at record prices. Micron also announced on 3 December 2025 that it would leave the Crucial consumer business, saying it wanted to improve supply for “larger, strategic customers in faster-growing segments”.
For gamers, every one of those dials ends up in a price tag. Graphics cards ship with GDDR memory bought alongside the GPU, so Nvidia’s 3GB GDDR7 modules costing about three times the 2GB parts helped kill that 24GB card. Consoles depend on the same DRAM industry, and Microsoft pointed to memory costs when it raised Xbox prices in June. Those pressures also sit behind questions over whether RAM shortages could affect the PS6, and behind analysts’ doubts that even GTA 6 can lift console sales while hardware keeps getting dearer.
Is this a cartel, or just three giants reading the same market?
Under US antitrust law, competitors acting in parallel is not illegal on its own. In a market with only three serious players, each can watch the others and cut output without ever agreeing to anything, which lawyers call conscious parallelism. To get past a motion to dismiss, plaintiffs must point to extra “plus factors” that make an actual agreement plausible, and the judge has to assume their allegations are true. That is a low bar compared with what comes later, but it is the bar the last DRAM case failed to clear.
Judge Wise found that this complaint clears it, according to legal reporting on the order. She said Samsung’s lag of about four and a half months behind its rivals did not defeat the parallel conduct claim, and that the HBM pivot on its own might not be enough. The customer vetting allegations, however, strongly supported a plausible inference of an agreement, in her view, partly because they came after the HBM shift had already begun. Taken together, she said the conduct looked “more akin to hawks flying in formation” than rivals simply watching one another.
The ruling was not a clean sweep for the plaintiffs. The judge gave no weight to investors’ talk of “supply discipline”, even though Micron has used that exact language, telling investors it “will continue to exercise supply and capex discipline”. She also set aside meetings at trade conferences and treated the three-firm market structure as neutral. The companies argued in their joint motion that they independently reduced production amid falling prices and then followed AI demand, and Samsung has called the allegations unfounded.
The industry’s history cuts both ways for the three defendants. Between 2004 and 2006, the US Justice Department collected about $731 million in criminal fines over a real DRAM cartel that ran from April 2001 to June 2002, according to its own account. Samsung paid $300 million, Hynix $185 million, Infineon $160 million and Elpida $84 million, executives went to prison, and Micron avoided a fine by cooperating. Yet a 2018 class action alleging output cuts was dismissed, and in March 2022 the Ninth Circuit agreed it showed “nothing more than conscious parallelism”.
That earlier defeat is why Judge Wise’s line about the old case matters. The companies argued that this suit simply repeats the old one. She rejected that argument, writing that “The Court finds that it is not”. The honest reading is that this case is now plausible and dangerous for the companies, but nowhere near proven, and AI demand is a real explanation they will press hard in discovery. China’s market regulator also opened its own probe into the same three companies in 2018.
The next stage is where cases like this are usually won or lost. Discovery will give the plaintiffs access to internal production plans, emails and meeting notes, which is the kind of evidence a court needs to see an actual agreement rather than parallel moves. They will also have to win class certification, which means showing that buyers of very different products suffered a common overcharge. Even if they manage both, antitrust cases of this size usually take years, and many settle before they ever reach a jury.
Slowed iPhones and a 3.5GB graphics card: why buyers stopped taking hardware makers at their word
Many readers will connect this case with a different kind of limiting, where products are held back after you buy them. That is not what the DRAM suit alleges, since it is about supply and prices, not software. The two do share something important, however, which is a long record of buyers being told a performance or price problem was natural, and later learning otherwise.
The best-known example remains Apple’s iPhone battery throttling scandal. Apple used iOS updates to slow older iPhones with worn batteries, which it presented as power management, and in November 2020 it agreed to pay $113 million to 34 US states. It also settled a US class action for up to $500 million, and France fined it €25 million earlier that year for failing to tell users. Italy’s competition authority had already fined Apple €10 million and Samsung €5 million in 2018 over updates that slowed older phones.
Samsung faced a fresh row in 2022, when its Game Optimizing Service was found to throttle thousands of apps and games while leaving benchmark apps alone. Geekbench delisted four generations of Galaxy S phones, and Samsung apologised and shipped an update that let users switch the limiter off. In graphics, Nvidia settled a class action in 2016 over the GTX 970, sold as a 4GB card although its last 0.5GB ran on a much slower segment, paying owners $30 each.
Each of those cases ended with regulators or courts forcing companies to disclose what they had done or to pay buyers back. The DRAM suit is years away from that point, if it ever gets there. The three companies must file their answers by 7 December, and the first case management conference is set for 12 January 2027.

items.title: US Treasury Secretary Bessent Says “Nvidia needs a dramatic shakeup” and an outside CEO as Musk pushes for Jensen Huang’s return
items.content:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has said Nvidia needs “a dramatic shakeup” in its leadership and should look outside the company for its next chief executive. Speaking on Fox News’s Sunday Morning Futures, he questioned whether Nvidia had pushed “seemingly illicit sales” of AI chips to boost its revenue. He also said he wanted answers from the board and its outside counsel within 10 days. His intervention puts the government at odds with a growing campaign, led by Elon Musk and Ruby on Rails creator David Heinemeier Hansson, to bring Jensen Huang back. Nvidia has not publicly responded to Bessent’s remarks.
Huang resigned as president and chief executive on 12 November, and chief financial officer Colette Kress is running the company on an interim basis, according to Nvidia’s announcement. The board has said it is choosing a search firm and has not formally approached any candidates. Kress now faces her first earnings call as interim chief executive on Tuesday, with Washington, investors and some of the most prominent figures in tech pulling the board in opposite directions.
Bessent says the question is Nvidia’s culture, not Huang’s private life
Bessent made clear that the scandal around Huang’s relationships was not his main concern. “It doesn’t matter to me whether she is a spy or not,” he said of Alice Huang, the former Megaspeed executive at the centre of the affair. Instead, he said he kept coming back to “what was the culture at Nvidia” and whether the company had pressed questionable sales “to goose their revenues and their earnings”. He also wants to know whether Nvidia missed warning signs about shell companies, many of them based in Singapore, that moved chips to China.
He compared Nvidia’s position with that of a bank in a compliance scandal, where he said several executives would be removed rather than one. “Jensen Huang is an incredible innovator,” Bessent said. “But that does not abrogate their duties of compliance,” he added. In his view, any problem runs deeper than a single chief executive, which is why he believes the board should hire from outside.
His comments build on a week of damaging reports. The Wall Street Journal reported that Megaspeed arranged nearly $12 billion worth of advanced chips for Chinese companies, and US lawmakers are now advancing bills to tighten AI chip exports. Reuters reported that Huang told Nvidia’s general counsel his dealings with Alice Huang and Megaspeed were standard business. Megaspeed denies diverting chips to China, and Nvidia has said it complies with US export law.
Musk and Hansson lead the push to put Huang back in charge
On the other side, some of the best-known names in tech want Huang reinstated. Musk said on Thursday that a petition to reinstate Huang was under way and that he was signing it, and the Stand with Jensen petition has since circulated widely. A day later, he argued that many of Nvidia’s supply deals were “a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract”, and that some of them would be lost without him. Musk has already said hiring Huang himself “would be an honour”.
Hansson, the Danish programmer behind Ruby on Rails and a co-founder of 37signals, went further on Sunday. He wrote on his X account that “we need @JensenHuang back at NVIDIA”, because “the free world depends on it”. Inside the company, 88% of Nvidia staff who answered a Blind survey before his resignation said he should stay.
Nvidia’s investors are split on the question as well. Altimeter Capital’s Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management’s Gavin Baker have asked the board to keep Huang’s return on the table and avoid a rushed replacement, which is close to the opposite of Bessent’s advice. Their funds hold a small fraction of Nvidia’s shares, however, and only the board can appoint a chief executive.
Nvidia’s board now has a Treasury deadline and Tuesday’s results to manage
The board is also running its own investigation into Huang’s conduct, led by Wachtell Lipton and former federal prosecutor Joon Kim, according to its statement. That review has not reported, and the board has not said whether it will cover the chip sales Bessent raised. Separately, filings show director Mark Stevens sold about $946 million of shares in August and September, before the scandal broke.
Nvidia reports its third-quarter results on Tuesday, 17 November, and the call will be its first since Huang left. Kress has said her focus as interim chief executive is on customers, partners and shareholders. Bessent’s 10-day window for answers from the board runs to around 25 November.
The post US Treasury Secretary Bessent Says “Nvidia needs a dramatic shakeup” and an outside CEO as Musk pushes for Jensen Huang’s return appeared first on TalkEsport.

Jowi Morales is a writer and journalist covering the tech beat since 2021. However, he’s been interested in technology far earlier than that. He started discovering desktop computers when his father brought home a Windows 95 PC, but his first real experience working under the hood of the PC was when the old computer’s hard drive was filled to the brim in the year 2000. He deleted the Windows folder to attempt to rectify the situation, which led to his dad buying a new desktop PC. Since then, he learned a lot more about computers, and he’s always been the go-to tech expert for his family and friends.

Jowi primarily uses a Windows workstation and an Android phone, but he also bought into the Apple ecosystem with the 6th-gen iPad, iPhone 14 Pro Max, and the M1 MacBook Air. Today, Jowi covers hardware and software from Redmond and Cupertino, while also looking at the tech industry in general.

Aside from covering technology, Jowi is an avid photographer and writes about automobiles, aviation, and tanks. You can find his bylines at MakeUseOf, SlashGear, and, of course, Tom’s Hardware.

items.title: XBOX 25th Anniversary Magazine: Explore 25 Years of Games, Stories, and Memories
items.content:
The 25th Anniversary of XBOX has given fans much to celebrate: the milestones, the memories, and a whole slate of fun news for our players.
We know that many of our longtime fans first learned about the original XBOX by reading about it in a magazine back in the day. For you, we created XBOX – The 25th Anniversary Magazine, a special publication designed not only to look back at 25 years of play, but also to celebrate the present and future of XBOX. We printed copies to share with community members at XBOX FanFest in Seattle this past week, and today, it’s available for all to read right here:
Protip: you can go full screen for easier reading by clicking the arrows in the lower right of the player.
The magazine explores games, hardware, and moments, past and present, told through the teams who are building them. You’ll revisit memories from your favorite franchises, learn some lore about XBOX’s storied history, and read new details about games that haven’t yet released; want to know more about Fable’s capital city of Bowerstone? Turn to page 38!
We hope you enjoy this decidedly analog celebration of the last quarter century and a first look at what’s ahead. XBOX’s story has always been written alongside our players. Thanks for reading, and for being part of what comes next.

Mark's enthusiasm for computers dampened at an early age by the rubber-keyed Sinclair Spectrum 48K and feelings of Commodore 64 envy. However, in the mid-80s, hope in a digital future was rekindled by the purchase of an Atari 520 STe. Since that time Mark has used a multitude of computers for fun and professional endeavors. He often owned both Macs and PCs but went cold on the former after OS9 was killed off, and warmed to the latter with the introduction of Windows XP.

Early work years were spent in artwork and reprographics but in the late noughties, Mark started to blog about computers, Taiwanese food culture, and guitar design. This activity led to a full-time position writing about breaking PC tech news for HEXUS, for the best part of a decade. When HEXUS was abruptly closed, Mark helped with the foundation of Club386, before finding a new home at Tom's Hardware.

When not wearing through the keycap legends on his PC keyboards, Mark can be found wandering the computer malls of Taiwan's neon-lit conurbations and enjoying local and international cuisine.

He quickly realized he had more fun figuring out how computers work than he did actually using the things. Kicking off a developer career with C and Assembly before moving to scripting languages, he's worn many hats, including both database architect and systems administration. As a teen, Bruno co-founded a web development outfit where he was for 17 years before moving on to spend nearly a decade at The Tech Report as a writer, editor, and (of course) developer. In this decade, he's been at Asus, MLCommons, and HotHardware, among others. When not fiddling with computers and games, his love for music and production sends him off to live shows and festivals. items.title: Bilibili Gaming are your 2026 World Champions after defeating all four LCK teams
items.content:
Bilibili Gaming took down Gen.G Esports in the League of Legends 2026 World Championship Grand Final, 3-1, successfully bringing back the Summoner’s Cup to the LPL since 2021. BLG also beat all four LCK representatives on their path to the championship.
The BLG roster that won Worlds 2026 are:
Top: Chen “Bin” Zebin
Jungle: Peng “Xun” Lixun
Mid: Zhuo “Knight” Ding
Bottom: Park “Viper” Do-hyeon
Support: Luo “ON” Wenjun
Top (Sub): Li “Flandre” Xuanjun (did not play)
Head Coach: Yang “Daeny” Dae-in
Check out the champions each BLG player can pick a skin for here.
Bilibili Gaming: The LCK slayers
Worlds 2026 marked BLG’s return to the Grand Final stage after a failed attempt versus T1 in 2024.
BLG and the rest of the LPL representatives did not have a good start to this year’s Worlds. BLG debuted their journey with a loss to Movistar KOI, and all the other LPL teams lost their opening matches as well.
They picked up the pace afterwards with best-of-one wins over Team Liquid and Karmine Corp sending them to qualification point. BLG then dropped a match against fellow LPL team Top Esports, causing them to go 2-2 and into the final round of Swiss.
BLG had a challenging path to the trophy. (Image credit: Stefan Wisnoski/Riot Games)
Here is where they faced their first LCK adversary: Hanwha Life Gaming. A clean, 2-0 sweep by BLG eliminated HLE, denying one of the tournament favorites a ticket to Knockouts.
Then, in the Quarterfinals, BLG also swept Dplus 3-0, marking the second LCK team they have beat and eliminated in a row. Next came T1 in the semifinals, where BLG broke hearts and denied them a chance to defend their title in the grand final.
Finally, the grand final against Gen.G makes four LCK teams in a row for BLG. And they like those odds.
BLG, THE LCK SLAYERS pic.twitter.com/w1UZ12vcvb
— LoL Esports (@lolesports) November 15, 2026
Finals MVP: Knight
Knight was awarded the Finals MVP award. He had an average KDA of 9.0 (13/6/41) across all four games – the highest amongst the ten players.
He is also the first non-Korean mid-laner to win Worlds since 2012 when Kurtis “Toyz” Lau won with Taipei Assassins.
Even during the years that an LPL team won, they all had imported Korean imports in the mid-lane:
Invictus Gaming (2018) – Lee “Scout” Ye-chan
FunPlus Phoenix (2019) – Kim “Doinb” Tae-sang
EDward Gaming (2021) – Scout
Worlds 2026 Final: BLG vs. Gen.G
When the grand final slate got finalized, fans and analysts alike were in agreement that the matchup was in favor of Gen.G Esports, albeit only slightly.
Predictions are in ✍️ #Worlds2026 pic.twitter.com/NRnz7r7bIV
— LoL Esports (@lolesports) November 14, 2026
Thus, when the LCK team took game one straight out of BLG’s hands, nobody was surprised. Gen.G’s late-game became too much for BLG to handle – the lead and pressure they had in the early game were not enough to tide them in the latter minutes of the game.
GEN JUST CANNOT LOSE A FIGHT AT ELDER pic.twitter.com/ibyRLtfpoC
— LoL Esports (@lolesports) November 14, 2026
The second game was the opposite, it looked like Gen.G had perfect control over the early game, especially with flashy plays and precise clicks coming from Park “Ruler” Jae-hyuk’s Ezreal.
CLEAN. https://t.co/dFa02Ch709 pic.twitter.com/ZfqU2hdPbD
— LoL Esports (@lolesports) November 14, 2026
However, Viper’s Ziggs scaled incredibly well, and set a record for the second-most damage per minute (DPM) dealt in a single Worlds game: 1776.
5 DPM. 🤏
That's all Viper was missing to erase Sneaky from the record books
1776 DPM in 53 minutes vs Gen.G: the 2nd best performance in Worlds history, a hair away from a 9-year-old record#Worlds2026 #BLGWIN pic.twitter.com/mAGWvyzKJB
— Monsieur Yordle 📊 (@MonsieurYordle) November 15, 2026
The record is still held by Zachary “Sneaky” Scuderi, set nine years ago.
Game 3 showed another draft masterclass from BLG coach Daeny, granting Viper another mage bot in Taliyah, paired with ON’s Alistar. This would turn out to be crucial to the game, especially as ON was instrumental in catching out Gen.G’s players off-guard.
MASSIVE FIGHT FOR BLG! pic.twitter.com/BFd4bsrJP7
— LoL Esports (@lolesports) November 14, 2026
Finally, game four closed out the series with Bin’s Gwen at the helm, despite combined efforts from Jeong “Chovy” Ji-hoon’s Akali and Ruler’s Xayah to make the game playable for their team.
ON FINDS THE POP BLOSSOM pic.twitter.com/KFDBG14tGK
— LoL Esports (@lolesports) November 14, 2026
League of Legends esports will resume in early 2027 with First Stand: All In, which Riot calls the biggest international event it has ever organized. League of Legends: New Dawn was also announced during the grand final weekend.
