Great news! Nier: Automata's install size is no longer 7x bigger than it should be (it was 366 GB)
Remember Nier: Automata’s 365GB patch? It’s fixed now
items.content:
Last week, Nier: Automata players were left scratching their heads after a Steam update appeared to inflate the game's storage requirements to more than 365GB. Fortunately, Square Enix has now resolved the issue.
As we reported previously, what should have been a routine update instead prompted reports from players claiming that Nier: Automata suddenly required hundreds of gigabytes of free space to install. At the time, Square Enix acknowledged the problem and began investigating, while advising affected users to temporarily disable the game's DLC if they needed to reinstall.
In a new statement posted to X, the official NieR account said: “We have identified the cause and now resolved this issue.” The team also apologised for any inconvenience caused.
Unfortunately, no further details were provided, so we still don't know exactly how an update for a 50GB game briefly ended up demanding more than 365GB of free storage. Still, if you've been holding off on reinstalling Nier: Automata while waiting for a fix, you should now be safe to jump back in.
KitGuru says: Have you ever seen a patch go quite this wrong before?

items.title: Epic Games Launcher will support SteamOS
items.content:
Epic Games has confirmed that its new native Linux launcher will support SteamOS, alongside distributions such as Fedora, Cachy and Omarchy.
While the client is currently in preview for Debian and Ubuntu, Epic communications director Jake Jones confirmed to GamingOnLinux (via VideoCardz) that the company plans to support as many Linux distributions as possible, including gaming-focused platforms such as SteamOS.
Epic is still evaluating how it will distribute the launcher across different Linux platforms. The current preview is available as a .deb package, but the company says it is testing additional packaging formats and plans to restore AppImage downloads later this month.
For Steam Deck owners, native support gives users an official way to access their Epic Games library without relying on third-party tools like Heroic Games Launcher. However, Epic has yet to confirm how the launcher will integrate with SteamOS Game Mode or whether any handheld-specific interface is planned.
SteamOS support also doesn't mean Fortnite will immediately become playable on Steam Deck. Epic previously confirmed that Fortnite's Linux release depends on the arrival of Easy Anti-Cheat Linux v2, with additional platform requirements still needing to be addressed. The company has previously said the Steam Deck does not currently meet all of those requirements, although discussions with Valve are ongoing.
KitGuru says: Steam Deck owners have been relying on unofficial solutions for years, so official support is certainly welcome. Would you switch from Heroic to Epic's own launcher?

Practice Makes Precise: At CoRL, NVIDIA and Partners Reveal How Robots Rehearse Delicate Work in Simulation
items.content:
Simulation, which has long been the proving ground for robots learning to walk, roll and hop, is now helping researchers teach robots tasks that require a finer touch: aligning gears, connecting cables and assembling small components.
The shift from locomotion to manipulation is taking center stage at this week’s Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) in Austin, Texas, alongside the rise of agentic robotics — a new paradigm that integrates frontier agents to create interpretable code for physical robotics systems.
At CoRL, NVIDIA is introducing new open robotics technologies, including world action models, simulation tools, benchmarks and agentic workflows.
Two NVIDIA papers are among six finalists out of thousands of submissions for the Best Paper Awards at CoRL:
GRAIL (Generating Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from World Models), which presents a digital generation pipeline for 3D assets and simulator-ready scenes for robot learning.
RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies, which introduces a robot model and training recipe that scales visuomotor context three orders of magnitude beyond state-of-the-art policies without growing inference latency.
These advancements help researchers train robots on complex tasks, evaluate their performance across changing conditions and use failures to guide further learning — building the precision, adaptability and autonomy needed to move from lab demonstrations to industrial deployment.
NVIDIA is working with partners like Ambi Robotics, Bosch Research, Dexmate, Dyna Robotics, FieldAI, Flexion, Noitom Robotics, Siemens, Skild AI, RLWRLD, UC Berkeley, Walden Robotics and the University of Washington to bring these advancements to the broader robotics community.
World Action Models Enable Next Level of Robot Autonomy
The next level of robot autonomy requires robots to perceive their surroundings, anticipate how their actions will change the environment and execute complex, multistep tasks with a high degree of precision. World action models enable exactly that.
At CoRL, NVIDIA is introducing GR00T 2, an open frontier world action model built on NVIDIA Cosmos. Trained on diverse robot and human data, including 100,000 hours of NVIDIA open source human egocentric data, the model enables robots to learn dexterous manipulation skills. Key features include:
Out-of-the-box performance: Completed 40 of 50 evaluated tasks at least once without task-specific demonstrations.
Skill transfer: Learns from human demonstrations and transfers skills between different robot bodies without robot demonstrations
Generalization with little data: Achieved 71% average success across 50 tasks with just one demonstration per task, increasing to 95% with five.
Agent control: AI agents can use GR00T 2’s application programming interface and supporting tools to run skills in sequence and recover from errors.
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/groot-2-shipping-label.mp4
GR00T 2 currently ranks among the top three models across all vision language action and world action model categories for the RoboCasa365, RoboLab, RoboDojo and MolmoSpaces benchmarks, with multiple leaderboard wins.
Nexuni is testing it for robotic laundry handling, Foxconn is applying GR00T 2 to factory automation for server manufacturing and Siemens is evaluating it across industrial use cases.
MicroAGI is using GR00T 2, post-trained through reinforcement learning, to perform Ethernet cable swapping with a YAM robotic arm. Its agentic robotics approach automates the creation and calibration of simulation environments using Isaac Lab 3.0 and Newton, where the policy is trained. The agentic robotics workflow will be demonstrated at CoRL.
Training capable robots requires diverse data. Open NVIDIA workflows and models equip researchers with better tools for data collection and annotation:
For researchers building robot-training datasets, NVIDIA’s new open Video to Data workflow turns human video into simulated robot demonstrations, with a challenge inviting researchers to advance it.
The NVIDIA EgoHand open model — being demoed at CoRL and with over 40,000 Hugging Face downloads in the two weeks since launch — reconstructs 3D hand motion, trained with data from Noitom Robotics.
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/egohand-demo.mp4
Where the Training and Scaling Happens — in Simulation
A pretrained model gives robots a core set of skills. Simulation lets researchers train, refine and evaluate skills at scale before deploying them on physical robots.
NVIDIA Isaac Lab, an open source robot-learning framework, provides the foundation for that work. Its latest release, Isaac Lab 3.0, allows researchers to use agents to quickly set up training environments with simulation-ready assets, switch between NVIDIA PhysX and Newton physics solvers, choose renderers for perception-based training and apply a new reinforcement post-training library to foundation models like GR00T.
Accurate physics is critical to transferring learned skills from simulation to the real robot. Tighter integration with Newton, an open source physics engine, now allows Isaac Lab to model deformable objects such as cables and cloth, along with complex articulated systems such as robotic hands with many interacting joints.
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/newton-strawberry.mp4
Integration with Newton simulates how a strawberry deforms under a robot’s grip.
Together, Isaac Lab and Newton combine accurate physics with scale to enable researchers to train thousands of simulated robots in parallel. In a vision-based dexterous manipulation benchmark, Isaac Lab 3.0 with Newton achieved up to 2.5x the training throughput of Isaac Lab 2.3 with PhysX.
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/newton-physx-web.mp4
Isaac Lab supports robot simulation with Newton and NVIDIA PhysX.
Developers are extending Newton’s capabilities. At CoRL, Skild AI announced Scalable Throughput-optimized Engine for Embodied Learning, or STEEL, a new rigid-body physics solver built on Newton to accelerate robot training with Isaac Lab.
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/robotics-montage-8s.mp4
Skild AI’s STEEL Solver.
Flexion showcased how Isaac Lab and Newton help train Reflect, its robot-intelligence model combining reasoning and whole-body manipulation.
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/flexion-newton-isaac-lab.mp4
Flexion uses Newton for RL with Isaac Lab.
FieldAI is using Newton — as well as Isaac Lab and Isaac Sim, built on NVIDIA Omniverse libraries — to train and validate robot policies for deployment in unstructured real-world environments. Dyna Robotics will demonstrate how parallel simulation in Isaac Lab helps train whole-body controllers for its semi-humanoid Taku robot for work in warehouses, hotels and food services.
Walden Robotics is using Isaac Sim’s photorealistic rendering to train and evaluate its general-purpose robot in virtual environments for manufacturing and logistics, while Dexmate is exploring how coding agents can rehearse and refine manipulation strategies in Isaac Sim before executing them on its Vega robot.
AlphaNIST, built in Isaac Lab, demonstrates how efficient practice can translate into precision. A single policy learns all 20 tasks on the NIST Assembly Task Board, manipulating millimeter-scale parts using only a yes-or-no success signal. It achieves more than 98% training success, compared with 81% for separate per-task policies, using roughly 39x less GPU time.
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/alphanist-6-16s-web.mp4
AlphaNIST uses Isaac Lab to train a single robot policy across 20 precision tasks on the NIST Assembly Task Board.
Behind those results is Success-Guided Sampling, or SGS, from the University of Washington and NVIDIA. The method focuses practice on tasks a policy succeeds at about half the time, directing training toward skills it’s still learning. With SGS, robot training can scale beyond a million parallel environments.
The University of Texas at Austin’s School of Computing and Texas Robotics uses Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab to train robotic skills in simulation, letting students start developing before physical hardware is available.
New Industrial Benchmarks for Robot Evaluation
Learning a skill is one challenge. Performing it reliably across changing conditions is another.
NVIDIA Isaac Lab-Arena, an open source framework for scaled policy evaluation, enables developers to compose diverse and repeatable evaluations, then run policies across thousands of variations in parallel. Analyses expose which conditions cause failures, so researchers know what to fix in their next training run. The developer preview of its latest version, 0.4, is arriving at CoRL.
DexBench and VABAR, two new open benchmarks, are among the first designed to measure robot dexterity and adaptability across industrial tasks using Isaac Lab-Arena and Newton.
DexBench, developed by RLWRLD in collaboration with NVIDIA, takes dexterity evaluation off the tabletop and into real-world workflows. Built using NVIDIA Isaac Lab-Arena, it features 15 tasks across four scenes spanning retail, logistics, manufacturing and hospitality, testing generalization across object, spatial and physics variations.
Genesis AI, mimic robotics and other industry partners are evaluating DexBench through early access.
Teams can run DexBench on Manifold, Bifrost’s evaluation platform for scaling robotics simulations, with no setup required, built-in failure analysis and free credits for initial evaluations.
VABAR — the Variational Automation Benchmark for Agentic Robotics — from UC Berkeley and NVIDIA, evaluates robots across six industrial tasks. Each carries standardized variations, difficulty tiers and success metrics.
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/task-tool-sorting.mp4
A simulated tool-sorting task demonstrates how VABAR evaluates robot manipulation skills for industrial workflows.
Agents Turn Skills Into Robot Programs
Successful task completion requires robots to coordinate multiple skills and adapt when something goes wrong. Building reliable programs for these multistep tasks remains a challenge.
Agentic robotics helps solve that challenge.
UC Berkeley’s new Graph-as-Policy (GaP) framework uses agents to connect individual skills into robot programs. Agents test these programs using NVIDIA Isaac open simulation technologies and refine them based on failures. This helps researchers scale development with less data while keeping the programs interpretable for engineers to review and verify before deployment.
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/wipe-the-bar.mp4
GaP uses agents and simulation to turn individual robot skills into coordinated actions, such as wiping a bar.
“To me, agentic robotics is the most exciting technological development since the internet in 1995,” said Ken Goldberg, professor of robotics at UC Berkeley and a lead on the VABAR and GaP projects.
Ambi Robotics is exploring GaP for industrial automation.
Ambi Robotics, Bosch Research and Siemens are all exploring GaP for its agentic robotics workflows across diverse industrial scenarios.
Learn more by joining NVIDIA at CoRL.

Death Stranding duology celebrates 7th anniversary with 28 million total players
items.content:
First released back in 2019 as a PlayStation exclusive, Hideo Kojima’s Death Stranding remains one of the more unique and niche AAA experiences out there, with the open-world ‘walking simulator’ proving to be a bit of a love-it-or-hate-it type of experience. Even so, in the 7 years since the first game’s arrival, Death Stranding has found a substantial audience, with Kojima Productions now revealing that the franchise has surpassed a total of 28 million players.
Taking to social media to celebrate the franchise’s 7th anniversary, Hideo Kojima revealed that in the “7 years since BB was born” Death Stranding and its sequel have amassed a total of “28 million porters worldwide.”
Of course, 28 million players does not equate to 28 million copies sold, with Kojima Productions themselves making sure to note that this figure “includes all console versions, PC versions, and free access as part of various subscription services.”
While DS2: On the Beach has yet to join any such subscriptions, the original Death Stranding has found its way onto a range of different services including PlayStation Plus, Xbox Game Pass and was even made available for free via the Epic Games Store for a limited time.
In terms of concrete sales, we have relatively little to go on, with the last official figure being announced all the way back in early 2021, when it was revealed that Death Stranding 1 had sold a total of 5 million copies across PS4 and PC.
Regardless, for a series as weird and unconventional as Death Stranding, amassing almost 30 million players in any capacity is an achievement worthy of celebration. It will be interesting to see whether the upcoming Death Stranding Isolations anime manages to bring in new players when it premieres next year.

items.content:
It’s not often that we see current-gen exclusives being back-ported to last-gen consoles months or even years after-the-fact, with some of the few examples being Star Wars Jedi: Survivor and Marvel Rivals. In a surprise move, it appears as though the first-party PS5-exclusive God of War: Sons of Sparta will be coming to PlayStation 4 sooner or later – with a PS4 version having now been added to Sony’s back-end servers.
As reported by reputable Twitter user ‘PlayStation Game Size’, it appears as though the PlayStation 5 exclusive God of War spin-off ‘Sons of Sparta’ is coming to PS4 at some point in the near future; with a last-gen version popping up on Sony’s backend PSN servers.
Released back in February of this year, Sons of Sparta was a surprise 2D metroidvania spin-off developed by Mega Cat Studios and Sony Santa Monica. While a welcome addition to the God of War canon, the game was met with a mixed reception owing to its relatively generic position within the greater metroidvania genre.
That said, for those less familiar with the genre in general, Sons of Sparta offered a solid experience overall, and so its perhaps makes sense that Sony would want to try to squeeze as many sales from the game as possible – especially as the title would have no issues running on last-gen hardware owing to its 2D pixel-art aesthetic.
Considering Sons of Sparta failed to make a splash on the sales charts back when it first launched, it is unlikely that a PS4 version would do much to change this fact. That said, for a port which is likely to be relatively cheap to develop, any extra eyes on this project would certainly be welcome.

Nvidia probes intelligence allegations linked to CEO
items.content:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is facing uncomfortable questions after a New York Times report claimed US intelligence agencies believed a Chinese businesswoman he had a relationship with was acting on behalf of Beijing. However, the report stops well short of accusing Huang himself of wrongdoing, and many of the key details remain unverified publicly.
According to a New York Times investigation, US intelligence agencies concluded that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang was working on behalf of Beijing. The report also claims surveillance uncovered a close personal relationship between Huang and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, prompting concerns among some US officials because of Nvidia's position in the AI and semiconductor industries.
Since then, the BBC reports that Nvidia's board has launched an independent investigation. Jensen Huang has admitted to being unfaithful and apologised to his wife and family, while Nvidia said it currently has no reason to believe company secrets or US national security were compromised. So far, no public evidence has emerged showing that Huang knowingly shared sensitive information or was aware of any alleged intelligence activity.
What remains unclear is Alice Huang's role in the story. While US intelligence agencies reportedly concluded she was acting on Beijing's behalf, the evidence behind that assessment has not been made public. It is also unclear whether any alleged intelligence work began before her relationship with Jensen Huang, overlapped with it, or developed afterwards. China has rejected the allegations, describing them as groundless.
The timing is noteworthy because concerns around espionage within the technology sector have been growing. Recent reporting, including The Telegraph's coverage of Silicon Valley spying concerns, has shown that executives working in AI, semiconductors and other strategically important industries may increasingly become targets for intelligence-gathering efforts.

items.title: Cancelled Dark Outlaw Games project was inspired by DOOM and COD Zombies
items.content:
Ever since his departure from Treyarch, Call of Duty Zombies veteran Jason Blundell has struggled to get a project out of the door, with studios Deviation Games and Dark Outlaw Games eventually being shut down before either could produce a complete product. With Blundell now working at the newly-built Magic Fractal, details on Dark Outlaw’s cancelled project have now been shared.
Back in March, just one year on from the studio’s official announcement, the Sony-aligned Dark Outlaw Games was shut down before the team could unveil what they were working on. According to a new report by YouTuber Glitching Queen (and expanded upon by known insider Tom Henderson via Insider-Gaming), Dark Outlaw Games was developing a gory first-person shooter which was said to be “heavily inspired by the DOOM series” – particularly DOOM Eternal’s gameplay and level-design.
Being headed by Jason Blundell, the game (said to have been known internally as project ‘Ignite’) also took plenty of inspiration from Call of Duty Zombies, with Henderson claiming that alongside its single-player / co-op campaign mode, the game would also feature “a Call of Duty Zombies-esque horde mode, plenty of Easter Eggs, mini games, and more.”
While the studio itself never showed off any of its progress before being shut down, Henderson claimed to have been privy to “gigabytes of screenshots, footage, and documents about Dark Outlaw Games’ title since the project was canceled” suggesting that work was proceeding rather rapidly.
In terms of the reason for its cancellation, Henderson revealed that it had little to do with the quality of the game itself, and was instead a result of “PlayStation executives [reprioritising] its portfolio budget amid ongoing market challenges.”
Nearly 7 years on from Blundell’s departure from Treyarch, the creative has unfortunately yet to release a new project. Given this, here’s to hoping that the recently-established indie studio ‘Magic Fractal’ proves that the 3rd time is indeed a charm.

items.title: Pragmata and Onimusha: Way of the Sword have “exceeded” sales expectations according to Capcom
items.content:
2026 has been a great year for Capcom, with the game developer/publisher having released a new IP, a highly-anticipated sequel; a long-dormant franchise revival and more – all of which appear to be both critical and commercial successes. Mirroring public sentiment, Capcom has now revealed that Pragmata; Onimush: Way of the Sword and the recently-released Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen have all “exceeded” internal sales expectations.
As part of the publisher’s latest Fiscal earnings report, Capcom shared updated sales stats for its games while also hosting its investor Q&A session – offering insight into the company’s mentality behind the games it released over the course of 2026.
When asked specifically regarding how they “evaluate sales of PRAGMATA and Onimusha: Way of the Sword compared with [their] initial expectations” Capcom claimed that: “Both titles are progressing ahead of plan,” noting that “PRAGMATA sold 2.7 million units cumulatively during the first half of the fiscal year, while Onimusha: Way of the Sword, the first new title in the series in 20 years, sold 1.7 million units.”
In a similar vein, Capcom appears to be pleased with the current performance of the recently-released and expanded Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen, stating that “the title has been highly rated by users, while sales are also progressing at a pace slightly ahead of our expectations.”
The one title which Capcom has struggled with somewhat however is 2025’s Monster Hunter Wilds. Despite selling 10 million copies in its first month on market back in February of last year, its sales have since slowed down significantly – even falling behind the likes of MH: World and Rise during recent quarters.
That said, the publisher remains hopeful when it comes to Wilds’ medium-long term, with Capcom stating: “Following the announcements of the Nintendo Switch 2 version and the massive expansion Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance, pricing measures helped improve the pace of sales and increase the number of concurrent players. We will continue rolling out promotional initiatives for Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance as we aim to expand sales over the medium- to long-term.”
Considering the fact that it feels as though the video games industry is collapsing left, right and centre, seeing Capcom continuing to thrive (mostly) off of new and dormant IPs is encouraging at the very least. It will be interesting to see what 2027 has in store.

Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT and NVIDIA hosted the MSIT-NVIDIA AI Startup Partnership Forum at COEX.
Ryu Je-myung, vice minister of science and ICT, joined NVIDIA leaders to meet with over 20 Korean startups across foundation models, physical AI, AI infrastructure and AI semiconductors.
NVIDIA also announced an investment in Korean startup Point2, with additional investments planned in Motif Technologies, RLWRLD and Upstage.
Point2 Technology, an AI interconnect company, builds scalable, radio frequency-based interconnects that move data between chips and racks in AI factories, offering an innovative alternative to conventional copper and optical interconnect solutions for AI cluster scale-up, delivering the reach, performance and efficiency needed for next-generation AI infrastructure.
Motif Technologies, a Seoul-based AI lab, develops foundation models for building AI agents that carry out complex tasks, including Motif-3, a large language model released with open weights.
RLWRLD, a physical AI startup based in San Francisco, Seoul and Tokyo, develops robotics foundation models that enable humanoid and industrial robots to perform complex real-world tasks that require five-finger dexterity, such as precisely inserting components, threading nuts onto bolts and kitting parts from moving conveyors.
Upstage, a Korean enterprise AI company, develops Solar language models and document AI tools that help businesses extract information from complex documents, streamline workflows and build AI applications for everyday operations.
The companies represent work across the full AI stack, from infrastructure to models to robotics applications.
The planned investments build on NVIDIA’s work with Korea’s startup and venture community, including more than 1,000 Korea-based members of NVIDIA Inception, a program that helps startups grow with access to preferred pricing, technical expertise and opportunities for investor introductions.

items.title: Korea Advances Physical AI Across Industries With NVIDIA
items.content:
Tapping into the country’s strengths in manufacturing and engineering, NVIDIA is helping advance Korea’s physical AI ecosystem.
The country’s industry leaders are applying accelerated computing, AI and simulation to everything from semiconductor manufacturing to robotics and autonomous vehicles.
These efforts are helping bring physical AI from development into real-world production.
Samsung Advances Semiconductor Engineering With Accelerated Computing and AI Physics
Samsung Electronics is expanding its collaboration with NVIDIA to advance semiconductor innovation through accelerated computing and AI physics. The work spans materials research, process development and device engineering.
In technology computer-aided design, Samsung is working with NVIDIA cuISS and NVIDIA cuDSS to accelerate computations involving sparse linear systems. The collaboration also extends to GPU acceleration for process and optical simulations. In materials research, Samsung’s sMOL platform has run selected quantum chemical calculations up to 5x faster end to end with NVIDIA cuEST. Samsung is also exploring NVIDIA cuEquivariance to speed up tensor operations used in training and inference for atomistic AI models.
Samsung is developing chip-scale thermal and mechanical analysis workflows with NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo. In one AI homogenization case, combining AI-predicted effective material properties, coarser grids and GPU acceleration resulted in a roughly 1,600x speedup. Simulation time fell from about 18 hours for a fine-grid solve on a 32-core CPU to 41 seconds for a GPU-accelerated coarse-grid solve.
Looking ahead, NVIDIA Agent Toolkit could connect these simulation tools and AI models, helping future engineering agents run analyses and compare design options.
Kakao Mobility Collaborates With NVIDIA to Advance Autonomous Driving Development
Kakao Mobility plans to build on NVIDIA’s autonomous vehicle computing and safety technologies to advance development of a level 4 autonomous driving system. The work combines Kakao Mobility’s proprietary driving software and experience operating in Seoul’s Gangnam district with NVIDIA’s vehicle computing platform.
Kakao Mobility plans to use NVIDIA Hyperion, a reference platform for vehicle sensors and compute, powered by NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor. It also plans to use NVIDIA Halos to support safety across the development and validation of its autonomous driving technology.
Initial development is planned around Kia purpose-built vehicles, integrating Kakao Mobility’s autonomous driving software with NVIDIA technologies. The effort aims to support future level 4 mobility services in Korea.
LG Electronics Advances Robot Learning and Factory Simulation
NVIDIA and LG Electronics successfully demonstrated NVIDIA Isaac GR00T-powered robotic manipulation and manufacturing tasks using LG’s CLOiD robot in an actual manufacturing environment.
The collaboration implemented a physical AI data flywheel connecting real-world data collection, NVIDIA Cosmos-based data augmentation, GR00T model training, NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor onboard computing and simulation-based evaluation, establishing reusable workflows for continued development and validation of CLOiD’s robotic capabilities.
The teams are using this work to refine a repeatable process for training, evaluating and improving robots for manufacturing.

items.title: Korea’s AI Ecosystem Advances and Secures Agentic AI With NVIDIA
items.content:
As AI agents take on more work, they need capable open models and security that advances alongside them.
Hyundai Motor Group is exploring NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprints and the NVIDIA OpenShell runtime, while AIM Intelligence is integrating its Starfort platform with NVIDIA OpenShell to support secure AI agents for employee productivity and enterprise workflows.
A key component of the NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform, OpenShell provides a secure runtime with sandboxed execution and policy-based controls to safeguard sensitive data, manage access to enterprise tools and govern autonomous agent actions.
AIM Intelligence, a Korean AI security company, is integrating its Starfort agent control platform with NVIDIA OpenShell. The goal is to combine OpenShell’s runtime access controls with Starfort’s detection of malicious instructions and data leakage. The company is also considering a preliminary proof of concept for the public energy sector, with potential applications across enterprise, industrial and robotics environments.
On the model side, LG AI Research is opening application programming interface access for K-EXAONE-2.5, developed using NVIDIA Nemotron datasets, including Nemotron-Personas-Korea.
Nemotron-Personas-Korea is an open dataset of 7 million fully synthetic Korean personas, grounded in official Korean statistics, that model builders use to ground training data and evaluation in Korean contexts. NVIDIA Nemotron is a family of open models, datasets and techniques that help developers build specialized, efficient AI agents.
Learn more about NVIDIA Nemotron open models and get started building secure agents with NVIDIA OpenShell.

items.title: From Chips to Skills, NVIDIA and Korea Expand Sovereign AI Collaboration
items.content:
NVIDIA and Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT) are expanding their collaboration across the country’s sovereign AI ecosystem, from AI semiconductors and data center infrastructure to talent, startups, models, agents and security.
The collaboration lays the groundwork for Korean NPU and XPU companies to explore participation in the NVIDIA NVLink Fusion ecosystem, and includes NVIDIA training and certification programs, hackathons and technical seminars to strengthen GPU utilization.
Through Korea’s AI for All initiative, NVIDIA will collaborate with three selected consortia and four leading Korean foundation model builders, using NVIDIA Dynamo software to optimize and scale AI inference.
In addition, NVIDIA today announced a collaboration with SK Telecom and Rebellions, supported by MSIT, to advance sovereign AI infrastructure for Korean models and workloads with NVIDIA NVLink Fusion. Read more in the press release.

items.title: NVIDIA Dynamo Recipes Bring Korea’s Leading Open Models to Production
items.content:
NVIDIA is releasing Dynamo-optimized deployment recipes for Korea’s leading open models: A.X K2 from SK Telecom, K-EXAONE 2.0 from LG AI Research, Solar Open 2 from Upstage and Motif-3 from Motif Technologies.
As models grow beyond the capacity of a single GPU, they must be split across multiple GPUs, requiring careful coordination of request routing and communication to maintain performance.
NVIDIA Dynamo is an open source, distributed inference-serving framework built to deploy models in multi-node environments at data center scale. It handles this routing and communication to maximize inference performance.
Optimized for NVIDIA B200 GPUs, these recipes take the guesswork out of deployment, delivering up to 2x performance out of the box. They help developers bring Korea’s open models into production faster and turn them into broadly accessible AI for All services.
Learn more about NVIDIA Dynamo.

Keychron launches four-key keypad for AI assistants
items.content:
Keychron has launched the F4 HE 8K Vibe Coding Keypad, a four-key macro pad aimed at users who regularly work with AI assistants such as Codex and Claude. The compact accessory is designed for common AI tasks such as sending prompts, using voice input and accepting or rejecting responses.
The F4 HE 8K Vibe Coding Keypad, spotted by ITHome, features four programmable keys, per-key RGB lighting and swappable dye-sublimated PBT keycaps, with 15 icon designs included in the box. Keychron is pitching it as a shortcut pad for common AI commands, replacing menus and keyboard shortcuts with dedicated hardware keys.
The keypad uses magnetic switches with adjustable actuation points, while Keychron's browser-based Launcher software allows users to remap keys, create macros and assign multiple actions to a single press through Dynamic Keystrokes. Preset layouts for Codex and Claude are included alongside onboard profile storage.
The F4 HE 8K supports an 8000Hz polling rate over USB-C, although users will need to supply their own compatible cable. Keychron's Launcher software is scheduled to leave beta on 9th November, while the keypad itself is available now for $35.
KitGuru says: Four keys may not sound like much, but Keychron is betting that many AI-assisted workflows boil down to a few frequently repeated actions. Could you see a dedicated macro pad earning a place on your desk?

items.title: MSI unveils 24.5-inch 1440p 360Hz gaming monitor
items.content:
MSI has introduced the MAG 256QR36, a 24.5-inch gaming monitor that combines a 2560×1440 resolution with a 360Hz refresh rate. The unusual pairing targets competitive gamers looking for the sharpness of 1440p without moving up to a larger 27-inch display.
Brought to our attention by ITHome, the MAG 256QR36 uses a Rapid IPS panel with a 0.5ms GtG response time, VESA DisplayHDR 400 certification and a peak HDR brightness of 400 nits. MSI also claims 94% Adobe RGB and 95% DCI-P3 colour gamut coverage, while support for AMD FreeSync Premium and G-Sync Compatible modes aims to keep gameplay free from tearing and stuttering.
While 27-inch panels dominate the 1440p gaming monitor market, MSI is instead pairing the resolution with a 24.5-inch screen. The result is a higher pixel density than a typical 27-inch 1440p display, while retaining the smaller format that many competitive players prefer. Combined with the 360Hz refresh rate, MSI appears to be targeting esports players who want both image sharpness and high refresh rates.
Connectivity includes 1x DisplayPort 1.4a, 2x HDMI 2.1 ports and a 3.5mm headphone jack. The monitor also supports HDMI CEC, includes a dedicated console mode and ships with a fully adjustable stand offering height, tilt, swivel and pivot adjustment.
KitGuru says: Most 1440p gaming monitors have settled on a 27-inch panel size, making MSI's decision to pair 1440p and 360Hz with a 24.5-inch display an interesting alternative. Is this the resolution and screen-size combination you've been waiting for?

items.title: This Week in Gaming (Week 46)
GOG Galaxy overhaul planned for 2027 with Linux support
items.content:
GOG has announced a major overhaul of its Galaxy launcher, bringing native Linux support, improved performance and a redesigned user interface. The revamped client is scheduled to launch in 2027, with beta registrations now open ahead of release.
Native Linux support is arguably the headline addition. Until now, Linux users have largely relied on third-party launchers to access and manage their GOG libraries, including on devices such as the Steam Deck. The upcoming update will allow GOG Galaxy to run natively on Linux for the first time, removing the need for unofficial workarounds.
Linux compatibility is only one part of a broader refresh for Galaxy. GOG says the launcher is being rebuilt across Windows, macOS and Linux with a cleaner interface, faster performance and expanded filtering tools aimed at making large game libraries easier to navigate. The company also stressed that Galaxy will remain entirely optional, with offline installers continuing to be available for users who prefer not to use a launcher.
While GOG has yet to provide a specific release date, the overhauled Galaxy client is currently targeting a 2027 launch window. Players interested in trying it early can already register for the beta.
KitGuru says: Native Linux support has been one of the most requested additions to GOG Galaxy for years, but the wider client overhaul could end up being just as important. Will you be signing up for the beta?

items.title: Sony cancels Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble ahead of global launch
items.content:
Sony and developer Oh BiBi have announced the cancellation of Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble ahead of its planned global launch. The free-to-play mobile multiplayer shooter will be removed from digital storefronts on 21st November, with servers set to shut down permanently on the 1st of May 2027.
Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble was first released as a regional soft launch for Android and iOS in late 2025 before expanding to additional territories, including the UK earlier this year. Sony had previously indicated that a wider worldwide release was planned, but that rollout will no longer go ahead.
As first reported by VGC, the game's final content update went live on 6th November. Existing players will still be able to jump in and play until servers shut down on 1st May 2027, although new downloads and in-app purchases are now being discontinued.
The developer thanked players for their support during the testing period, adding that community feedback helped shape the project throughout development. The game's Qwark Pass seasons will remain active until the shutdown date, while the previously paid Super Pass has been made free for all remaining players.

items.title: 10 Funniest 'Far Side' Comics About Cows
items.content: From 1980 until 1995, cartoonist Gary Larson wrote and drew The Far Side. It was a single panel comic strip filled with non-sequitur, surreal jokes mostly aimed at adults instead of children, which was unusual for newspaper comics at the time. Also unusual was the fact that, unlike most daily comic strips, The Far Side had no recurring characters. Peanuts has its gang of kids and Garfield has its cast of humans and animals, but every panel of The Far Side introduces new characters and scenarios all aimed at delivering one single joke.

Cards typically generate tokens of the same color, like white Warriors for Secure the Wastes, green Squirrels for Deranged Hermit, and black Zombies for Ghoulish Procession. Yet numerous cards in Magic: The Gathering Star Trek generate 1/1 red Officer tokens regardless of the base color, from the white Captain Benjamin Sisko to the green MACO Strike Team. The discrepancy is a nod to the sci-fi franchise’s darkest running joke.

Cat-Astrophy: How a Build Can Change Every Expedition
items.content:
Summary
How every expedition can lead to a different build.
Change the way you fight through module synergies and directional attacks.
Every build creates a unique path to uncover Polo’s story.
When I enter a new expedition in Cat-Astrophy, I don’t start with a fixed build that I have to repeat. I start with a question: what kind of Polo am I going to build this time? That idea is at the core of the module system, and it’s why two runs can take me down completely different paths, even when I return to a planet I already know.
During each run, I find modules that can modify specific abilities, stats, or systems. Some improve close-range combat, while others favour mobility, defence, or a more strategic approach. The key is that I don’t have to decide everything before I start: the build takes shape through what I find, what I keep, and how I react to each situation.
The most interesting part comes when modules stop working as isolated pieces. Some can evolve, while others hide synergies that only become apparent when combined. An upgrade that seems simple on its own can end up changing the way I move, attack, or navigate a room. At that point, the expedition becomes more than a succession of fights. It becomes an experiment: I try a combination, see what it does, and decide whether it’s worth building around.
The same principle extends to combat. Cat-Astrophy uses directional attacks that can be customized for forward, upward, and downward strikes. Each direction has different variants and can create synergies with my modules. On top of that, fatigue builds up as you chain attacks together, so maintaining a combo isn’t simply about using the same attack over and over. You have to decide when to keep pushing and when to stop and regain control of the situation. The result is a system that rewards precision and adaptation rather than relying on a single optimal combination.
Route selection is also part of the build. Each planet has different mechanics, enemies, and rewards, and you can choose their order from the ship that serves as your central hub. One route might favour an offensive build, while another could work better with a setup focused on survival or mobility. At the same time, rooms don’t follow a single path: you can encounter combat, parkour sections, events, shops, and minibosses, and decide how far you want to deviate from your route to look for a reward.
And even when an expedition ends with Polo’s death, not everything resets. The Star Fragments you collect can be used to unlock permanent upgrades, new options, and new routes for future runs. You can also discover memory fragments that gradually reveal Polo’s past and the truth behind his abduction. This gives every attempt two layers of progression: the build you’re creating now and the possibilities you’re unlocking for later.
That’s why there is no single “correct” build in Cat-Astrophy. You can prioritise fast attacks and combos, look for a more durable setup, or focus on mobility. Even the same planet can feel different when you arrive with a different combination of modules, a different route, and a different approach to combat. The reward isn’t just finding a powerful upgrade, but understanding why it works and what other decisions it can unlock.
For me, that experimentation is the true heart of the experience. Every run starts with a handful of tools and ends up telling a small story through its decisions: the unexpected combination that worked, the risk that paid off, the module that completely changed a strategy, or the route that opened up a new opportunity. In a roguelite, repetition can be part of the challenge; in Cat-Astrophy, every repetition also gives you a reason to try something different.
Cat-Astrophy is out now on XBOX, alongside Steam, Nintendo Switch, and PlayStation. The combination of builds, routes, and permanent progression is designed so that every expedition can start in a similar way and end up completely differently.

Cat-Astrophy is a fast-paced, challenging space action roguelite: its Star Cursor system and evolving modules force you to adapt your build and playstyle in every run, generating chaotic combat and precise jumps. The game delivers constant tension and rewards both improvisation and technical mastery.
In each run, you’ll travel across procedurally generated planets, combining abilities, choosing paths, and mastering parkour and real-time combat mechanics. Runs are unique: find modules that alter your capabilities, discover hidden synergies, and decide whether to take risks or secure permanent upgrades with star fragments. Death is permanent: dying means learning, reconfiguring, and retrying with new strategies.
● Cosmic Procedural Exploration: Traverse different planets each run, with rooms, routes, and secrets that constantly change, forcing you to adapt your decisions on the fly.
● Agile, Strategic Combat: Use the Star Cursor to direct precise attacks while moving Polo; action is fluid, sharp, and packed with risk-reward moments.
● Unique Builds Every Run: Discover modules and reconfigure abilities to create combinations that completely transform your playstyle.
● Permanent Progression: Collect star fragments to unlock lasting upgrades that open new routes and tactical options between runs.
● Impactful Paths and Decisions: Choose which planets to explore and which rewards to pursue; your choices shape the pace and difficulty of the adventure.
● Parkour and Precision: Deadly jumps and challenging platforming sections that blend movement and combat in every encounter.
● Cosmic Pixel Art Aesthetic: Vibrant worlds, alien creatures, and environments with personality reinforce the game’s tense and frantic tone.
● Mystery-Driven Story: Discover why Polo was abducted and what forces caused the cat-astrophe; the narrative complements the action without overshadowing gameplay.
Cat-Astrophy is for players seeking intensity, replayability, and meaningful decisions. Every death teaches you something new: learn, adjust your build, and overcome what once defeated you.

items.content: Jacob got his hands on a gaming PC for the first time when he was about 12 years old. items.title: EA restores seven classic PC games using recovered archive footage
items.content:
EA has restored seven classic PC games, including Road Rash and multiple Wing Commander titles, after uncovering an archive of long-lost master footage. The newly released Anniversary Editions arrive alongside a wider rollout of classic EA games on Steam, GOG and the EA App.
According to EA, the restoration project began after the discovery of an archive containing thousands of Betacam, VHS and D1 tapes. The footage allowed the team to recover and digitise higher-quality source material, resulting in more than 1,500 restored FMV sequences across the seven Anniversary Edition releases. Alongside the restored video content, the games also include controller support, quality-of-life improvements and other modern compatibility updates.
EA also worked directly with long-standing Wing Commander community modders during development, with some existing fan-made improvements making their way into the official releases. Players who already own digital copies of the affected Wing Commander titles through GOG or the EA App will receive the Anniversary Edition upgrades free of charge on their existing platform.
Alongside the Anniversary Editions, EA has expanded its classic game catalogue on Steam with titles from the Ultima and Crusader series, as well as Theme Hospital, Strike Commander and additional Wing Commander releases. Anniversary Editions are priced at £8.99/$9.99/€9.99, while the remaining classic titles cost £4.99/$4.99/€4.99. Introductory discounts are available on Steam and GOG until 19th November.

items.title: Hozy brings calm, tactile home restoration to PS5 on November 9
items.content:
Imagine actually enjoying cleaning your house or ripping out old tiles. Unhinged, isn’t it?
You put on your favourite music and open the windows to let the fresh air in. The dust disappears, the floor begins to shine with every sweep of the mop, and the rooms start to transform into cozy, welcoming spaces. There’s something incredibly satisfying about seeing it all come together, one step at a time.
That’s exactly what we wanted to capture in Hozy – a cozy, tactile and stress-free home restoration game that is coming to PlayStation 5 on November 9.
Welcome to Littleville
Hozy is a game where you can completely unwind. There are no timers, no scores and no pressure.
Each level in Hozy features a space with its own atmosphere and story. Your first job is to tidy it up and renovate it. Then furnish it using the sets of furniture and décor provided. Don’t worry about being overwhelmed with an endless catalogue – each level features a carefully curated set of items you’ll need so that the end result always looks worthy of the interior design magazine.
Comfort in every detail
To help you tackle the tasks of refurbishing the rooms with ease, you’ll have access to an array of tools: from a simple mop to a crowbar. We all know what it’s like to mop the floors… But in Hozy, even this is a real pleasure. We’ve done our best to ensure that using each tool brings nothing but joy.
You can also interact with the surroundings and a whole host of furniture. Open the window to let the breeze play with the dust particles. Light a lamp by the sofa to create a cosy reading nook. Play a tune on the piano or find secret messages in one of the drawers – experiment with different objects to discover what other interesting effects await you.
Every surface, every object and instrument has its own unique sound. And the music changes dynamically as you progress through the level – we recommend playing with headphones or a home cinema system to fully appreciate the sounds of the world around you.
Immersive cozy gameplay
This is something we’re particularly proud of. When we first started developing Hozy, our main aim was to make using the instruments as enjoyable and responsive as possible. And the DualSense wireless controller is simply perfect for complementing and enhancing that experience.
Thanks to haptic feedback, interacting with objects and surfaces becomes even more realistic, as every action you take is accompanied by a unique set of vibrations. For example, when a mop glides smoothly across the floor or when you’re arranging furniture. Combined with the adaptive triggers, you’ll naturally feel the resistance of the floorboards as they finally give way to the crowbar.
The DualSense’s built-in speaker helps you immerse yourself even further in the game’s atmosphere, subtly emitting additional sounds from the instruments you are currently using.
More ways to play
Once you’ve completed the Hozy storyline, comprising nine unique levels, your journey into the world of cosiness isn’t over yet. Come back to the houses you’ve already restored to discover… new versions of the previous rooms. The ‘Game+’ mode will help you look at these rooms in a new light (literally) – now you can switch between day and night, as well as furnish rooms with different sets of furniture. Some of them will change beyond recognition.
If you fancy creating something truly yours, Hozy has just the thing for you – a Sandbox mode with every item available in the game. Mix and match, duplicate, and customize your rooms however you wish. Who are we to tell you which wallpaper, background colour, window shape, support beams or light switches to choose?
But there’s more: we also have plans for seasonal events and various DLCs, both free and paid.
Make it Hozy
Of course, we haven’t forgotten about the various accessibility features, so that as many renovators as possible can enjoy Hozy. The game is available in 11 different languages and includes a range of visual and control settings. Adjust the movement speed of your tools, invert the camera, change colour display settings and much more.
If you want to make playing Hozy even more comfortable – settle into your favourite armchair, pour yourself a cup of hot chocolate and launch the game on PlayStation Portal.
We’re looking forward to November 9, when you’ll be able to enjoy Hozy at your own pace.

A Blade for the Innocent: Into the War-Torn Hutuo Region of Where Winds Meet on XBOX
items.content:
Summary
Where Winds Meet’s Hutuo anniversary update arrives on XBOX Series X|S on November 13 (PT), bringing a new war-torn campaign centered on the Battle of Zhongdu Bridge.
Players can face new bosses, try Horse Racing Chess and Jianghu Tactics, and wield the Dual Spears martial art.
Anniversary events offer more than $150 worth of gifts, including a free Outfit Set of your choice and 42 Resonating Melody draws and 27 Lingering Melody draws.
As our anniversary theme region, Hutuo, prepares to go live on XBOX Series X|S, we couldn’t be more excited to give you a glimpse of what’s to come. On November 13, wanderers across the XBOX community will step into this active, mud-and-steel warzone, navigating the devastating fallout of a sixteen-year conflict and throwing themselves into the desperate frontline defense at the battle of Zhongdu Bridge.
In Hutuo, the relentless advance of invading northern forces is set to turn the riverbanks into a brutal proving ground. Amid the chaos, we wanted to confront players with the hardest question in Wuxia: what keeps your blade raised when empires crumble and the powers above fail?
Righteousness and Conviction: Rethinking The True Essence of ‘Xia’
In Where Winds Meet, Hutuo delves deeply into the Eastern philosophy of ‘Xia’: a moral compass governed not by blind obedience to authority, but by an individual’s duty to protect the innocent and uphold justice when institutions fracture.
At Zhongdu Bridge, loyalty to a crumbling throne and righteousness toward the people pull in opposite directions. The core of this story is not about glorifying the clash of armies, but honoring the courage of ordinary folk and sworn companions who choose to stand as a living shield before an unstoppable force.
To ground that philosophy, the frontier is filled with intimate side quests showing the war from varied, ground-level perspectives. You will encounter conflicted soldiers choosing conscience over cruel military orders, displaced families holding onto hope along the reed-lined rivers, and nameless villagers risking their lives to shelter refugees. Even in history’s bleakest chapters, true heroism emerges not from imperial mandates, but from the quiet resilience of everyday lives.
Mastering the Frontline: Surviving Hutuo’s Toughest Encounters
Warfare on the frontier demands a more aggressive, tactical approach to combat. If you are preparing to cross the river, mastering enemy stance dynamics is essential.
Conquering the Fierce General, Xiao Han: Serving as the climax of the Hutuo River Campaign, Xiao Han is fortified by Blood-forged Super Armor. To counter his relentless assault, focus on high-impact parries, bait out his overextended thrusts, and execute stance-breaking counterstrikes to shatter his armor before committing to full damage rotations
Taming Moonveil Knoll with Bingshen: This solitary wanderer relies on rapid gap-closers and sweeping area attacks born of lifelong regret. Maintaining spatial discipline and dodging into—rather than away from—his follow-up strikes will give you clean openings to punish his recoveries.
Surviving Yelu Abuli’s Dark Rituals: Facing this mystic royal and shaman requires close arena awareness. Yelu Abuli manipulates ceremonial fire, forcing players to remain mobile, interrupt channeled incantations, and bait area hazards away from the center of the battlefield.
Tactical Versatility: Yuen Woo-ping’s Dual Spears (Arriving Nov 26)
To counter these escalating battlefield threats, legendary action director Yuen Woo-ping (“Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon”) led the motion capture and choreography for the upcoming Dual Spears martial art, arriving November 26.
Designed around fluid transitions, the weapon system combines two complementary combat roles. By executing the Dual-Weapon Skill mid-combo, players seamlessly weave light thrusts (Sustained Firepower) into heavy downward strikes (Stance-Breaking Impact) without resetting attack frames, sustaining uninterrupted offensive pressure against armored targets like Xiao Han.
Two Strategic Tabletop Breaks: Horse Racing Chess & Jianghu Tactics
When you need respite from the siege lines, Hutuo introduces two rich, casual-yet-tactical board game modes playable across the Jianghu:
Horse Racing Chess: Step directly onto the board as living game pieces. Roll dice, trigger familiar Mystic Skills, and race fellow players to the finish line in a lively competitive sprint.
Jianghu Tactics: A deeper strategic mode that brings the game’s Heroic Spirit roster to a tactical board. Victory hinges on clever board positioning, gear allocation, and activating character bonds to build winning synergies round after round.
Optimized for XBOX Series X|S
Exploring Hutuo’s war-torn frontier is built for the XBOX living-room experience, with Smart Delivery, HDR support, AMD FSR 2 upscaling, and an updated interface with larger text. XBOX Series X delivers a 4K upscale from 1080p, while XBOX Series S delivers a 2K upscale from 900p. Memory optimizations help keep gameplay smooth.
XBOX Game Pass Perks
After the update on November 13, simply log in and take part in anniversary events to claim over $150 worth of gifts! Just for logging in, choose a free Outfit Set worth 2,580 Echo Beads, from 12 distinct style, and easily earn 42 Resonating Melody draws and 27 Lingering Melody draws through anniversary events!
To welcome XBOX players to the Jianghu, XBOX Game Pass members could claim a launch Perks bundle featuring 450 Echo Jade, 90,000 Coins, 6 Attunement Stones, 30 Large Tuning Stones, 3 Pillow Pills, and 3 Lingering Melodies. The claim period ended January 7, 2027. There are even more ongoing anniversary perks coming to XGP – stay turn!
Experience a story of unwavering conviction, camaraderie, and the true meaning of heroism, and claim the most generous rewards we’ve offered since launch, available on XBOX Series X|S on November (PT). Come celebrate our first anniversary with us in Hutuo!

Jianghu knows no bounds: Cross-play available on XBOX, PS5, PC, and Mobile. Where Winds Meet is an epic open-world action-adventure RPG rooted in the rich legacy of Wuxia. Set during the turbulent era of tenth-century China, you take on the role of a young sword master, uncovering forgotten truths and the mysteries of your own identity. As the wind stirs across mountains and rivers, so too will your legend rise.
An Era on the Brink. A Hero on the Rise
Explore China's Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period, where political intrigue, power struggles, and epic battles shape the course of history. From the bustling heart of the imperial capital to the hidden corners of forgotten wilderness, every path is layered with secrets, sights, and stories waiting to be discovered.
Who are you — a hero, or an agent of chaos?
Here, freedom is yours, but every action has its weight. Cause chaos, defy the law, and face bounties, pursuit, even time behind bars. Or walk a nobler path: befriend villagers, forge alliances, and grow your reputation as a hero of the Wuxia world. In a world torn by chaos, become the spark that ignites change and forge your legacy!
An Open World of Infinite Possibilities
From bustling cities to forgotten temples hidden deep within emerald forests, the world flows with life—changing with time, weather, and your actions.
Traverse vast landscapes in Wuxia style: scale rooftops with fluid parkour, ride the windstride across miles in moments, or use fast travel points to leap between regions.
Uncover thousands of points of interests, discover over 20 distinct regions, interact with diverse characters, and engage with numerous authentic activities in a world that teems with life. Explore ancient cities, reveal forbidden tombs, play flutes beneath swaying willows, or drink under lantern-lit skies.
Master Your Way of Wuxia Combat
Build your fighting style to match your rhythm—whether you thrive in the heart of melee, strike from afar, or move unseen in the shadows. Choose how you engage, and build a loadout that supports your playstyle.
Take control of fluid, responsive martial arts combat built around classic wuxia weaponry, skills, and strategy. Wield weapons both familiar and legendary—sword, spear, dual blades, glaive, fan and umbrella. Switch between weapons, bows, and mystic martial arts like Taichi to outmaneuver your enemies.
Create and customize your character and progression, choose your role in a fractured world. Align with powerful factions, explore distinct professions, and forge your identity through your actions.
Adventure Alone or Forge Your Community
Embark on a rich, narrative-driven adventure with over 150 hours of solo gameplay, or open your world to up to 4 friends in seamless co-op.
Build or join a Guild to unlock a wide range of group activities—from intense guild wars to challenging multiplayer dungeons and epic raids.
Prove your might in competitive duels, or step into a shared, ever-evolving world with thousands of fellow adventurers.

Microsoft is rolling out a major update for the Xbox PC app, with the company claiming launch times are now up to 60% faster. The update also refreshes navigation across the app, making it quicker to access games, friends and Xbox Game Pass content.

The update extends beyond the desktop app. Microsoft is expanding its refreshed cloud gaming experience on the web, which was previously available through Insider previews. A new Library tab brings together owned cloud-compatible games and Xbox Game Pass titles, with additional filters for genres and input methods. The web experience is also gaining a dedicated desktop mode for larger screens, alongside new visual customisation options including dark, light and high-contrast themes.
Microsoft says the updated design and navigation elements will also roll out to Xbox cloud gaming apps on supported smart TVs and VR headsets in the coming weeks, bringing a more consistent experience across devices.

After buying EA, Silver Lake and PIF reportedly set sights on Unity
items.content:
Just months after taking Electronic Arts private in a $55 billion deal, a consortium led by Silver Lake Partners and Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund is now reportedly exploring another major gaming acquisition. According to Reuters, the group has recently approached Unity Software regarding a potential takeover.
According to a Reuters report, Silver Lake and PIF have held discussions with Unity in recent weeks regarding a deal that could value the company at around $25 billion. Unity's market capitalisation currently sits closer to $21.5 billion following its latest earnings report. Reuters claims Unity has been working with an investment bank following the approach, although discussions remain ongoing and no deal is guaranteed.
Silver Lake's interest is hardly surprising given that it already owns around 8% of Unity after investing up to $400 million in the company back in 2017. The firm has also become increasingly active in gaming alongside PIF, most recently as part of the consortium that completed the acquisition of Electronic Arts earlier this year.
A deal would take private one of the world's largest game development software companies. Unity's engine and development tools are used across PC, console and mobile game development, and Reuters notes that a successful acquisition would rank among the largest software-sector buyouts in recent years. Unity, Silver Lake and PIF have yet to publicly comment on the reported talks.

items.title: How NVIDIA Open Source Tools Are Helping Researchers Build Next-Generation 6G Networks
items.content:
A year ago, NVIDIA open sourced its Aerial wireless software, joining Sionna and a broader suite of open source tools for accelerating next-generation 6G network development. Together, they give researchers a foundation for testing ideas, comparing results and building on each other’s work — connecting simulation and AI training with experiments on real over-the-air wireless systems.
Today, researchers and developers are using these tools to build 6G-ready networks that do more than just transmit data — receiving signals more effectively, keeping robots and autonomous systems connected when it matters most, and adapting in real time as devices move through the world.
Over the past year, global developer adoption of NVIDIA AI Aerial and NVIDIA Sionna software has grown 10x, while NVIDIA’s open source 5G/6G tools have surpassed 1 million downloads. More than 8,000 research and academic institutions worldwide are using these platforms.
The projects emerging today offer a view of how future networks could look. Each addresses a different challenge, but together point toward a broader ambition for building AI-native 6G networks that deliver connectivity, computing and sensing over a converged software-defined platform for billions of people, machines and agents.
Networks That Help Robots React Faster
A robot picking up an object needs to understand its surroundings and act before they change. When the AI powering that decision runs on a nearby server or in the cloud, the wireless connection becomes part of the response time.
Researchers are exploring a more efficient approach called goal-oriented semantic communications. Instead of sending full images, robots transmit compact descriptions of objects, their positions and their relationships. Transmitting just as much information as needed allows robots to more quickly respond, especially in dynamic environments like workplaces and warehouses.
At King’s College London, researchers connected a camera-equipped robot arm to an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin running NVIDIA Sionna, which supports both software-defined 5G network and edge AI processing. In fruit-packing and cube-stacking experiments with deliberately introduced faults, the approach reduced robot task completion time by up to 52.6% and improved task success compared with sending periodic images.
In addition to quicker responses and less processing overhead, the system also proved more resilient — detecting dropped objects, recovering from unsuccessful actions and, in configurations using a digital twin, checking planned movements for potential collisions before execution.
Networks That Learn to Receive Signals Better
For a firefighter receiving live drone footage or a rescue team searching for a missing person, timely images can help guide urgent decisions. But interference and changing radio conditions can make wireless signals harder to decode, causing errors and retransmissions that delay information from the field.
AI receivers address this challenge by learning to recover information from incoming signals more effectively. Better reception could help responders maintain a clearer, more current view of a fire scene or search area.
SoftBank demonstrated this by integrating a neural receiver into NVIDIA Aerial CUDA-Accelerated RAN (ACAR) and testing it with a commercial 5G smartphone. In controlled tests with interference, the neural receiver delivered higher uplink throughput than a conventional receiver at all 15 tested settings, with a maximum gain of roughly 60%.
Another way to improve reception is to teach receivers about the environments where they operate. Using NVIDIA Aerial Testbed, ETH Zurich researchers found that tuning neural receivers using local measurements reduced block error rates by more than one-third compared with selected pretrained versions.
Networks That Learn When to Save Power
As 6G connects more devices and supports more AI applications, managing energy demand will become increasingly important.
For example, a network may need enough capacity to serve a busy stadium, but demand changes when the crowd leaves. AI can help identify when spare capacity can power down — and when it needs to come back online — so operators can reduce electricity use without dropping connections.
At the University of Leeds, researchers developed a system that predicts network demand 10 minutes ahead and uses those forecasts to guide base station sleep decisions. Before powering down, it checks that neighboring active stations can continue serving affected devices and monitors for changes that require capacity to be restored.
The team tested their approach using a portable, NVIDIA DGX Spark-powered 5G “network-in-a-box” alongside a digital twin for validating decisions against real wireless equipment. The result: researchers reported a 45.6% reduction in RAN power consumption relative to a full-power baseline while maintaining device connectivity.
Networks That Can Be Tested Faster — Before They’re Built
Before deploying a network, researchers need to know how it will perform when hundreds of devices compete for connections or radio signals run into interference. Simulating these conditions helps teams evaluate designs before committing to costly equipment and field trials. But realistic simulations can take hours, limiting how many ideas researchers can explore.
The Centre Tecnològic de Telecomunicacions de Catalunya (CTTC) is accelerating that process by bringing GPU-accelerated radio channel models, running on ACAR, into CTTC’s open source 5G-LENA network simulator. These models calculate how wireless signals travel between antennas and devices — a computation that grows increasingly demanding as simulated networks grow.
In an early evaluation, the approach reduced simulation runtime from approximately three hours to 10-20 minutes, depending on the integration, while preserving the expected statistical behavior and network performance.
Faster simulations let researchers compare more designs, investigate more demanding scenarios and refine ideas sooner. As the industry develops 6G, this could shorten the path from a proposed innovation to a thoroughly evaluated network design — helping teams build better connectivity before deploying it in the real world.
At NVIDIA GTC Washington, D.C., attend 6G Developer Sessions where researchers and developers will showcase more innovations shaping the future of wireless networks.
NVIDIA AI Aerial and NVIDIA Sionna are available on GitHub.

items.title: 20 Years of Gears
items.content:
Summary
Gears of War celebrates 20 years with a special anniversary event in Gears of War: E-Day, honoring two decades of brotherhood, community, and unforgettable memories.
Jump into limited-time Versus and Horde modes, unlock new rewards, claim RAAM as a free multiplayer character.
Get ready for Season 2: Legacy, bringing fan-favorite maps, modes, and character skins back to the battlefield. Season 2 arrives December 1.
It’s hard to believe that 20 years ago, Gears of War launched on XBOX 360 and introduced the world to Marcus Fenix, Dominic Santiago, and the genius of putting a chainsaw on a gun.
Since then, a lot has happened.
We’ve released new games, introduced new characters and enemies, and welcomed millions of players into the world of Gears. But when we think about what makes this franchise special, it’s not just the games or the stories we’ve told. It’s the people who have made Gears of War part of their lives.
Over the years, we’ve heard some incredible stories from our fans. Stories of friendships that started in multiplayer lobbies and have lasted for decades. Of campaign playthroughs with fathers or brothers, or groups of friends who made playing Horde together a weekly tradition. Soldiers that have played during military deployments and couples who met playing Gears, fell in love, and eventually got married. Not bad for a game about chainsawing monsters.
And then there are the stories that hit a little harder. Fans who have shared how Gears helped them through a dark and difficult time, whether it was dealing with loss, feeling isolated, or just needing a few hours with Delta Squad to forget about everything else going on in their lives. Sometimes a familiar game and a few friends on the other end of a headset can make a real difference.
For us at The Coalition, these are the stories that matter most.
We’ve always talked about Gears being a franchise built on brotherhood, loyalty, and having each other’s backs. It’s what makes the relationship between Marcus, Dom and the rest of the Gears so important, and it’s been at the heart of the series since the beginning.
But what’s really special is seeing those same values reflected in the community that’s grown around the games. The friendships, the relationships, the shared experiences, and the sense of belonging that comes from finding your people.
It’s an incredible privilege to steward this franchise, to build on the legacy of the creators at EPIC Games, the voice actors and all the creative collaborators who have had a hand in this universe. And to create games that people care so deeply about.
Thank you for making Gears part of your lives, and for letting us be a small part of yours.
Never Fight Alone.
A Special Birthday Gift
To celebrate our 20th Anniversary, this week we kicked off a 2-week anniversary event in Gears of War: E-Day featuring limited time modes and new rewards. In Versus, play Guardian, where only one leader makes it out alive. And in Horde Siege, try out the For the Queen mode, where the supply cache is disabled, leaving you and the squad to rely on your loadouts.

AI may be the reason GTA 6 reaches PC sooner than expected
items.content:
Recent reports suggest the gap between GTA 6's console and PC releases could be much shorter than previous Rockstar launches. Now, former Rockstar technical director Obbe Vermeij believes advances in AI may give Rockstar another reason to bring the PC version forward.
Speaking to Rock Paper Shotgun, Vermeij speculated that Rockstar could be motivated to shorten the traditional wait between console and PC releases in order to avoid losing sales to AI-generated clones, emulators or unofficial PC versions.
“I think I would be concerned, if I was Rockstar, that somebody would just take the PS5 version and get AI to change it to PC,” Vermeij said. While he acknowledged such efforts would likely be inferior to Rockstar's own work, he believes they could still impact sales.
The comments follow recent claims that GTA 6 could arrive on PC much sooner than expected. Some analysts believe a PC release could follow as early as March 2026, while other estimates place it closer to May. Neither timeline has been confirmed by Rockstar, but both would represent a much shorter delay than PC players have experienced with previous Grand Theft Auto releases.
Rockstar has yet to officially announce GTA 6 for PC and the studio has also remained silent on its plans for the next version of GTA Online. For now, Vermeij's comments offer an interesting theory as to why Rockstar may choose to accelerate its PC release plans, but whether that ultimately happens remains to be seen.

items.title: Nier: Automata’s latest patch somehow requires 366GB of free space
items.content:
Believe it or not, Nier: Automata is still getting new patches a decade later. Unfortunately, the most recent patch for PC did something a little unexpected – ballooning the game's install size to over 365GB.
What should have been a simple 8GB update instead left some Steam users staring at storage requirements normally associated with modern Call of Duty releases. Reports began appearing shortly after the patch went live, with players claiming that updating Nier: Automata now requires more than 365GB of free space to complete the installation process.
Fortunately, Square Enix is already aware of the issue and is investigating a fix. In a statement posted to social media, the company confirmed that it had identified a problem causing the Steam version of the game to display storage requirements that are significantly higher than expected following the latest update.
As a temporary workaround, Square Enix recommends downloading the base game by disabling the DLC through Steam's Properties menu. The publisher says it is currently investigating the cause of the issue and working on a permanent solution. While some recent Steam reviews have called out the storage bug, it appears to be tied to the installation process rather than the game's actual installed size. With a fix already in development, the mishap is unlikely to have any long-term impact beyond temporarily frustrating players who suddenly found themselves needing hundreds of gigabytes of supposedly free storage space.

Razer launches handheld-focused Hammerhead V3 Chroma earbuds
items.content:
Razer has unveiled the Hammerhead V3 Chroma, a new pair of wired USB-C gaming earbuds designed for handheld gaming. Priced at £79.99, the earbuds pair active noise cancellation with dual-driver audio and a 90° USB-C connector aimed at making long sessions on handheld devices more comfortable.
The Hammerhead V3 Chroma support PCs, smartphones and gaming handhelds. Rather than sticking straight out from the side of a device, the angled USB-C connector sits flush against the edge, helping to keep cables out of the way while gaming in landscape mode. The wired design also means there is no battery to charge and none of the latency concerns that can sometimes come with wireless audio.
Inside each earbud is an 11mm dynamic driver paired with a dedicated 6mm tweeter. Feed-Forward ANC helps cut down background noise, while PC players can enable THX Surround Sound 7.1 through Razer Synapse. Audio presets for gaming, music, movies and calls are included, with custom EQ adjustments available for those who prefer to fine-tune their sound profile.
The earbuds carry an IPX4 rating against sweat and splashes, while an in-line controller provides quick access to volume, media and ANC controls. A built-in microphone handles voice chat and calls, and each earbud features customisable Chroma RGB lighting. The Razer Hammerhead V3 Chroma is available now for £79.99/$79.99/€89.99.
